articles.title: Asymmetric Elongation of Uranyl within a Silver Nanocluster
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Confinement within nanoscale cavities can profoundly alter molecular structure and electronic properties, but this strategy has never been applied to inherently linear and symmetric uranyl cations (UO22+). Here, we report the first example of uranyl encapsulation within a self-assembled silver nanocluster, [UO2F5@Ag21(CCBut)14](BF4)3F (CCBut = 3,3-dimethyl-1-butynyl), abbreviated as UO2F5@Ag21. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction reveals asymmetric elongation of the axial O ≡ U≡O bonds from the ideal symmetric value of 1.77 Å to 1.788(9) and 1.837(9) Å, respectively. Raman and IR spectroscopy show extreme redshifts of both symmetric and asymmetric stretching vibrations (ν1 down to 765 cm–1). Transient absorption spectroscopy further reveals an excited-state quenching process of the (UO2F5)3– guest driven by unique confinement. High-energy-resolved fluorescence detected X-ray absorption near edge structure (HERFD-XANES) at the U M4 edge demonstrates re-engineered 5f electronic states, with a shifted and broadened 5fσ* feature indicating reduced U≡O covalency. This work establishes nanoconfinement as a powerful new route to reshape the electronic structure and property of actinide-based materials.

articles.title: Catalytic Asymmetric 1,6-Diene Cyclization via Designed Carbocationic 5- and 6- exo Pathways
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Catalytic asymmetric electrophilic alkene functionalization provides a powerful strategy for the construction of complex chiral molecules. Despite significant progress in this field, the asymmetric functionalization of alkenes promoted by an electrophilic carbon species via an exo-cyclization mode remains a formidable challenge. Herein, we report a solution to this challenge: alkenes can undergo designed 5-exo- and 6-exo-carbocationic cyclizations to generate optically pure, complex chiral compounds with high enantio- and diastereoselectivities. In this approach, for 1,6-dienes bearing bulky sulfonamide or quaternary carbon linkers, one double bond of the substrate interacts with an external electrophile, such as a trifluoromethylthio, arylthio, alkylthio, or chlorine species, generating an electrophilic carbon species that promotes the transformation of 1,6-dienes under chiral indane-based chalcogenide catalysis. Notably, the reaction can be terminated by intramolecular nucleophiles via cis-addition or can be captured by various intermolecular nucleophiles. A diverse array of optically pure polycyclic and monocyclic compounds can be obtained, including 5-5-6 tricyclic N-heterocycles and pentasubstituted chiral cyclohexanes. The same strategy can also be efficiently applied to 6-endo cyclizations, leading to the formation of 6-6-6 tricyclic and monocyclic N-heterocycles. The resulting products can be readily converted to various other valuable compounds, further demonstrating the utility of this methodology. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations were performed to rationalize the observed selectivities, revealing that the preferential transition-state conformations lower the activation barriers for the desired cyclization pathways. This work offers a versatile platform for the synthesis of enantioenriched chiral scaffolds prevalent in bioactive molecules and pharmaceuticals, significantly expanding the scope of polyene cyclization chemistry.

articles.title: Chemical Bonding Rules for Stacking-Sequence Stability in Bismuth Oxychloride Intergrowths and Their Consequences for Band Structure
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Metal oxyhalides are versatile materials, exhibiting properties relevant to photocatalysis, solid-state battery systems, ferromagnetism, multiferroics, and nonlinear optics. Here, mixed-metal oxyhalide intergrowths, layered materials formed by intercalating SrBi3O4Cl3 and Bi2GdO4Cl blocks along the c direction within a crystal, are reported. They are synthesized through a flux-based approach in which the SrBi3O4Cl3-to-Bi2GdO4Cl ratio can be precisely controlled. Despite the structural and compositional flexibility of such intergrowths, there is no general framework for predicting which local structural arrangements are preferred. Density functional theory combined with Bader charge analysis shows that preferred stacking sequences are those that minimize charge disproportionation across distinct chlorine environments, consistent with Pauling’s fifth rule, and we support this bonding-based framework through computational cation substitution that shifts the ionic-covalent balance of the metal–chloride bonding. With the preferred stacking arrangement established, this same system further reveals that intergrowth layering and Sr/Bi site occupancy modulate the interaction between the Bi3+ lone pair and anion p orbitals. Density functional theory calculations reveal that intergrowth formation destabilizes the O-2p orbitals, raising the valence band maximum for visible-light absorption, with the lone-pair interaction and layering-driven internal electrostatic field acting as competing effects on the resulting band gap. Significantly, this experimental-computational study establishes a transferable, bonding-based framework for stacking-sequence stability in layered oxyhalide intergrowths, while also clarifying how the same structural levers used to control stability can be tuned to engineer band structure.

articles.title: Clickable Photolabile Linkers for Convenient Immobilization and Light-Controlled Release of Substrates from Solid Support
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Photolabile linkers (PLLs) enable spatiotemporal control over substrate release but often suffer from slow photorelease kinetics, low quantum yields, or limited functionalization options. Here, we report a family of heterobifunctional PLLs based on (3-hydroxy-5-alkoxynaphthalen-2-yl)methyl (NQMP) chromophores that combine rapid, high-yielding photochemical cleavage with orthogonal conjugation chemistries for efficient substrate immobilization and light-triggered release. Six heterobifunctional NQMP-based linkers bearing terminal acetylene, cyclooctyne, amine, carboxyl, allyl, and biotin groups were synthesized and employed for the immobilization of fluorescent dyes, acetylsalicylic acid, biotin, avidin, and doxorubicin on silica microspheres and mesoporous silica nanoparticles. Mild UV-A irradiation resulted in efficient release of the attached payloads while preserving the integrity of the solid support. Mesoporous silica nanoparticles provide high loading capacity and are suitable for light-controlled drug delivery. The modular design, excellent photochemical efficiency, orthogonal conjugation chemistries, and compatibility with diverse substrates make NQMP-based PLLs versatile tools for reversible surface functionalization, controlled cargo release, affinity capture, and photoresponsive drug delivery applications.

articles.title: Direct Detection of the Calcium–Sodium–Calcium Metal Triad in Thermostable α-Amylases from Bacillus sp. Bacteria in Aqueous Solution by 23Na Quadrupole-Central-Transition NMR Spectroscopy
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: We report that the Na+ ion within the calcium–sodium–calcium (Ca–Na–Ca) metal triad in two thermostable bacterial α-amylases (ca. 58 kDa) can be directly detected by 23Na (I = 3/2) quadrupole-central-transition (QCT) NMR spectroscopy in aqueous solution. We show that 23Na QCT NMR signals from hyperthermostable Bacillus licheniformis α-amylase (BLA) and its mesophilic homologue, Bacillus amyloliquefaciens α-amylase (BAA), exhibit remarkable subppm spectral resolution, which is unprecedented in NMR studies of quadrupolar nuclei in proteins. Using this new 23Na QCT NMR methodology, we examine the pH-dependent unfolding, melting temperatures (Tm), long-term thermal inactivation profiles, and chemical denaturing of BAA and BLA. We also use 23Na QCT NMR to monitor EDTA titration experiments, which yielded the apparent binding constants of the Na+ ion to BAA and BLA to be (0.3 ± 0.1) × 109 and (0.6 ± 0.1) × 109 M–1, respectively. Because the Ca–Na–Ca metal triad is located in the vicinity of the active cleft, the subppm spectral resolution of 23Na QCT NMR makes it possible to detect subtle changes of the enzyme structure caused by the presence of inhibitors such as acarbose and quercetin. This work represents the first time that Na+ ions tightly bound to an enzyme are directly observed by 23Na QCT NMR in aqueous solution. This new 23Na QCT NMR approach can potentially be extended to detection of other metal ions with quadrupolar nuclei such as K+, Mg2+, and Zn2+ in metalloenzymes in their native aqueous environment.

articles.title: Giant Baromagnetic Effect Induced by Spin Engineering in Mn3(Zn0.25Sn0.25Ga0.25Ge0.25)C
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Baromagnetic effect (BME), arising from pressure-induced spin reorientation, holds great potential for next-generation information technologies owing to its strong multifield coupling characteristics. However, the practical implementation of BME is hindered by the small magnetization change and the large driving pressure required in conventional materials. Guided by spin-polarized calculations, this work successfully obtains a giant BME material Mn3(Zn0.25Sn0.25Ga0.25Ge0.25)C, which exhibits a remarkable pressure-induced maximum magnetization change (|ΔMmax|) of 2.63 μB·f.u.–1 and an exceptionally large baromagnetic coefficient (BMC, d) of 15.0 μB·f.u.–1·GPa–1. Temperature-dependent neutron powder diffraction (NPD) measurements reveal a clear evolution from the nearly collinear antiferromagnetic (cAFM) configuration with k = (1/2, 1/2, 1/2) to the ferromagnetic (FM) configuration, indicating that the spins are highly susceptible to reorientation under external perturbations. First-principles calculations further clarify that pressure modulates the energy difference (ΔE) between the cAFM and FM configurations via the Ruderman-Kittel-Kasuya-Yosida (RKKY) interaction, elucidating the microscopic origin of the giant BME. This demonstration establishes spin engineering, achieved through precise control of spin configurations via targeted element selection, as an effective strategy for realizing high-performance baromagnetic systems. It further provides clear guidance for designing materials with superior functional properties.

articles.title: Group Theory-Guided Orbital Symmetry Engineering of cis -Quinacridone: From Symmetry-Forbidden to Dipole-Allowed Transitions for Efficient Narrowband Emissions
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Although group theory is widely used to analyze symmetry and electronic transition selection rules in condensed matter physics and coordination chemistry, its use as a predictive design tool for organic light-emitting diodes (OLEDs) remains largely unexplored. This is particularly important for highly symmetric emitters, where orbital-symmetry constraints can render the lowest-energy transition symmetry-forbidden. Herein, guided by quantum-chemical and group-theoretical analyses, we revisit the long-known cis- and trans-quinacridone isomers and reveal that the lowest-energy transition of cis-quinacridone (cis-QA) is symmetry-forbidden, resulting in a negligible transition dipole moment and intrinsically weak emission. We address this limitation through a group theory-guided orbital-symmetry engineering strategy based on carbonyl-to-imine transformation of the cis-QA skeleton. This targeted structural modification reorganizes the frontier orbital symmetry, converting the lowest-energy transition from symmetry-forbidden to dipole-allowed, while preserving the rigid, highly symmetric molecular framework and suppressing excited-state structural relaxation and vibronic coupling. The resulting cis-I2A2 derivatives exhibit high photoluminescence quantum yields (ΦPL) of 70–99% and narrow emission bandwidths with full-widths at half-maximum (fwhm’s) of 20–32 nm. An OLED based on cis-I2A2-3 delivers narrowband yellow electroluminescence with an emission maximum at 550 nm, a maximum external quantum efficiency (EQE) of 32.4%, and substantially mitigated efficiency roll-off relative to conventional cis-quinacridone emitters. This work establishes orbital-symmetry engineering as a rational strategy for decoupling orbital symmetry from overall molecular symmetry, providing a general approach to transforming intrinsically weak luminophores into efficient narrowband emitters.

articles.title: Imaging of Electrochemically Programmed Single-Molecule Reactions
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Single-molecule reactions reveal intrinsic heterogeneity that is obscured in ensemble measurements. However, most existing approaches rely on extreme dilution, ultrasmall solution volumes, or physical confinement to keep individual events sufficiently sparse. Here, we introduce electrochemically programmed single-molecule reactions (PSMR), a pulse-regulated strategy that shifts single-molecule electrochemistry from passive observation to active control. It converts continuous interfacial reactions to a sequence of short, repeatable reaction trials. By tailoring the pulse waveform, PSMR controls the driving force and duration of each reaction trial, thereby regulating the probability of single-molecule reactions, while the relaxation interval between pulses allows the interface to recover before the next trial. This coordinated control enables single-molecule reactions to be actively regulated under conventional solution volumes and reaction concentrations. By coupling individual reaction events to single-photon emission through electrogenerated chemiluminescence (ECL), we can directly count and image the reactions. The ultrashort reaction windows and relaxation periods suppress diffusion-layer buildup, thereby preserving sensitivity to local reaction kinetics, even at high overpotentials. Using this approach, individual Au nanoparticles were imaged over a broad potential range, and particles as small as 5 nm were distinguished from the substrate background. Sparse photon events were accumulated over repeated trials and further analyzed using localization- and fluctuation-based algorithms, enabling super-resolution mapping of reaction activity beyond the optical diffraction limit. PSMR therefore provides a framework for actively regulating, quantitatively imaging, and spatially mapping single-molecule electrochemical reactions at nanointerfaces, opening new opportunities for mechanistic studies and rational design across molecular electrochemistry, electrocatalysis, and energy conversion.

articles.title: Kinetic Programming of Heteromolecular Contacts in Boron- and Nitrogen-Containing π-Systems via External and Internal Cross-Seeding
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: We establish a kinetic strategy for controlling the supramolecular copolymerization of boron- and nitrogen-containing π-electron systems by exploiting intramolecular hydrogen bonding in cystine-based dimeric diamides. Two dimeric diamides bearing solubilizing alkyl chains, DBB and DNN, were designed and synthesized by functionalization with planarized triarylborane (PTAB) and planarized triarylamine (PTAA) units, respectively. In low-polarity solvents, both molecules form one-dimensional nanostructures upon ultrasonication. Intramolecular hydrogen bonding between the two diamide units within the cystine framework suppresses spontaneous nucleation and generates metastable monomeric states, thereby providing a kinetic window for seeded supramolecular polymerization. Despite a difference of more than 10 kJ mol–1 between their Gibbs free energy changes for homopolymerization, external cross-seeding with preformed DBB seeds initiates the supramolecular polymerization of metastable DNN monomers. The resulting supramolecular copolymers exhibit long-lived emission arising from spatially confined interactions between the PTAB and PTAA units. The extent of heteromolecular contact formation can be modulated by switching between external and internal cross-seeding protocols. In the internal cross-seeding process, DBB assemblies are generated in situ in the presence of DNN monomers, enabling their incorporation during supramolecular growth and producing coassemblies with an enhanced contribution of heteromolecular excited-state interactions. These results demonstrate that kinetic control over nucleation and elongation enables pathway-dependent regulation of heteromolecular contacts in equimolar binary supramolecular polymers with markedly different homopolymerization propensities.

articles.title: Multicomponent Nanocrystal Superlattice Structure Prediction from First-Principles Validated against Two Decades of Experiments
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Predicting nanocrystal (nanoparticle) assembly into ordered arrays (superlattices) is a grand challenge in materials chemistry that has largely resisted first-principles theories. Here, we extend MOLT-CF, a classical density functional theory, to multicomponent nanocrystal systems and subject it to a rigorous validation by comparing against nearly 300 experiments spanning two decades of literature. We use MOLT-CF to predict stability and phase diagrams for binary superlattices of nanocrystals with linear hydrocarbon ligands, as well as many other fine structural details, for example, lattice constants, packing fractions, ligand structure, and, in the case of (cubic) perovskite nanocrystals, orientation. Significant discrepancies from experiments are noted only for the Li3Bi and Cu3Au superlattices. In the former, we predict that this lattice is stabilized by particle fractionalization, which is supported by a reexamination of experimental data in the literature. In the case of Cu3Au (for which MOLT-CF predicts thermodynamic instability against phase separation into single-component lattices), we propose two alternative candidate structures that reconcile theory with experimental observations. These results establish MOLT-CF as a rigorous platform for the computational design of next-generation functional nanoparticle materials.

articles.title: On-Surface Synthesis of a Low Bandgap Cyclopenta[ c , d ]azulene-Based Polymer
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Nonbenzenoid topologies offer a compelling strategy to tailor the electronic properties of low-dimensional carbon materials. Here, we report the on-surface synthesis of a nonalternant polymer incorporating a [7–5–5] cyclopenta[c,d]azulene (CPA) motif on Au(111) via thermally induced Ullmann coupling. Bond-resolved scanning tunneling microscopy confirms the robustness of the [7–5–5] framework. Scanning tunneling spectroscopy, together with dI/dV mapping supported by density functional theory calculations, reveals a remarkable narrow polymeric bandgap of 1.5 eV. The electronic structure is governed by the intramolecular charge transfer from the heptagonal ring to the adjacent fused pentagonal rings, resulting in a pronounced dipole moment despite being composed exclusively of carbon and hydrogen. Aromaticity analyses indicate the coexistence of locally aromatic and slightly antiaromatic regions, highlighting the intrinsic electronic frustration associated with the nonalternant topology. These findings demonstrate how the controlled incorporation of [7–5–5] motifs enables the rational bandgap engineering in carbon-based polymers and expands the scope of nonbenzenoid design in on-surface synthesis.

articles.title: Reactivity and Selectivity of Photocatalytic Nitrate Reduction Reaction to Ammonia: Pt, Pd, Ir, and Rh Single Atoms on p-Type TiO2 Nanotubes
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: We present a systematic study of noble metal (Pt, Pd, Ir, and Rh) single-atom cocatalysts decorated on p-type and quantum-confined TiO2 nanotubes for photocatalytic nitrate reduction to ammonia. All single-atom cocatalysts were prepared through a reactive deposition using different metal precursors, resulting in a single-atom oxidation state (δ+) of δ ≈ 2. At a similar loading concentration (0.2–0.3 at%) and in the absence of any sacrificial agent, Pd single atoms exhibit the highest element-specific activity for ammonia production, while Pt single atoms display a prominent photocatalytic activity with a strong tendency of nitrite reduction toward ammonia. Rh single atoms achieve the highest ammonia selectivity, whereas Ir single atoms predominantly produce nitrite due to inhibited subsequent reduction. Comparisons with single atoms deposited on conventional TiO2 (P25) and with nanoparticles supported on the nanotubes reveal that both the semiconductor properties (quantum confinement effect and p-type conductivity) and the speciation of the cocatalyst (single atom) can significantly enhance activity and selectivity. These findings aid in establishing design principles for different single-atom catalysts toward efficient and selective photocatalytic nitrogen valorization.

articles.title: Redox Properties of the Copper Centers in Particulate Methane Monooxygenase
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Particulate methane monooxygenase (pMMO) and its homolog ammonia monooxygenase (AMO), central enzymes in the global carbon and nitrogen cycles, contain three highly conserved mononuclear copper centers, denoted CuB, CuC, and CuD. While these sites have been well characterized structurally and spectroscopically, with recent studies identifying CuD as the active site, their reduction potentials have not been measured. This knowledge gap has hindered efforts to determine how the two electrons and two protons required for substrate oxidation are sourced and delivered. Here, we have elucidated the redox properties of each copper center in pMMO/AMO by protein film voltammetry using samples with copper occupancies known from cryoelectron microscopy (cryoEM) structures. The reduction potential of the CuB site, −72 to −139 mV, is significantly lower than the ∼400 mV measured for the CuD site, with consistent values determined for pMMOs and AMO from different species. Mutation of a residue in the second sphere of CuB, Glu35, alters the redox potential and impairs cell growth and pMMO activity, indicating that redox chemistry at CuB might be functionally relevant. Finally, a Pourbaix diagram constructed for the CuBII/I and CuDII/I half-reactions suggests that a proton-coupled electron transfer (PCET) process occurs at the CuD site but not at the CuB site. Thermochemical analysis of this proposed PCET process is compatible with electron delivery by a quinol reductant. These results provide new context for future investigations of the pMMO and AMO reaction mechanisms.

articles.title: Redox-Induced Polymeric Micelle-to-Coacervate Transition for Enhanced Endosomal Escape, Prolonged Drug Retention, and Improved Sequential Drug Delivery
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Polymeric micelles (PMs) and coacervate microdroplets (CMs) are both promising delivery vehicles, yet each suffers from distinct limitations. The delivery efficiency of PMs is often hindered by factors, such as limited endosome escape and uncontrolled drug release. On the other hand, CMs are prone to coalescence and aging, which hamper long-term storage and systemic injection. Here, by employing an intracellular morphological transition strategy, these drawbacks can be efficiently addressed without compromising their inherent advantages. The system exists as nanosized PMs during storage and circulation. Upon internalization by the tumor cells, the highly reductive intracellular environment induces the detachment of the poly(ethylene glycol) (PEG) shell and results in in situ formation of CMs. The formed CMs can effectively escape from endosomes by disrupting the endosomal membrane, facilitating the release of drugs into the cytoplasm. Furthermore, the CMs can serve as drug reservoirs, protecting the cargo from burst release and degradation, thus significantly prolonging the retention time and improving systemic delivery efficacy. Notably, the CMs can also sequester free drugs from the surrounding environment, enhancing sequential therapy by increasing the intratumoral accumulation of the temporally staggered agents. Thus, this micelle-to-coacervate transformable platform illuminates new possibilities for both types of drug-delivery systems.

articles.title: Tailoring Superhydrophobic Ultramicropores in Covalent Organic Frameworks for Humidity-Resistant Methane Purification
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Efficient purification of methane from raw natural gas under humid conditions remains challenging because water adsorption often degrades the separation performance and structural stability of porous adsorbents. Here we report a topology- and stacking-guided molecular design strategy that integrates ultramicropore engineering with pore-surface fluorination to construct superhydrophobic covalent organic frameworks (COFs) for humidity-resistant methane purification. Two isoreticular fluorinated COFs, TF-COF and NF-COF, were constructed by rationally controlling framework topology and interlayer stacking, generating well-defined ultramicropores for size-selective discrimination of C1–C3 hydrocarbons. Fluorination simultaneously enhances pore-wall hydrophobicity and strengthens host–guest interactions, creating a confined adsorption environment that promotes hydrocarbon recognition while effectively suppressing competitive water adsorption. As a result, NF-COF exhibits a propane uptake of 99.4 cm3 g–1 and an exceptional C3H8/CH4 IAST selectivity of 251.7 at 298 K. Dynamic breakthrough experiments further demonstrate efficient methane purification under both dry and highly humid conditions, with the separation performance fully retained at 97% relative humidity owing to its superhydrophobic surface. Theoretical calculations reveal that densely distributed fluorine atoms generate synergistic pore confinement and multiple C–H···F van der Waals interactions, simultaneously maximizing adsorption capacity and molecular discrimination. These findings establish fluorinated superhydrophobic COFs as a robust platform for energy-efficient natural gas upgrading under industrially relevant humid conditions.

articles.title: The Molecular Logic of Platelet-Activating Factor (PAF)
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Platelet-activating factor (PAF) is a well-known if enigmatic lipid signal with important roles in inflammatory responses, allergic reactions, autoimmune diseases, and thrombotic cascades. Several lines of evidence suggest that our current model of PAF’s molecular mechanism is inadequate. This report describes a recontextualized model for PAF. The revised model embeds PAF in a plasmalogen-based molecular mechanism in which activation is a spontaneous chemical reaction triggered by environmental conditions that liberates a PAF receptor (PAF-R) agonist from a membrane-bound phospholipid. The active ligand subsequently undergoes a thermodynamically driven spontaneous rearrangement into an inactive isomer, a feature that controls response lifetime. The revised model is a molecule-autonomous set of transformations that create a response with spatial and temporal control. More generally the revised model’s congruence with a similar model for RORγt supports a picture in which plasmalogens form a part of the immune system that is separate from the cell-based innate and adaptive immune systems.

articles.title: Unlocking the Tertiary Nitrogen Effect in 3D Anisotropic Covalent Organic Frameworks to Achieve Record Iodine Capture under Industrial Conditions
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Using porous adsorbents to achieve efficient capture of radioactive iodine from nuclear waste under industrial conditions remains a formidable challenge, since most adsorbents just exhibit a low iodine uptake under such conditions. We herein show two 3D [8 + 4]-assembled covalent organic frameworks (COFs, ECUT-COF-99 and ECUT-COF-100) for this challenging target. The two COFs feature a minimal-transitivity [3 4] flu-derived net, which allows anisotropic isoreticular expansion through a general sequential derived-net approach. ECUT-COF-100 was found to give an ultrahigh iodine uptake of 1.51 g/g under simulated industrial conditions (150 °C and 150 ppmv I2), 5.2-fold that of ECUT-COF-99 (0.29 g/g). Such performance also far exceeds all established organic adsorbents for this use. Mechanism studies reveal that nonaromatic tertiary nitrogen atoms allow for strong charge transfer from the lone-pair electrons of tertiary nitrogen to I2, leading to the formation of ionic iodides (I3– and I5–) and the N·+ radical cation and then fixing of ionic iodides by Coulomb interactions. This work not only provides a promising adsorbent with record iodine uptake for radioactive iodine capture from nuclear waste but also highlights a new insight into the tertiary nitrogen effect in 3D COFs for efficient iodine capture.

Can weakly interlayer-coupled transition metal dichalcogenides open up a new prospect of two-dimensional family?
articles.abstract: Weak interlayer coupling, originating from electron interactions of adjacent layers, can provide promising prospects for two-dimensional (2D) transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDCs), which can be respectively evaluated by energy criteria qualitatively and by band-gap transformation and band-shifting ratios quantitatively. Weakly interlayer-coupled TMDCs will promote the development of all-2D processing-in-memory devices together with strongly interlayer-coupled ones.

articles.title: Metal-organic pulsed laser deposition for complex oxide heterostructures
articles.abstract: Point defects govern the properties of complex oxides, yet they are hard to control precisely. Lee et al. introduce metal-organic pulsed laser deposition (MOPLD), which tunes the cation stoichiometry of SrTiO3 films to within a 0.1% solubility limit. By selectively adjusting antisite and vacancy populations, MOPLD suppresses oxygen vacancies and boosts the low-temperature mobility of the LaAlO3/SrTiO3 electron gas, offering a general route to defect engineering in oxide heterostructures for quantum materials research.

articles.title: Thermodynamic decoupling of polymer pre-aggregation in sustainable solvents enables high-detectivity flexible organic photodiodes
articles.abstract: Precise control of solution aggregation enables flexible organic photodiodes processed from sustainable solvents to combine high detectivity with strong mechanical durability. By slowing rapid nucleation and improving film formation, this approach reduces trap formation and structural defects, offering a practical route toward sustainably manufactured wearable optoelectronics.

articles.title: STING engages PKR to drive lysosomal cell death in lung ischemia-reperfusion injury
articles.abstract: Gao et al. identify protein kinase (PKR) as a non-canonical stimulator of interferon genes (STING) effector in lung ischemia-reperfusion injury. STING oligomerization at the endoplasmic reticulum drives PKR-S33 autophosphorylation and TBK1-independent IKK-NF-κB activation. This pathway induces LAMP3-dependent lysosomal cell death, and its inhibition attenuates epithelial injury.

All-Optical Ultrafast Pure Spin Current in the Altermagnet Cr2SO
articles.abstract: All-optical generation of pure spin current─the flow of spin in the absence of a corresponding charge flow─relies on symmetry based compensation between the two spin channels. 2D d-wave altermagnets, which in many respects are ideal spintronic materials due to their very low spin–orbit coupling, possess a magnetic point group and highly anisotropic valley manifolds that would appear to preclude such current compensation, excluding them as materials for the ultrafast generation of pure spin current. Here we show that infrared valley excitation combined with a THz pulse envelope allows the generation of large and nearly 100% pure spin currents in the 2D altermagnet Cr2SO. Our approach is based on a valley selection rule coupling linearly polarized light to opposite spin valleys, along with the intrinsic momentum shift that a co-occurring THz pulse imbues a valley spin excitation with. These results provide a practical and all-optical route to the generation of pure spin current in 2D d-wave altermagnets, opening a path to lightwave control of spin in an environment with very low intrinsic spin–orbit coupling.

articles.title: Atomic-Scale Mapping of an Emergent Interfacial Two-Dimensional Electron Gas at Anatase/LaAlO3
articles.abstract: Atomic-level insight into structure, charge distribution, chemistry, and electronic states is essential for understanding emergent properties at oxide interfaces. Here, we leverage the quasi-strain-free anatase TiO2/LaAlO3 interface as an ideal model system to decouple intrinsic polar discontinuities from complex strain artifacts. By combining atomic-resolution electron energy loss spectroscopy with integrated differential phase contrast, we spatially map the electronic states associated with the formation of a two-dimensional electron gas (2DEG). This correlative approach enables the direct real-space disentanglement of intrinsic 2DEG-related states from extrinsic Ti3+ defect states. Supported by density functional theory and inelastic scattering simulations, we reveal a physical superposition: the intrinsic polar electronic reconstruction anchors metallic states directly at the boundary, while oxygen vacancies accumulate further into the film, acting as a donor reservoir. This work not only resolves long-standing ambiguities regarding oxide interfacial conductivity but also provides a robust, transferable framework for related material systems.

articles.title: Broadband Near-Field Imaging of Strong Polariton Coupling in Graphene/CrI3 Heterostructures
articles.abstract: Interfacial charge transfer in van der Waals heterostructures provides a powerful, contact-free mechanism to activate two-dimensional plasmons. Chromium iodide (CrI3), a layered ferromagnetic insulator, induces significant doping in adjacent graphene, yet its nanoscale polaritonic response and the optical manifestation of this charge transfer remain unexplored. Here, we report the direct real-space observation of propagating graphene surface plasmon polaritons (SPPs) sustained entirely by spontaneous interfacial charge transfer at the graphene/CrI3 interface. Interestingly, a distinct polaritonic anticrossing near 214 cm–1 (6.4 THz) between the charge-transfer-induced graphene SPP and the CrI3 phonon is identified, suggesting this hybrid system lies within the strong-coupling regime. Our work is enabled by the recent advances in broadband synchrotron near-field nanospectroscopy and suggests intriguing opportunities for magnetically switchable polaritonics in the hybrid charge-transfer heterostructures.

articles.title: Buoyancy-Mediated in Situ Phase-Transition Microbubbles Enable Efficient Aqueous Humor Drug Delivery for Accelerated Corneal Endothelial Regeneration
articles.abstract: The corneal endothelium plays a pivotal role in maintaining corneal clarity, and its damage leads to a hydration dysfunction and secondary glaucoma. We previously identified XMU-MP-1, a Hippo pathway inhibitor, as a potent stimulator of corneal endothelial cell proliferation in nonhuman primate models. However, its therapeutic potential is limited by poor intraocular permeability and low bioavailability. Herein, we report an engineered perfluoropentane (PFP)-cored lipid microbubble (MB) platform for the buoyancy-mediated targeted delivery of XMU-MP-1. Post intracameral injection, drug-loaded microbubbles (D@MB) undergo spontaneous in situ liquid-to-gas phase transition at physiological temperature, which grants them buoyancy-driven upward movement in aqueous humor to maintain continuous direct contact with the endothelial layer, achieving an extended retention of over 72 h in the anterior chamber. Finally, the D@MB drug delivery platform accelerates regenerative processes and restores both the corneal ultrastructure and physiological function. This study highlights a minimally invasive approach that bypasses traditional surgical interventions to stimulate the repair of the damaged corneal endothelium.

articles.title: Managing Proton-Involved Kinetics via Cooperative Acceptance and Diffusion of Protons for Stable Acidic Water Oxidation under Fluctuating Power
articles.abstract: Practical application of RuO2 for the acidic oxygen evolution reaction (OER) is hindered by its sluggish kinetics and serious degradation. Here, we manage proton-involved kinetics via cooperative acceptance and diffusion of protons by constructing CrOx islands on the RuO2 surface. This architecture renders two distinct yet spatially coupled functions: interfacial Cr–OH groups at the perimeters act as proton acceptors to promote the deprotonation of OER intermediates, while the hydroxyl-rich CrOx islands dynamically restructure interfacial water networks with potentials to facilitate proton diffusion away from catalyst-electrolyte interfaces. This enhances the OER kinetics but, more critically, reduces the local acidification to secure operational stability under fluctuating power. Water electrolyzers with this CrOx/RuO2 need a low voltage of 1.61 V at 1 A cm–2 and operate for over 1600 h under square-wave loading conditions (cycling between 0.1 and 1 A cm–2, each for 12 h), exceeding that using RuO2 (stability <12 h).

articles.title: Probing and Sensing Layer-Dependent van der Waals Interaction via Induced Anisotropy
articles.abstract: Van der Waals (vdW) interaction, a fundamental force, plays an important role in two-dimensional (2D) systems by enabling atomically sharp assemblies and giving rise to many emergent phenomena. However, experimentally probing and sensing the evolution of vdW interaction between 2D layers remains challenging due to its extreme weakness, very short range, and the difficulty of keeping two atomic layers perfectly parallel while finely adjusting the interaction. Here, we demonstrate an optical strategy to indirectly probe vdW interactions by exploiting induced anisotropy in MoS2/NbIrTe4 heterostructures. We construct heterostructures using isotropic MoS2 and anisotropic NbIrTe4 to ensure perfect parallelism. We modulate and probe the vdW interaction by varying the NbIrTe4 thickness and monitor the vdW-interaction-induced anisotropy in MoS2. We find such induced anisotropy to strongly depend on the NbIrTe4 thickness and clearly observe its fast-decaying nature. This work provides a simple, noncontact approach for indirectly probing interlayer vdW interactions.

articles.title: Regulating Chemomechanical Interactions in a High-Compaction Na4Fe3(PO4)2P2O7 Cathode for Durable Sodium Storage
articles.abstract: The polyanionic Na4Fe3(PO4)2P2O7 (NFPP) cathode is recognized for its cost-effectiveness and three-dimensional framework structure. However, its anisotropic lattice evolution induces internal stress accumulation. Furthermore, the pursuit of high energy density necessitates high-compaction processing, which exacerbates localized stress buildup. Herein, this study explores and regulates the chemomechanical interactions of NFPP under high-compaction conditions. The formation of microcracks and new reaction interfaces constitutes a chemomechanical failure pathway. To suppress this, the introduction of large-sized La promotes grain refinement and close packing, thereby enhancing mechanical strength. Meanwhile, lattice substitution triggers local FeO6 structural rearrangement, strengthening the Fe–O bonds and mitigating lattice strain. The optimized NFPP-La exhibits a remarkable reversible capacity of 90.4 mAh g–1 at 10 C and retains 92.2% capacity after 5000 cycles under high compaction conditions. Moreover, pouch cell evaluation validated its outstanding temperature adaptability (−40 to 60 °C) and robust cycling stability.

articles.title: Tunable Nonlinear Landscapes in Graphene Nanoelectromechanical Systems
articles.abstract: Nonlinear nanomechanical resonators give convenient solid-state access to classical analogs of extreme nonlinear optics and to phononic signal processing. Here we report integer harmonic generation, phononic frequency sideband comb, and reverse period-doubling dynamics in a single platform of a suspended graphene resonator. A gate voltage breaks the out-of-plane symmetry of the membrane and establishes a 1:2 internal resonance between mechanical resonators. Under a single drive tone, integer harmonics are generated sequentially, forming a dense sideband frequency comb at larger drive. Raising the drive further, we find a reverse period-doubling transition: the comb spacing doubles, the line density halves, and energy flows back into the even-order comb lines. The measured spectrum yields the quadratic (ζ) and cubic (β) nonlinear coefficients of the membrane. These results demonstrate electrical control of several nonlinear landscapes in a single graphene resonator, enabling frequency multiplication, sideband comb generation, and broadband irregular motion.

articles.title: Twist-Induced Out-of-Plane Ferroelectricity in Bilayer Hafnia
articles.abstract: Ferroelectric HfO2 is a promising candidate for next-generation memory devices due to its CMOS compatibility and ability to retain polarization at nanometer scales. However, the polar orthorhombic phase responsible for ferroelectricity is metastable and requires extrinsic stabilization, complicating integration with silicon. Here, we predict that twist-induced symmetry breaking in bilayer 1T-HfO2 enables robust, switchable out-of-plane (OOP) polarization. First-principles density functional theory shows that monolayer 1T-HfO2, cleaved from the (111) surface of cubic HfO2, is dynamically stable. Twisting two aligned monolayers forms a moiré superlattice that breaks interlayer symmetry and yields bistable OOP polarization. At a twist angle of 7.34°, the bilayer exhibits ∼16 μC/cm2 polarization, primarily from polar displacements within AB stacking domains. The polarization can be switched via interlayer sliding with a low energy barrier (∼8 meV per formula unit), enabling electric-field tunability in atomically thin ferroelectric devices.

articles.title: A nanosystem manipulates angiocrine signaling for cardioprotection in male mice by relocalizing endothelial exosomes
Bioinspired nanozyme-exoskeletonized yeast-derived polysaccharides for treating comorbid anxiety and depression in inflammatory bowel disease
articles.abstract: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is a chronic condition frequently accompanied by psychological comorbidities, such as anxiety and depression. Although current treatments may alleviate some of these symptoms, the intricate pathogenesis of these comorbidities highlights an urgent need for therapeutic strategies with combined anti-inflammatory, barrier-reparative, and microbiota-modulating effects. Herein, we develop a series of nanozyme-exoskeletonized yeast-derived polysaccharides (NZEP) by integrating nanozymes with yeast-derived polysaccharides using an insect sclerotization-inspired strategy. Among them, NZEP TA-Ce , with the highest degree of nanozyme-exoskeletonization, is capable of disrupting the inflammatory vicious cycle by inhibiting MAPK and NF-κB-mediated inflammatory signaling pathways. Oral administration of NZEP TA-Ce in mice enables effective retention and accumulation in inflamed colonic regions, reverses the homeostasis imbalance of intestinal inflammation and promotes intestinal barrier repair. Furthermore, NZEP TA-Ce treatment reverses gut microbiota dysbiosis and optimizes the composition of microbial metabolites, thereby alleviating anxiety and depressive symptoms associated with IBD. This study provides a safe and promising therapeutic strategy for the management of IBD patients and their associated psychological comorbidities.

articles.title: Enhancing ω-transaminase catalysis of bulky substrates guided by binding mechanism
From ancient practice to modern innovation solving the clay mineral puzzle in brickmaking
articles.abstract: Clay minerals are the most crucial constituents in brickmaking clays, yet the specific role of different clay minerals remain poorly understood due to their natural coexistence and formidable challenges of separation. Here, we design a kaolinite-illite-quartz-feldspar system through a multiple-stage purification strategy, enabling direct evaluation of two of the most critical clay minerals for brick making - kaolinite and illite. Precise tuning the initial clay mineral assemblage yields brick strengths up to 8.5 times the ASTM C62 Grade MW requirement, without upgrading existing production methods. Mineralogical mechanisms responsible for substantial strength enhancement are revealed. Extensive analyses of 60 brick formulations uncovered a breakdown of conventional linear relationships among different brick properties due to the temperature-dependent responses of kaolinite and illite; specific formation pathways of mullite and amorphous phases; and over-firing defects above 1200 °C due to K + -induced fluxing from illite. Notably, a previously unrecognized negative correlation between mullite and brick strength is identified, suggesting a need to reconsider the widely held assumption of mullite as a strengthening phase. This work not only presents insights for optimizing high-strength brick formulations but also opens avenues for investigating the intricate contributions of distinct starting components to key brick performance.

articles.title: Hemispheric asymmetry in predicted range shifts of anti-tropical fish under future climate change
Integrated multi-omics identifies distinct immune signatures with diagnostic and therapeutic implications in immune checkpoint inhibitor-induced myocarditis
articles.abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitor-associated myocarditis (ICI-myocarditis) is a rare but frequently fatal immune-related adverse event. A comprehensive understanding of the cellular and molecular determinants driving ICI-myocarditis is essential for improving diagnostic precision and developing targeted interventions. We delineate the immune landscape of ICI-myocarditis via scRNA-seq, flow cytometry, Olink proteomics, and multiplex cytokine profiling. We demonstrate that high levels of baseline ISG15⁺CD8⁺ T cells are linked to the proinflammatory features of monocytes and in vitro experiments confirm the existence of circulating ISG15⁺CD8⁺ T cells with a high potential to induce cardiomyocyte apoptosis, supporting their pathogenic potential for cardiomyocyte cytotoxicity. Notably, intercellular crosstalk between these subsets is possibly mediated via the CCL2-CCR2 axis, and its blockade attenuated ICI-induced cardiac injury in vivo. Based on the inflammatory signature in ICI-myocarditis, we develop an 8-protein custom panel with promising performance in distinguishing ICI-myocarditis from other ICIs-treated controls. JAK-STAT pathway activation promotes inflammatory programs in both ISG15⁺CD8⁺ T cells and monocytes. Furthermore, JAK-STAT inhibition ameliorates cardiac dysfunction and inflammatory infiltration while enhancing the response to anti-PD-1 therapy in mouse models. In summary, this study implicates immune-pathogenic features of ICI-myocarditis and provides a possible basis for future therapies.

articles.title: Luminal geometry and coiled coil length determine submembrane localization of type II transmembrane Golgi proteins
Multiplexed live imaging deciphers nuclear force-driven chromatin dynamics and embryo development
On predictability of slip, rupture geometry, and speed of the 2025 M7.8 Mandalay, Myanmar, earthquake
articles.abstract: The 2025 M 7.8 Mandalay earthquake ruptured ~480 km of the Sagaing Fault, producing one of the longest strike-slip events documented and impacting a vulnerable region. Here we combine remote sensing observations and numerical modeling to show that the subsurface fault geometry and slip distribution could be anticipated from pre-event observations. Along-strike variations in coseismic and interseismic deformation reveal a helix-shaped fault geometry. The average coseismic slip equals or exceeds the interseismic slip deficit, consistent with a minimally slip-predictable model. We generate an ensemble of 3D dynamic rupture models, constrained by the best-fit static slip model, then discriminate among them using independent space-geodetic, seismic, and near-field video observations. The preferred scenario begins bilaterally, then transitions to unilateral southward supershear propagation at depth, while shallow rupture remains subshear. These dynamics are shaped by localized stress heterogeneity and low fracture energy, characteristic of a structurally mature fault zone. Our approach can inform rupture scenarios in understudied regions.

articles.title: Orientation tomography of lanthanide-doped nanoprobes by polarization-resolved micro-spectroscopy
articles.abstract: Quantifying three-dimensional (3D) orientation is critical for understanding self-assembly and collective behavior in soft matter and biological systems. Moreover, orientational analysis of anisotropic particles can characterize locally applied forces in fluids. We present a methodology for 3D orientation tomography based on polarization-resolved spectroscopy of lanthanide-doped nanorods exhibiting multiple emission dipoles, enabling 3D orientation measurements from a single viewing angle. We develop a confocal imaging setup optimized for lanthanide luminescence and a theoretical framework to extract both the local director and order parameter in nanorod assemblies. The technique achieves 0.5 μm lateral and 1 μm axial spatial resolution and is demonstrated in dense nematic liquid-crystal assemblies, resolving complex 3D topological structures, and in microfluidic flows, mapping alignment under hydrodynamic shear. This approach provides a versatile platform for quantitative studies of collective orientation, self-assembly mechanics, and alignment induced by external forces, and can be extended to other lanthanide-labeled particles and molecular probes.

articles.title: Regulation of PDH via cysteine oxidation on DLAT
articles.abstract: Pyruvate dehydrogenase (PDH) complex is a key regulator of metabolism, controlling flux from glycolysis into the tricarboxylic acid (TCA) cycle. PDH is often dysregulated in metabolic diseases and cancer. We discover here that in addition to its well characterized regulation by phosphorylation, PDH activity is also regulated via inhibitory oxidation of three cysteines of the DLAT subunit - Cys488, Cys586 and Cys618. Oxidation of these cysteines increases under oxidative stress, and is highly prevalent in mouse and human tissues. This mechanism enables cells to efficiently fight oxidative stress. Under oxidative stress, cells execute a metabolic shift, blocking glycolytic flux into the TCA cycle to shunt glycolytic carbons toward the pentose phosphate pathway. This generates NADPH which cells use to detoxify H 2 O 2 and to reduce oxidized cysteines. We find that DLAT oxidation is required for cells to mount an effective antioxidant response. Mutations preventing DLAT oxidation render PDH resistant to oxidative inhibition, impair NADPH generation, reduce peroxide detoxification, and sensitize cells to oxidative damage and death. DLAT oxidation also drives a Warburg-like metabolic phenotype of increased glucose uptake, elevated lactate secretion, and reduced TCA cycle activity. Thus DLAT oxidation is a redox-sensing mechanism that regulates PDH activity and central carbon metabolism.

articles.title: Shifting balance between habitat and climate in boreal biodiversity patterns across space, time and taxa
Signatures of bi-altermagnetism revealed by sublattice-specific circular dichroism in resonant inelastic X-ray scattering
Small viruses reveal bidirectional evolution between HK97-fold viruses and encapsulins via procapsids
articles.abstract: The HK97-fold is an ancient, conserved protein structure that assembles protein shells, forming the capsids of Duplodnaviria viruses and prokaryotic biochemical compartments called encapsulsins. It has been proposed that encapsulins evolved from HK97-fold viruses. But the higher complexity of viral capsids represents a biophysical paradox in the evolution of HK97-fold protein shells. To resolve this problem, we hypothesize the existence of simpler HK97-fold viral capsids associated with smaller genomes than those of known HK97-fold viruses. Such small viral genomes are searched in environmental metagenomes across public databases, including IMG/M and MGnify. Using hidden Markov models and protein language models, we identify and characterize small viral genomes encoding HK97-fold proteins that exhibit molecular similarities to encapsulins yet lack portal and tail genes. The phylogenetic analyses of HK97-fold proteins reveal independent mixed groups of viruses and encapsulins, and structural analyses identify similarities between encapsulins and procapsids, the immature state of viral capsids. The observations support a bidirectional evolution between encapsulins and HK97-fold viruses enabled by the viral procapsid state. Using biophysical and genomic arguments, we introduce an evolutionary model of HK97-fold protein shells, predicting that they emerged as lower-symmetry biochemical compartments and that HK97-fold viral capsids may retain biochemical functions.

articles.title: Spontaneous ferromagnetic Fe–La geminal atoms with spin and coordination modulation for acidic oxygen reduction
Vacancy-mediated ultrafast oxide-ion conduction in excess-oxygen Sillén oxybromides
articles.abstract: Solid oxide fuel cells (SOFCs) require electrolytes with high oxide-ion conductivity at low temperatures (200–400 °C) to reduce costs. Here, we report that Bi 1.9 Te 0.1 LaO 4.05 Br exhibits oxide-ion conductivity of 0.01 S cm⁻¹ at 233 °C within the “Norby gap” in dry atmospheres. This performance exceeds that of leading proton conductors, such as BaZr 0.8 Y 0.2 O 2.9 and BaZr 0.4 Ce 0.4 Y 0.1 Yb 0.1 O 2.9 , as well as representative oxide-ion conductors, including yttria-stabilized zirconia (YSZ), LaGaO 3 -based phases (LSGM), and Bi 2 V 0.7 Sb 0.3 O 5.5 . Bi 1.9 Te 0.1 LaO 4.05 Br also exhibits negligible chemical expansion and high chemical stability under oxidizing, reducing, and CO 2 -containing atmospheres. The high conductivity is associated with a layered Sillén structure composed of Bi-containing triple fluorite-like slabs and Br layers, together with oxygen vacancies that enable vacancy-mediated oxide-ion migration. Despite the presence of excess oxide ions, oxide-ion transport predominantly occurs via a vacancy mechanism, as revealed by ab initio molecular dynamics simulations, static density functional theory calculations, and neutron diffraction analyses. These findings establish a design principle for high-performance oxide-ion conductors based on vacancy-mediated oxide-ion transport in excess-oxygen Bi-containing Sillén oxyhalides.

articles.title: Compartment-specific PPARδ activity controls the outcome of cancer–immune cell competition and immunotherapy efficacy
articles.abstract: Cancer cells and immune cells compete for metabolic fitness within the tumor microenvironment. Here the authors show that PPARδ is instrumental in this battle and that activating it in immune cells can boost immunotherapy in resistant mouse tumors and improve human chimeric antigen receptor T cells.

articles.title: Evidence for maternal autoantibodies in the pathogenesis of preterm birth
articles.abstract: Preterm birth is associated with breakdown of maternal–fetal tolerance and remains the leading cause of global mortality in young children. However, the role of self-reactive antibodies has been limited to a handful of pathogenic allo- and autoantibodies linked to pregnancy complications. Here we identify a shared autoreactive signature of pregnancy in pregnant sera (n = 2,719) relative to never-pregnant controls (n = 130), using proteome-wide autoantibody profiling. Across eight human pregnancy cohorts, we define autoreactivities associated with preterm birth by comparing preterm (n = 688) and term (n = 1,505) pregnancies. Within the signature, antibodies to IL1 receptor antagonist (IL1RA) induce resorption, inflammation and vascular malperfusion in pregnant mice. IL1RA localizes to placental endothelial adherens junctions, suggesting a role in vascular integrity. These findings identify a term pregnancy humoral immune program and shared changes preceding preterm delivery, including anti-IL1RA, which may have direct pathogenic consequences. Preterm labor is linked to breakdown of maternal–fetal tolerance. Rackaityte et al. report that some pregnant mothers harbor maternal autoantibodies, including those against IL-1 receptor antagonist, that may contribute to preterm delivery.

Atomically ordered dual atomic pairs in CuAuZn2 intermetallics for efficient urea electrosynthesis
articles.abstract: Atomically ordered CuAuZn2 intermetallics with high-density Cu–Zn and Au–Zn dual atomic pairs are developed for urea electrosynthesis. The Cu–Zn sites facilitate nitrate reduction to *NH2, while neighbouring Au–Zn sites enhance CO2 reduction to *COOH and urea formation. This overcomes the kinetic mismatches between carbon and nitrogen intermediates, enabling the selective production of urea.

articles.title: Enantioselective synthesis of π-extended carbo[17]helicene via sequence-controlled quadruple [2+2+2] cycloadditions
articles.abstract: Sequence-controlled quadruple [2+2+2] cycloadditions, followed by onward Scholl reactions, enable the enantioselective synthesis of a giant π-extended carbo[17]helicene from a dodecayne substrate. This Ni-catalysed process forms a chiral nanocarbon that exhibits strong circularly polarized luminescence.

articles.title: Mechanoradical-chain C(sp3)–C(sp2) coupling with unactivated arenes
articles.abstract: Mechanically generated radicals are often considered detrimental in materials. Now, a method for mechanically generating reactive carbon-based radicals and applying them in selective C(sp3)–C(sp2) bond formation is reported. Polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons and polymers are compatible with the process, forming benzylated arene products without the need for a solvent.

articles.title: Intermittent or Continuous Renal-Replacement Therapy in Acute Kidney Injury
A comparative study of pseudo-dipole arrays and standard arrays based on the high-density DC resistivity method
articles.abstract: High-density direct current resistivity surveys play a crucial role in characterizing aquifer structures and groundwater contamination. However, the necessity of using multiple electrode arrays to achieve comprehensive subsurface imaging significantly prolongs field data acquisition, posing challenges to efficient hydrological investigations. This study validates an efficient approach that employs a single pseudo-dipole array to derive comprehensive datasets equivalent to those obtained from multiple standard arrays (e.g., Wenner α, β, γ). The pseudo-dipole configuration, which utilizes fixed reference electrodes positioned at the line ends, demonstrates vertical resolution comparable to that of conventional dipole arrays, while offering superior lateral resolution in our analysis. Numerical modeling and analytical solutions for homogeneous half-space, vertical contact, and multi-anomaly models confirmed that the pseudo-dipole array exhibits enhanced sensitivity to subsurface anomalies. Numerical experiments demonstrate that high-resolution apparent resistivity pseudosections and reliable inversion models, derived from transformed pseudo-dipole data, can effectively identify hydrological units. This method provides a time-efficient solution for detailed aquifer mapping and contamination plume monitoring, thereby enhancing the utility of electrical resistivity tomography in water resource management.

articles.title: A stochastic fractional model for computer virus propagation with memory effects and exponential delay
articles.abstract: A computer virus is a type of malware that, upon execution, can replicate itself by modifying other computer programs and inserting its code into them. This study develops a stochastic fractional-order delay differential equation model (SFDDE) to describe computer-virus dynamics by partitioning the system into uninfected S(t), latent infected L(t), and actively seizing V(t) computer populations. The model establishes the well-posedness of solutions, including existence, uniqueness, positivity, and boundedness, and identifies two equilibria: the computer-virus-free equilibrium (CV-FE) and the computer-virus-present equilibrium (CV-PE). The basic reproduction number is derived using the next-generation matrix method, followed by local and global stability analyses of the equilibrium points. A sensitivity analysis is performed to assess the influence of key parameters on virus transmission. Furthermore, a stochastic Non-Standard Finite Difference (NSFD) scheme is constructed to preserve the essential qualitative properties of the model, and its numerical performance is compared with the fractional Euler–Maruyama method using step-size refinement and quantitative error measures. The numerical experiments illustrate the effects of fractional memory, transmission delay, and stochastic perturbations on computer-virus dynamics. The results provide mathematical insight into computer-virus propagation and indicate the importance of reducing virus transmission and improving detection, removal, and recovery processes for effective cybersecurity management. The study demonstrates the usefulness of stochastic fractional-order delay modeling and structure-preserving numerical methods for analyzing complex computer-virus dynamics.

articles.title: Age-related differences in the clinical and microbiological profile of pediatric microbial keratitis in Eastern India
articles.abstract: Purpose To evaluate the demographics, predisposing factors, microbiological profile, management, and outcomes of pediatric microbial keratitis in Eastern India, with particular emphasis on age-related differences. Materials and methods This prospective study included children with clinically diagnosed microbial keratitis between April 2024 and September 2025. Clinical, microbiological, nutritional, treatment, and outcome data were recorded. Children were categorized into two age groups: ≤ 5 years and >5 years for comparative analysis. Results Ninety-nine eyes of 86 children were analyzed. The mean age was 5.9 ± 4.8 years, and 42 of 86 children were aged ≤5 years. Bilateral keratitis was observed exclusively in children ≤5 years (p 5 years. Mean duration of presentation, ulcer size, and ulcer severity did not differ significantly between the two age groups, although perforation at presentation was more frequent in children >5 years. Fungal keratitis was significantly more common in children >5 years, whereas unidentified cases were more frequent in ≤5 years. Corneal ulcers resolved with medical therapy alone in 59.6% of eyes. Surgery was required in 40.4% of eyes overall, including 18.2% of eyes in children ≤5 years and 22.2% in children >5 years. At 3 months, corneal opacity was the most common outcome. Conclusion Pediatric microbial keratitis showed clear age-related differences. Younger children were more often affected by systemic and nutritional vulnerability with predominantly sterile or bacterial keratitis, whereas older children had more trauma-related and fungal disease. Early referral, improved nutritional support, and timely globe-preserving management may reduce visual loss. Conference presentation This research work has been selected for presentation at ARVO 2026, Denver, Colo. May 3 - 7

articles.title: Alterations of SLC14A1 mRNA structure are frequently detected in weak Jka presenting donors
articles.abstract: RNA structural changes caused by mis-splicing or transcription errors may affect antigenic features of cell surface proteins. They are especially noteworthy in the field of blood transfusion where the discrepancy between DNA-based molecular testing and serological blood typing are often encountered in clinical practice and lead to mismatched blood transfusion. In the Kidd (JK) blood group system weak Jka (Jk(a + w)) phenotype is usually missed in routine serological tests and causes delayed hemolytic transfusion reactions. However molecular bases underlying Jk(a + w) phenotype are still not clear although plentiful genomic DNA-based studies have been conducted. In this study, we used PacBio long-read sequencing to characterize open reading frame (ORF) region of SLC14A1 mRNA obtained from reticulocytes of 18 blood donors possessing JK*A alleles. Among them, 8 donors were determined as normal Jka antigen presentation and 10 donors showed Jk(a + w) phenotype in routine serological tests. We found that Jk(a + w) subjects demonstrated different exon combination patterns compared to those individuals presenting normal Jka antigens, implying the resulted SLC14A1 protein isoforms could make different contributions to the formation of the JK antigenicity. Moreover, exon skipping and exon inclusion that were frequently found in Jk(a + w) individuals could induce frameshift mutations. In addition, high levels of nucleotide insertions or deletions (indels) at 130A position were detected in the transcripts of Jk(a + w) individuals. Technical artifacts were examined using synthesized RNA templates and the results suggested that artifacts generated in reverse transcription and PCR amplification (RT-PCR) processes were unlikely the causes of these observations. All the results indicate that SLC14A1 RNA splicing and transcription fidelity play crucial roles in determining Jka antigen presentation.

articles.title: An operational key performance indicator framework and reference data from a multi-room pencil beam scanning proton therapy center
articles.abstract: Purpose Multi-room proton therapy centers face unique operational challenges related to shared beam delivery systems, extended treatment hours, and high clinical complexity. This study presents a structured framework of key performance indicators (KPIs) and reports longitudinal single-institution operational reference data from a multi-room proton therapy center to support operational assessment and continuous quality improvement. Methods and materials Operational KPIs were retrospectively evaluated for calendar year 2024 at a three-room proton therapy center utilizing pencil beam scanning. KPIs were categorized into three areas: beam performance, treatment planning and pre-treatment workflow, and treatment room operations. Beam performance metrics included site- and room-specific uptime and beam pauses. Treatment planning metrics quantified CT simulation–to–patient scheduling timelines with attribution to physician, dosimetry, and physics components. Treatment room operations metrics included appointment variance, slot utilization, and waiting-for-beam (WFB) time. Data were collected automatically using a commercial analytics platform integrating radio-frequency identification tracking and oncology information system. Metrics were analyzed longitudinally and stratified by treatment room, disease site, and workflow component. Results For calendar year 2024, aggregate site uptime was 95.3%, weighted according to clinical operating time across the three treatment rooms; individual room uptimes ranged from 91.8% to 97.2%. Beam pauses were frequent but brief, resulting in 2,238 minutes of cumulative lost treatment time across 2024, equivalent to approximately 0.5% of total clinical operating time. Annual mean treatment planning time was 8.5 business days, with physician-related activities contributing the greatest variability across disease sites. Monthly average appointment variance ranged from 5 to 11 minutes, with most treatments initiated within 10 minutes of scheduled time. Across 2024, slot utilization was stable, with 73% of fractions completed within scheduled slots. Mean overrun and underrun durations were modest, although P90 overrun durations exceeded 10 minutes throughout the year. Mean WFB times were low and consistent, ranging from 1.5 to 2.3 minutes. Conclusions This study presents a practical KPI framework and a single-institution operational reference data for multi-room proton therapy center. These metrics may support longitudinal monitoring, identification of workflow inefficiencies, data-driven decision-making, and future multi-institutional benchmarking efforts.

articles.title: Calculation and application of the selenium toxicity coefficient for potential ecological risk assessment
articles.abstract: To address the lack of a unified quantitative index for the ecological risk assessment of selenium (Se) in soils, the toxicity coefficient of Se was first determined based on Håkanson’s principles, and the spatial distribution and potential ecological risk of Se in surface soils across China were systematically evaluated. The results showed that the toxicity coefficient of Se was determined as 2. Based on the corrected background reference value, approximately 69.9% of the sampling sites were classified as low to moderate ecological risk, 24.4% as considerable risk, and 5.7% as high or very high risk. The elevated risk sites were predominantly confined to localized areas underlain by Se-rich strata, such as Enshi in Hubei Province and Ziyang in Shaanxi Province. A substantial consistency was observed between the potential ecological risk factor (Eri) and the geoaccumulation index (Igeo), with a quadratic weighted Kappa coefficient (κw) of 0.729, indicating that the two classification systems yield comparable results in terms of risk ranking. This study provides a preliminary screening benchmark for identifying areas that warrant further site-specific investigation.

articles.title: Deep learning-based predictions and analysis of Norovirus dynamics using a fractional-order mathematical model
articles.abstract: Norovirus, which is extremely contagious and has a significant impact on the gastrointestinal tract, has also been one of the main potential threats to health in the population. The use of fractional calculus has received much interest in the past few years with regard to the modeling of infectious diseases, especially because it allows modeling the memory and nonlocal processes in a dynamic system. In this study, a mathematical model is developed to investigate the transmission dynamics of norovirus. The proposed model consists of five epidemiological compartments: susceptible, exposed, infected, vaccinated, and recovered populations. The existence and uniqueness of the mathematical model are proven by a fixed-point theorem. The findings demonstrate that the sustainability of the disease-free equilibrium increases with a decrease in fractional order. In order to observe the effects of the fractional order on the dynamics of disease, numerical simulations are carried out based on the three-step Adams-Bashforth procedure, which supports the theoretical results with graphical illustrations. Moreover, the results are validated through the comparison with deep neural networks. The comprehensive nature of numerical simulations carried out at different fractional orders and transmission parameters indicates that the dynamics of fractional orders are effective in describing memory and heterogeneity of the disease transmission, which are characterized by classical integer-order models only to a limited extent. The results also indicate that the high coverage of vaccination and improvement in the effectiveness of treatment will greatly decrease the prevalence of infections. Further, the model has been demonstrated to be numerically stable and positive in real parameter disclosures. Altogether, this study provides a reliable mathematical approach and better understanding for analyzing disease dynamics and may be extended to other applications in epidemiology and related scientific fields.

articles.title: Dietary and lifestyle quality and endometrial cancer: Incidence and survivorship outcomes—An umbrella review of systematic reviews and meta-analyses
articles.abstract: Composite dietary and lifestyle indices capture the combined effects of multiple health-related behaviours and may better reflect real-world cancer risk and survivorship than single exposures. This umbrella review aimed to evaluate and grade the strength of evidence for associations between adherence to composite dietary and lifestyle quality indices and endometrial cancer (EC) outcomes, including risk, EC-specific survival, overall survival, disease recurrence, quality of life, and new-onset cardiometabolic diseases. PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, CINAHL, and Cochrane Library databases were systematically searched for relevant systematic reviews. Evidence was graded using prespecified umbrella review criteria. A total of 21 systematic reviews were included. Nine investigated diet quality (7 meta-analyses) and 12 investigated lifestyle exposure or interventions (8 meta-analyses). The outcomes assessed were EC risk (N = 14), all-cause or cancer-specific mortality (N = 5), recurrence (N = 4), overall or cancer-specific survival (N = 3), QoL (N = 5), and cardiometabolic events (N = 1). Following a Mediterranean diet was associated with 29% lower odds of EC (pooled OR = 0.71, 95% CI 0.51–0.98; class IV), whereas Western dietary patterns were associated with 20% higher odds of EC (pooled OR = 1.20, 95% CI 1.03–1.39; class IV). A combined healthy diet and lifestyle approach was associated with a 46% lower hazard of EC incidence (pooled HR = 0.54, 95% CI 0.42–0.71; class III), although heterogeneity was high. No significant associations were observed between lifestyle interventions and global or domain-specific quality of life (QoL) across follow-up durations ranging from 9 weeks to 12 months, irrespective of the validated assessment instruments used. Evidence remains limited regarding the associations between diet and lifestyle factors and EC recurrence, survival, mortality, and cardiometabolic outcomes. Our umbrella review identified suggestive (class III–IV) evidence for associations between healthy dietary patterns, particularly the Mediterranean diet, and combined healthy lifestyle approaches with lower EC incidence. Evidence remains insufficient or non‐significant for post-diagnosis outcomes, underscoring the need for further high-quality research.

articles.title: Digital patient decision aids for cancer prevention in socially disadvantaged women: A scoping review protocol
articles.abstract: This scoping review aims to map and analyze the existing evidence on digital Patient Decision Aids (PtDAs) for cancer prevention targeting socially disadvantaged women. Cancer is a leading cause of premature mortality among women. Cancer prevention strategies can effectively reduce cancer incidence and mortality. Socially disadvantaged women face lower screening rates and higher mortality. Effective cancer prevention requires informed decision-making. One approach is the use of digital PtDAs. They represent a promising innovation for this population. However, their characteristics, development process, and evaluation for cancer prevention targeting this population remain underexplored. This scoping review will include digital PtDAs designed to meet the needs of socially disadvantaged women aged 18–75 in the context of cancer prevention and meeting the minimum criteria established by the International Patient Decision Aid Standards. We will include studies and sources covering quantitative and qualitative research, and gray literature. This scoping review will follow the JBI methodology for scoping reviews. A comprehensive three-step search will be conducted across MEDLINE, CINAHL, Embase, Web of Science, Cochrane databases, Google Scholar and gray literature sources. All studies and sources available in any language will be considered. Citations will be imported into Rayyan for screening. Two independent reviewers will conduct study selection, data extraction, and analysis. Data will be summarized using tables and descriptive content analysis to identify characteristics, development processes, and evaluation methods of digital PtDAs. The review will be reported in accordance with PRISMA-ScR guidelines. Findings will be submitted for publication in an international peer-reviewed journal and presented at national and international conferences focused on cancer prevention, shared decision-making, digital health or socially disadvantaged women. We will share findings with healthcare professionals, public health and cancer prevention stakeholders, and socially disadvantaged communities and their network. This protocol has been registered with the Open Science Framework (https://osf.io/f3428/).

articles.title: Dynamics and optimal harvesting of a fractional predator–prey system with fear and anti-predator mechanisms
articles.abstract: Wild prey are shaped by predators long before they are caught. Fear alone suppresses reproduction, physical refuges reduce exposure, and many species strike back directly at their attackers, imposing real costs on the hunter. To investigate the combined effects of these behavioral mechanisms, we develop a Caputo fractional-order predator–prey model incorporating fear-induced reproductive suppression, proportional prey refuge, active anti-predator retaliation, a Holling type II functional response, and nonlinear saturation harvesting. The fractional memory order accounts for hereditary effects in ecological interactions, with the classical integer-order system recovered as a special case. Fundamental dynamical properties of the model, including non-negativity, uniform boundedness, and existence and uniqueness of solutions, are established. All biologically feasible equilibria are characterized, and local and global asymptotic stability conditions are derived using Matignon’s criterion and Lyapunov function techniques. The analysis further reveals that the coexistence equilibrium can lose stability through a Hopf bifurcation induced by the fractional memory order, and a critical threshold for the onset of this bifurcation is derived. Numerical evaluation of the first Lyapunov coefficient provides evidence that the bifurcation is supercritical, leading to the emergence of stable periodic oscillations. Applying Pontryagin’s Maximum Principle, we derive a bang–singular–bang optimal harvesting strategy that improves discounted net revenue while maintaining ecologically sustainable population levels. Numerical simulations support the theoretical results and illustrate the combined influence of fear, refuge, anti-predator behavior, harvesting, and memory on ecosystem dynamics.
