More than half of insured, asymptomatic adults with risk factors screened in this community program had abnormal results, with steep age and sex gradients and unexplained variation across health systems. Black, Hispanic, and female residents were under-represented relative to the county

articles.title: Risk factors for a low five-minute Apgar score at a provincial referral hospital in southern Mozambique: A secondary analysis of a matched case-control study
articles.abstract: Perinatal asphyxia is a leading cause of neonatal death in Mozambique and the main cause of early neonatal death in the referral hospitals of Gaza Province. Where blood gas analysis is unavailable, a low five-minute Apgar score remains a key marker of intrapartum compromise. This study aimed to identify maternal, obstetric, fetal and institutional factors associated with a low five-minute Apgar score at Xai-Xai Provincial Hospital, Mozambique. We conducted a secondary analysis of the records of 471 newborns delivered between January 2016 and December 2018, drawn from a matched case-control study of early neonatal death. The outcome was a five-minute Apgar score below 7. Associations were estimated with bivariate and multivariable conditional logistic regression and are reported as odds ratios with 95% confidence intervals. Of the 471 newborns, 76 (16.1%) had a low five-minute Apgar score. In the multivariable model, a gestational age of 42 weeks or more (adjusted odds ratio 4.04; 95% confidence interval 1.18-13.82) and ruptured membranes on admission (adjusted odds ratio 3.69; 95% confidence interval 1.37-9.96) were associated with higher odds of a low score, whereas partograph use during labour was associated with lower odds (adjusted odds ratio 0.07; 95% confidence interval 0.01-0.31). The association with preterm birth was attenuated after adjustment for birth weight. Post-term birth and ruptured membranes on admission were associated with a low five-minute Apgar score, and partograph use with lower odds. Because the sample was drawn from a study of early neonatal death, these associations should be confirmed in unselected birth cohorts. They nonetheless support strengthening intrapartum monitoring in Mozambican referral maternities.

articles.title: Small Enough to Use, Sharper Together: VQIDS and FIRM in U.S. Youth Ages 6 18
articles.abstract: Objective: Brief measures of depressive symptoms and family psychiatry history may support the identification of youth who warrant further assessment, but their interpretation requires population-based measurement evidence. This study evaluated the Very Quick Inventory of Depressive Symptomatology (VQIDS) and Family Index of Risk for Mood (FIRM) in the BENCHMARK 2025 national survey. Method: The sample consisted of 2,252 parent reports for children aged 6-18 years and 1,008 linked adolescent self-reports aged 12-18 years. Analyses examined VQIDS dimensionality, reliability, item functioning, age- and sex-based norms, and informant agreement, alongside FIRM score distributions, alternative scoring approaches, and associations with depressive symptoms. Results: VQIDS findings supported a single dimension and good internal consistency, with greatest IRT precision at elevated symptom levels and no practically meaningful differential item functioning across age or sex. Two-week stability was moderate, and parent-adolescent agreement was lower within more symptomatic subsets. FIRM totals showed stronger cross-informant agreement and retest stability. Family history scores were associated with higher VQIDS percentiles and discriminated scores at or above the 90th percentile across informants (AUROC = .670-.698). FIRMs associations were strongest with internalizing symptoms, although evidence was mixed for mood specificity. Conclusions: These findings provide a measurement and normative foundation for brief depressive symptom assessment and support family history as a complementary correlate of symptom elevation. Diagnostic and prospective prediction utility require further evaluation.

articles.title: Smartphone pupillometry to predict hematoma expansion in Hemorrhagic stroke patients: A protocol for prospective cohort study
articles.abstract: Introduction: Hematoma expansion is a main cause of early worsening after spontaneous intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH). Many hospitals in low income countries have no invasive pressure monitoring and no automated pupillometer. Staff use the Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) and a penlight to check the pupils, and pupil changes seen with a penlight usually come late. The speed of pupil constriction may change earlier, and smartphones record video fast enough to measure it. Methods and analysis: This will be a single-centre prospective cohort study of 120 adults with ICH on non-contrast computed tomography (NCCT) who arrive within 24 hours of symptom onset. At admission and every 6 hours until 48 hours, we will record a 6 second smartphone video of each eye reacting to a flash, using an eyecup that blocks ward light. Open-source software will measure the pupil diameter in every frame. The main measure is constriction velocity (CV). The primary outcome is hematoma expansion (an increase of more than 6 mL or more than 33%) on NCCT at 24 hours. Secondary outcomes are a fall of 2 or more GCS points within 48 hours and in-hospital death. The primary analysis estimates the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve for the percentage fall in CV from each patient's first recording. Ethics and dissemination: Patients or their legal representatives will give written consent. Results will be submitted to a peer-reviewed journal, and the analysis code will be made public.

articles.title: Stage-Aware and Explainable Machine Learning for Predicting IVF Implantation
articles.abstract: Predicting implantation outcomes in vitro fertilization (IVF) is challenging because clinically relevant information becomes available at different points during treatment. In this study, we developed a stage-aware, leakage-conscious, and explainable machine-learning framework to predict implantation using a public IVF dataset. {beta}-HCG was excluded to avoid potential downstream target leakage. The data were divided into training, validation, and independent test sets. Several machine-learning models, including Logistic Regression, Random Forest (RF), Extra Trees, XGBoost, and Hist Gradient Boosting, were optimized using stratified cross-validation. A fixed RF model was then evaluated at three stages of the IVF process, using baseline couple characteristics, gamete and fertilization variables, and embryological variables, respectively. Model performance improved as additional treatment-related information became available, with the largest improvement observed after the inclusion of embryological variables. The final RF model showed good predictive performance on the independent test set. The number of embryos was consistently identified as the most important predictor across RF, permutation, and SHAP analyses. Overall, the findings suggest that IVF implantation prediction becomes more accurate as later-stage treatment information is incorporated, particularly information related to embryological characteristics. The proposed approach also provides interpretable predictions while reducing the risk of information leakage. Further evaluation using independent clinical datasets is needed before the framework can be considered for clinical use.

articles.title: Stage-specific overall survival with complete five-year follow-up after D2 gastrectomy for gastric cancer at a referral hospital in Shanghai, China: a reference for comparing hospitals
articles.abstract: Background. Comparing long-term outcomes of gastric cancer surgery between hospitals requires a common reference. Risk-adjusted benchmarks depend on the model and population used to build them and are difficult for another hospital to reproduce. TNM stage is a prognostic classification already recorded for every resected gastric cancer. We report unadjusted stage-specific overall survival from a consecutive cohort with complete follow-up as reference data and propose a minimal dataset for producing comparable figures elsewhere. Methods. The cohort comprised 690 consecutive eligible patients who underwent curative-intent D2 gastrectomy for stage I to III adenocarcinoma at Ruijin Hospital, Shanghai, in 2019. All operations were performed by eight experienced, high-volume consultant surgeons. Stage followed the AJCC 8th edition: pTNM after upfront surgery (n = 570) and ypTNM after neoadjuvant chemotherapy (n = 120). Overall survival was estimated by the Kaplan-Meier method without adjustment. Results. There were 199 deaths, 181 within five years. Every survivor was followed for at least 68.1 months. After upfront surgery, five-year overall survival was 95.0% (95% CI 91.4 to 97.1) for stage I, 83.8% (76.5 to 89.0) for stage II and 56.5% (49.2 to 63.1) for stage III, and was 95.0% in IA and 95.2% in IB, falling to 26.7% in IIIC. After neoadjuvant chemotherapy, five-year survival was 78.6%, 61.9% and 31.3% for ypStage I, II and III. Pooling pTNM and ypTNM lowered stage III five-year survival to 50.2%. The proposed minimal dataset has 16 items, 13 of them recorded during the admission for gastrectomy. Conclusions. These figures are intended as a reference for comparing hospitals rather than as a standard of care. We propose 16 items, most of them routinely recorded, from which another hospital can produce the same table and compare its results by stage.

articles.title: Testing structural interpretations beyond goodness-of-fit in a phenomenological epidemic model: A reproducibility-oriented case study
articles.abstract: Simulation models are widely used to support counterfactual inference in settings where direct experimental validation is difficult or infeasible. However, for phenomenological models calibrated to observational time series, goodness-of-fit does not necessarily establish that the structural assumptions underlying such inferences are uniquely supported by the data. Here, we examine this issue using a published COVID-19 transmission model for Japan that incorporates empirical inputs including human mobility, variant prevalence, and vaccination and has been used to estimate the effects of alternative vaccination scenarios. Using the publicly archived code together with a reconstructed substitute for a restricted-access input file required by the released implementation, we first reproduced the published model behaviour. We then performed two complementary computational stress tests. First, the vaccination-related input was suppressed and the remaining parameters were re-estimated against the original epidemic trajectory. Second, as a complementary test of trajectory-level flexibility, the model was refitted to synthetic target series with qualitatively different temporal structures while retaining the empirical mobility and variant inputs. The model retained substantial fitting capacity in both tests: suppression of the vaccination-related input caused only a limited deterioration in fit to the original trajectory, while qualitatively different synthetic trajectories could also be reproduced through parameter adjustment. Variation in fitted parameters across these conditions was also consistent with compensatory parameter behaviour. These results do not imply that vaccination had no effect or that the original model is invalid. Rather, they provide empirical evidence that, in this case, goodness-of-fit to the observed epidemic trajectory alone does not uniquely support the structural interpretation required for vaccination-related counterfactual inference. The study illustrates the value of reproducible computational stress testing as a complement to, rather than a substitute for, formal identifiability or model-comparison analyses.

articles.title: The cry as a vital sign: A smartphone based study protocol of neonatal cry acoustics in hypoxic ischemic encephalopathy
articles.abstract: Background. Many Indian special newborn care units (SNCUs) cannot offer amplitude-integrated EEG (aEEG) or early MRI, so bedside judgement decides which newborns receive closer neurological attention. Earlier work found that asphyxiated newborns cry with a higher pitch and shorter phonation than healthy newborns, and a meta-analysis reported higher fundamental frequency, dysphonation and atypical melody in infants with neurological dysfunction, with wide differences between studies. Aim. To determine whether basic acoustic features of a smartphone-recorded pain cry (following a heel prick) can differentiate term newborns with HIE from control newborns. Also, to track changes in cry acoustics over the first 72 hours of life and evaluate their association with the clinical severity and short-term outcomes of encephalopathy. Design. A prospective, single centre diagnostic accuracy and cohort study in a tertiary SNCU. Three groups of term newborns are recorded: newborns with HIE, healthy comparators, and sick comparators who do not have HIE. Every newborn is recorded after the same stimulus, the first clinically indicated heel-prick. Newborns with HIE and sick comparators are recorded again at 24 hours, 72 hours and before discharge. A cry that is late or absent counts as a result and not as a missing value. Three clinicians blinded to group also classify the cries by listening, so the phone-based measures can be compared with the human ear. Analysis. The primary outcome is the area under the ROC curve of a logistic model with five pre-specified acoustic predictors. The target is 180 analyzable newborns (70 with HIE and 110 comparators). Reporting follows STARD and TRIPOD+AI. Relevance. In a South Asian trial, cooling did not reduce death or disability at 18 months and increased death alone. A cry tool in this setting is therefore proposed to help prioritize EEG, seizure surveillance, closer observation and referral. It is not proposed as a trigger for cooling. Keywords: neonatal encephalopathy; infant cry; acoustic analysis; smartphone; diagnostic accuracy; low-resource setting.

articles.title: Uncovering Social Media Influencers' Health Posts: A Youth-Driven Mixed Method Study
articles.abstract: Social media influencers serve as a key source of health information for adolescents but often lack expertise, have commercial motives, and may spread misleading or harmful content. This study examines the health-related content shared by influencers, the prevalence of advertising, and how adolescents evaluate potential benefits and risks. Using a mixed-methods approach, we employed a quantitative descriptive method involving citizen science (Study 1) and a qualitative content analysis (Study 2). In Study 1, 336 adolescents from 16 Austrian schools documented and categorized 2,147 posts from 255 influencers. The most common topics included sports and fitness (50.5%), beauty ideals (29.6%), food and nutrition (27.6%), and cooking (19.1%). Although advertisements appeared in 41.5% of posts, adolescents rated 60.4% of them as beneficial and only 4.5% as harmful. The qualitative analysis of a subsample of the 90 most prominent posts showed that adolescents appreciated motivational aspects (e.g., healthy eating) but often overlooked problematic elements such as misleading claims, sexualized body ideals, and the linking of health messages to commercial products. Enhancing persuasion knowledge and critical thinking through education, along with stricter regulation of harmful products, is crucial to safeguarding youth online.

articles.title: Unnoticed high human infection incidence for West Nile virus and Usutu virus in the Netherlands: evidence from a longitudinal nationwide cohort, 2020-2023
articles.abstract: Background Ecological surveillance indicates (regional) establishment of West Nile virus (WNV) and Usutu virus (USUV) in the Netherlands. However, the incidence of human infections remains unknown. Methods We identified WNV and USUV infections in the Netherlands in 2020-2023, using a longitudinal, nationwide population-based cohort, applying a two-tiered serology approach based on protein micro-array and virus neutralization. IgG data were used to estimate overall seroprevalence and infection incidence, and to study antibody longevity. Study set-up enabled tracking of the period of seroconversion and linking of self-reported travel history. The analyses took account of the survey design and weights were incorporated to match the Dutch population distribution following census data. Findings Among 4290 participants, we identified 113 probable WNV and/or USUV cases, including 55 seroconversions. Thirty-six cases were confirmed by antibody neutralization, of which 12 seroconverted. Six confirmed seroconverters were identified as autochthonous infections. The overall weighted seroprevalence was estimated at 0.54% (0.21-0.87%) for WNV and 0.25% (0.09-0.40%) for USUV. The weighted incidence for autochthonous WNV and USUV infection was estimated as respectively 0.06% (95% CI 0-0.12%) and 0.04% (95% CI 0-0.09%). Interpretation The estimated infection incidence and seroprevalence of WNV and USUV indicate a substantial underdiagnosis of clinical cases in the Netherlands in 2020-2023. These observations highlight the need for increased awareness among physicians to identify cases and the need for continued paired syndromic-laboratory surveillance for these viruses.

articles.title: Whole person health across sociodemographic groups of adults in the United States
articles.abstract: Chronic disease accounts for most health care expenditures in the United States (US), highlighting the need for approaches that address health across interconnected spiritual, mental/emotional, behavioral, physical (including environmental), and social domains. Whole person health (WPH) is increasingly recognized as important for alleviating chronic disease burdens but has not been well-described across various sociodemographic groups of US adults. Using cross-sectional data from the 2025 National Health Interview Survey, we sought to describe the prevalence of WPH and its components among US adults overall and by age, sex, and race along with ethnicity. Participants responded to the nine-item Whole Person Health Index (WPHI), which we used to assess continuous scores (range: 9-45, where higher scores indicated improved health) and ''optimal'' (excellent/very good vs. good/fair/poor) overall and domain-specific WPH. Using survey procedures, we estimated medians (IQR) and prevalence (95% CI) and compared subgroups using multiple comparison correction. Among 23,884 NHIS participants aged 18 years and older (mean age (SE)=48 (0.2) years), representing approximately 261,620,640 US adults, the median WPHI score was 33 (28-37) and slightly over half (57% [56%-58%]) of adults were classified as having ''optimal'' overall WPH. Optimal social/family connections (72% [72%-73%]) were frequently reported; ''optimal'' sleep was infrequently reported (36% [35%-37%]). WPH and its components were generally highest among younger adults. Men and women differed in WPH domains but not in overall WPH. Non-Hispanic (NH) American Indian/Native Alaskan and NH-Black adults generally had lowest prevalence of optimal WPH and its components, which was often higher among Hispanic/Latino adults and highest among NH-Asian and White adults. These results showing variation in WPH in the US may inform future investigations of WPH, related predictors and health outcomes, and health disparities.

articles.title: X-chromosome methylation patterns in females with multiple sclerosis
articles.abstract: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is approximately three times more common in females than in males, but sex-linked epigenetic mechanisms remain incompletely understood. We tested whether X-chromosome DNA methylation differs in females with MS and whether associated sites preferentially map to genes normally subject to X-chromosome inactivation (XCI). An X-chromosome-focused epigenome-wide association study was performed in whole blood from three datasets comprising 496 females with MS and 509 female controls, with independent evaluation in isolated CD4+ T cells (80 cases, 76 controls). At FDR < 0.01, 3 182 X-chromosome CpGs were hypomethylated in MS (mean {Delta}{beta} = -0.035). Hypomethylated CpGs were strongly enriched in non-escape genes normally subject to XCI relative to escape genes (OR 6.77; p = 1.55x10-57) and mapped to immune and chromatin-related processes. Exploratory cis-mQTL analysis identified strong local genetic effects at a small subset of loci, including WAS, IRAK1 and TLR7. In CD4+ T cells, 2 080 of the 3,182 whole-blood hypomethylated CpGs (65.4%) were also significantly hypomethylated. These findings identify a reproducible X-chromosome hypomethylation signature in female MS and support direct investigation of inactive-X regulation, XCI escape and X-linked immune gene dosage.

articles.title: A Redox-Switchable Framework Bridges Dilute-Stream CO2 Capture and Conversion
articles.abstract: Integrating CO2 capture from dilute sources with electrochemical conversion could bypass the energy-intensive separation and regeneration required in conventional carbon capture and utilization. Yet combining these functions, particularly for multicarbon electrosynthesis, remains challenging. Here, we report an ion-regulated conjugated pyridine-imine framework (Cr-PyN) that performs both electrochemical CO2 capture and selective conversion to acetate within a single metal-free molecular platform through potential-dependent molecular reactivity. Reduction activates the pyridine-imine unit for CO2 binding, while Na+ coordination within the crown cavity regulates the interfacial environment and suppresses hydrogen evolution. Cr-PyN captures CO2 directly from simulated flue gas (9.3% CO2, 3% O2) with an electron utilization efficiency of 0.98 and a minimum electrical energy requirement of 39 kJ mol–1 CO2. At more cathodic potentials in an aqueous flow electrolyzer, the same molecular framework selectively produces acetate with 71% Faradaic efficiency at –0.4 V versus the reversible hydrogen electrode and remains stable over 120 h. Complementary in situ and ex situ spectroscopic studies, including operando FTIR and NMR, along with DFT calculations, support CO2 binding and subsequent reaction pathways toward multicarbon conversion.

articles.title: Bifunctional Bi-OOH Motifs for Oxygen-Promoted CO2 Photoreduction via Inhibition of Oxygen Reduction
articles.abstract: Photocatalytic CO2 reduction reaction from practical gas sources is often severely compromised by the competitive O2 reduction reaction. Herein, we report an approach to switch O2 from a competitor into a promoter by arresting the oxygen reduction reaction pathway at the *OOH intermediate stage on BiOBr photocatalysts. The introduction of oxygen vacancies (VO) facilitates O2 reduction to *OOH, which is robustly anchored by VO-induced Lewis acidic Bi sites to form stable Bi-OOH motifs. The Bi-OOH motifs arrest further oxygen reduction pathways and preferentially adsorb CO2 to stabilize *COOH intermediates. A clear linear correlation between the VO concentration and the activity further verifies the vital role of these sites. The BiOBr-VO-0.7 photocatalyst with an optimized VO concentration achieves a 3.4-fold enhancement under 20% O2 (69.2 μmol g–1 h–1) and a 2.9-fold enhancement under simulated flue gas compared to anaerobic conditions for CO2 reduction to CO. Isotope-labeling experiments with 13C confirmed that the CO originated from CO2 reduction. Its practical viability is further demonstrated under natural sunlight and ambient air with a CO generation rate of 5.6 μmol g–1 h–1. This work provides a paradigm shift in the design of catalysts that can use real CO2 sources.

articles.title: Boosting Ethanol Production via Strategic CO Co-Feeding in CO2 Hydrogenation over Rh-Based Catalysts
articles.abstract: The catalytic hydrogenation of carbon dioxide (CO2) to ethanol is a highly promising reaction for carbon utilization and the production of renewable fuels and chemicals. Achieving high ethanol selectivity remains the biggest challenge in the field. Ethanol formation on rhodium (Rh)-based catalysts from CO2 hydrogenation relies on the carbon monoxide (CO) insertion pathway that is kinetically limited compared to the competing hydrogenation of methyl intermediates to methane. In this study, we demonstrate that adding CO to the CO2 hydrogenation reaction stream over colloidally synthesized Rh/Fe/Li–TiO2 catalysts can effectively overcome this limitation. This direct co-feeding strategy promotes C–C coupling and suppresses methanation, increasing ethanol selectivity 5-fold to 24% and boosting the space-time yield 6-fold with only a 15% CO cofeed (CO/(CO + CO2)). Under optimized, hydrogen-deficient conditions (H2/(CO + CO2)), the ethanol selectivity further increases to 32%. Our findings present an efficient, simplified pathway for upgrading CO2-rich streams into higher-value chemicals.

articles.title: Divergent Kinetics and Rate-Determining Steps for 1-Butene and 2-Butene Hydroformylation with a Bidentate Phosphoramidite Ligand: A Combined Experimental and Density Functional Theory Study
articles.abstract: The hydroformylation of mixed butenes (1-butene and 2-butene) to n-valeraldehyde is an important industrial process, yet the distinct kinetic behaviors of the two isomers under identical catalytic conditions remain insufficiently understood. Herein, a comprehensive kinetic and mechanistic investigation of 1-butene and 2-butene was conducted using a robust, water- and air-stable, highly regioselective bidentate phosphoramidite ligand-modified rhodium catalyst in a homogeneous system. Systematic kinetic experiments revealed that the hydroformylation of 2-butene exhibits a strong positive dependence on H2 pressure and obvious substrate inhibition at high concentrations, whereas 1-butene shows little H2 dependence and no substrate inhibition. Using a semi-empirical hyperbolic kinetic modeling, the rate equations capture these distinct behaviors with high accuracy (R2 = 0.9746 for 2-butene, 0.9642 for 1-butene). Kinetic studies revealed distinct rate behaviors for 1-butene and 2-butene hydroformylation. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations on the n-valeraldehyde pathway further showed that hydride insertion to the internal C═C double bond has the highest barrier for 2-butene, while CO insertion to the linear rhodium n-butyl intermediate has the highest barrier for 1-butene, providing the mechanistic origin for the observed kinetic differences. The iso-valeraldehyde pathway is additionally disfavored by a 2.7 kcal·mol–1 higher RDS barrier, consistent with the good n-selectivity. In situ high-pressure FTIR spectroscopy further confirmed the five-coordinate hydride HRh(CO)2(P)2 as the catalyst resting state. These findings offer quantitative guidance for optimizing industrial hydroformylation processes using mixed butene feedstocks.

articles.title: Enantioselective Alcohol Oxidation Reactions Catalyzed by Unspecific Peroxygenases
articles.abstract: The enantioselective oxidation of alcohols can be achieved via kinetic resolution of racemic alcohols or the desymmetrization of meso-diols. Biocatalytic alcohol oxidation approaches are known, using alcohol dehydrogenases and copper-and flavin-dependent oxidases, but the application of unspecific peroxygenases (UPOs) to enantioselective alcohol oxidation has received very little attention. As part of ongoing research into the catalytic promiscuity of UPOs, we present three distinct enantioselective biocatalytic alcohol oxidation approaches: the UPO-catalyzed oxidation of meso-diols via desymmetrization, the chemoselective oxidation of nonbenzylic sites in unsymmetrical diols, and the kinetic resolution of axially chiral biaryl alcohols. In each of the three reaction classes, the isolation of enantiomerically enriched oxidized products is demonstrated on a preparative scale.

articles.title: Engineering a Proton-Regulating Interfacial Microenvironment for Durable RuO2 Electrocatalysis in PEM Water Electrolysis
articles.abstract: Proton exchange membrane (PEM) water electrolysis is a technology for hydrogen production, but its deployment is limited by the cost and durability of acidic oxygen evolution reaction (OER) catalysts. RuO2 exhibits intrinsic OER activity yet degrades rapidly under high-current-density operation and start–stop cycles. Sluggish interfacial proton dissipation may contribute to this instability by promoting proton accumulation and local acidification. Here, we report an atomic-level microenvironment engineering strategy via aliovalent strontium incorporation into rutile RuO2. Modified RuO2 features a structurally distorted and electronically polarized interface that, according to calculations, alters interfacial water organization and may favor oxygen-end-oriented water configurations near the Sr-modified regions. This modified interfacial environment is associated with alleviated local acidification, facilitated proton-transfer-related processes, suppressed lattice oxygen participation, and favored surface-confined oxygen coupling. Operando characterization in a PEM membrane–electrode assembly further supports dynamic interfacial water reorganization and enhanced proton-transfer kinetics under device-relevant conditions. Modified RuO2 delivers 10 mA cm–2 at 197 mV in acidic electrolyte and, in a PEM electrolyzer, achieves 1 A cm–2 at 1.686 V, operates for over 400 h with Ru dissolution suppressed to 5.79 ng h–1, and withstands 3102 start–stop cycles. These findings support interfacial microenvironment regulation as a strategy for improving the durability of Ru-based acidic OER catalysts.

articles.title: Nano-CeO2-Derived BaCeO3– x N y H z : A High-Purity Oxynitride-Hydride Support for Enhanced Ammonia Synthesis
articles.abstract: Hetero-anion doping has emerged as an effective approach to modulate the physicochemical and catalytic properties of perovskite-type oxides. In this study, nanosized CeO2 synthesized by a continuous flow-type supercritical hydrothermal synthesis (SHS) process was employed as a precursor for a solid-state reaction with Ba(NH2)2, enabling the low-temperature synthesis of single-phase perovskite oxynitride–hydride BaCeO3–xNyHz (BaCeO3–xNyHz–SHS) with a high surface area and abundant N3– and H– species. Ru-loaded BaCeO3–xNyHz–SHS exhibited a maximum ammonia synthesis rate of 9.0 mmol g–1 h–1 at 300 °C and 0.9 MPa and showed up to a 6-fold enhancement in activity compared with the corresponding Ru/BaCeO3–xNyHz prepared from commercial CeO2, owing to the enhanced generation of anion vacancies at the Ru–support interface. Moreover, BaCeO3–xNyHz–SHS acted as a highly efficient support for various transition metals in ammonia synthesis and for Ni in ammonia decomposition, achieving >99% conversion at 560 °C with a low apparent activation energy (75 kJ mol–1). These findings demonstrate that enhancing the solid-state reactivity of oxide precursors through nanoscale engineering provides a general strategy for the low-temperature synthesis of highly active hetero-anion perovskite catalysts for ammonia synthesis and decomposition.

articles.title: Selective Formyl Deuteration of Aldehydes by Surface-Enriched Oxygen Vacancy Stabilized Pt on Ceria
articles.abstract: Hydrogen isotope exchange (HIE) is a widely used methodology for deuteration; however, achieving both high isotope abundance and site-selectivity remains challenging for heterogeneous catalysts. Herein, we present a ceria supported platinum catalyst with surface-enriched oxygen vacancy (Ov) that shows impressive formyl deuteration performance with deuterium oxide (D2O) as the deuterium source under hydrogen-free conditions. Using p-methylbenzaldehyde as a model substrate, the typical catalyst achieves >95% deuterium incorporation (D-inc.) at the formyl position while effectively suppressing undesired reductive deuteration pathway. Experimental and theoretical results suggest that the surface-enriched Ov promotes the preferential adsorption of formyl groups on undercoordinated Ce sites, where the local charge redistribution renders the formyl-protons electron-deficient. Simultaneously, the anchored Pt centers effectively catalyze D2O dissociation, generating abundant D* and OD* species. These deuterium species readily interact with the electron-deficient formyl groups, driving hydrogen isotope exchange and forming deuterated aldehydes with high D-formyl selectivity. Substrate scope exploration and gram-scale continuous-flow deuteration experiments demonstrate broad compatibility, revealing its great potential for the selective synthesis of deuterated aldehydes.

articles.title: Sequential Oxygen Vacancy Formation Governs Cu Size-Dependent Methanol Synthesis at Cu–ZrO2 Interfaces
articles.abstract: Methanol synthesis at Cu–ZrO2 interfaces requires CO2 activation, H2 dissociation, and conversion of oxygenated intermediates to proceed in concert, yet how Cu aggregation coordinates these functions remains unclear. Electronic-structure calculations, molecular dynamics, and catalytic experiments show that Cu size governs sequential oxygen vacancy formation and the adsorption landscape of HCOO*. Isolated Cu atoms favor formation of the initial vacancy and lower the HCOO* formation barrier to 17.41 kcal mol–1, consistent with high methanol selectivity and the highest apparent turnover frequency at 240 °C. When a second vacancy is introduced near isolated Cu in the calculation, HCOO* adsorption strengthens by 31.41 kcal mol–1 and creates a deep thermodynamic trap. Cu clusters instead change HCOO* adsorption by only 4.66 kcal mol–1 as the second vacancy forms and couple bidentate CO2 activation at the vacancy with H2 dissociation on adjacent Cu atoms. This balanced interface gives the highest CO2 conversion and methanol space–time yield of 562.90 mgMeOH gcat–1 h–1 at 280 °C and remains stable for 100 h. Cu nanoparticles, despite their higher Cu loading, interact weakly with CO2 and have the highest HCOO* formation barrier of 27.28 kcal mol–1, giving the lowest productivity. Controlled-reduction EPR reveals Cu-size-dependent changes in defect-related signals, while transient DRIFTS shows distinct reduction- and treatment-dependent changes in the observable HCOO-related surface pools. Their correspondence with the calculated vacancy energetics and adsorption responses supports a Cu-size-dependent balance among defect formation, reactant activation, and intermediate conversion. Cu clusters couple reactant activation with intermediate conversion to sustain methanol production.

articles.title: d -Electron Descriptors for Nitrate Reduction Reaction Activity in Co-Based Heusler Phase Electrocatalysts
articles.abstract: The tunability of electronic structure in intermetallics opens the door to systematic studies in catalysis. Here, we experimentally investigate various descriptors for the electrocatalytic nitrate reduction reaction using 9 Heusler phases as catalysts (Co2VSn, Co2MnAl, Co2MnGe, Co2MnSn, Co2FeGe, Co2MnSb, Ni2MnSn, Co2FeSi, and Co2FeAl). In contrast to previous studies with Co-based Heusler phases and oxide perovskites for OER, we find that generally, the total valence electron count, rather than eg filling, provides a better prediction of the activity. However, with period 5 Y elements, such as Sn and Sb, at high valence electron counts, Y-site d-band centers must also be considered. Reaction mechanism analysis by DFT also clarifies the role of X/Y sites. Hence, a single descriptor alone is not sufficient to rationalize catalytic activity across the full spectrum of Heusler phase compositions. So far, valence electron control has relied on single metal or binary alloy compositions for nitrate reduction; however, these Heusler phases help decouple the element identity and valence count while also serving as a guide for more catalysts based on ternary intermetallics. This work thus establishes multi-descriptor guidance for a wide group of catalyst compositions that were previously relatively unexplored.

articles.title: Facet-Dependent Plating/Stripping Behavior and Crystallographic Evolution during Cycling on Zn Metal Anodes
articles.abstract: Aqueous zinc metal batteries offer a safe and low-cost option for scalable energy storage; however, their practical reversibility is limited by nonuniform Zn plating/stripping and dendritic growth. Here, Zn single-crystal electrodes exposing well-defined (002), (100), and (101) crystalline facets were used to isolate the role of crystallography in Zn metal cycling. Zn deposition is strongly facet-dependent, forming hexagonal, rectangular/prismatic, and corner-defined morphologies on (002), (100), and (101) facets, respectively. Time-dependent SEM further reveals that Zn growth proceeds via discrete edge- or corner-initiated crystallographic units rather than uniform terrace coverage. During stripping, Zn metal is removed via facet-preserved mesoscopic dissolution domains, leaving geometry-defined pits rather than random corrosion-like features. However, these pits are not preferentially refilled during subsequent plating. Repeated cycling redirects Zn growth to protrusions and roughened regions, causing mossy/dendritic accumulation, mixed-texture evolution, and loss of epitaxial reversibility. These findings highlight the need to control both oriented deposition and poststripping surface reconstruction.

articles.title: Overcoming the Trade-off Between the Activity, Stability, and Cost of OER Catalysts for Proton Exchange Membrane Water Electrolysis in a Self-Driving Laboratory
articles.abstract: Proton exchange membrane water electrolysis (PEMWE) offers a sustainable route to hydrogen production, yet its practical deployment is limited by trade-offs among activity, stability, and precursor cost of acidic oxygen evolution reaction (OER) catalysts. Here, we present a self-driving laboratory (SDL) integrating automated batch synthesis, electrochemical half-cell testing, and AI-guided decision-making to simultaneously optimize these properties. A composition-constrained design space, clustering-based batch selection, and relaxed-percentile Pareto filtering enable efficient exploration of ternary Ir–Ru–X (X = Ni, Co, Fe) systems. Using this framework, the platform conducted 24 experiments per ternary system and identified Ir10Ru65Ni25/C as a Pareto-balanced composition exhibiting an overpotential of 211.8 mV at 10 mA cm–2, limited degradation after accelerated durability testing, and reduced Ir content. In PEMWE, Ir10Ru65Ni25 delivered 3.90 A cm–2 at 1.8 V and stable operation for 1000 h at 1.0 A cm–2, demonstrating SDL-driven discovery of multimetallic OER catalysts.

articles.title: Self-Healing Armor Enables Electrode Integrity and Interfacial Stability for Durable Silicon Anodes
articles.abstract: Polymer coatings are widely used to stabilize silicon anodes, yet repeated volume changes can fracture the coating and accelerate continuous SEI reconstruction. Here, we construct a self-healing fluorinated acrylate/methacrylate copolymer coating in situ on silicon-based anodes through the UV-induced copolymerization of HFBA and MPS. The resulting copolymer combines strong adhesion with dynamic self-recovery through reversible dipole-dipole interactions, enabling microcrack repair within 1 min. Meanwhile, the HFBA-derived segments act as a fluorine reservoir, promoting the formation of a thin SEI with a polymer-rich outer layer and a LiF-rich inner layer. Consequently, SiOx-P(HFBA+MPS)||Li cells deliver 73.5% capacity retention after 500 cycles at 800 mA g–1. A practical 1.5 Ah NCM811||Si/C/Gr-P(HFBA+MPS) pouch cell achieves 71.9% capacity retention after 300 cycles and shows improved thermal safety. This work provides a scalable strategy for durable and safe silicon-based batteries by integrating autonomous self-healing of the polymer coating with sustained fluorine-assisted interphase stabilization.

articles.title: A Capacitively Coupled Dual-Gate 2D Transistor Unifying Logic-in-Memory and Tunable Synaptic Plasticity
articles.abstract: Integrating logic control with adaptive synaptic learning at the device level is a key step toward high-performance computing-in-memory (CIM) hardware. However, the integration of logic-in-memory (LIM) and synaptic plasticity within a homogeneous device is hindered by the incompatibility between stable logic output and dynamic weight modulation. Here, we demonstrate a logic-synapse function-integrated device based on a two-dimensional (2D) floating-gate field-effect transistor (FGFET) with a coplanar dual-control-gate architecture. With two independent gate-coupling coefficients, the nominally symmetric design allows the gate-induced potential increments to superpose on the floating gate: cooperative inputs induce charge tunneling and write a new memory state, whereas antagonistic inputs approximately cancel the pulse-induced potential increment and latch the stored state. This rule directly implements LIM within a single device, enabling 14 reconfigurable Boolean logic operations with in situ nonvolatile output storage, a logic read margin of 104, and no external cascading for the demonstrated two-input logic functions. The same coupling framework further supports tunable synaptic plasticity, including lateral enhancement/inhibition and spatiotemporal competition/cooperation among multiple synaptic inputs. In particular, asynchronous competitive modulation modifies history-dependent conductance updates, improving the depression nonlinearity to 0.0833 while retaining a dynamic range of 22.82. These results establish an all-electrical device-level route for integrating logic control and neural weight adaptation in compact CIM hardware.

articles.title: Boosting Electron/Mass Transport via Interfacial Coupling in a Dual-Supported Catalyst toward Ampere-Level Hydrogen Evolution
articles.abstract: Developing hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) electrocatalysts with high activity and long-term durability at industrial current densities remains challenging because catalytic kinetics, electron transport, and mass transport must be optimized simultaneously. Here, we report a one-pot method to anchor Pt-single-atom-modified NiCoP onto MXene with a high surface coverage of ∼97%. The Pt-NiCoP@MXene catalyst requires overpotentials of only 13.8 and 175 mV in 1 M KOH to deliver 10 and 1000 mA cm–2, respectively, and exhibits an ultralow decay rate of 7.1 μV h–1 over 1000 h at 1000 mA cm–2 in a three-electrode system. In an anion-exchange membrane electrolyzer, it achieves 1 A cm–2 at 1.74 V in a 4 cm2 cell with 98% voltage retention after 1000 h and maintains 97% retention over 500 h with a scaled 25 cm2 cell. Experiments and DFT calculations demonstrate the interface strong coupling via Ni/Co–O–Ti bonding bridges NiCoP and MXene effectively and accelerates the electron transport of catalytic layer, while the uniform dispersion of NiCoP on MXene improves surface wettability and facilitates bubble release and electrolyte replenishment. Additionally, Pt–P coordination increases the metallicity of Pt atoms and optimizes hydrogen adsorption/desorption. This work provides a facile strategy for synthesizing high-quality dual-supported catalysts and validates their industrial application potential.

articles.title: Electronic Structure Modulation in Isomeric Carborane-Thiolated Cu4 Nanoclusters Boosts CO2 Electroreduction to Methane
articles.abstract: Electrochemical CO2 reduction (eCO2R) to energy-dense hydrocarbons is central to sustainable carbon recycling, although achieving selective conversion at high current density and lower overpotential remains challenging. Here, we explore three molecularly precise nanomaterials, comprising nearly square planar Cu4 kernel protected by isomeric carborane-thiolate (CBT) cages, viz., Cu4-oCBT (ortho-carborane), Cu4-mCBT (meta-carborane), and Cu4-ICBT (iodinated-ortho-carborane), for eCO2R. Among them, Cu4-mCBT shows the most favorable performance, achieving ∼74% overall eCO2R selectivity and a CH4 Faradaic efficiency (FE) of ∼45% at high current densities of 500 mA cm–2 (−0.87 V vs RHE) while maintaining promising production of C2+ products. Furthermore, Cu4-mCBT and Cu4-ICBT catalysts deliver industrially relevant CH4 partial current densities (JCH4 ∼ 323 mA cm–2 at −0.99 V) at low overpotential, representing competitive performance compared to Cu nanoclusters (NCs) stabilized by conventional ligands. First-principles calculations reveal that Cu4-mCBT lowers the free energy barrier for *CHO to *CHOH hydrogenation, the rate-limiting step for methane formation, due to better orbital interactions with the intermediates. In situ attenuated total reflectance surface-enhanced infrared absorption spectroscopy (ATR-SEIRAS) confirms the transient intermediate species formed in the predicted eCO2R-to-CH4 pathway. Charge density difference, projected density of states, and in situ X-ray absorption studies demonstrate the primary catalytic role of the Cu-core, while three-dimensional cage-like ligand shells modulate the electronic structure of exposed metal atoms, thereby optimizing the intermediate binding. This study investigates the catalytic performance of carborane-appended tetranuclear copper clusters toward CO2 reduction pathways and elucidates their structure–activity relationships.

articles.title: Emergent Phenomena in Wurtzite Ferroelectric Semiconductors
articles.abstract: The emergence of ferroelectricity in wurtzite-structured semiconducting materials broadens the material landscape beyond traditional perovskites, introducing design rules for scalable nanoelectronic devices with an inherent thermal robustness. These materials combine large spontaneous polarization, ultrathin scalability, and compatibility with back-end-of-line processing. This review discusses the state-of-the-art and recent progress in understanding their ferroelectric behavior, from atomic-scale switching pathways and proximity-triggered, electrically controlled polarization states to charged yet intrinsically stable domain walls. Progress in compositional tuning, strain and interface engineering, heterostructure design, and advanced synthesis strategies is highlighted, including key material and device challenges for the integration of wurtzite ferroelectrics into next-generation memory, logic-in-memory, and neuromorphic computing systems.

articles.title: Flexible Zwitterionic Hydrogel Ultrasonic Patch Enables Spatiotemporally Controlled Delivery of Mangiferin-Loaded Micelles for Accelerating Diabetic Wound Healing
articles.abstract: Diabetic wounds are characterized by persistent inflammation, oxidative stress, impaired angiogenesis, and delayed tissue remodeling, often resulting in chronic nonhealing ulcers. Low-intensity pulsed ultrasound (LIPUS) offers a promising noninvasive therapeutic strategy; however, its clinical efficacy remains constrained by unstable acoustic coupling interfaces and the lack of integrated biological activity. Here, we report an ultrasound-responsive zwitterionic hydrogel patch by incorporating mangiferin-loaded micelles into a topologically entangled PCBOH hydrogel (MF@PCBOH). The mechanically robust hydrogel forms a stable and conformal acoustic interface that efficiently transmits ultrasound under dynamic conditions, whereas the incorporated micelles improve the aqueous dispersibility of mangiferin and enable ultrasound-enhanced release. Under LIPUS stimulation, released mangiferin reduces intracellular ROS, shifts macrophages toward a reparative phenotype, promotes endothelial angiogenesis, and enhances cell migration. As a result, MF@PCBOH accelerates diabetic wound healing in rats, accompanied by reduced inflammation, improved collagen remodeling, and enhanced vascular maturation. Similar therapeutic benefits are observed in a full-thickness porcine wound model, supporting the effectiveness of the hydrogel patch in a large-animal setting. This study demonstrates that integrating a durable acoustic interface with ultrasound-responsive drug delivery offers an effective strategy for diabetic wound repair.

articles.title: Generation of Bloch Points with Controlled Spin Texture Using Geometrical Boundary Conditions
articles.abstract: Bloch points are three-dimensional topological singularities in magnetization that play a key role in topological transformations of spin textures such as skyrmion creation or annihilation. While topology often enforces the existence of Bloch points in confined geometries such as cylindrical nanowires, deterministic control over their position and magnetic configuration remains challenging. Here, we demonstrate the generation of Bloch points with controlled spin texture by engineering geometrical boundary conditions in three-dimensional nanomagnets. By introducing a chirality interface between two three-dimensional double-helix nanowires of opposite handedness, forming a kinked, noncollinear structure, we impose competing topological constraints that uniquely define the magnetization configuration surrounding the Bloch point. A saturating magnetic field nucleates head-to-head or tail-to-tail domain configurations at the chirality interface, producing a Bloch-point domain wall with deterministic polarity, circulation, and helicity. This geometrical approach enables full three-dimensional control of Bloch point domain walls, allowing deterministic engineering of their spin texture and its selective coupling to current-induced Oersted fields.

articles.title: Nanoscale Spintronic Microwave Devices: From Fundamental Mechanisms to Emerging Applications
articles.abstract: With the rapid deployment of next-generation communication technologies, the demand for highly sensitive and miniaturized microwave detectors has become extremely urgent. Conventional semiconductor diodes suffer from intrinsic drawbacks when detecting submicrowatt signals. Spintronics provides an optimal alternative via the spin rectification effect, which enables widely tunable, low-power microwave rectification at room temperature. This Review examines recent advances in spintronic microwave rectifiers and their future prospects. We discuss diverse physical platforms, including devices with uniform magnetization and special nonuniform topological spin textures. Furthermore, we highlight multiorder-of-magnitude performance improvements in such devices, focusing on strategies to boost sensitivity, reduce noise equivalent power (NEP), and extend broadband as well as multiband detection capacity. Apart from core performance metrics, we discuss emerging applications: ambient radio frequency (RF) energy harvesting, high-resolution vector microwave-field imaging, monolithically integrated spintronic microwave systems, and microwave neural networks that can directly process high-frequency signals for neuromorphic computing. By sorting out the complete technical development route of this field, this Review aims to provide a systematic theoretical framework and technical references to promote the development of spintronic devices for next-generation wireless communication and edge artificial intelligence.

articles.title: Robust and Wide-Range Friction Regulation via Interfacial Bridging-Promoted Hydration Switching in Phase-Separated Gels
articles.abstract: Interfacial friction strongly influences materials performance, but achieving controllable friction with both high robustness and wide-range tunability remains difficult. In conventional friction regulation systems based on phase separations, rigid and incompatible hydrophilic–hydrophobic interfaces often cause interfacial cracking and poor stability. Here, inspired by the toughening mechanism of cartilage, we introduce amphiphilic bridging segments between hydrophilic and hydrophobic phases to construct an interfacial bridging nanophase-separated gel (IBNSGel) for robust friction control. This design transforms the fragile phase interface into a tough bridging interphase, suppresses aggregation, promotes uniform nanophase separation, and enhances interfacial stability during hydration-induced phase separation. Owing to this bridging effect, IBNSGel exhibits synergistic surface-bulk friction switching upon hydration: the surface forms a stable hydration layer for excellent lubrication, while the bulk hardens with higher modulus and lower damping, reducing conformal contact dissipation. As a result, this gel achieves stable, reversible, and wide-range coefficient of friction (CoF) switching during hydration–dehydration, with switching ratios of 150 at the macroscale and 330 at the microscale. Based on its excellent multimedium stability and biocompatibility, this friction control material demonstrates great application potential in smart medical devices, soft robots, and interface intelligent transportation systems.

articles.title: Targeting the Immune-Neurovascular Interface to Ameliorate Pericyte Dysfunction with a Multifunctional Peptide–Drug Conjugate Nanoprodrug for Multiple Sclerosis Therapy
articles.abstract: Pericyte dysfunction triggers blood–brain barrier (BBB) disruption and subsequent aberrant immune infiltration in multiple sclerosis (MS), yet targeted interventions remain lacking. Here, we engineered a dual-functional fusion peptide (VLC) for pericyte targeting and therapeutic intervention and subsequently conjugated it with luteolin to construct a peptide–drug conjugate (PDC)-based ROS-responsive nanoprodrug (VLC@Lut-NPs). This system significantly suppressed MMP-9 overactivation and mitigated neuroinflammation. To optimize the pharmacokinetic profile of the PDC nanotherapeutic, we adopted subcutaneous administration, achieving a prolonged circulation half-life and enhancing brain drug accumulation (AUCbrain) by 2.65-fold compared with intravenous injection. In two MS models, VLC@Lut-NPs restored pericyte homeostasis, reinforced BBB integrity, attenuated aberrant peripheral immune infiltration, and ultimately promoted myelin repair and regeneration. Notably, a once-every-other-day subcutaneous regimen outperformed daily intravenous administration. By bridging peripheral immunity and the neurovascular unit, this work identifies pericytes as a central regulatory node and establishes a pericyte-targeted PDC nanoplatform for durable MS treatment, highlighting its translational potential as a complementary strategy to conventional immunomodulatory approaches.

articles.title: The Future of Nanoscience: Reaching Early-Career Scientists
Turn Shield into Sword: Pathological Hydroxyapatite-Targeting Micelles Drive Metabolic Stress-Induced Autophagy Dysfunction for Bone Metastasis Therapy
articles.abstract: Bone metastasis remains a major clinical challenge in advanced breast cancer because therapeutic efficacy is limited by poor lesion targeting and systemic toxicity. Moreover, the hypoxic bone microenvironment induces protective autophagy in tumor cells, which maintains metabolic homeostasis and limits therapeutic efficacy. Herein, we develop a bone metastasis-targeted micellar system (AD/R) to overcome this protective autophagy “shield”. Based on the low crystallinity of pathological hydroxyapatite (HAP) and the hypoxic bone microenvironment, a pathological HAP-targeting polymer (DSPE-PEG-ALN, DPA) and a hypoxia-responsive polymer (DSPE-AZO-PEG, DAP) are coassembled into micelles encapsulating the oxidative phosphorylation inhibitor resveratrol (RES). Following selective accumulation in bone-metastatic lesions, AD/R undergoes hypoxia-triggered disassembly. The released DPA induces calcium-mediated membrane mineralization to restrict oxygen and nutrient supply, whereas RES suppresses oxidative phosphorylation and ATP production. This “external blockade” and “internal disruption” synergistically aggravate metabolic stress, activate AMPK-dependent autophagy, and impair lysosomal degradation through lysosomal membrane permeabilization, ultimately inducing autophagy dysfunction and autophagy-associated tumor cell death. In murine breast cancer bone metastasis models, AD/R effectively suppresses bone and secondary lung metastases and restores bone homeostasis. This work establishes a “turn shield into sword” paradigm by converting protective autophagy into metabolic stress-induced autophagy dysfunction for the treatment of bone metastasis.

articles.title: Unconventionally Dynamical Regime of Colloidal Nanocrystals on Spherical Surfaces
articles.abstract: Crystallography of colloidal nanocrystals on spherical surfaces underpins the structural organization of a wide range of functional soft and biological materials, from viral capsids and protein nanocages to colloidal microcapsules and curvature-engineered metamaterials. In these systems, the topology dictates that crystalline order on a sphere must incorporate topological defects that can self-organize into scars whose conformations undergo fluctuations. However, how these conformations collectively affect phase transitions on spheres remains unknown. Here, we investigate the phase transitions of colloidal nanocrystal packing on the spherical surface and identify an unconventional regime in the solid phase, which exhibits rapid dynamics with enhanced fluctuations of scars. Further analysis reveals that this regime is governed by the conformational entropy of the scars. Such an entropic effect on dynamics exhibits a nonmonotonic dependence on system size and causes disparate scaling laws at intermediate and large system sizes, which are absent in previous experiments and theoretical models. The findings provide insights into the effect of topological defects on curved manifolds and reveal the critical role of the conformational entropy of defect scars in geometrically frustrated systems of colloidal nanocrystals.

articles.title: Strength and thermal conductivity enhancement by solute substitution during laser powder bed fusion of NiWCo/Cu dissimilar alloy joint
Molecularly Aligned Insoluble Nanoaggregates for Ah‐Level Aqueous Zinc‐Ion Batteries
articles.abstract: Achieving stable Ah‐level aqueous zinc‐ion batteries (AZIBs) remains a critical challenge due to severe water decomposition and dendrite growth. Conventional aqueous electrolytes adopt soluble ligands to stabilize the interfaces, yet these species are insufficient to isolate interfacial water contact owing to their intrinsic hydrophilicity. Herein, we design a molecularly aligned electrolyte (MAE) that incorporates insoluble ligands in aqueous solutions to stabilize both electrodes. By utilizing the π−π stacking between benzylideneacetone (BA) and 2‐naphthol polyoxyethylene (NPE), insoluble BA molecules form nanoaggregates with NPE and are stably dispersed within the aqueous electrolyte. At both interfaces, the BA−NPE nanoaggregates form hydrophobic interfacial layers that prevent water attack, thereby effectively suppressing side reactions. In addition, BA−NPE nanoaggregates substantially increase the nucleation overpotential and form a fluorine‐rich solid electrolyte interphase (SEI), promoting dendrite‐free Zn plating/stripping. Consequently, the Zn//Zn cell exhibits stable cycling for over 4500 h at 1 mA cm−2 and 1 mAh cm−2. More impressively, the Zn//NH4V4O10 pouch cell delivers capacities exceeding 1.3 Ah for over 900 cycles with a retention rate of 81.8%, validating the significance of the insoluble ligand strategy under practical conditions.

articles.title: Rational Solvent Fluorination Design for Solvation Regulation Enabling Stable Interfaces in High‐Voltage Li‐Ion Batteries
articles.abstract: Fluorinating electrolyte solvents is an effective strategy to enhance the interfacial stability of lithium‐ion batteries (LIBs) under high‐voltage conditions, where severe interfacial side reactions typically undermine the long‐term performance. However, the influence of both the number and positional arrangement of fluorinated groups on solvation structure remains poorly understood. In this work, we systematically investigate how trifluoromethyl group number and substitution position in diethyl carbonate (DEC) derivatives affect Li+ solvation behavior. It is revealed that the introduction of a DEC‐based solvent with symmetric two trifluoromethyl groups tends to regulate the solvation structure enriched with anions and fluoroethylene carbonate (FEC). This optimized solvation structure facilitates the formation of a robust cathode‐electrolyte interphase derived from both anions and FEC. Consequently, Ni‐rich LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2 cathodes with a high loading mass of 10.5 mg cm−2 achieve stable cycling at 4.6 V, retaining 80% of their capacity after 300 cycles. These findings provide fresh insights into the rational design of fluorinated solvents for high‐voltage LIBs.

articles.title: 2D Ferroelectrics: Toward Non‐Volatile Memory and Neuromorphic Computing
articles.abstract: With the rapid development of Artificial Intelligence and Internet of Things technologies, the demand for massive data storage and complex intelligent computing has surged dramatically. Two‐dimensional (2D) ferroelectrics, with the unique spontaneous polarization, atomic‐scale thickness, low power consumption, and flexible stacking, are driving the development of non‐volatile storage and neuromorphic computing toward ultra‐highenergy efficiency and high‐density integration. Here, we review the recent progress in 2D ferroelectrics and their applications. First, we analyze in‐depth the ferroelectric origins and progress of displacement‐type, sliding‐type, and defect‐type 2D ferroelectrics. Subsequently, the types, operating mechanisms, and non‐volatile memory performances of ferroelectric memory are summarized. Furthermore, we highlight the applications of 2D ferroelectric devices in neuromorphic computing, systematically summarizing research progress in synaptic plasticity simulation, biological neural behavior demonstration, and image recognition. Finally, the opportunities and challenges of 2D ferroelectrics and devices are discussed. This review provides guidance to researchers of 2D ferroelectrics who aim to push the frontier forward.

articles.title: A Flexible Light‐Activated Pyro‐Phototronic Cascade Platform for Antibacterial Immunomodulation and Infected Wound Healing
articles.abstract: Efficient infected wound healing requires both rapid bacterial eradication and precisely regulated immune activation; however, achieving these two objectives within a single therapeutic platform remains challenging. Herein, we report a light‐activated multifunctional P(VDF‐TrFE)/C@MnOx@CdS composite film (P(VDF‐TrFE)/CMS) that integrates photothermal conversion, pyrocatalysis, photocatalysis, and Mn2+‐mediated immunomodulation into a pyro‐phototronic cascade therapeutic system. Under cyclic light irradiation, the photothermal effect of C@MnOx induces transient pyroelectric polarization in P(VDF‐TrFE), generating an internal pyroelectric field that not only triggers pyrocatalytic reactive oxygen species (ROS) production but also promotes photogenerated charge separation in CdS through the pyro‐phototronic effect. More importantly, the enhanced carrier separation accelerates the Mn redox cycle, thereby regulating Mn2+ release to synergistically activate M1‐like macrophages while sustaining efficient ROS generation for bacterial eradication. Consequently, the P(VDF‐TrFE)/CMS film achieves highly efficient antibacterial activity and accelerates wound closure by approximately 54.5% compared with the PBS control group. This work establishes a pyro‐phototronic cascade strategy that couples catalytic antibacterial therapy with programmable immune regulation, offering a promising approach for the treatment of infected wounds.

articles.title: A Mimosa‐Inspired Multifunctional Ionogel with Tunable Microphase Separation for High Strength, Shape Memory, and Sensing
articles.abstract: The development of multifunctional ionogels for flexible ionotronics is often hampered by the trade‐off between mechanical robustness and the integration of stimuli‐responsive functionalities. Drawing functional inspiration from the stimulus‐deformation‐signal transduction cascade of Mimosa pudica, we report a liquid crystal‐based click ionogel with a tunable microphase separation that simultaneously achieves high strength, shape memory, and ionic conductivity. This architecture, comprising rigid poly(liquid crystal) domains as the incompatible phase and a soft poly(ionic liquid) network as the compatible matrix, not only reinforces the ionogel (tensile strength >3 MPa, elongation >300%) but also endows it with both shape‐memory and sensing capabilities. The resulting ionogel enables high‐precision flexible sensing across a wide range of deformations, from large‐scale motions to subtle physiological signals. Furthermore, we demonstrate a biomimetic, temperature‐controlled switch that leverages the ionogel's thermally triggered deformation to actuate an alarm circuit, showcasing its potential in intelligent ionotronic devices. This phase‐engineering strategy provides a pathway to circumvent performance trade‐offs in the design of next‐generation soft materials.

articles.title: All 3D Printed Load‐bearing Zn‐ion Hybrid Supercapacitors
articles.abstract: The rapid development of smart equipment and emerging energy technologies demands structural components that are lightweight, mechanically robust, energy-dense, and geometrically versatile. Yet load-bearing electrochemical energy-storage devices remain constrained by the challenge of simultaneously improving electrode activity and ion/electron transport while maintaining mechanical robustness. Here, we report a low-cost 3D printing strategy for the integrated fabrication of load-bearing Zn-ion hybrid supercapacitors using functional core–shell continuous carbon fiber prepreg filaments, where “fully 3D-printed” refers to the one-step additive manufacturing of the structural framework (electrodes and electrolyte matrix) followed by necessary post-printing treatments (supercritical foaming and gelation) to activate electrochemical performance. On the electrode side, supercritical fluid-assisted laser-induced graphitization converts continuous carbon fiber bundles into hierarchical porous graphene cathodes, delivering a 2.4-fold increase in areal capacitance over conventional LIG electrodes. On the electrolyte side, a biphasic PP/PVA semi-solid electrolyte is engineered by supercritical foaming to construct interconnected open ion-transport channels, increasing the ionic conductivity from 0.5 to 4.2 mS cm− 1. Together, these designs enable fully 3D-printed continuous fiber devices with integrated mechanical load-bearing and electrochemical energy-storage functions. This work establishes a versatile, cost-effective, and scalable route toward multifunctional structural power sources for next-generation integrated devices.

articles.title: All 3D Printed Load‐bearing Zn‐ion Hybrid Supercapacitors (Adv. Funct. Mater. 82/2026)
articles.abstract: 3D‐Printed Structural Energy Storage In their Research Article (DOI: 10.1002/adfm.76654), Weijun Zhu and co‐workers report a customizable, load‐bearing zinc‐ion hybrid supercapacitor. By integrating continuous‐fiber 3D printing, supercritical‐fluid‐assisted laser graphenization, and supercritical foaming, this strategy strikes an effective balance between mechanical load‐bearing capability and electrochemical performance, thereby advancing the integration of structural support and energy storage for potential applications in flying cars, mobile robots, and other electrically powered mobile devices.

articles.title: Architecting Zincophilic‐Hydrophobic Domains Within Co‐Crosslinked Hydrogels for All‐Climate Aqueous Zinc‐Ion Batteries
articles.abstract: Aqueous zinc‐ion batteries with hydrogel electrolytes have attracted considerable attention for wearable energy‐storage devices owing to their intrinsic safety and mechanical flexibility. However, conventional hydrogel electrolytes often exhibit limited rate capability and environmental adaptability, which are closely related to the decoupled regulation of ion transport and interfacial chemistry. To overcome these limitations, a spatially cooperative electrolyte‐engineering approach was developed through constructing a co‐crosslinked network (p(AM‐co‐VIB)) through the copolymerization of acrylamide (AM) and 1‐vinyl‐3‐butylimidazolium bromide (VIB), while introducing 3‐(N,N‐dimethylmyristylammonio) propane sulfonate (ST) to construct a hydrogel electrolyte (PV‐S). The p(AM‐co‐VIB) network provides efficient ion‐transport pathways and structural robustness, while the ST‐derived zincophilic‐hydrophobic domains regulate the local Zn2+ coordination environment, promoting homogeneous Zn2+ distribution and confining interfacial water. Consequently, the PV‐S electrolyte delivers an average coulombic efficiency of 99.57%. Furthermore, the Zn||Zn symmetric cells sustain highly reversible Zn plating/stripping across a broad current‐density range of 1–40 mA cm−2. Notably, stable operation can be maintained over a wide temperature window (−40°C to 80°C), with prolonged cycling exceeding 2800 h at −20°C. Additionally, the Zn||NVO full cell retains 82.4% capacity retention over 850 cycles. Remarkably, the Zn||NVO pouch cell with a limited N/P ratio (3.9) retains 92.1% capacity after 220 cycles.

articles.title: Artificial Intelligence for Functional Battery Materials: From Multimodal Mechanism Mining to Closed‐Loop Autonomous Optimization
articles.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping battery‐materials research, but its value extends beyond prediction accuracy on static datasets. Functional battery materials involve strongly coupled chemical, structural, electrochemical, interfacial, and processing variables, requiring contextualized data, mechanistic credibility, uncertainty assessment, and experimental validation. This review presents a unified framework connecting multimodal data infrastructure, task‐matched AI models, mechanism mining, and closed‐loop optimization. We examine battery data sources, representations, FAIR principles, ontologies, reusable platforms, and benchmark limitations, highlighting metadata completeness, domain shift, dataset bias, negative results, and computational‐label uncertainty. We compare major model families according to the battery questions they address, their risks, and validation requirements, and discuss applications to cathodes, anodes, electrolytes, solid‐state interfaces, and beyond‐Li systems. Particular emphasis is placed on whether AI‐derived descriptors and latent features can be linked to experimentally testable mechanisms. We further assess active learning, Bayesian optimization, robotic experimentation, real‐time control, smart batteries, and digital twins through evidence‐hierarchy and closed‐loop‐maturity perspectives. We argue that battery AI should progress from isolated prediction toward multimodal, mechanism‐aware, uncertainty‐quantified, and experimentally validated closed‐loop discovery.

articles.title: Atomic‐Scale Regulation of Spin Polarization in High‐Entropy Frameworks for Efficient Low‐Frequency Electromagnetic Wave Attenuation
articles.abstract: High-performance electromagnetic wave (EMW) absorption in the low-frequency S and C bands (2–8 GHz) remains challenging due to fundamental constraints like the Snoek limit and difficulty in achieving proper impedance matching, which conventional ferromagnetic materials cannot overcome through extrinsic morphology engineering alone. Here, an electronic-structure-driven strategy is reported to design a series of (Fe, Co, Ni, Cu, and Cr)Se2 high-entropy selenides (HESe) that translate atomic-scale orbital regulation into enhanced macroscopic EMW absorption. By integrating magnetic elements (Fe, Co, and Ni) with trivalent chromium, the distinctive t2g 3eg 0 electron configuration of the Cr (III) ion generates high spin polarization and strengthened spin-orbit coupling, which increases the magnetocrystalline anisotropy constant (K) and shifts magnetic resonance toward the low-frequency region without compromising saturation magnetization. Moreover, controlled introduction of Se vacancies further modulates the dielectric environment by inducing lattice distortion and interfacial polarization, thereby optimizing impedance matching. As a result, the vacancy-engineered pentanary material (HESe-Vr) exhibits a minimum reflection loss of −50.13 dB at 2.92 GHz with an effective bandwidth spanning the S and C bands. This work demonstrates that d-orbital electron configuration engineering in high-entropy compounds provides a viable route for tailoring intrinsic electromagnetic responses, offering a new paradigm for the rational design of next-generation EMW absorbing materials.

articles.title: Beyond Planar Graphene: Roughness‐Conforming Microlaminates Enable Superior Heat Removal
articles.abstract: The escalating cooling demands of high‐heat‐flux electronic systems require materials that deliver efficient heat spreading, phase‐change enhancement, and scalable manufacturability—capabilities rarely found simultaneously on a single platform. Here, we introduce a microlaminate strategy that translates graphene's intrinsically two‐dimensional phonon transport into three‐dimensional heat removal from localized hot spots, without relying on volumetric composites or geometry‐dominated architectures. As a representative implementation, we demonstrate graphene‐based microlaminates integrated with laser‐microstructured copper, where the metal serves as a technologically relevant model substrate rather than a fundamental constraint. The interface‐engineered microlaminates preserve graphene's ultrahigh in‐plane thermal conductance, while enabling efficient coupling to macroscopic heat‐rejection pathways. Experiments and supporting analyses reveal exceptional performance across multiple thermal‐management regimes: (a) ∼20% reduction in hotspot temperature under single‐phase liquid cooling at heat fluxes approaching ∼150 W cm−2, (b) ∼15% enhancement in heat‐transfer coefficient during dropwise condensation, and (c) record in‐plane effective thermal conductivity of ∼1.5 × 104 W m−1 K−1 in vapor‐chamber heat spreaders – among the highest reported for thermal‐management devices to date. While copper is employed here as a model system, the microlaminate framework is material‐agnostic and readily extendable to other thermally conductive substrates, establishing a general pathway for integrating planar nanomaterials into three‐dimensional thermal platforms.

articles.title: Biodegradable Polyester Separator With Ion‐Dipole Interaction for Modulating Interfacial Li‐Ion Flux in Lithium Metal Batteries
articles.abstract: Lithium metal batteries (LMBs) are regarded as promising next‐generation energy storage systems owing to their ultrahigh theoretical energy density. However, conventional polyolefin separators suffer from poor electrolyte wettability and limited capability to regulate ion transport, leading to uncontrolled dendritic growth and unstable solid electrolyte interphases (SEIs) that severely compromise battery safety and cycling stability. Herein, a biodegradable polybutylene succinate@polylactic acid (PBS@PLA) composite separator is developed to synergistically regulate Li‐ion transport and enhance interfacial stability. The PBS domains facilitate efficient electrolyte uptake and enhance ionic conductivity, while the highly polar PLA domains modulate Li‐ion distribution through ion–dipole interactions. This cooperative ion‐regulation architecture accelerates charge‐transfer kinetics and promotes the formation of a dense LiF‐rich SEI. Leveraging these advantages, the PBS@PLA separator enables an ionic conductivity of 2.1 mS cm−1 in the regular 1 M carbonate electrolyte and sustains stable Li plating/stripping at a high current density of 10 mA cm−2. The Li||LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2 full cells also retain 80.2% of their initial capacity after 300 cycles at 5C. Moreover, the intrinsic biodegradability of the PBS@PLA separator enables controllable end‐of‐life degradation, facilitating material recycling. This work establishes a viable separator‐engineering strategy that integrates high performance with eco‐friendly recyclability for LMB technologies.

articles.title: Biomaterials Meet Organic Electrochemical Transistors: Materials, Interfaces, and Biosensing Frontiers
articles.abstract: Organic electrochemical transistors (OECTs) are emerging as powerful biosensing platforms, offering high transduction efficiency, low‐voltage operation, and intrinsic compatibility with aqueous and physiological environments. Central to their recent progress is the strategic integration of biomaterials, which govern interfacial charge transfer, doping dynamics, and recognition specificity. A complete understanding of biomaterial‐enabled OECTs requires not only insights into intrinsic material chemistry but also interface engineering and device design principles that dictate signal transduction and reproducibility. In this review, we critically examine the full spectrum of biomaterials integrated into OECT biosensors (from natural macromolecules, such as proteins, nucleic acids, and polysaccharides to biocompatible polymers and synthetic engineered interfaces). Particular emphasis is placed on interfacial chemistries, including silanization and click reactions, that control receptor orientation, density, and long‐term stability. Beyond materials design, we discuss operating physics, signal transduction mechanisms, and device engineering strategies, thereby linking molecular‐scale chemistry with device‐level performance. By consolidating these interdisciplinary advances, we provide a timely roadmap for reproducible, scalable, and clinically relevant OECT biosensors. With growing demand for high‐performance and sustainable sensing platforms in precision medicine and environmental monitoring, this review highlights both key achievements and outstanding challenges that will shape the next generation of bioelectronic technologies.

articles.title: Biomaterials Meet Organic Electrochemical Transistors: Materials, Interfaces, and Biosensing Frontiers (Adv. Funct. Mater. 82/2026)
articles.abstract: Organic Electrochemical Transistors Biomaterials and organic electrochemical transistors (OECTs) converge at the interface between biology and electronics. The cover illustrates this interaction as a living bioelectronic landscape, where biomolecular recognition and ionic‐electronic coupling generate amplified electrical signals, highlighting the potential of biomaterial‐integrated OECTs for advanced biosensing and next‐generation bioelectronic technologies. More details can be found in the Review Article by Ali Nawaz, Leandro Merces, and Prashant Sonar (DOI: 10.1002/adfm.77800).

articles.title: Biomimetic Janus Eutectogels With Dynamic Compliance for High‐Fidelity Bioelectronic Interfaces
articles.abstract: The recording of high‐fidelity electrophysiological signals is the cornerstone of bioelectronics development. However, overcoming signal interference caused by motion artifacts and unintended adhesion during daily activities remains a challenge.
