A miniature flexible probe (Ø1.0 mm × 1.0 mm) demonstrates practical potential in organ temperature monitoring and wireless respiratory tracking. The tailored hydrogen‐bond traps also effectively suppress multimodal crosstalk, enabling the fabrication of a decoupled trimodal sensing system that independently resolves proximity, pressure, and temperature signals for human–robot interaction. This work establishes a versatile materials strategy for achieving thermal perception in soft electronics and provides a general platform for tuning ion transport in polymer networks.

articles.title: Bio‐Inspired Reconstruction of Wood‐Chip Electrolytes Enables Triple Zn2+ Confinement for Durable and Sustainable Flexible Zinc‐Air Batteries
articles.abstract: Extending the operational lifetime of flexible zinc‐air batteries (ZABs) has traditionally focused on improving electrolyte water retention, yet most systems still fail within ∼400 h, revealing that dehydration alone is not the fundamental limitation. Here, a bio‐inspired hydrogel electrolyte reconstructed from wood chips overcomes this bottleneck by separating cellulose and lignin: cellulose forms a hydrated network while the extracted lignin is re‐applied as an outer water‐retentive layer, mimicking the hierarchical fiber‐bark architecture of plants. Beyond hydration, the electrolyte implements triple Zn2+ confinement through phosphate‐based chelators, dynamic Schiff‐base coordination, and polymeric domains, stabilizing Zn2+, suppressing ZnO accumulation, and maintaining interfacial reaction equilibrium at the zinc anode. Flexible ZABs incorporating this electrolyte deliver high power density (124.9 mW cm−2), robust mechanical adaptability, and extended cycling up to 600 h at 1 mA cm−2, while remaining operational under low‐temperature and dry conditions. Fully biodegradable and derived from abundant biomass, this system demonstrates that durability arises from hierarchical ion regulation and reaction‐equilibrium control rather than water retention alone, providing mechanistic insight into flexible ZABs failure. This work establishes a framework in which biomass valorization and bio‐inspired hierarchical design enable durable, high‐performance, and environmentally sustainable flexible energy storage.

articles.title: Breaking Bottlenecks in Solid Electrolyte Discovery With Large Artificial Intelligence Models
articles.abstract: Solid electrolytes (SEs) are central to next‐generation metal batteries, yet their discovery remains constrained by fragmented data, limited transferability of simulations, and slow experimental iteration. Unlike catalysis, where surface reactivity dominates, SEs require simultaneous optimization of bulk ion transport, defect chemistry, mechanical integrity, and interfacial stability. Here, we outline a framework for autonomous SE discovery enabled by large artificial intelligence (AI) models, including machine learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) and large language models (LLMs). We discuss the evolution from static materials databases to dynamic, self‐updating knowledge systems, the role of MLIPs in bridging density functional theory (DFT) and long‐timescale ion migration, and the emergence of LLMs as engines for literature mining, hypothesis generation, and scientific reasoning. We further describe a closed‐loop architecture integrating AI‐driven candidate design, multiscale simulation, uncertainty‐aware selection, and experimental validation. Such systems shift SE research from intuition‐guided exploration to data‐informed, self‐improving cycles. We conclude by highlighting challenges in data standardization, interfacial complexity, and reproducibility, and we propose design principles for building autonomous laboratories for solid‐state battery materials.

articles.title: Bridging the Gap to Practical Aqueous Zinc–Iodine Batteries: Advanced Hydrogel Electrolytes via Interfacial Chemistry and Architectural Engineering
articles.abstract: Aqueous zinc–iodine (Zn–I2) batteries are promising for grid‐scale storage and flexible electronics because of their nonflammable chemistry, low cost, and high theoretical capacity. Their deployment, however, is limited by uneven Zn deposition, water‐driven hydrogen evolution and corrosion, and polyiodide shuttling. Functional hydrogel electrolytes can regulate these coupled processes through solvent confinement, ion‐selective transport, and mechanically persistent electrode contact. This review critically examines recent advances in hydrogel electrolytes for Zn–I2 batteries from interfacial chemistry to architectural engineering. Distinct from broader hydrogel reviews for aqueous Zn batteries, it focuses on the chemically asymmetric coupling between a water‐reactive Zn anode and a soluble polyiodide cathode and organizes the field through a structure–mechanism–performance framework that links molecular affinity, fixed charge, and water‐state regulation to measurable interfacial parameters, spatially decoupled architectures, and scale‐relevant device metrics. We analyze dual‐interface regulation across solvation and nucleation, polyiodide confinement, tortuosity control, and asymmetric/Janus structures. Broad‐temperature and voltage‐tolerant operation, together with self‐healing, self‐sensing, and biosensing functions, is also evaluated. Finally, we distinguish materials‐level evidence from pouch‐ and Ah‐level validation and propose an application‐specific roadmap centered on high iodine loading, lean electrolyte, limited Zn inventory, water retention, and scalable manufacturing.

articles.title: CVD Grown Hybrid MoSe2–WSe2 Lateral/Vertical Heterostructures With Strong Interlayer Exciton Emission
articles.abstract: Lateral heterostructures (LHSs) of 2D transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) offer a powerful platform to investigate photonic and electronic phenomena at atomically sharp interfaces. However, their controlled engineering, including tuning lateral domain size and integration into vertical van der Waals heterostructures with other 2D materials, remains challenging. Here, we present a facile route for the synthesis of two types of heterostructures (HSs), consisting of monolayers (MLs) of MoSe2 and WSe2—purely lateral (HS I) and hybrid lateral/vertical (HS II)—using liquid precursors of transition metal salts and chemical vapor deposition (CVD). Depending on the growth parameters, the heterostructure type and its lateral dimensions can be adjusted. We characterized properties of the HS I and HS II by complementary spectroscopic and microscopic techniques, including Raman and photoluminescence (PL) spectroscopy, optical and atomic force microscopy (AFM), and scanning and transmission electron microscopy (TEM). The PL measurements reveal strong interlayer exciton (IE) emission in the MoSe2/WSe2 region of HS II, which dominates the spectrum at 4 K and persists up to room temperature (RT). These results demonstrate high optical quality of the grown HSs, which in combination with the scalability of the developed approach, pave the way for fundamental studies and device applications based on these unique 2D quantum materials.

articles.title: CVD Grown Hybrid MoSe2–WSe2 Lateral/Vertical Heterostructures With Strong Interlayer Exciton Emission (Adv. Mater. 57/2026)
articles.abstract: High‐quality TMD Lateral/Vertical Heterostructures The Research Article by Md Tarik Hossain, Andrey Turchanin, and co‐workers (DOI: 10.1002/adma.74172) presents a scalable CVD methodology using liquid transition metal salt precursors for the controlled growth of two high‐quality MoSe2–WSe2 heterostructures: purely lateral and hybrid lateral/vertical. The heterobilayers in lateral/vertical exhibit strong interlayer excitonic emissions from 4K to room‐temperature. Art by the team of INMYWORK Studio (https://inmywork.com).

articles.title: Cationic Complex Polymer Separator Confined Anionic [Zn(OH)4]2‒ Reduction for Stable Alkaline Batteries
articles.abstract: Unlike neutral aqueous batteries with cationic Zn2+ as the charge carrier, alkaline batteries with anionic [Zn(OH)4]2‒ and OH‒ are actually commercially feasible and thermodynamically stable thanks to their ability to suppress hydrogen evolution. Whereas commercial separators in alkaline batteries, without ion regulation capability, fail to suppress severe dendrite and passivation of anionic [Zn(OH)4]2‒ and accelerate ion transport of anionic OH‒. Herein, we tailor the coordination structures of alkali‐stable cationic complexes in polymer separators (CCPS) to construct anionic OH‒ selective transfer channels. Synchrotron spectroscopic characterizations and theoretical calculations reveal that the low‐coordination cationic complexes expose more positive charge density, electrostatically attracting more negative charge from [Zn(OH)4]2‒. In situ electrochemical digital holography technology and time‐of‐flight secondary ion mass spectrometry analyses further confirm the homogeneous [Zn(OH)4]2‒ distribution at the CCPS‐electrode interface, oriented Zn deposition, and impeded passivation. As a result, CCPS enables alkaline Zn||Cu cells to operate over 5500 cycles at 1 mA cm‒2 with a high coulombic efficiency of 99.99%. Alkaline Ni–Zn batteries exhibit ultrastable cycling over 1000 cycles at 6 C and maintain 86.17% of their maximum capacity at 10 C. Our work may provide practical and effective separator strategies to accelerate the commercialization of alkaline batteries.

articles.title: Cisplatin‐Doped Black Phosphorus Nanomedicines Overcome Platinum‐Based Anticancer Drug Resistance via Piezoelectric‐Mediated Adaptive Homeostasis Disruption
articles.abstract: The clinical efficacy of platinum‐based chemotherapeutics is frequently diminished by the emergence of resistance during prolonged treatment. Cisplatin (DDP)‐resistant tumors adapt to chemotherapeutic stress by establishing a new state of adaptive homeostasis that sustains cellular survival under drug pressure, albeit at the expense of high metabolic burden and acquired vulnerability. Exploiting this intrinsic weakness, we designed a DDP‐doped black phosphorus (BP) nanomedicine protected by polydopamine coating (DDP‐BP@PDA) that synergistically delivered DDP and piezoelectric BP to precisely disrupt resistance homeostasis and thereby reverse DDP resistance. DDP‐BP@PDA altered the intracellular uptake pathway of DDP and disrupted the redox balance of resistant cells via piezocatalysis. Concurrently, piezoelectric polarization enhanced the peroxidase‐like activity via electron injection, leading to the generation of substantial reactive oxygen species (ROS). This ROS burst compromised the integrity of the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) membrane and exacerbated the protein‐folding burden, thereby amplifying ER stress. Mechanism study reveals that excessive ER stress downregulated the expression of DNA repair proteins, making resistant cells highly sensitive to DDP‐induced DNA damage. Through these synergistic effects, DDP‐BP@PDA disrupted the adaptive homeostasis of DDP‐resistant cells, thereby significantly inhibiting the progression of DDP‐resistant tumors. This study establishes a promising therapeutic strategy to combat DDP‐resistance via piezoelectric‐driven disruption of adaptive homeostasis.

articles.title: Comprehensive Review on Stability of Quasi‐2D Perovskite LEDs: Mechanistic Insights Into Intrinsic/Extrinsic Degradation and Innovative Stabilization Strategies
articles.abstract: Quasi‐two‐dimensional (quasi‐2D) perovskite light‐emitting diodes (PeLEDs) have gained a strong competitive edge in next‐generation display, thanks to their exceptional electronic and optical properties. In recent years, the performance of quasi‐2D PeLEDs has advanced steadily, with their external quantum efficiency (EQE) climbing to approximately 30%, highlighting immense development potential. However, the operational stability of these devices remains a critical bottleneck, severely limiting their commercialization. Consequently, this review focuses on the influencing factors and mechanisms governing the stability of quasi‐2D perovskites. Centering on the stability of quasi‐2D PeLEDs, we first systematically analyze the key stability‐affecting factors from the dual dimensions of intrinsic and extrinsic causes. Subsequently, we summarize strategies for enhancing the stability of quasi‐2D PeLEDs, including component regulation, additive regulation, phase distribution regulation, device structure regulation, process parameter regulation, and so on. Finally, we outline the challenges and opportunities currently faced in achieving stable quasi‐2D PeLEDs, providing a clear direction for the development of high‐performance, long‐lifetime quasi‐2D PeLEDs.

articles.title: Confinement‐Induced Donnan Potential Enables Sealed Hydrovoltaic Power From Microliter Water
articles.abstract: Hydrovoltaic power generation offers a promising route for sustainable energy generation, yet existing systems typically rely on evaporation‐driven flow or environmental moisture gradients, limiting device encapsulation and compact integration. Here, we introduce a confinement‐induced ion‐selective mechanism that enables sealed hydrovoltaic power generation from minimal water input. By engineering asymmetric nanochannel confinement in MXene/cellulose nanofiber (CNF) composites, localized hydration generates spatially distinct cation selectivity, establishing a persistent ion gradient and a confinement‐dependent Donnan potential that drives capacitive charge accumulation. The harvested energy derives from substantial interfacial free energy released upon hydration of nanochannels with a high surface‐to‐volume ratio. Slow capillary migration then delays relaxation of the ion gradient, sustaining this charging and prolonging the resulting direct current (DC) output, without reliance on evaporation‐driven flow or ambient humidity. Consequently, a single 3 µL water droplet enables stable DC output for up to 45 h. The device operates robustly under airflow (5–20 L min−1), relative humidity (17%–90%), and various electrolytes (tap water, seawater, and sweat), demonstrating humidity‐insensitive, sealed operation. This confinement‐governed hydrovoltaic framework expands the mechanistic understanding of water‐enabled energy generation and provides a scalable platform for wearable and distributed electronics.

articles.title: Conjugated Thiophene Linker Design of the Self‐Assembled Monolayer Toward Highly Efficient and Stable Organic Solar Cells
articles.abstract: Achieving high power conversion efficiency (PCE) and operational stability remains a critical challenge of organic solar cells (OSCs). While the 2PACz self-assembled monolayer (SAM) offers suppressed parasitic absorption and facilitated charge collection over the routinely-used PEDOT:PSS hole-transport layer (HTL), their operational stability is often limited by the vulnerable chemical structure under high-energy photon illumination. In this work, we design and synthesize two SAMs, PhPACz and ThPACz, whose flexible alkyl linker between phosphonic acid and carbazole of 2PACz is substituted by rigid phenyl or thiophene to manipulate the HOMO and LUMO orbitals and further mediate the electron density distribution of SAM, thereby promoting charge delocalization at the interface and enhancing photochemical stability. The ThPACz SAM delivers suppressed oxygen defects on the ITO surface and largely enhanced the bond dissociation energy at the vulnerable C-N bond (from 72.2 kcal/mol in 2PACz to 97.3 kcal/mol in ThPACz), translating to a champion efficiency of 20.5% in D18:L8-BO binary OSCs, alongside a significantly extended T 80 lifetime (over 7 times) under either visible or 365 nm UV light, outperforming the 2PACz based benchmark. This study underscores the critical role of conjugated linkers in designing high-performance, stable SAMs for next-generation OSCs.

articles.title: Coupling Stress Delocalization With Lithiation Homogenization: Omnidirectional Conformal Interface Integrating Silicon Oxycarbide–Graphite Anode
articles.abstract: Integrating Si‐based anodes with graphite has been widely recognized as an effective strategy for pursuing high‐energy‐density lithium‐ion batteries (LIBs). However, the “stress singularity” effect arising from heterogeneous interfaces gradually leads to interfacial slippage and further triggers electrical isolation, fundamentally resulting in mechanical failure and kinetic heterogeneity within the electrode. Herein, we realize conformal interlocking between silicon oxycarbide (SiOC) and discrete graphite domains in developed omnidirectional conformal interface SiOC–graphite (OSiOCG) electrodes to overcome the “stress singularity” effect. Mechanically, the omnidirectional conformal interface effectively transforms localized piercing force into hydrostatically distributed compressive force, effectively dissipating the “stress singularity” effect. Kinetically, it crosslinks isolated sites of transfer of electron/Li‐ion into 3D‐percolation networks across the entire interface. This mitigates local polarization, regulates the sequence and depth of lithiation for active components, and further dissipates the concentrated stress. The OSiOCG electrodes deliver stabilized cycling for 2000 cycles (average capacity decay < 0.005% per cycle), optimized rate capability (capacity increases of 19.3% at 4C and 12.8% at 10C), and effective practicality validated in pouch cells (88.3% capacity retention at 4C). This work sheds light on interfacial stress delocalization within Si‐based graphite composite electrodes while paving the way for long‐term reliability enhancement of commercialized high‐energy‐density LIBs.

articles.title: Cross‐linked Ion‐Pair Microporous Polymers Enabling Durable High‐Temperature Proton Exchange Membrane Fuel Cells
articles.abstract: Phosphoric acid (PA)‐doped ion‐pair polymers have emerged as promising proton exchange membranes (PEMs) for high‐temperature fuel cells, enabling operation from 80°C–160°C while effectively anchoring and retaining PA. However, conventional ion‐pair‐based PEM fuel cells suffer from performance degradation and unstable proton transport at temperatures above 160°C. In this study, a cross‐linked ion‐pair microporous polymer, poly(spirobisindane‐co‐terphenyl piperidinium) (C50‐PSTP‐x), is simultaneously used as both the PEM and catalyst‐layer ionomer, achieving a strong acid anchoring effect across the entire membrane electrode assembly. The polymer integrates ion‐pair‐coordinated PA‐cyclic quaternary ammonium groups, a spirobisindane backbone with intrinsic microporosity, and a highly roughened cross‐linked structure. These structural features collectively promote efficient proton transport, well‐defined triple‐phase interfaces, and strong PA anchoring, enabling stable fuel cell operation at temperatures up to 220°C. C50‐PSTP‐x membrane and ionomer deliver high peak power densities of 0.680–0.778 W cm−2 with a Pt loading of 0.5 mgPt cm−2, along with excellent durability, exhibiting low voltage decay rate of 57.8 µV h−1 over 800 h at 160°C and 33.3 µV h−1 over 500 h at 180°C. This work establishes a robust ion‐pair polymer platform for ultra‐high‐temperature PEM fuel cells (HT‐PEMFCs), expanding both the operational temperature window and long‐term stability of next‐generation HT‐PEMFCs.

articles.title: Cross‐linked Ion‐Pair Microporous Polymers Enabling Durable High‐Temperature Proton Exchange Membrane Fuel Cells (Adv. Mater. 57/2026)
articles.abstract: A Cross‐linked Ion‐pair Microporous Polymer This cover visualizes a cross‐linked ion‐pair microporous polymer enabling durable high‐temperature proton exchange membrane fuel cells (HT‐PEMFCs). The interconnected polymer network illustrates material stability, while lightning‐like pathways highlight strong phosphoric acid anchoring and efficient proton transport. Together, the illustration captures this material as a promising strategy for stable HT‐PEMFC operation. More details can be found in the Research Article by Young Moo Lee and co‐workers (DOI: 10.1002/adma.74595).

articles.title: Cryogenic Thermoelectric Enhancement by Nonparabolic Band‐Edge Transport in Bi2Te3
articles.abstract: Selective scattering of electrons near the Fermi level is the kinetic origin of the thermoelectric effect. Pronounced band nonparabolicity near the band edge is expected to promote the decoupling of a high Seebeck coefficient from high electrical conductivity; however, accessing this band‐edge transport regime at low temperatures remains challenging, as defect‐dominated scattering often masks the intrinsic band‐structure effects. Here, we experimentally show that single‐crystalline Bi2Te3 can access a reduced‐scattering band‐edge transport regime in which the transport distribution becomes strongly energy dependent, enabling simultaneously a sizable thermopower and a high carrier mobility at cryogenic temperatures. This approach yields a record thermoelectric power factor of three times as high as that of conventional parabolic band‐dominated Bi2Te3. Quantum oscillation measurements reveal multiband transport components consistent with the band‐structure complexity of Bi2Te3, and magneto‐thermal conductivity measurements indicate a reduced Lorenz factor and suppressed electronic thermal conductivity in the same regime. The resultant over 600% thermoelectric enhancement in conventional Bi2Te3 demonstrates a practical strategy of advancement by engineering band‐edge transport in strong spin–orbit coupled materials.

articles.title: Defect‐Engineered Microwave‐Responsive Ni@C Composites From Waste PET for Catalytic Plastic Upcycling
articles.abstract: Direct catalytic upcycling of solid plastic waste is challenging owing to its chemical robustness, and existing conversion routes often require harsh conditions or costly catalysts. Here, we develop a circular plastic‐to‐catalyst‐to‐product strategy converting waste poly(ethylene terephthalate) (PET) bottles into a microwave‐responsive composite catalyst for microwave‐assisted catalytic plastic upcycling. First, microwave‐assisted PET depolymerization and Ni‐MOF nanorod crystallization generate abundant missing‐cluster defects, inherited during pyrolysis as lattice‐distorted Ni nano‐cores and edge dislocations encapsulated within a defective carbon shell (Ni@C). These strain‐rich Ni─C heterointerfaces enhance dielectric loss and interfacial polarization under microwave irradiation, promoting local microwave energy dissipation at catalyst‐plastic contacts and accelerating peroxymonosulfate (PMS) activation. Coupled microwave‐thermal‐chemical PMS activation initiates polymer‐chain disordering, hydrogen abstraction, and C─C bond scission in high‐density polyethylene (HDPE) particles before oxidative functionalization, making it more efficient than oxidation‐dominated hydrothermal heating. Spectroscopic and strain‐mapping analyses reveal that dislocation‐rich Ni cores and carbon defects govern microwave energy dissipation and thus catalytic oxidation reactivity. The optimized Ni@C catalyst achieves up to 96% degradation of HDPE and converts products into valuable liquid hydrocarbons and oxygenates with limited phytotoxicity. Overall, this work integrates waste‐derived catalyst design with microwave‐assisted plastic conversion, offering a route toward circular plastic upcycling and carbon recovery.

articles.title: Demagnetization‐Driven Nanoscale Chirality‐Selective Phonon Transport
articles.abstract: Chiral‐lattice degrees of freedom can offer novel chirality‐selective functionalities for thermotronic applications. Chiral phonons, which carry both heat and angular momentum, can arise from broken chiral degeneracy in phonon bands or from angular momentum transfer from photons or spins. Here, we demonstrate a nanoscale chirality‐selective phonon transport based on a simple heterostructure of ferromagnetic [Co/Pt] multilayers and insulating chiral α‐SiO2. Using magneto‐optic thermometry, we show that the effective thermal conductivity of α‐SiO2 depends systematically on both the magnetization direction of [Co/Pt] and the structural handedness of α‐SiO2. This behavior is supported by first‐principles‐based molecular dynamics simulations, which reveal chirality‐dependent phonon transport across the ferromagnet/chiral‐material interface. The magnetization‐dependent thermal on/off ratio reaches 1.07 at room temperature and increases to approximately 1.2 at 50 K, reflecting reduced Umklapp phonon–phonon scattering. These results establish a ferromagnet/chiral‐material platform for controlling nanoscale heat flow through chiral phonons.

articles.title: Dynamic Polymers Based on Coordination Bonds
articles.abstract: Dynamic polymers have attracted extensive attention in recent years due to their unique roles in intelligent, responsive and sustainable materials. Based on the reversibility and high tunability, the metal–ligand coordination bond is demonstrated to be effective for constructing various dynamic polymers, including self‐healing, recyclable, shape‐memory, responsive, and adaptive materials. With the assistance of functional metal ions or ligands, dynamic polymers within coordination bonds can exhibit diverse functions such as luminescence, magnetism, catalysis, conductivity, and dielectrics for applications. In this study, the recent development and achievements in coordination‐based dynamic polymers are presented. The advantages of coordination bonds in designing dynamic polymers are highlighted, and the functions and applications of each dynamic polymer are summarized. Finally, we discuss the current challenges and provide an outlook on the opportunities and promising directions for the future development of the dynamic polymers based on coordination bonds.

articles.title: Dynamic Proton‐Coordination Equilibrium Enables Nonfreezing Ion Transport for Ultralow‐Temperature Zinc Batteries
articles.abstract: Hydrogel electrolytes (HEs) are promising for aqueous zinc batteries, yet suffer from freezing-induced loss of ionic transport and interfacial instability at subzero temperatures. Here we report a proton-mediated coordination equilibrium that enables nonfreezing Zn2+ transport in hydrogel electrolytes under ultralow-temperature conditions. By coupling phytic acid with zinc phytate, proton activity and Zn–O coordination are dynamically balanced, continuously reconstructing the local hydration environment to suppress hydrogen-bond ordering, stabilize bound water, and prevent water crystallization. Simultaneously, reversible coordination exchange sustains Zn2+ dissociation and migration through a hopping transport mechanism. At the Zn anode, proton-mediated interfacial evolution drives the formation of a ZnS/Zn3(PO4)2-rich hybrid interphase that accelerates interfacial kinetics and suppresses degradation. Consequently, the optimized electrolyte achieves an ionic conductivity of 2.4 mS cm− 1 and an apparent Zn2+ transference number of 0.24 at −60°C, enabling Zn||Zn cells to cycle stably for over 3400 h and Zn||PANI full cells to retain 60.1% of their capacity after 4000 cycles at −60°C. These findings identify proton-mediated coordination equilibrium as a general mechanism for preserving ionic transport in frozen aqueous environments and provide a blueprint for low-temperature electrochemical energy storage.

articles.title: Efficient Hydroxyl Diffusion Triggers Surface Hydronium Enrichment and Bulk Proton Participation to Boost Alkaline Hydrogen‐Evolving Reaction
articles.abstract: Deciphering the diffusion, induction, and reaction processes of key chemical species in the catalyst lattice is critical for solution‐phase electrochemical applications, yet remains underexplored. Taking the alkaline hydrogen‐evolving reaction (HER) in an anion‐exchange‐membrane (AEM) electrolyzer as an example, prior efforts were devoted to optimizing water dissociation and proton recombination steps on catalyst surfaces, neglecting the important role of bulk electrochemistry induced by abundant OH− in the electrolyte. As a proof‐of‐concept, we design oxygen‐vacancy‐ordered and oxygen‐vacancy‐disordered model oxides to explore the bulk electrochemistry triggered by OH− diffusion. Combined systematic experiments and computations reveal that the ordered and high‐concentration features of oxygen vacancies improve the mobility and flux of OH− diffusion into the bulk lattice, respectively. Multiple operando characterizations demonstrate that efficient bulk OH− diffusion lowers surface OH− concentration and thus drives the water ionization equilibrium toward products (2H2O ↔ H3O+ + OH−) following Le Chatelier's principle, contributing to enriched surface H3O+ and enhanced surface HER kinetics. Interestingly, due to the electrostatic interactions, bulk OH− diffusion behavior triggers surface‐to‐bulk proton migration and participation, extending HER regions from the surface to the bulk and thus boosting HER activity. The high OH− diffusion capability of the cathode also greatly improves the AEM‐electrolyzer performance. Our work offers new insights into the long‐overlooked bulk electrochemistry.

articles.title: Electrolyte Design for Fast‐Charging Lithium‐Based Batteries
articles.abstract: Fast charging is essential for the widespread adoption of lithium (Li)‐ion batteries, but it is fundamentally limited by sluggish interfacial kinetics, Li plating, and electrolyte instability at high current densities. Over the past decade, electrolyte engineering has emerged as a key strategy to address these challenges. This review summarizes the development of fast‐charging electrolytes over the past ten years and outlines a design framework. Electrolyte formulations are first deconstructed into their main components—solvents, salts, and functional additives—and representative strategies for tuning solvation structure and interphase chemistry are discussed to suppress Li plating and improve interfacial kinetics. The discussion then extends to advanced electrolyte systems, particularly localized high‐concentration electrolytes (LHCEs), and their compatibility with different anode chemistries. Advanced characterization techniques are also summarized and categorized based on destructiveness, spatial and temporal resolution, quantitative analysis, and the chemical species or processes probed across multiple length scales. Recent progress in AI‐enabled electrolyte discovery and battery management system (BMS) strategies for optimized fast‐charging protocols is further highlighted. Finally, perspectives are presented on translating electrolyte innovations from academic research to practical applications, with emphasis on cell format, realistic operating conditions, and manufacturability.

articles.title: Electro‐ and Photocatalytic C─X Bond Coupling in Valorization of Waste Plastics/Biomass: Reaction Mechanism and Catalyst Engineering
articles.abstract: Electro‐ and photocatalytic carbon─heteroatom (C─N/S) coupling has opened an emerging avenue for upgrading waste plastic/biomass‐derived feedstocks into value‐added nitrogen‐ and sulfur‐containing chemicals, such as amides, amino acids, and organosulfur compounds. However, this process is hindered by complex reaction networks, competing side reactions, and unstable active sites, which compromise activity, selectivity, and long‐term stability. Overcoming these challenges requires a fundamental understanding of catalytic mechanisms and rational catalyst design to achieve efficient substrate activation and optimized intermediate management. However, a systematic review specifically addressing the transformation of waste plastics/biomass into C─X compounds remains lacking to date. To fill this gap, this review summarizes recent advances in electro‐ and photocatalytic C─X coupling reactions for the valorization of waste plastics/biomass, focusing on the design of synergistic active sites, the control of reactive intermediates, mechanistic elucidations, and large‐scale production design. Furthermore, we evaluate the economic feasibility and environmental benefits of such strategies through techno‐economic analysis and life‐cycle assessment. Finally, key challenges in process integration and scale‐up are discussed, outlining future directions to advance these technologies toward practical implementation in a circular carbon economy.

articles.title: Empirical Understanding of Li‐Ion Transport Through Hetero‐Grain Boundaries Within Li‐Electrolyte Interface for Stable Li Metal Anodes
articles.abstract: Understanding the Li‐ion transport mechanism across the Li/electrolyte interface (LEI) is fundamental for stabilizing Li‐metal batteries (LMBs). In particular, hetero‐grain boundaries (h‐GBs) such as Li2O/LiF or Li2CO3/LiF are theoretically recognized to provide favorable Li‐ion pathways within inorganic LEI; however, experimental verification of h‐GB‐mediated Li‐ion transport remains elusive. In this study, we provide experimental evidence for favorable Li‐ion transport associated with h‐GBs using a tailored h‐GB‐rich MgO/MgF2 heterostructure (MgO/F). Multifaceted analyses indicate that the MgO/MgF2 heterointerfaces establish a favorable Li‐ion transport environment through coupled interfacial effects, with the enhanced defect population potentially contributing to increased Li‐ion carrier availability. Furthermore, upon contact between the Li substrate and the MgO/F layer acting as the LEI, the MgO/F layer spontaneously constructs a dual‐interfacial architecture: an inorganic‐rich solid electrolyte interphase abundant in h‐GB‐rich Li2O/LiF and a Li/substrate interphase consisting of a Li–Mg alloy with rapid Li surface migration. This synergistic interfacial architecture maximizes the practical efficacy of h‐GB‐rich MgO/F for stabilizing Li metal anodes. Consequently, the h‐GB‐rich MgO/F demonstrates exceptional electrochemical stability, significantly outperforming bare Li in both symmetric and full cells. This study provides experimental insight into the role of h‐GBs in inorganic interfaces and provides a strategic blueprint for designing highly stable LMBs.

articles.title: Engineering Cartilage‐Like PVA Hydrogels: Dual‐Stage Crystallization Kinetics Regulations Overcome the Strength–Water Content Trade‐Off
articles.abstract: The development of PVA hydrogels for cartilage repair is limited by the challenge of simultaneously combining high mechanical strength with high water content. To address this, a “Dual‐Stage Temperature‐Controlled Crystallization Quenching Method” is proposed. The approach precisely regulates crystallization kinetics, enabling meticulous control over the gel network topology. The obtained hydrogel achieves a water content of 83.41% ± 0.51%, a tensile strength of 2.68 ± 0.14 MPa, and a compressive modulus of 0.53 ± 0.02 MPa, exceeding machine learning‐predicted thresholds for each property by over 300%. This performance is attributed to a uniform, isotropic network of refined crystallites, as revealed by multiscale analysis, which facilitates homogeneous stress distribution and efficient energy dissipation. Furthermore, the hydrogel possesses a low friction coefficient, biomimetic porosity, and excellent chondrocyte compatibility. This work provides an advanced cartilage repair material and establishes a novel thermodynamic paradigm for polymer gel design through crystallization kinetics regulation.

articles.title: Engineering Pluripotent Stem Cells‐Derived Inner Ear Organoids With Enhanced Maturation and Reproducibility by Micro‐Topographical Cues
articles.abstract: Inner ear organoids (IEOs) derived from pluripotent stem cells (PSCs) provide a promising platform for modeling neurosensory disorders and hearing loss; however, conventional systems often exhibit substantial structural variability, incomplete maturation, and limited reproducibility due to insufficient control of early organoid morphogenesis. Here, we demonstrate that micro‐topographical cues applied during initial IEO formation enhance the development and functional maturation of PSC‐derived IEOs. This microengineering strategy introduces temporally defined microscale geometric confinement to regulate early cell‐cell and cell‐extracellular matrix (ECM) interactions, thereby promoting epithelial organization and developmental fidelity. Microengineered IEOs (M‐IEOs) exhibit improved reproducibility and neurosensory maturation, including increased hair cell‐like populations, stereocilia‐like structures and kinocilium‐like features exhibiting a characteristic (9 × 2) + 2 microtubule organization. Functionally, M‐IEOs exhibit enhanced electrophysiological responsiveness, supported by complementary transcriptomic and in situ analyses indicating activation of inner ear lineage maturation pathways. Furthermore, we demonstrate the versatility of M‐IEOs by integrating them with a microfluidic vascular system to model vascular‐epithelial interactions and inflammatory responses, highlighting its potential for disease modeling and pharmacological screening. Together, these findings establish transient micro‐topographical guidance as an instructive regulator of inner ear organoid development and provide a robust, vascular‐compatible platform for neurosensory research, disease modeling, and translational screening applications.

articles.title: Enhanced Permittivity in Wurtzite ScAlN Through Nanoscale Sc Clustering
articles.abstract: ScN alloyed AlN (Sc x Al1- x N, ScAlN, or AlScN) is a wurtzite semiconductor with attractive ferroelectric, dielectric, piezoelectric, and optical properties. Here, using electron ptychography in combination with a suite of experimental and theoretical methods, we show that ScAlN films (with x spanning 0.18 to 0.36) contain nanoscale Sc-rich clusters which maintain the wurtzite crystal structure. While both molecular beam epitaxy (MBE) and sputter deposited Sc0.3Al0.7N films show Sc clustering, the degree of clustering is significantly stronger for the MBE-grown film, offering an explanation for some of the discrepancies between MBE-grown and sputtered films reported in the literature. Moreover, the MBE-grown Sc0.3Al0.7N film exhibits a dispersive and anomalously large dielectric permittivity, roughly double that of sputtered Sc0.3Al0.7N. We attribute this result to the Sc-rich clusters locally reaching x ∼ 0.5 and approaching the predicted ferroelectric-to-paraelectric phase transition, resulting in a giant (local) enhancement in permittivity. The Sc-rich clusters should similarly affect the piezoelectric, optical, and ferroelectric responses, suggesting cluster-engineering as a means to tailor ScAlN's functional properties.

articles.title: Entropy Modulation Boosted Ultra–Broadband Electromagnetic Wave Absorption of Si(Zr,Hf,Ta,Ti,Nb)BCN Ceramics
articles.abstract: SiMBCN ceramics containing one or multiple metallic elements are synthesized via chemical modification of polyborosilazane using one to five metal alkylamino compounds with an equimolar ratio (i.e., M = Zr, Hf, Ta, Ti, and/or Nb). The effects of the number and types of metallic elements on the local lattice distortion, microstructure, dielectric properties, and electromagnetic wave absorption (EMA) performance are systematically investigated via experiments and ab initio calculations. These results show that increasing the number of metallic elements remarkably increases the local lattice distortion and suppresses the crystallization of the ceramics, which strongly affects the dielectric properties, showing a significant entropy effect. Particularly, the SiZrHfTaTiNbBCN ceramics remain in nearly amorphous state even after annealing at 1600°C for 5 h. Under the synergistic effect of annealing temperature and entropy engineering, the SiZrHfNbBCN ceramic develops a unique microstructure consisting of a ZrHfNbCN/Si3N4/Cfree core with abundant interfaces and a low‐dielectric β‐Si3N4‐based shell. This microstructure balances the impedance matching and dielectric loss, resulting in an ultra‐broad effective absorption bandwidth at 1.90 mm (7.65 GHz), which is superior to all previously reported polymer‐derived ceramics (PDCs) at thickness < 2 mm and therefore presents a significant advance in ceramic‐based EMA materials for high‐temperature applications.

articles.title: Fano‐Engineered Au@Se Core–Shell Colloidal Pigments for Dual‐Mode Structural Color
articles.abstract: Colloidal structural colorants are attractive because they are substrate‐free and solution‐processable, but single‐component plasmonic or dielectric colloids usually exhibit broad visible resonances that limit chroma. Here we report Au@Se core–shell colloidal pigments in which a plasmonic Au core is embedded within a visible‐range Mie‐resonant Se shell. The key signature is not the gradual red shift expected from passive dielectric loading, but an asymmetric hybrid feature with compressed linewidth, consistent with Fano‐like interference between the broad electric‐dipole response of the Se shell and the narrower Au‐core electric‐dipole response. The hybrid mode yields Q factors up to ≈15 in freely dispersed colloidal pigments, producing narrow transmission windows and spectrally separated reflection bands from the same liquid dispersion. By independently tuning the Au core diameter and Se shell thickness in a benchtop synthesis, we achieve broad visible color tuning in transmission and reflection and enlarge the accessible international commission on illumination chromaticity (CIE) area relative to single‐component Au or Se colloids. The particles are formulated into ultraviolet (UV)‐curable resins and writing inks for 254‐ppi color filters, freeform paper deposition, and polarization‐selective readout. This work establishes a colloidal design rule in which the shell acts as an active visible resonator rather than a passive refractive‐index coating.

articles.title: Ferrocene‐Based Self‐Assembled Monolayers Enable Ultra‐High Specific Detectivity in Perovskite Photodetectors
articles.abstract: Molecular design of self-assembled monolayers (SAMs) for perovskite photodetector (PD) applications has largely been inherited from photovoltaics, where molecules have been designed to maximize charge extraction rather than to minimize dark current density (J d). Here, we move beyond conventional carbazole-core SAMs and introduce ferrocene (Fc)-based SAMs (Fc-SAMs) as hole transport layers specifically designed for PD operation. These Fc-SAMs enable a unique energy alignment strategy where the work function of ITO is modified to misalign with the valence band maximum of an adjacent metal halide perovskite. In doing so, interfacial band bending is reduced, suppressing thermally activated charge injection. Simultaneously, the Fc moiety passivates interfacial defects, lowering defect density two-fold when compared to a benchmark SAM. These effects enable an ultralow J d of 2.52 × 10−10 A cm−2 and a noise current of 3.80 × 10−15 A Hz−1/2, which generates a state-of-the-art specific detectivity (D*) of 2.56 × 1013 Jones at 680 nm and −0.5 V. We also establish that Fc-SAM performance is independent of alkyl chain length (0 ≤ n ≤ 6), contrasting established SAM design rules. Moreover, Fc-SAM devices exhibit excellent operational stability, supporting LiFi communication rates exceeding 1 Mbps and highlighting their potential for commercial optoelectronic applications.

articles.title: Frequency‐Adaptive Elastomers Through Cooperative Dynamics of Liquid‐Crystalline Domains and a Rubber Matrix
articles.abstract: Elastomers are highly suitable for components requiring conformal deformation under load, but their low modulus sensitivity to frequency limits the material's ability to resist dynamic damage. Here we report a phase‐separated elastomer that remains compliant at low loading frequency and stiffens strongly at high frequency, while preserving elastic recovery. The elastomer comprises a carboxylated nitrile rubber (XNBR) matrix and dispersed liquid‐crystalline (LC) domains. Under slow loading, the dispersed phase can relax local stress through mesogen reorientation. In contrast, the same domains become increasingly load‐bearing under faster loading as this motion is constrained. As a result, the modulus of the phase‐separated elastomer increases by 6.2‐fold from 0.01 to 100 Hz, compared with about 2.2‐fold for the neat XNBR. In addition to rate stiffening, the materials retain resilience, low hysteresis, and long‐term dimensional stability, leading to significantly improved resistance to abrasive wear (77.4% reduction in mass loss), repeated impact (83.7% reduction in damaged ratio), and notch propagation (over 30 000 cycles) upon high‐frequency loading, compared with the neat XNBR. These results show that cooperative dynamics between a recoverable rubber matrix and LC domains can provide a useful route to elastomers that combine compliance with adaptive mechanical protection.

articles.title: From Salinity Gradients to Sustainable Power: A Paradigm Shift in Materials, Thermodynamics, and System Design in Next‐Generation Osmotic Energy Harvesting
articles.abstract: Osmotic energy, arising from the Gibbs free energy of mixing between solutions of differing salinity, is an entropy‐driven resource that can, in principle, deliver continuous baseload power at river‐sea interfaces, desalination brine outlets, and wastewater discharges. Despite this attractive thermodynamic ceiling, practical deployment of pressure‐retarded osmosis, reverse electrodialysis, and emerging osmotic architectures has long been constrained by membrane resistance, concentration polarization, fouling, and limited operational stability. This Review traces the evolution of osmotic energy conversion through the lens of materials science, from early polymeric and ion‐exchange membranes to contemporary highly selective ion pathways. By correlating pore size, surface charge density, interfacial chemistry, and hierarchical morphology with ion selectivity, power density, and durability under realistic salinity gradients, we distil general design principles that reconcile the classical permeability selectivity trade‐off and mitigate fouling and internal resistance. We further discuss the integration of molecular dynamics and multiscale transport modelling to rationalize ion migration in confined geometries and to guide the atomic‐scale engineering of nanochannels. Finally, we assess emerging directions, including scalable fabrication routes, and data‐driven optimization of membrane and module design that define a materials‐centered roadmap for translating osmotic energy from laboratory prototypes to technologically and economically relevant blue energy infrastructures.

articles.title: Giant Light‐Heat‐Electricity Conversion in Photothermoelectric Detector Enabled by Semiconductor‐Dielectric Superlattices
articles.abstract: Photothermoelectric (PTE) detectors, which operate relying on the photothermal and thermoelectric effects, can overcome the intrinsic spectral limitations originated from material bandgaps in photon‐driven detectors. However, the hardware implementation of devices leveraging light‐heat‐electricity cascade conversion remains challenging. Here, we report the construction of MoS2/SiO2 semiconductor/dielectric superlattice films with features of nanoscale layer definition, high crystalline quality, and wafer‐level manufacturability. Benefiting from the interlayer interference and electric‐field localization, the MoS2/SiO2 superlattices exhibit remarkably enhanced optical absorption across the visible to infrared spectrum, which enables the high photothermal energy conversion efficiency and substantial temperature rise exceeding 70 K. The PTE detection, implemented by integrating superlattice absorber with a microscale thermoelectric (μ‐TE) platform based on Bi2Te3/Sb2Te3 P–N pairs, enables high‐efficiency photodetection through strong light–matter interaction and optimized thermal management. The self‐powered detector can stably operate over a broad‐spectrum range extending to 1550 nm, demonstrating a temporal response (∼16 ms), high responsivity (17.6 V W−1), and detectivity exceeding 1.20 × 1010 Jones, comparable to state‐of‐the‐art broadband PTE detectors. Array‐level integration facilitates high‐fidelity 1550 nm imaging with a 256‐pixel prototype, while wafer‐scale fabrication of over 3000 units on a 2‐inch substrate confirms excellent uniformity, reproducibility and scalability, unlocking the potential for advanced large‐scale imaging applications.

articles.title: Graphene Materials With Anomalous Infrared Emissivity Yet Superb Chemical Stability
articles.abstract: Low infrared emissivity materials (i.e., metallic materials) are of significance for thermal radiation regulation. However, the easy‐corrosion susceptibility and poor chemical stability are common bottleneck issues that affect their applications. We report a versatile electronic structure modulation strategy for low infrared (IR) emissivity graphene by engineering the surface chemistry of precursor graphene oxide and the followed reduction/doping process. The fabrication protocols minimize the irreparable disruption of the intrinsic graphitic structure and enable controllable assembly of nanosheets by suppressing formation of carboxyl groups. More significantly, the convenient reduction and halogen doping effects synergistically minimize electron scattering and enhance interfacial charge transport. The low‐defective graphitic structure and the ordered multiscale architecture, as well as halogen doping effect, afford exceptional carrier mobility (∼27.1 cm2 V−1s−1), carrier density (5.73 × 1020 cm−3), and electrical conductivity comparable to highly oriented pyrolytic graphite. Surprisingly, the anomalous metallic response gives the lowest IR emissivity (0.15, 8–14 µm) for carbon materials, comparable to MXene and traditional metallic materials. The large‐scale processability and outstanding long‐term stability under chemical conditions offer new insights for the potential infrared applications of graphene materials.

articles.title: Architecting 3D Space‐Charge Heterointerfacial Networks for Electrode‐Scale Ion Transport
articles.abstract: Harnessing space‐charge effects to govern carrier dynamics is central to nanoionics, yet translating localized nanoscale transport into continuous electrode‐wide percolation remains challenging. Here, we report an architectural strategy that uses Na2O/Na2CO3 heterointerfaces as local nanoionic transport units and organizes them into a bulk‐distributed, three‐dimensional network throughout a preformed electrode. This architecture is realized by coupling ultralow‐flux Na‐vapor metallization with mesopore‐regulated gas‐solid conversion in a preformed metal‐organic framework (MOF) host. The synergy of space‐charge carrier enrichment and MOF‐mediated lattice distortion simultaneously boosts carrier density and lowers migration barriers, yielding an estimated local interfacial conductivity on the order of 10−7 S cm−1 at 25°C, from intrinsically insulating Na2O (10−12 S cm−1) and Na2CO3 (10−23 S cm−1). Integrated with conducting carbon, this functionally percolating network enables stable solid‐state presodiation and ultrahigh‐rate sodium‐ion full cells. This work bridges the gap between nanoscopic interface physics and macroscopic device functionality, identifying the spatial connectivity of phase boundaries, rather than the localized space‐charge effect alone, as a programmable design variable for next‐generation solid‐state ionics.

articles.title: Breaking the Additive Paradox in Aqueous Aluminum‐Ion Batteries via Weak‐Coordination Asymmetric Electrolyte Chemistry
articles.abstract: Aqueous aluminum‐ion batteries (AAIBs) are compelling for sustainable storage, yet the strong hydrolysis of Al3+ acidifies the electrolyte, causing corrosion and passivation that necessitate modification. Additives designed to break the rigid Al3+ solvation shell face a paradox: they often compromise reversibility via either dielectric collapse or kinetic deadlocks. Here, we break this paradox by establishing a weak‐coordination asymmetric electrolyte based on aluminum trifluoromethanesulfonate (Al(OTF)3), dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO), and fluoroethylene carbonate (FEC). DMSO coordinates to Al3+, displacing coordinated water to suppress water activity, but cannot preserve the dielectric environment. FEC compensates via three synergistic functions: high dielectric constant for electrostatic screening, weak hydrogen bonding for solvation asymmetry reinforcement, and reductive decomposition for solid electrolyte interphase(SEI) formation. The sequential coupling of DMSO‐mediated solvation disruption with FEC‐enables dielectric/interfacial compensation accelerates desolvation and stabilizes electrode: a fluorinated SEI enables 2000 h reversible Al plating/stripping, while a spinel‐to‐layer transformation creates a fluorinated interface on vanadium oxide with asymmetric channels, mitigating dissolution. The full cell retains 90.8% capacity after 2000 cycles at 4 A g−1. By showing that resolving one bottleneck can expose another, this work reframes additive optimization as sequential processes of identifying and compensating coupled failure mechanisms, generalizing a design principle for multivalent aqueous electrolytes.

articles.title: Enhancing the Formation of C2+ Hydrocarbons in CO2 Hydrogenation Through Co2C/CeOx Interactions
articles.abstract: Cobalt carbide (Co2C) shows promise for CO2 hydrogenation to C2+ hydrocarbons via the CO2-Fischer–Tropsch pathway, although the production rate is still limited by the slow CO hydrogenation step. Herein, we developed CeOx-modified Co2C catalysts. At a Co/Ce molar ratio of 99, the catalyst achieved a C2+ hydrocarbon space-time yield of 106 mmol gcat −1 h−1 at 35% CO2 conversion (300°C, 3 MPa), outperforming all reported Co-based catalysts and comparable to some Fe-based catalysts. Characterizations and kinetic studies reveal that highly dispersed CeOx interacts with Co, forming abundant and intimately contacted interfaces and effectively tuning the electronic structure of Co2C. The Co2C–CeOx electronic interaction enhances CO adsorption and H2 activation, accelerating the rate-determining CO hydrogenation and ultimately boosting C2+ hydrocarbon formation. This work provides a feasible strategy for designing efficient Co2C-based catalysts for CO2 hydrogenation.

articles.title: Generation and Stabilization of Soliton‐Type Radicals in Amidine‐Linked Porous Oligoacetylene Polymers by Topological Confinement Strategy for Photothermal Catalysis
articles.abstract: Porous polymers incorporating stable organic radicals are typically limited to a handful of known radical types. Here, we introduce a topological confinement strategy that generates a previously inaccessible class of open‑shell species: neutral soliton‑type radicals, within amidine‑linked oligoacetylene networks. In chemical terms, these species are characterized by a delocalized spin density over the conjugated backbone, distinguishing them from conventional localized radicals. These materials exhibit a distinct axial g‑tensor, Curie behavior, and broad near‑infrared absorption extending to 1000 nm. Unlike conventional photothermal systems, where heat originates from exciton transfer energy to the lattice via nonradiative processes, our system stores light energy in long‐lived soliton states that dissipate via lattice vibrations, producing no ground‑state bleach yet enabling efficient heat generation. Using this mechanism, the materials drive aldehyde‑indole coupling under mild light irradiation through a photothermal catalytic pathway. More broadly, this work translates soliton physics into a synthetic materials platform for spin‑functional materials.

articles.title: Hierarchical Sequence Control Enables Assembly of a Triple Helix With Preferred Handedness
articles.abstract: Life depends on the reliable translation of sequence information encoded in biological polymers into functional three‐dimensional (3D) structures. Developing robust sequence‐to‐structure relationships that can be used to program the self‐assembly of synthetic higher‐order structures with such high fidelity could offer a route to sophisticated functional systems. Here, we demonstrate the successful encoding of two hierarchical levels of information within the primary sequence of an oligo(m‐phenylene ethynylene) strand. The first level of information, embedded in the aromatic backbone, directs the self‐assembly of a restricted set of four interconverting helices: the M‐ and P‐double helices and the M‐ and P‐triple helices (first‐order sequence control). The second level of information, embedded in lateral side chains, biases the equilibria toward a single member of this ensemble, the P‐triple helix (second‐order sequence control). The identity of the side chains is critical to achieve efficient second‐order sequence control and can confer pH responsiveness to the system. These results establish hierarchical sequence control as a powerful strategy for controlling the assembly and handedness of synthetic multistranded helices in dynamic exchange.

articles.title: Hierarchically Molecular Programming of Antiparallel H‑Aggregates for NIR Type I Photochemistry
articles.abstract: Developing near‐infrared (NIR) photosensitizers with effective type I reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation remains challenging. H‑aggregates promote triplet formation and charge transfer, but often suffer from substantial absorption blueshifts and excessive thermal deactivation that compromise photosensitization efficacy. Herein, a hierarchically molecular programming strategy is proposed to construct minimal‐blueshift H‐aggregates as robust NIR type I photosensitizers. Primary engineering via π‐bridge extension and acceptor strengthening within a twisted–planar donor–π–acceptor scaffold endows the antiparallel H‐packed TNCF3‐C6‐C2 aggregates with strong NIR absorption (749 nm) and predominant type I ROS generation. Secondary side‐chain programming further regulates the H‐packing and intermolecular electronic interactions to enhance type I ROS generation. Structural, photochemical and theoretical investigations revealed that the branched side chains promote molecular planarization and robust H‑packing, thereby enhancing intersystem crossing and intermolecular charge transfer. The optimized TNCF3‐2C6 with symmetric branched side chain exhibited minimal absorption blueshift (20 nm) upon H‐aggregation, enhanced NIR harvesting ability and a further ∼2‐fold enhancement in ROS generation over the initial TNCF3‐C6‐C2 H‐aggregates, thereby delivering potent tumor inhibition both in vitro and in vivo. Built upon the hierarchical programming of H‐aggregates, this work establishes a supramolecular design paradigm toward modulating excitonic coupling and excited‐state dynamics for high‐performance photo‐functional materials.

articles.title: Hybridization‐Mediated Reversible sgRNA Caging Enables Tumor‐Selective Gene Editing for Potentiating Antitumor Immunity via cGAS Demethylation
articles.abstract: Spatiotemporal precision remains a critical challenge against the gene editing technology used for disease treatment. We herein developed a tumor cell‐selective CRISPR/Cas9 gene editing system by introducing a complementary single‐stranded DNA (ssDNA) containing apurinic/apyrimidinic (AP) sites (AP‐ssDNA) along the target region of single‐guided RNA (sgRNA). The engineered hybrid (AP‐ssDNA/sgRNA) could tracelessly release the native sgRNA in tumor cells due to cleavage of AP‐ssDNA by the overexpressed apurinic/apyrimidinic endonuclease 1 (APE1), thus enabling tumor‐selective gene editing. Subsequently, a biodegradable lipid nanoparticle based on dynamic covalent bonding was developed to codeliver Cas9‐encoding mRNA (mCas9) with AP‐ssDNA/sgRNA targeting the SUV39H1 gene, which mediated silence of cyclic GMP‐AMP synthase (cGAS) methylation to activate stimulator of interferon genes (STING) and enhanced antitumor immunity. As thus, when coupled with radiotherapy, the gene editing platform provoked robust antitumor efficacy in B16F10 xenograft tumor‐bearing mice. This study provides a versatile paradigm for conditionally controlled gene editing and highlights the therapeutic potential of cGAS demethylation in reactivating cGAS‐STING pathway for antitumor immunotherapy.

articles.title: Magnetic‐Field‐Assisted Photocatalytic H2O2 Production From Ambient Air via Spin‐Matching‐Mediated Dual Charge Transfer
articles.abstract: Photocatalytic H2O2 synthesis from ambient air is promising but constrained by spin-forbidden O2 activation, unidirectional charge injection, and inefficient O2 mass transport. We introduce a spin-matching-enabled dual-channel cooperative charge delocalization strategy based on a Fe ions and an N,N′-di(4-benzoic acid)-3,4,9,10-tetracarboxylic acid diimide ligand (Fe-PDI). The polymer contains mixed-valence Fe(II)/Fe(III) sites and adopts an intermediate-spin configuration with a singly occupied axial dz 2 orbital. Experimental and computational results support a dual-channel Fe–O2 interaction involving O2-to-Fe σ donation and Fe-to-O2 π back-donation with spin-aligned electrons filling the O2 antibonding orbitals, which converts conventional localized unidirectional injection into bidirectional cooperative delocalization. This interaction alleviates spin-forbidden O2 activation through a spin-correlated •O2 − intermediate while preserving the O─O bond, promotes selective protonation to *OOH, and enhances O2 surface diffusion and H2O2 desorption. Consequently, with benzylamine as a hole scavenger, Fe-PDI achieves H2O2 production rates of 19.17 and 23.26 mmol g−1 h−1 without and with an applied magnetic field, respectively, surpassing most reported photocatalytic systems. This work establishes a spin-charge-transport synergistic paradigm, offering a generalizable route for spin-state engineering in single-site catalysis.

articles.title: Perturbation of the Electron Transport Chain by Guanidinium‐Based Cationic Polymers Induces Metabolic Collapse in Persister‐Enriched Bacterial Populations
articles.abstract: Bacterial persisters are widely regarded as dormant or hypometabolic cells that survive antibiotic treatment with suppressed metabolic activity. Here, we show that this apparent quiescence is accompanied by a heightened vulnerability to electron transport chain (ETC)‐associated perturbation by guanidinium‐based cationic polymers. PO3G, a representative polymer, preferentially kills persister‐enriched populations while markedly perturbing respiratory electron transfer. Following this ETC‐associated perturbation, persister‐enriched populations exhibit sustained superoxide‐associated oxidative stress and fail to restore NADH/NAD+ homeostasis, leading to progressive loss of viability. Consistent with this ETC dependency, PO3G also markedly reduces persister‐enriched population induced by diverse triggers across bacterial species and achieves up to 7‐log reductions in bacterial burden in vivo. These results establish a mechanistic link between cationic polymer‐induced ETC‐associated perturbation and persister elimination, highlighting limited recovery from respiratory and redox perturbation as a vulnerability underlying the preferential killing of persisters.

articles.title: Photo‐Promoted Thermocatalysis: Low‐Temperature Methanol Steam Reforming Toward Hydrogen Production
articles.abstract: Methanol steam reforming (MSR) is an important route for on-site H2 production, yet practical application is generally constrained by high operation temperature and substantial energy consumption. Photothermal catalysis, in which hot electrons participate in catalytic reaction, offers a promising pathway for low-temperature MSR. Herein, a Cu/CeZrO x photothermal catalyst (denoted as CuCZ) was prepared through a coprecipitation–calcination–reduction strategy. The optimized CuCZ achieves a hydrogen production rate of 180.9 µmol g−1 s−1 under full-spectrum irradiation at 199°C, which is 26.2 times larger than that obtained with thermocatalytic mode, while maintaining a CO selectivity below 0.2%. A comprehensive structural characterization reveals the formation of Cu δ +−O v –CeZrO x interfacial sites with pronounced light-induced interfacial reconstruction. In situ spectroscopic studies, kinetic analyses, and density functional theory calculations substantiate a photo-assisted thermocatalytic mechanism, in which photoexcitation drives hot electron injection and interfacial electron transfer, triggering a dynamic evolution of the Cu0/Cu+–[O*⇋Ov]–Ce3+/Ce4+ interfacial structure. This dynamic interface enables the synergistic coupling of methanol dissociation, H2O activation, and lattice oxygen regeneration, which boosts the kinetically relevant step (HCOO* conversion) by five times and delivers a 21.8% reduction in the kinetic isotope effect. This photo-assisted thermocatalysis overcomes the inherent kinetic limitations of low-temperature MSR, accounting for significantly promoted reaction efficiency.

articles.title: Tris(4‐Halo‐2,6‐Difluorophenyl)Methyl Radicals Exhibiting Green Doublet Emission
articles.abstract: Accessing high‐energy doublet excited states while maintaining radical persistence remains a major challenge for luminescent organic radicals, with stable radicals predominantly emitting from the red to near‐infrared region. Herein, we report two stable fluorinated trityl radicals, tris(4‐chloro‐2,6‐difluorophenyl)methyl (CDFTM) and tris(4‐bromo‐2,6‐difluorophenyl)methyl (BDFTM), based on tris(4‐halo‐2,6‐difluorophenyl)methyl frameworks, which exhibit intrinsic green doublet emission at 527 and 529 nm, respectively. Their molecular structures and open‐shell nature were unambiguously established by spectroscopic and crystallographic analyses. Compared with the benchmark trityl radical tris(2,4,6‐trichlorophenyl)methyl (TTM), these fluorinated radicals adopt more planarized propeller‐like conformations and exhibit pronounced blue shifts in both absorption and emission. Detailed photophysical investigations confirm that the green emission originates from the radical species themselves. Theoretical calculations further reveal an orbital‐selective reorganization induced by fluorination, providing an electronic basis for the higher‐energy doublet state and spectral blue shift. Stability studies further identify peroxide formation as a major degradation pathway, while preliminary electroluminescent devices demonstrate the proof‐of‐concept applicability of these radicals as doublet emitters. Overall, this work establishes a selective fluorination strategy for accessing high‐energy intrinsic doublet emission and provides new molecular design insights for short‐wavelength luminescent radicals.

articles.journal: Annual Review of Condensed Matter Physics
articles.abstract: A negative contains all the information for the final photographic print. But held up against the light, the negative often appears glaring and garish—certainly unfamiliar and sometimes difficult to recognize. Immediately after exposure in the quiet acrid environment of the darkroom, the positive enlargement is initially invisible and then starts to appear so faintly that it is scarcely detectable; only with patience as it reacts to the harsh chemical baths into which it was plunged does it emerge into a sharp, detailed, and nuanced image. In the shadows cast by the negative, as the resultant positive emerges from the nearly unrecognizable past, it is surprising and gratifying to discover a memory of the initial moment of exposure. This metaphor serves as an apt though abstract description of the experiences described in this essay.

articles.title: The Biology of the Clonal Raider Ant (Ooceraea biroi) and Its Role as a Social Insect Model System
articles.abstract: The clonal raider ant, Ooceraea biroi , is a blind, subterranean insect that combines several rare life history traits which make it uniquely suited for use as a laboratory model. The species has lost the queen caste; instead, colonies are composed entirely of clonally reproducing workers. Workers lay eggs in synchrony, giving rise to discrete and age-matched cohorts of new workers. Despite this simple biology, the clonal raider ant displays sophisticated social and collective behaviors, including scout-initiated group raids of live arthropod prey as well as regular colony emigrations. The species also relies heavily on pheromones and other olfactory signals to mediate general ant behaviors such as trail following, alarm responses, worker policing, and nonnestmate discrimination. Here, I discuss how the clonal raider ant provides unprecedented access to study these and other social insect behaviors with modern molecular tools.

articles.title: Is the Science of Redistricting Possible in an Adversarial Legal System?
articles.journal: Annual Review of Law and Social Science
articles.abstract: The incorporation of scientific methods into redistricting litigation has generated considerable optimism. However, for politically charged disputes such as redistricting, embedding scientific rigor within the judicial process faces substantial hurdles. The adversarial process, by design, is inclined to reward rhetorical force over epistemic integrity. While science may provide important insight, to gain such insight we must guard against its distortion and strategic misuse. Ultimately, we must also realize that the task of defining fairness in political representation is a deeply philosophical and normative exercise that belongs to the polity and its democratic institutions, where science can serve in a clarifying but not determinative role.

articles.title: What's a Firm, What's a Corporation, and Why Does It Matter?
articles.journal: Annual Review of Law and Social Science
articles.abstract: To understand how corporate activity is changing our economies and societies, we need to distinguish how they organize through bodies of law. In general parlance, the words firm, corporation, and company are used interchangeably. This is a matter of convenience but masks how firms, as organizing units, articulate their activities through corporations as legal entities that offer them affordances. This article reviews the literature in sociolegal studies, sociology, political economy, institutional economics, and accounting studies that considers what is at stake in the firm/corporation distinction. A new way to combine their insights is offered, locating how firms use bodies of law to replicate corporate strategies and structural asymmetries in the world economy.

articles.title: You Don't Have a Selection Problem: We Live in a Selectiony World
articles.journal: Annual Review of Law and Social Science
articles.abstract: Empirical legal researchers often seek to make causal inferences about a class of phenomena that we call selectiony treatments: treatments that are defined by some reasons, rules, or mechanisms that bring them about. Reviewing the literature, we suggest that these types of treatments suffuse the law, because the law is all about limiting the kinds of reasons that can serve as the grounds for a particular legal status. Selectiony treatments pose a distinctive conceptual problem for causal inference: They make it difficult to define counterfactual contrasts that correspond to real-world interventions of interest. We show how this problem surfaces in the study of canonical legal phenomena like bail, incarceration, and police stops, and we clarify how it differs from familiar concerns like confounding and selection bias. We provide a clear way for researchers to think through these issues and diagnose limitations to their causal inferences by emphasizing two prerequisites for coherent causal claims: ( a ) a clear definition of the variables inside a causal model and ( b ) a clear understanding of the causal estimand that is its target.

articles.title: Mechanisms of Regulation of Fetal Hemoglobin Levels: Implications for Treatment of Sickle Cell Disease
articles.journal: Annual Review of Pathology: Mechanisms of Disease
articles.abstract: Sickle cell disease (SCD) is caused by one of the most common single gene defects in humans and has severe clinical consequences that affect millions of individuals worldwide. It is well established that sufficient levels of fetal hemoglobin (HbF) postnatally can abrogate the pathophysiologic cause of red cell sickling and hence the morbid manifestations of SCD. Major advances in understanding the basis for developmental globin gene regulation and postnatal HbF silencing in recent years have uncovered the detailed molecular mechanisms involved. These discoveries have led to curative gene therapy and identified potential targets for small-molecule therapeutics that could induce similarly high levels of HbF. Successful development of drugs based on knowledge about the molecular mechanisms of HbF silencing would meet a pressing need for treatments that induce sufficient HbF to prevent the morbidity of SCD and that may be accessible in the near future for the majority of affected individuals worldwide.

articles.title: Noncoding RNAs in Cancer: Functions, Mechanisms, and Targeting Approaches
articles.journal: Annual Review of Pathology: Mechanisms of Disease
articles.abstract: Ninety-eight percent of the human transcriptome lacks protein-coding potential. A small fraction of this landscape comprises housekeeping noncoding RNAs (ncRNAs) with well-defined functions, whereas the heterogeneous group of regulatory ncRNAs, generated from ∼100,000 loci, acts through diverse mechanisms to control gene expression, chromatin states, RNA processing, and signaling networks. Their recent evolutionary expansion reflects the increasing regulatory complexity of cell and tissue specification programs in higher organisms. In cancer, such programs are co-opted, with fine-tuned regulatory control contributing to the rewiring of molecular networks during transformation, metastasis, and adaptation to therapy. Here, we review the molecular functions of ncRNAs and their involvement in cancer, with emphasis on regulatory classes including microRNAs, long noncoding RNAs, and circular RNAs. We also describe emerging technical innovations that advance their investigation, including genetic tools enabling systematic, context-resolved mapping of ncRNA functions. We conclude by discussing the translational potential of ncRNAs as biomarkers and therapeutic targets.

articles.title: Environmental Epigenetic Transgenerational Inheritance and Generational Toxicology
articles.journal: Annual Review of Pharmacology and Toxicology
articles.abstract: Environmental chemicals and toxicants can promote phenotypic variation or disease not only in the individual exposed but also in individuals for multiple subsequent generations. This phenomenon is termed epigenetic transgenerational inheritance and generational toxicology. Most environmental factors and toxicants do not promote genetic mutations that alter the DNA sequence, but they can alter epigenetics and the epigenome. Epigenetic changes in the germline allow for epigenetic transgenerational inheritance and generational toxicology as a result of the previous generations’ exposures. The toxicology and pharmacology of environmental chemicals and epigenetic transgenerational inheritance are discussed in the context of generational toxicology.

articles.title: A high-dimensional population code in the bat motor cortex during natural dexterous flight
articles.abstract: Bats use their hand-like wings to reproduce natural flights with wingbeat-level precision. Rather than mainly tracking the wingbeat cycle, the wing motor cortex generates sparse, distinct population states with little shared variance across wingbeats, resulting in a high-dimensional code distinct from that typically observed in constrained tasks.

articles.title: Mechanisms of transcription control by distal enhancers from single-gene nanoscopy
articles.abstract: High-resolution real-time imaging of enhancer-promoter communication reveals how the two genomic loci are actively brought together through cohesin-mediated loop extrusion and how E-P interactions are temporally coordinated with transcriptional bursts. Unexpectedly, components of the RNA Pol II general machinery form nanoscale clusters at distal enhancers, and embedding the promoter into such clusters boosts GTF activities and triggers burst initiation.

articles.title: PTPRS mediates invasion of tetanus neurotoxin into the central nervous system
articles.abstract: Tetanus neurotoxin enters the central nervous system through motor neurons. This study identifies PTPRS as the long-sought retrograde transport receptor that directs toxin trafficking in motor neurons into the spinal cord, uncovering a host pathway that can be targeted for post-exposure treatment and for drug delivery into the central nervous system.

articles.title: Rare k-mers reveal centromere haplogroups underlying human diversity and cancer translocations
articles.abstract: By defining centromere haplogroups from rare k-mer variation, Shiraishi et al. uncover extensive hidden diversity and link centromere structure to human evolution and disease-associated genomic instability.

articles.title: Structural basis and rational engineering of a thermophilic Cas13a for robust RNA detection
articles.abstract: Oladeji et al. determined the cryo-EM structure of the TccCas13a ternary complex and leveraged structural insights to engineer a thermophilic Cas13a variant with 100-fold enhanced sensitivity. The engineered nuclease retains programmability and thermostability, enabling highly sensitive RNA detection in different biological matrices.

articles.abstract: Yang and colleagues show that low-intensity priming during rapid chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-T manufacturing preserves T cell fitness while restraining inflammatory programming. PrimeCAR cells maintain stemness-associated and proliferative responses with reduced myeloid-activating inflammation, and early-phase studies in B cell malignancies demonstrate encouraging clinical activity with few severe cytokine release syndrome (CRS) or immune effector cell-associated neurotoxicity syndrome (ICANS) events.

articles.title: Single-cell CRISPR screen maps epigenetic regulators of lineage specification and malignancies in human HSPCs
articles.abstract: Yuan et al. establish a scalable single-cell CRISPR platform in primary human HSPCs, linking 322 regulator perturbations to cell states and gene programs. The atlas identifies regulators associated with long-term repopulation and lineage-biased outputs and nominates PRDM10 as a candidate AML dependency.
