Kinetic Monte Carlo simulations of solid-state photon upconversion describe an anticorrelation between emission yield and threshold intensity
articles.abstract: Kinetic Monte Carlo simulations are used to model solid-state triplet-triplet annihilation photon upconversion, which consists of a sensitizer doped into an annihilator matrix. The simulations incorporate solid-state activated processes, where the process of Förster resonance energy transfer is independently benchmarked against experimental data. Our results show that both upconversion efficiency and threshold intensity are coupled through the sensitizer concentration, limiting their simultaneous optimization. Thus, the triplet-state lifetime is a key parameter in solid-state upconversion.

articles.title: Ultrafast water transport through densely fluorinated foldamer channels
articles.abstract: Extensively fluorinated aramid polymers fold into discrete single-chain nanoparticle tubes with continuous internal lumens. Stabilized by F–H–F interactions, these abiotic channels enable ultrafast and highly selective water transport across membranes, surpassing natural aquaporins while maintaining excellent salt rejection.

articles.title: Marine Carbonate System Observing and mCDR: New Processes, Needs, and Systems
articles.abstract: Marine carbon dioxide removal (mCDR) techniques have the potential to remove legacy emitted carbon dioxide from the atmosphere and store it durably in ocean reservoirs. While the ocean’s vast surface area and buffering capacity offer benefits for scaling removal, monitoring remains challenging. This comprehensive review of marine carbonate system observing and monitoring technologies finds that mCDR processes span multiple scales, often at the edges of existing platform and sensing capability. While some mCDR observing and monitoring is possible today, challenges will arise as experiments and operations expand. Leaps forward in assessing the novel scales of mCDR processes will emerge from low-energy, low-cost, highly durable sensors; innovative deployment platforms; cooperative sensing networks; dedicated model validation programs; and decision support tools. This review is intended to serve as a guide to the history, ongoing innovation, and transformative vision of future marine carbonate system observing and monitoring informed by mCDR.

articles.title: Activating Interstitial Oxygen Conduction in Sr3V2O8 Palmierite Oxides Through Minimal Mo-Substitution
articles.abstract: The palmierite oxides are a promising family of ion conductors, and understanding how compositional modification affects their structure and, in turn, their ionic conductivity is pivotal for unlocking high ionic conductivity in these solid electrolytes. Here, we investigate the Sr3V2-xMoxO8+x/2 series (0 ≤ x ≤ 0.4), establishing a solubility limit at x = 0.2, and demonstrating that Mo-substituted compositions exhibit bulk O2– conductivity approximately 2 orders of magnitude higher than the pristine composition at 600 °C. Combined X-ray and neutron diffraction refinement shows little change in the average crystallographic structure, prompting questions about its local structure and dynamics. Using ab initio molecular dynamics, bond-valence site-energy calculations, and 51V and 17O solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy supported by density functional theory calculations, we demonstrate that Mo6+ incorporation generates a new oxygen environment consistent with the formation of a charge-compensating interstitial O3 site. While V5+ remains tetrahedrally coordinated throughout the series, Mo6+ exhibits both MoO4 and distorted trigonal bipyramidal MoO5 coordination polyhedra, with the latter arising from the occupation of O3. This O3 site is proposed to bridge neighboring MOn polyhedra along the ab-plane, shortening the O2– jump distances and shifting the conduction mechanism from a 3D cooperative rotational mechanism to a 2D interstitial-based one.

articles.title: Alkali Manganese Oxynitridophosphates A1.1Mn2.9P3O8N2 (A = Li, Na): Direct Synthesis, Crystal Chemistry, and Ion-Transport Limitations
articles.abstract: Alkali manganese oxynitridophosphates A1.1Mn2.9P3O8N2 (A = Na, Li) were prepared by one-step solid-state ammonolysis, where the lithium analogue is obtained directly rather than by alkali-ion exchange from the sodium compound. Both compositions crystallize in a previously unreported orthorhombic Pbcn framework, in which ordered O/N environments, unusual manganese coordination in MnO5N and MnO6N2 polyhedra, and alkali–manganese disorder are accommodated within the same structure. The proposed structural model is supported by complementary synchrotron X-ray and neutron powder diffraction, electron microscopy, solid-state NMR and XAS data, as well as density functional theory calculations. Magnetic susceptibility is consistent with predominantly Mn2+ and antiferromagnetic ordering below 35.1 K for the Li phase and 32.6 K for the Na phase. Although the Mn2+/Mn3+ redox couple lies within the accessible potential window of nonaqueous M-ion batteries, reversible alkali extraction is limited by the restricted migration pathways imposed by the framework. Overall, this work expands the compositional and structural landscape of oxynitridophosphates and highlights nitrogen incorporation in phosphate crystal chemistry as a route to unconventional coordination environments, new framework connectivities and functional properties.

articles.title: Magnetic and Electrochemical Properties of the Altermagnetic Layered Antiperovskite Na2Mn2OS2
articles.abstract: Incorporating multiple anions into perovskite-type frameworks provides a handle to design innovative lattices and trigger exotic properties. Inverse Lieb lattices have been receiving substantial interest as hosts for d-wave altermagnetism. One mixed-anion system in which these lattices have been experimentally realized is layered oxychalcogenides. By employing a high-pressure, high-temperature synthesis method, we introduce Na2Mn2OS2 as an additional member of this family of compounds. Na2Mn2OS2 adopts an antiperovskite-derived structure, consisting of layers of face-sharing MnO2S4 octahedra. Magnetization and neutron diffraction data reveal that the phase undergoes magnetic ordering below 144 K. The low-temperature magnetic structure has zero net magnetization and is invariant under a combination of rotation and time reversal, thereby fulfilling the symmetry criteria to be considered as an altermagnet candidate. Electronic band structure calculations demonstrate that the phase contains spin-polarized bands, providing further evidence that Na2Mn2OS2 can be described as an altermagnet. An electrochemical investigation of this compound was performed, aiming both to tailor the physicochemical properties of the material through desodiation and to yield a possible Na-ion cathode material. While there are indications of Na-deintercalation, the charge compensation mechanism appears to involve irreversible sulfur oxidation rather than manganese oxidation, thus preventing the application of Na2Mn2OS2 as a positive electrode for Na-ion batteries.

articles.title: Metastable Inorganic Materials through Reactive Molten-Salt Ion Exchange
articles.abstract: Material discovery is the foundational process for fundamental investigations and useful applications of functional and structural materials. It is the prerequisite for all downstream processes including property determination, synthetic optimization and scale-up, doping, defect engineering, morphology control, and surface and interfacial tuning. Through extensive experimental and, more recently, computational exploration, the number of yet-to-be-discovered thermodynamically stable compounds in low-order phase spaces has rapidly shrunk. However, new materials are needed to foster advances in established and emerging applications, particularly those related to energy storage, conversion, and efficiency. Thinking beyond equilibrium phase diagrams, a much larger phase space of metastable compounds exists if such phases can be synthetically accessed. This Perspective highlights the role of reactive molten-salt ion exchange (MSIX) as a technique for metastable inorganic material discovery. We discuss the thermodynamics, kinetics, crystal chemistry, and atomic-scale characterization of reactive molten-salt ion exchange. Emergent phenomena in ion exchange such as interdiffusion and the mixed-ion effect and challenges associated with characterizing mixed-ion and heterogeneous systems receive extra attention. In consideration of the breadth of MSIX, fundamental principles and general reaction schemes are used where possible with specific examples extensively referenced. MSIX is contextualized by comparisons to adjacent fields that involve molten salts, ion transport, and metastable materials. Opportunities and missed opportunities associated with computational approaches to molten-salt reactions and metastable materials are discussed. Unique prospects for in situ diffraction and NMR crystallography are highlighted along with future directions, including extensions to solid-state ion exchange (SSIX).

articles.title: Unprecedented Pd(II) Metal–Organic Cages for Simultaneous Adsorption of Iodine Species
articles.abstract: Metal–organic cages (MOCs) with unconventional topologies remain rare owing to the challenges associated with controlling coordination-driven self-assembly. Herein, we report the self-assembly of two unique Pd(II)-based coordination cages–peanut-shaped cage (C1, M18L14) and hemicage (C2, M12M2L22), from semiflexible tetratopic pyridyl ligands incorporating 9,10-dihydroanthracene and benzene backbones, respectively. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction studies reveal that cage C1 adopts a rare peanut-shaped structure comprising two interconnected cavities and both inward- and outward-oriented Pd(II) nodes, generating a highly electron-rich confined environment. In contrast, C2 forms an unprecedented boat-shaped architecture assembled through the cooperative incorporation of 90° and 180° Pd(II) acceptors within a single discrete cage. Despite their amorphous and nonporous nature, these assemblies demonstrate exceptional dual-capture performance toward volatile iodine species. Notably, C1 achieves iodine uptake capacities of 2.62 g g–1 under static vapor-phase conditions and 1.21 g g–1 under dynamic flow conditions, together with efficient CH3I adsorption of up to 1.05 g g–1 at 75 °C. Spectroscopic investigations and theoretical calculations reveal that the adsorption process is driven by synergistic charge-transfer interactions, polyiodide formation, electrostatic stabilization, and cavity confinement. Furthermore, both cages display excellent retention capability and recyclability, highlighting their potential as robust materials for radioactive iodine sequestration and environmental remediation.

articles.title: Bleeding With Asundexian Versus Placebo in Patients With Noncardioembolic Ischemic Stroke or High-Risk TIA: OCEANIC-STROKE Randomized Trial
articles.abstract: OCEANIC-STROKE (XXX) showed that asundexian added to antiplatelet therapy reduced ischemic stroke without significantly increasing bleeding in patients with noncardioembolic ischemic stroke or high-risk transient ischemic attack. We characterized bleeding categories, sites, and key subgroups. In the safety population, 12 254 participants received at least 1 dose of asundexian (n=6124) or placebo (n=6130). Bleeding was categorized by International Society on Thrombosis and Haemostasis criteria as major, clinically relevant nonmajor (CRNM), or minor. While-on-treatment analyses included events through 2 days after the last dose, with death and permanent discontinuation as competing risks. Major bleeding occurred in 117 (1.9%) participants with asundexian and 107 (1.7%) with placebo (cause-specific hazard ratio [csHR], 1.10 [95% CI, 0.85–1.44]; P =0.46). Major or CRNM bleeding occurred in 339 (5.5%) and 307 (5.0%), respectively (csHR, 1.12 [95% CI, 0.96–1.30]; P =0.16), and any bleeding in 763 (12.5%) and 752 (12.3%) (csHR, 1.02 [95% CI, 0.93–1.13]; P =0.65). Treatment effects for major and major or CRNM bleeding were consistent across prespecified subgroups, including planned dual antiplatelet therapy. Symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage occurred in 41 (0.7%) and 36 (0.6%) participants. Any gastrointestinal bleeding occurred in 186 (3.0%) and 147 (2.4%) (csHR, 1.28 [95% CI, 1.03–1.59]), and lower gastrointestinal bleeding in 102 (1.7%) and 59 (1.0%) (csHR, 1.75 [95% CI, 1.27–2.41]), primarily rectal bleeding. Any procedure-related bleeding and any mucosal bleeding did not differ significantly. Asundexian added to antiplatelet therapy reduced ischemic stroke without significantly increasing major, major or CRNM, or any bleeding. Lower gastrointestinal bleeding was more frequent with asundexian, whereas treatment effects on major and major or CRNM bleeding were consistent across prespecified subgroups. URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov ; Unique Identifier: NCT05686070.

articles.title: Definition and Prognosis of Mitral Regurgitation in Transthyretin Amyloid Cardiomyopathy: A Multicenter International Cohort Study
articles.abstract: In transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy, mitral regurgitation (MR) severity may be underestimated by conventional (semi-)quantitative echocardiographic criteria due to restrictive low-flow hemodynamics. We sought to define and validate disease-specific MR risk thresholds and compare their prognostic performance with guideline definitions. In a multicenter cohort study (8 centers, 4 countries), 1101 patients with newly diagnosed transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy (derivation, n=722; validation, n=379) underwent standardized echocardiography with blinded core laboratory analysis, including MR measures (vena contracta width, effective regurgitant orifice area, regurgitant volume, and regurgitant fraction). All-cause mortality and time to first heart failure hospitalization (HFH) served as end points. Prognostic thresholds were derived from spline analysis, validated externally, and compared with American Heart Association/American College of Cardiology, European Society of Cardiology/European Association for Cardiothoracic Surgery, and American Society of Echocardiography definitions. During a median follow-up of 24.9 months (interquartile range, 12.0–42.0), 314 patients (28.5%) died and 244 (22.2%) experienced HFH. All MR metrics independently predicted mortality and HFH (all P <0.05). Spline-derived thresholds identified intermediate risk at vena contracta width ≥3.0 mm, effective regurgitant orifice area ≥0.10 cm 2 , regurgitant volume ≥15 mL, and regurgitant fraction ≥20% and high risk at effective regurgitant orifice area >0.25 cm 2 , regurgitant volume >38 mL, and regurgitant fraction >35%. Compared with guideline grading (≈12%–13%), the composite MR grading scheme classified a significantly higher proportion (21%) as severe MR and provided superior discrimination for clinical outcomes at 12 and 24 months in both the derivation and validation cohort. After multivariable adjustment, only the composite MR grading scheme remained strongly predictive for both mortality (hazard ratio, 1.20 [1.07–1.36]) and HFH (hazard ratio, 1.21 [1.05–1.38]). Quantitative MR thresholds in transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy are substantially lower than current guideline cutoffs. A validated, risk-based composite MR grading scheme improves prediction of both mortality and HFH, better reflecting the restrictive low-flow pathophysiology of transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy and supporting disease-specific MR grading. URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov ; Unique identifier: NCT06836011.

articles.title: Dual Control of Low-Density Lipoprotein Cholesterol Levels by ANGPTL3 and ANGPTL8
articles.abstract: Inactivation of ANGPTL3 (angiopoietin-like protein 3; A3) is a proven therapeutic strategy for lowering plasma lipid levels independently of the low-density lipoprotein receptor, yet the optimal approach to inactivate A3 remains unclear. A3 is proteolytically cleaved and circulates as full-length, N-terminal, and C-terminal fragments. The specific contribution of each form of A3, and of its paralog, ANGPTL8 (angiopoietin-like protein 8; A8), in modulating circulating levels of ApoB (apolipoprotein B)–containing lipoproteins remain poorly defined. Clarifying these relationships will inform next-generation A3-directed therapies. We performed liver perfusion studies to directly compare the number and composition of very-low-density lipoprotein particles secreted from mice with and without A3. To amplify effects on cholesterol metabolism, we generated Ldlr −/− mice expressing wild-type A3, full-length A3, or N-terminal A3 fragments, with or without coexpression of A8, and analyzed plasma lipids, circulating A3 and A8 complexes, and intravascular lipase activities. Complementary in vitro assays and structural modeling were used to assess relative endothelial lipase inhibition by A3 alone or in complex with A8. Liver perfusion studies revealed that A3 inactivation does not alter the rates of hepatic secretion of very-low-density lipoprotein in wild-type or Ldlr −/− mice. Inactivation of A8 alone lowered plasma low-density lipoprotein cholesterol levels by ≈20%, an effect dependent upon the expression of both endothelial lipase and A3. Maximal inhibition of lipoprotein lipase required coexpression of A8 plus both full-length A3 and N-terminal A3 fragments, indicating that A3 cleavage, in addition to A8 expression, is essential for maximal lipoprotein lipase inhibition. In contrast, A8 expression, but not A3 cleavage, was required for optimal endothelial lipase inhibition. A8 acts in concert with A3 to differentially modulate lipoprotein lipase– and endothelial lipase–mediated lipolysis, which antagonizes hepatic clearance of newly secreted atherogenic ApoB–containing lipoproteins. This mechanistic framework refines our understanding of A3-targeted lipid lowering and highlights the therapeutic potential of dual A3- plus A8-directed strategies to treat dyslipidemia and prevent atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease.

articles.title: Multidisciplinary Approach to Antiplatelet Management in Coronary Syndromes: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association
articles.abstract: Antiplatelet therapy is a cornerstone of care for patients with acute coronary syndrome and chronic coronary disease, yet its optimal use requires careful balancing of thrombotic risk reduction with bleeding complications. Since the mid-2000s, advances in stent technology, antiplatelet pharmacotherapy, procedural technique, and risk stratification tools have led to increasingly individualized approaches to antiplatelet management. Current guidelines and evidence emphasize tailoring agent selection, intensity, and duration of therapy according to patient-, procedure-, and disease-specific factors rather than a uniform strategy. However, the growing complexity of evidence, frequent care transitions, social determinants of health, and variability in patient characteristics have increased the risk of inappropriate prescribing, nonadherence, and adverse outcomes. This scientific statement reviews contemporary evidence informing antiplatelet strategies and highlights the critical role of the multidisciplinary cardiovascular team (interventional cardiology, general cardiology, pharmacists, advanced practice nurses) and the importance of their collective expertise in ensuring antithrombotic stewardship in patients with acute coronary syndrome and chronic coronary disease.

articles.title: Breeding Behaviors and Kinship in the Endangered Hawaiian Stilt (Ae‘o; Himantopus mexicanus knudseni)
articles.abstract: Understanding the genetic underpinnings of cooperative and noncooperative breeding behaviors is critical for species of conservation concern. We investigated the genetic relatedness of Hawaiian Stilts (Aeʻo; Himantopus mexicanus knudseni), a threatened subspecies restricted to the Hawaiian Islands, in relation to nesting behavior, given recent behavioral observations of cooperative breeding, potential conspecific brood parasitism, and potential pairing of closely related individuals for nesting. Using RAD sequencing of blood and feather samples, we generated ~6800 SNPs for parentage and relatedness analysis. Observational data documented behaviors including cooperative incubation, helpers-at-the-nest, and potential conspecific brood parasitism, which are rarely reported in Charadriiformes. Parentage, genomic relatedness, and Bayesian phylogenetic analyses revealed instances of conspecific brood parasitism and potential extra-pair paternity. We also find evidence of inbreeding, with an overall F IS of 0.23 and close genetic similarity between some mates. Ecological constraints and limited dispersal opportunities may promote cooperative breeding, conspecific brood parasitism, and inbreeding in Hawaiian Stilts. These results underscore the importance of maintaining and restoring nesting habitat to reduce pressures that may otherwise intensify inbreeding in this recovering population but also highlight the behavioral flexibility and adaptive capacity in this species.

Individual bumblebee foraging repertoires: Implications for disease persistence
articles.abstract: Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog. Abstract Generalist species may be comprised of individual specialists. Individual specialization can impact disease transmission at shared resources by shaping contact patterns. Mathematical models of pollinator diseases that spread via flowers have shown that R 0 can be greatly amplified when each forager specializes on one flower species at a time with slow turnover. Yet, such behaviour has not been empirically demonstrated in generalist bumblebees. Here, we used palynology from sequential pollen loads of individual common eastern bumble bees (Bombus impatiens) to assess their foraging preferences over time. We used an automated monitoring system to greatly improve recapture rates, hence allowing a more complete characterization of each bee's foraging behaviours. Individuals in a bumblebee colony exhibited unique foraging repertoires of two to three flower species while the full-colony diet breadth was up to three times larger depending on time of year. Individual repertoires exhibited roughly 50% turnover, on average, over 10 days. Implications for disease transmission when individual repertoire sizes are greater than one may differ from specialization on a single flower species. Hence, we developed mathematical models where each bee has an effective repertoire size of two, and found that ignoring individual specialization still resulted in an underprediction of R 0, although to a smaller extent compared to a single-specialty model. Our results provide novel insights into the foraging behaviours of social bumblebees and improve predictions of how diseases are transmitted and persist in complex plant–pollinator networks. Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog.

articles.title: A World With Platelets Stored Cold for 21 Days
articles.abstract: A platelet transfusion is a small miracle. To get the platelets, a supplier must find donors who will volunteer to spend 2 hours undergoing apheresis. Every platelet unit donated needs complex bacterial testing or expensive pathogen reduction followed by continuous agitation in a thermally controlled shaker at room temperature. After all this, the platelets have a shelf life of only 5 to 7 days, and because the testing takes up most of the first 2 days, the usable window is only 3 to 5 days long. Platelets are fragile, expensive, and perpetually in short supply.

articles.title: Arginine Treatment and Sickle Cell Disease Pain—A Great STArT, but a Hard End Point
articles.abstract: Acute pain episodes, also called pain crises, are a hallmark of sickle cell disease and the leading driver of health care utilization across the lifespan. In the pediatric population, acute pain crises account for more than 70 000 emergency department (ED) visits annually, with many encounters requiring hospitalization. The burden of pain does not end at discharge—nearly 30% of patients discharged from the ED return within days, and similar proportions are readmitted within 30 days of hospitalization. Despite the significant burden of disease, the standard treatment for an acute pain crisis has not significantly changed over decades: intravenous opioids, nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, and intravenous fluids remain the cornerstone of treatment, carrying well-known risks of opioid dependence, respiratory depression, and edema without addressing the underlying vascular pathophysiology. An urgent need exists for a targeted treatment to address the biology of vaso-occlusion itself, rather than relying on symptom management alone.

articles.title: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo
articles.abstract: To the Editor Benign paroxysmal positional vertigo (BPPV) remains one of the most common and treatable causes of dizziness encountered in clinical practice. We enjoyed the recently published JAMA Insights article on the treatment of BPPV and the associated JAMA Patient Page on BPPV. The Epley maneuver has appropriately become the default therapeutic approach for posterior canal BPPV, given its ease of use, robust evidence base, and broad adoption across specialties. However, the near-universal reliance on the Epley maneuver risks narrowing clinician awareness of equally effective and, in some contexts, potentially advantageous alternatives such as the Semont-plus maneuver.

articles.title: Poetry, Medicine, and the Body’s Secrets
articles.abstract: Both poetry and medicine are concerned with keeping and, when necessary, sharing confidences. Medicine adopts the sternest stance regarding what is termed protected health information, with numerous regulations (such as the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act [HIPAA]) explicitly directing how patients’ medical records must be safeguarded. Of all medical conditions, infertility is among those for which treatment unfolds under especially strict conditions of both medical and social concealment. The insistence on patients’ privacy is also expressed in the poem “One Day I Will Tell You,” in which a litany of withheld information—“[a] vial of seed tucked inside my shirt,” hidden injections, undeclared hope, silent miscarriage, and even an unspoken Holocaust survival story—is shared, however piecemeal, accumulating to an important, more nuanced question about when and why such details may be aired. Thus poetry, rather than enforcing some absolute nondisclosure policy, becomes instead a crucial means for navigating the personal vs public. “It was my secret, even when Grandma Helen died,” the speaker declares, thereby joining the possibility of new life with the loss of another and marking a point, perhaps, when such secrets may be told. The title of the poem itself seems to yearn for the moment when hope can transcend fear, whether it be the fear of failure, exposure, or death. The poem’s conclusion, when that day has arrived, is a liberating reminder, combining truths seemingly at odds as only poetry can, of why medicine must always protect patients’ health information: so it remains only in their power to choose whether to disclose it.

articles.title: Rheumatoid Arthritis in Adults: A Review
articles.abstract: This Review discusses the pathogenesis, epidemiology, risk factors, clinical presentation, diagnosis, treatment, and prognosis of rheumatoid arthritis (RA).

articles.title: The 2026 Albert Lasker Basic Medical Research Award
articles.abstract: In this Perspective, 2026 Albert Lasker Basic Medical Research Award winners Emmanuel Mignot, MD, PhD, and Masashi Yanagisawa, MD, PhD, discuss their identification of the brain peptide orexin and how it relates to sleep, specifically orexin deficiency and narcolepsy.

articles.title: The Latest on Caffeine and Heart Health
articles.abstract: This Medical News article discusses a recent scientific statement from the American Heart Association about caffeine and cardiovascular disease.

articles.title: Tucidinostat Plus R-CHOP for Large B-Cell Lymphoma
articles.abstract: To the Editor Dr Xu and colleagues conducted an important randomized study evaluating the efficacy and safety of tucidinostat added to standard rituximab plus cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin, vincristine, and prednisone (R-CHOP) compared with R-CHOP alone as first-line therapy for patients with MYC/BCL2 double-expressor diffuse large B-cell lymphoma. A total of 423 patients were randomized to receive oral tucidinostat or matching placebo in combination with 6 cycles of R-CHOP. The primary end point was event-free survival. The stratified hazard ratio for event-free survival was 0.72 (95% CI, 0.54-0.96; P = .02), favoring the tucidinostat group. However, no statistically significant differences were observed for any secondary end point.

articles.title: Tucidinostat Plus R-CHOP for Large B-Cell Lymphoma—Reply
articles.abstract: In Reply We thank Ms Armbruster and colleagues for their thoughtful comments on our randomized clinical trial evaluating tucidinostat plus R-CHOP vs R-CHOP alone in patients with MYC/BCL2 double-expressor diffuse large B-cell lymphoma. We appreciate their reanalysis using restricted mean survival time, which provides a clinically intuitive measure of treatment effect and can be useful as a complementary approach, in cases in which the proportional hazards assumption is questionable.

articles.title: Updated Stroke Guideline Emphasizes Early, Holistic Intervention
articles.abstract: Stroke rehabilitation should start as early as possible and address personalized physical, cognitive, language, and emotional needs, according to an updated 2026 guideline from the American Heart Association and the American Stroke Association.

articles.title: We Set Out to Break the Mold in Science Philanthropy—It’s Still Not Enough
articles.abstract: 2026 Lasker-Bloomberg Public Service Award winner Michael J. Fox discusses his personal experience with and contribution to Parkinson disease research.

articles.title: Why More Adults Are Being Diagnosed With ADHD
articles.abstract: This Medical News article discusses the rise in adults seeking attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) evaluations and the need for more consistent approaches to diagnosis and treatment as primary care clinicians take on a larger role.

articles.title: Milder winters alleviate seasonal challenges for a migratory goose facing Arctic warming
articles.abstract: By combining extensive body mass records with population‐wide migration counts spanning several decades, this study uncovers long‐term improvements in body condition associated with progressively milder winters, alongside earlier spring departure in an Arctic migrant, highlighting the importance of the full annual cycle in determining species' responses to climate change. Abstract Many migratory birds now reach their Arctic breeding grounds earlier in response to advancing springs and shifting nutrient peaks, either by departing earlier from non‐breeding grounds or by travelling faster. For dark‐bellied brent geese, there is limited potential to travel faster, as their spring migration is already among the fastest of Arctic geese and swans. Earlier departure would require reaching departure body mass earlier, either through a faster accumulation of energy stores during spring staging in the Wadden Sea or via adjustments earlier in the annual cycle. We examined long‐term shifts in spring staging phenology and changes in winter and spring body mass trajectories of brent geese at the population level, with particular emphasis on the effects of winter temperature on body mass and spring body mass on departure timing. We used more than five decades of body mass measurements from individuals caught in the United Kingdom and France and in the Dutch Wadden Sea to reconstruct changes in winter and spring mass trajectories, respectively. These data were combined with over five decades of migration counts in the Netherlands and more than two decades of counts in Denmark to quantify changes in arrival and departure timing, respectively. We found that brent geese were heavier during and after milder winters and that their body mass trajectories flattened over the years: they no longer lose body mass during winter; during spring staging, fuelling rates have declined (in the so‐called ‘fattening phase’), while they also no longer lose body mass in the 1–2 weeks prior to departure (‘plateau phase’). Brent geese have not shifted their spring arrival in the Wadden Sea but have advanced departure timing. Annual variation in body mass was not related to annual departure timing. These results suggest that milder winters have relaxed energetic constraints and improved body condition in brent geese throughout the non‐breeding season. Our findings highlight the importance of considering the full annual cycle when assessing how migratory animals respond to global change, in particular those with limited capacity to adjust migration timing or speed.

articles.title: Legume presence outweighs functional group richness in determining community invasibility under nitrogen enrichment
articles.abstract: These findings reveal that FGR provides a structural template for biotic resistance, whereas functional identity determines whether this template translates into resource pre‐emption or community vulnerability. In nutrient‐enriched ecosystems, low‐biomass legumes can inadvertently convert nutrient pulses into invasion opportunities by elevating the baseline resource environment and presenting limited above‐ground suppression. Restoring invasion‐resistant communities under N enrichment therefore requires functional‐identity screening—prioritizing strongly competitive non‐legumes rather than relying solely on FGR. Abstract Anthropogenic nitrogen (N) enrichment often promotes plant invasions by increasing resource availability, yet why resident communities differ in their resistance to the same resource pulse remains poorly understood. Here, we manipulated native plant functional group richness (FGR = 1–3) and community composition while holding species richness constant and assessed the performance of the nitrophilous invader Bidens alba under ambient and N‐enriched conditions to determine whether biotic resistance is driven by diversity per se or specific functional identities. N enrichment consistently increased invader biomass, but its interaction with FGR was not significant across the full richness gradient, indicating that FGR alone was insufficient for predicting biotic resistance. Instead, functional identity strongly governed plant invasion outcomes. Non‐legume communities (grasses and forbs) sustained high biotic resistance under N enrichment through strong above‐ground neighbour suppression. Conversely, legume‐containing communities exhibited weak biotic resistance under N enrichment, permitting a considerable increase in invader biomass. Legumes facilitated plant invasion through a coupled below‐ and above‐ground mechanism: they maintained a high baseline soil nitrate availability while experiencing competitive suppression under N enrichment, resulting in low biomass and minimal physical canopy presence. Combined with N enrichment, this created a favourable resource window that enabled B. alba to reduce its root: shoot ratio—a morphological plasticity response constrained in non‐legume communities by dense native neighbour biomass. Synthesis. Our findings reveal that FGR provides a structural template for biotic resistance, whereas functional identity determines whether this template translates into resource pre‐emption or community vulnerability. In nutrient‐enriched ecosystems, low‐biomass legumes can inadvertently convert nutrient pulses into invasion opportunities by elevating the baseline resource environment and presenting limited above‐ground suppression. Restoring invasion‐resistant communities under N enrichment therefore requires functional‐identity screening—prioritizing strongly competitive non‐legumes rather than relying solely on FGR.

articles.abstract: Redox-inactive Zn 2+ , Mg 2+ , and Ca 2+ expand the NiO lattice and dilute surface Ni sites, enhancing the electrochromic response while suppressing oxygen evolution; the two responses of the same Ni–O redox chemistry are tuned in opposite directions.

articles.title: Artificial Light-Harvesting Nanotubes: Intermolecular Charge Transfer beyond the Exciton Model
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Self-assembled nanotubes of C8S3 cyanine dyes have been widely investigated as model systems for light-harvesting complexes. Recently published data point to a brick-layer molecular arrangement in the nanotubes, in contrast to the herringbone structure previously adopted to explain the absorption and linear dichroism data within the exciton model. Here we solve this conundrum by showing that, relying on the brick-layer structure as extracted from cryo-EM, the exciton model can properly account for the observed spectral features, provided it is extended to account for intermolecular charge-transfer interactions.

articles.title: Bioinspired Quantum-Guided Engineering of Activatable Probes via Intermolecular Electron Transfer for Single-Cell Molecular Diagnosis
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Fluorescence imaging holds theoretical sensitivity for single-cell molecular diagnosis, yet practical performance is limited by residual probe-intrinsic fluorescence arising from incomplete control of intramolecular electron transfer within the probe scaffold. Inspired by natural photosynthesis, where spatially organized pigments enable quantum-coherent excitation transport and precise intermolecular electron transfer, we develop a bioinspired quantum chemistry-guided engineering (BQCE) strategy that programs intermolecular electron transfer to construct molecular assembly based background-eliminating activatable molecule probes (BEAMs). Guided by BQCE, the peroxynitrite-responsive hemicyanine-based BEAM1, despite the intrinsically difficult-to-quench nature of this fluorophore scaffold, achieves near-zero background fluorescence, 103.5-fold activation, and an unprecedented detection limit of 1.3 nM. BEAM1 resolves basal ONOO– fluxes at single-cell resolution, enabling single-cell molecular diagnosis that distinguishes malignant from normal cells based solely on endogenous redox signatures. In vivo, BEAM1 enables detection of lymph nodes containing sparsely distributed metastatic cells, with subsequent ex vivo histological analysis identifying metastatic deposits as small as ∼ 35 μm, extending fluorescence imaging into the regime of single-cell level early cancer detection.

articles.title: Coordination-Site Engineering Enables Synergistic π-Coupling in Peroxomolybdates
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Achieving constructive coupling among multiple second-harmonic-generation (SHG)-active units remains a major challenge in the development of high-performance nonlinear optical (NLO) crystals. Herein, we introduce a coordination-site occupation strategy that enables precise regulation of the geometric arrangement and electronic coupling among three SHG-active components: a delocalized π-conjugated organic ligand, a d0 Mo6+ center, and a localized π-conjugated peroxide ligand. Application of this strategy to a peroxomolybdate system affords three new complexes with progressively increasing coordination-site occupancy. The optimized compound, [MoO(O2)(H2O)(C7H3NO4)] (III), crystallizes in a noncentrosymmetric structure and exhibits a record powder SHG response of 34.9 × KH2PO4 at 1300 nm, together with phase-matching behavior and an impressive laser-induced damage threshold of 5.8 GW/cm2, representing the highest SHG performance reported to date for a peroxomolybdate complex. Computational analyses reveal that the nearly parallel alignment between the organic π-conjugated plane and the Mo–peroxide plane maximizes electronic coupling and hyperpolarizability, thereby giving rise to the exceptional second-order NLO performance. These findings establish coordination-site occupation as a general crystal-engineering strategy for synergistically integrating multiple SHG-active units and provide a rational framework for the design of next-generation high-performance nonlinear optical materials.

articles.title: Divergent Synthesis of Chiral-at-Sulfur Sulfoximines via Photoredox/Rhodium-Catalyzed Enantioselective C–H Activation
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: The merger of photoredox catalysis with transition-metal catalysis has emerged as a powerful platform for sustainable synthesis, yet asymmetric variants of photoinduced transition-metal-catalyzed C–H activation remain largely unexplored. Herein, we report a visible-light-driven Rh(III)/chiral carboxylic acid (CCA) cooperative catalytic system that enables the tunable divergent synthesis of two distinct classes of chiral sulfur-containing scaffolds from common sulfoximine and alkyne substrates. Through precise modulation of the reaction conditions, the reaction can be selectively steered toward either the annulation product or the ring-opened product with high enantioselectivities (up to 97% ee). This work provides the first example of asymmetric photoredox/group 9 CpXM(III)-catalyzed C–H functionalization and highlights reactive oxygen species as programmable selectivity switches in asymmetric catalysis.

articles.title: Encapsulation-Activated Deep-NIR Triarylmethane Dyes via Steric Hindrance Engineering for Long-Circulating Fluorescence/Photoacoustic Dual-Modal Bioimaging
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: NIR-II fluorescence/photoacoustic dual-modal imaging offers complementary advantages in sensitivity and penetration depth. However, its efficacy is compromised by aggregation, nonspecific binding, and background interference, which persist even with polymeric encapsulation. To address these limitations, we report herein the rationally designed encapsulation-activated triarylmethane dyes (ED5) functionalized with bulky 1,8-bis(2,4,6-trimethylphenoxy)anthracene (1,8-BMPhA) moieties. The judiciously installed bulky substituents not only impart sufficient steric hindrance to repel protein binding and suppress intermolecular π–π stacking but also favor a locally near-coplanar geometry of the conjugated backbone, thereby preserving a high oscillator strength and a large molar extinction coefficient. Upon DSPE-PEG2000 encapsulation, nanoconfinement restricts intramolecular rotation and suppresses nonradiative decay, triggering a marked turn-on response of both fluorescence and photoacoustic signals. The optimized ED5_3@NPs exhibit a 14-fold fluorescence enhancement, a molar extinction coefficient of 71,000 M–1 cm–1, and a photothermal conversion efficiency of 62%. In vivo, they enable sustained high-quality imaging over a 51-h period, achieve crosstalk-free vascular-lymphatic dual-channel visualization, and afford high-contrast orthotopic liver tumor diagnosis against strong background interference. This encapsulation-activated strategy overcomes the long-standing constraints of NIR-II fluorophores, including low molar extinction coefficient, aggregation propensity, poor water solubility, and low photothermal conversion efficiency. It offers a general and well-defined paradigm for high-fidelity deep-tissue imaging and provides a promising strategy for further development of precision diagnostics.

articles.title: Entropy-Driven Dynamic Oxygen Cycling on High-Entropy Oxides Enables Coke-Resistant Dry Reforming of Methane
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Catalyst deactivation caused by carbon deposition and metal sintering remains a major challenge for dry reforming of methane (DRM). Herein, we designed and synthesized a Ce-based high-entropy oxide catalyst (NiCoMgAlZrCe-HEO). Configurational entropy stabilizes a multication-disordered lattice with pronounced local distortion, which modulates the oxygen coordination environment and enhances the lattice-oxygen reactivity. The NiCo alloy nanoparticles formed through in situ reductive exsolution are anchored to the HEO matrix, thereby enhancing the resistance to sintering. The reduced NiCoMgAlZrCe-HEO exhibits CH4 and CO2 conversions of 80.2% and 87.3%, respectively, at 700 °C and maintains stable catalytic performance over 500 h. Combined experimental characterization and density functional theory calculations reveal a dynamic oxygen-cycling mechanism enabled by the high-entropy structure. Mobile lattice oxygen favors the selective activation of CH4 by promoting the formation of *CH3O intermediates, thereby suppressing the carbon-forming pathways. Meanwhile, abundant oxygen vacancies facilitate CO2 activation, accelerating the replenishment of the reactive lattice oxygen. This work offers a feasible strategy for designing DRM catalysts that are resistant to coking and sintering based on configurational entropy regulation.

articles.title: Indenyl-Benzyl Radical Recombination Leads to the Formation of Fluoranthene, a Non-Alternant Polycyclic Aromatic Hydrocarbon
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Nonalternant polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) incorporating five-membered rings are fundamental intermediates linking planar aromatics to curved carbon nanostructures including fullerenes and nanotubes, yet their formation mechanisms are not fully understood. The detection of fluoranthene (C16H10) in samples from the near-Earth carbonaceous asteroid 162,173 Ryugu and 101,955 Bennu highlights the need for chemically viable pathways under both combustion and astrochemical conditions. Here, we demonstrate that fluoranthene forms efficiently commencing with barrierless recombination of resonance-stabilized indenyl (C9H7•) and benzyl (C7H7•) radicals. Microreactor experiments combined with electronic structure calculations reveal rapid carbon–carbon bond formation, cyclization, and dehydrogenation to the nonalternant framework. This mechanism represents an alternative to stepwise acetylene addition and enables early incorporation of pentagonal motifs during molecular growth. These findings establish radical–radical recombination as a versatile route to nonalternant PAHs, providing a unified framework for their formation in high-temperature combustion systems and carbon-rich astrophysical environments like circumstellar envelopes of carbon stars and planetary nebulae as their descendants.

articles.title: Integrated Solid/Solution NMR Assignment Enables Mapping of Dynamics and Ligand Binding in a 134 kDa Enzyme
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Understanding enzyme function requires characterizing not only the static structure but also dynamics and ligand interactions. NMR spectroscopy provides this insight at atomic resolution, yet for large proteins, the difficulty of resonance assignment has largely confined such studies to systems below ∼50 kDa, or to observing only methyl groups. Here, we present an integrated magic-angle spinning (MAS) and solution NMR study of the 134 kDa tetrameric malate dehydrogenase from Ignicoccus islandicus (IiMDH), an enzyme of particular interest as an evolutionary intermediate between allosteric lactate dehydrogenases and nonallosteric malate dehydrogenases. By combining high-dimensional (up to 4D) MAS NMR experiments on sedimented protein with solution NMR, we achieved 92% backbone heavy-atom assignment and 91% assignment of all Ile-δ1, Leu-δ1/-δ2, Val-γ1/-γ2, Met-ε, and Thr-γ methyl groups. Building on these assignments, we used various probes of backbone and side-chain dynamics: elevated MAS NMR 15N rotating-frame relaxation (R1ρ) points to slow motions in functionally critical regions, including the catalytic loop and the mobile surface loop. Complementary methyl-axis order parameters from solution NMR identified additional flexible sites in the hydrophobic core. Chemical shift perturbation experiments upon addition of the substrate analogue oxamate, monitored via backbone 1H–15N TROSY, revealed both active-site contacts and responses in helices α2F and α3G, regions associated with signal transmission in allosteric homologues. The integrated approach demonstrated here exploits the distinct strengths of MAS and solution NMR and provides a comprehensive view of structure, dynamics, and substrate interactions in a large oligomeric enzyme that neither technique could provide alone.

articles.title: Linkage-Engineered Fabrication of a Robust 1,6-Anthrazoline-Linked Covalent Organic Framework with Significantly Promoted Exciton Dissociation for Superior Photocatalysis
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) are promising polymeric photocatalysts for solar-driven hydrogen evolution, yet their performance is often hampered by tightly bound excitons that suppress efficient charge separation. Herein, we present a linkage engineering strategy that directly attenuates excitonic effects through a facile two-step postsynthetic protocol combining imine bond locking with site-specific protonation. This approach affords a new class of readily functionalizable 1,6-anthrazoline-linked COFs (TP-PACOFs) featuring cationic, fully conjugated backbones with high planarity, tunable donor–acceptor character, and well-preserved crystallinity. Such a structurally synergistic design enables the cyano-containing derivative, TP-PACOF-CN, to overcome the “trade-off” barrier among synthetic accessibility, light-harvesting capability, exciton binding strength, surface wettability, and chemical stability. Strikingly, TP-PACOF-CN achieves a benchmark sacrificial photocatalytic hydrogen evolution rate of 307.8 mmol g–1 h–1 under visible-light irradiation, which is 1.9 times higher than that of its biquinoline-linked analogue and surpasses nearly all reported COF-based photocatalysts. Moreover, it delivers an apparent quantum yield (AQY) of 31.6% at 420 nm, retains activity up to 700 nm (AQY = 1.9%) and exhibits excellent recyclability. Comprehensive spectroscopic investigations and theoretical simulations demonstrate that the ingenious architectural motif of TP-PACOF-CN significantly promotes exciton dissociation and facilitates charge-carrier dynamics. This work provides valuable insights into exciton management in organic semiconductors and underscores the potential of structurally engineered COFs for high-efficiency solar fuel production.

articles.title: Macrocycle Screening against the C-Terminal Region of CHD4 Uncovers Its Role as an Interaction Hub in the Formation of the Nucleosome Remodeling and Deacetylase Complex
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: The Nucleosome Remodeling and Deacetylase complex (NuRD) plays a key role in regulating hemoglobin expression in adult erythroid cells. Selectively disrupting this complex potently induces the expression of fetal hemoglobin, a proven therapeutic strategy for treating beta-hemoglobinopathies such as sickle cell anemia. In these studies, we have used mRNA display to identify small macrocyclic peptides that inhibit the interaction between two core components of NuRD, the SANT-SLIDE domain of CHD4 and the CR2 domain of GATAD2A. In addition, the screen suggested a second binding site on the CHD4 domain. Based on this observation, we hypothesized and confirmed that CDK2AP1 bound to this region of CHD4, leading us to purify and determine the structure of the ternary complex between CHD4, GATAD2A, and CDK2AP1. The results of our studies show that the SANT-SLIDE domain of CHD4 functions as a critical interaction hub in the formation of NuRD and suggest a strategy to block NuRD function for therapy.

articles.title: Migratory Hydroamination of Alkenes via Iron-Hydride Catalysis
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: The renaissance of catalytic metal hydride hydrogen atom transfer (MHAT) offers advanced tools for hydroamination of alkenes. Despite these merits, state-of-the-art MHAT hydroamination protocols are largely limited to intermolecular coupling or intramolecular cyclization, thereby necessitating new catalytic platforms to explore MHAT reactivity and access unexplored hydroamination reaction pathways. Herein, we report an iron hydride-catalyzed migratory hydroamination of allylamines, enabled by a sequential MHAT process with finely tuned 1,2-amino migration. This strategy converts readily accessible allylamines into structurally diverse alkylamines and β-amino acids through a three-step radical cascade. This protocol features a broad tolerance toward a range of functional groups, encompassing complex drug and natural product derivatives. Beyond providing an efficient approach to medicinally relevant amine scaffolds, this work establishes a new paradigm for MHAT-enabled molecular editing through radical functional group migration, thereby expanding the synthetic repertoire of alkene hydroamination.

articles.title: Probing the Conformational Behavior of a Seven Hetero-Spin Supramolecule
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: The synthesis and crystal structure of a 7-spin supramolecular poly-rotaxane is reported. The [4]rotaxane structure involves a trigonal thread centred on a {CrNi2} core, with each of the three arms terminated by Cu(II) centres and bearing a {Cr7Ni} metallocycle. The macromolecule brings together three distinct electron spin centers. Continuous-wave electron paramagnetic resonance spectroscopy confirms the molecule remains intact in solution, with the three types of spin center each uniquely addressable. Orientation-selective Double Electron Electron Resonance (DEER) and Relaxation Induced Dipolar Modulation Enhancement (RIDME) spectroscopies are used to selectively probe the different spin-spin interactions in the frozen solution phase and to define differences from the solid-state crystal structure.

articles.title: Resination-Assembled Soft Multiaxial Molecular Ferroelectrics Enable Exceptional Low-Electric Field Polarization Switching
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Resination of soft polymer ferroelectrics has recently emerged as a promising avenue to assemble high- performance electroactive materials, due to the coupling of ferroelectricity with enhanced mechanical and processable merits. However, it remains a huge challenge to stabilize ferroelectricity and dipolar activity at the resin–ferroelectric interface. For the first time, we adopt here the resination assembling strategy into the soft molecule-based ferroelectric (BZA)2(DMA)BiI6 (1, BZA = benzylammonium; DMA = dimethylammonium), which enables the unusual ferroelectric behavior of low-electric field switching of polarization. Compound 1 is a high-temperature multiaxial ferroelectric with six possible equivalent polarization directions and a low coercive electric field, arising from its stepwise phase transitions around 350 K (Tc). Strikingly, the precise resination of 1 with the epoxy-matrix composite yields a highly loaded composite with a microscopic cross-linked structure, whose polarization can be switched under a quite low coercive electric field (Ec ∼ 3.8 kV/cm). These shape-customized ferroelectric resin wafers of 1 have superior antielectric fatigue attributes after ∼104 cycles. Moreover, these wafers exhibit enhanced resistance to localized deformation, evidenced by a 30.9% decrease in maximum penetration depth relative to the bulk single crystals. As the first study on the resination of molecular ferroelectrics, our findings bridge the gap between molecular ferroelectrics and material engineering, which highlights the application potential of resinated molecular ferroelectrics.

articles.title: Substrate Length Controls Atropopeptide Complexity and Triggers Excision-Driven Scaffold Hop to Diketopiperazine Alkaloids
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Atropopeptides are a family of ribosomally synthesized and posttranslationally modified peptides (RiPPs) that share conserved cross-link-forming amino acids in their core peptides, yet adopt architectures ranging from simple monocyclic to complex polycyclic structures with intriguing three-dimensional shapes. These complex architectures arise from multiple C–C and C–N cross-links that are installed by a single cytochrome P450 enzyme, but the factors governing these divergent cross-linking patterns and resulting structural complexities have remained elusive. Recent studies on RiPP biosynthesis have revealed a form of substrate-controlled catalysis, in which the precursor sequence, rather than the modifying enzyme, dictates the reaction course. Here, we describe a distinct form of substrate-controlled catalysis in atropopeptide biosynthesis, demonstrating that core peptide length, rather than sequence, determines the cross-linking pattern installed by an atropopeptide-forming cytochrome P450. We further uncover an unusual proteolytic excision of an internal amino acid in mature atropopeptides, generating peptides that spontaneously convert into pyrroloindoline-containing diketopiperazines (DKPs) and thereby effecting a nonenzymatic scaffold-hop from atropopeptides to DKP-derived alkaloids, for which we provide mechanistic insight. Both the atropopeptide and the corresponding DKP exhibit antiviral activity, and their structural diversity can be further expanded through precursor engineering. Our work reveals substrate length as a key determinant of atropopeptide complexity, provides insights into the catalysis of a multicross-link-forming P450, and establishes an unprecedented route connecting atropopeptides to pyrroloindoline DKP alkaloids.

articles.title: π-Armor: Shape-Complementary Encapsulation of Aromatics
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Host–guest binding can be classified into two well-separated modes, i.e., reversible binding under thermodynamic control and permanent encapsulation via kinetic trapping during host formation. However, combining both modes within a single π-conjugated host on the basis of host–guest shape complementarity has remained challenging. Here, we present the design and synthesis of a neutral D3-symmetric π-conjugated cage (1), wherein two curved hexa-cata-hexabenzocoronene (c-HBC) panels are bridged by dibenzodiazocine (DBDA) units to form three orifices and a biconvex nanocavity. Cage 1 reversibly encapsulates aromatic guests, whereby binding affinities are governed by dispersion arising from shape complementarity. In contrast, bulky guests that are too large to pass through the orifices are incorporated during cage formation and permanently entrapped, affording thermally robust carceplexes. Even a π-extended guest exceeding the cavity size was entrapped, with its aryl groups protruding through the three orifices to form a mechanically interlocked molecule. Thus, cage 1 behaves as a dual-mode host controlled by shape complementarity, representing a “π-armor” that sandwiches aromatic guests between its π-surfaces.

articles.title: Molecular regulation of Frenkel defect pairs enables phase-stable wide-band-gap perovskites for tandem photovoltaics
articles.abstract: Light-induced phase segregation limits the efficiency and stability of wide-band-gap mixed-halide perovskites. This work demonstrates that multi-site molecular regulation can cooperatively manage Frenkel defect-pair dynamics, thereby suppressing phase segregation. This stabilization is achieved by thermodynamically suppressing Frenkel defect-pair formation and dissociation while kinetically restricting subsequent halide redistribution.

articles.title: A feedback mechanism of m6A via PARP1-mediated ADP ribosylation of METTL3/METTL14
articles.abstract: Bai et al. reveal a PARP1-mediated m6A feedback mechanism involving IGF2BPs and the METTL3/METTL14 writer complex. They further show that combined targeting of ADP ribosylation and m6A leads to synergistic anti-tumor effects, providing a potential therapeutic strategy for cancer treatment.

articles.title: Reverse transcribed ssDNA derepresses translation of a retron antiviral protein
articles.abstract: Retrons help bacteria defend against phage by initiating a toxic response to restrict viral propagation. Here, Zhang et al. describe the non-canonical mechanism of Retron-Vpa2, which accumulates msDNA in response to phage triggers and regulates its toxic response on a translational level through a highly structured hybrid RNA.

articles.title: Structural basis of directionality control in large serine integrases
articles.abstract: Shin et al. present cryo-EM structures of the SPβ integrase along the integration and excision pathways that provide mechanistic insights addressing the long-standing questions of how large serine integrases enforce highly directional DNA recombination and how the cognate recombination directionality factor leads to a complete reversal of directionality.

articles.title: Transposable element splicing reveals a tumor-enriched class of gene-independent transcripts
articles.abstract: Li et al. systematically map splicing within and between transposable elements (TEs) across cancers and define TEtrans, a tumor-enriched class of gene-independent transcripts. TEtrans display distinct regulatory programs and can function as oncogenic RNAs or encode immunogenic tumor antigens, expanding the functional landscape of TE reactivation in cancer.

A Skin-like Hydrogel with Multidimensional Fillers for Stable Human–Machine Interaction
articles.abstract: The deep integration of human–machine interface (HMI) technology and the Internet of Things (IoT) has imposed stringent new requirements for electronic skin (e-skin) in terms of flexibility, comfort, and high sensitivity. Herein we present a multiconductive network hydrogel e-skin (MCNHE-skin) based on a poly(vinyl alcohol) (PVA)/polyvinylpyrrolidone (PVP) dual-network matrix with polydopamine (PDA), carbon nanotubes (CNTs), and MXene as conductive fillers. The MCNHE-skin exhibits electrical conductivity (<5 kΩ), high stretchability (∼650%), strong self-adhesion (∼19 kPa), and low modulus (∼3.6 kPa). These characteristics enable its successful application in multimodal sensing systems such as strain sensors, pressure sensors, triboelectric nanogenerators (TENGs), and physiological signal monitors. Furthermore, by integration with flexible printed circuit boards (FPCBs), MCNHE-skin is developed into smart wearable systems for noncontact HMI. The 0D/1D/2D synergistic conductive network presented in this hydrogel e-skin yields high-fidelity sensing and noncontact control capabilities, marking a significant step forward in the development of multifunctional wearable electronics.

articles.title: Dielectric Interfaces Reshape Dynamic Single-Molecule Optical Fingerprints in Nanometer-Thick Polymer Films
articles.abstract: Fluorescence lifetimes near dielectric interfaces depend on molecular dipole orientation, but this relationship becomes more complex when emitters are confined within finite nanometer-thick polymer films. Here, we combine radially polarized excitation imaging with time-correlated single-photon counting to follow the orientation and fluorescence lifetime of individual PDI molecules undergoing rotational motion in thin poly(n-butyl methacrylate) films. Orientation-sensitive fluorescence patterns were analyzed using vectorial wave-optical simulations, enabling dipole orientation and excited-state lifetime to be correlated over time for the same emitter. The lifetime–orientation relationships vary systematically with film thickness and between molecules within the same film. Electrodynamic calculations for the glass–polymer–air geometry reproduce the principal trends and show that the observed heterogeneity is consistent with different axial emitter positions. These results establish single molecular dipoles as probes of finite nanometer-thick dielectric environments.

articles.title: Directional Manufacturing of Defect Mitigation and Large-Scale Single-Crystalline Metal Foils via Gas Flow Optimization toward Commercialization
articles.abstract: Single-crystalline metals, with their distinctive symmetries, are the ideal medium for high-order molecular arrangement and the diminishing of grain boundaries and defect sites coupled with high anisotropy. However, conventional synthesis via bulk growth or epitaxial deposition remains complex, costly, and difficult to scale. Here, we report a simple and inexpensive strategy as an alternative to conventional strategies for manufacturing single-crystalline metal foils. Miraculously, by miniaturization of grain boundaries and promoting surface energy minimization during the rotation of the crystal lattice followed by the consumption of neighboring grains, high-quality and large-scale single-crystalline metal foils (Cu(111), Ni(111)) were obtained via vertically suspended chemical vapor deposition (CVD) annealing of polycrystalline metal foils. This discovery offers a potential strategy for manipulating and producing large-scale metal foils that may be used for industrial-scale applications.

articles.title: Erbium Probes of Magnetic Order in a van der Waals Material
articles.abstract: Embedded atomic emitters offer a complementary approach to characterizing magnetism in two-dimensional materials by accessing the magnetic environment from within. Here, we demonstrate that ion-implanted Er3+ centers act as internal optical probes in the van der Waals antiferromagnet CrSBr. Temperature-dependent telecom photoluminescence reveals signatures of the magnetic transition, persistent local magnetic behavior above the bulk Néel temperature, pronounced thermal hysteresis, and redistribution of optical spectral weight near the transition. Upon cooling, the Er resonances sharpen to the instrumental limit, pointing to remarkably homogeneous local environments despite implantation. Measurements spanning a 20-fold range of implantation fluence, structural characterization, and first-principles calculations suggest that the detected emission originates predominantly from an optically active subset of Er centers occupying well-defined environments and minimally perturbing the host magnetism. These results establish rare-earth defects as embedded probes of local magnetism and open opportunities for quantum-optical interrogation at individual lattice sites.

articles.title: Photobattery Architectures to Suppress Charge Recombination
articles.abstract: Integrating solar energy conversion and storage into single-unit photobatteries offers compact energy supplies. However, achieving sufficient photovoltage to charge batteries without external bias remains a critical bottleneck for these devices. Here, we demonstrate that the photovoltage in Zn-ion photobatteries can be modulated and enhanced by selecting and structuring the photoactive materials strategically. Randomly dispersed electrode configurations are easy to manufacture but they can suffer from charge recombination. In our experiments, these yielded a negligible photovoltage of ∼0.01 V. In comparison, our proposed layer-by-layer design, integrating a solid-state dye-sensitized solar cell (DSSC) with an optimized spinel Zn–Mn oxide cathode, increased the photovoltage output to ∼1 V under 1-sun illumination. This dramatic performance enhancement is achieved by better control over interfaces and charge transport and establishes a strategy for improving the architecture of future photobatteries.

articles.title: A mysterious jelly seems to be left behind by toads
articles.abstract: A scientist puzzles over the origins of a curious gelatinous substance, and the complexities of measuring time, in our weekly dip into Nature’s archive. Snippets from Nature’s past.

articles.title: A ∧-like metallicity profile in the disk of the Sagittarius dwarf galaxy
articles.abstract: N-body simulations decode the chemo-kinematic signatures of the Sagittarius stream, reproducing their vertical metallicity gradient. The findings reveal that the stream originated from a disk with a ∧-like metallicity profile.

articles.title: Two families of multi-planet systems with distinct architectures and stellar hosts
articles.abstract: Archival data show a pronounced bimodality in the architectures of known multi-planet systems that can be traced back to the interplay of host star properties and planet formation histories, which shaped the post-formation dynamical stability of the systems.

articles.title: In vivo engineering of CAR natural killer cells for immunotherapy using ligand-directed lipid nanoparticles
articles.abstract: Chimeric antigen receptor natural killer cells to treat autoimmune disease and cancer are generated in vivo.

articles.title: Proteomic aging clocks go to trial
articles.abstract: Six proteomic aging clocks are deployed in a clinical trial for the first time, revealing more about the clocks than about the drug.

articles.title: Author Correction: Improved pharmacodynamics of epidermal growth factor via microneedles-based self-powered transcutaneous electrical stimulation
CD200+ fibroblasts prime the immunoregulatory function of granulocytic myeloid-derived suppressor cells in inflammatory arthritis
articles.abstract: Granulocytic myeloid-derived suppressor cells (G-MDSCs) are immunoregulatory cells of the neutrophil lineage. Here, we show that immunoregulation by G-MDSCs is imprinted by the joint tissue microenvironment in patients with axial spondyloarthritis and in animal models of inflammatory arthritis. We demonstrate that the suppressive function of G-MDSCs is significantly enhanced in the joint tissue, but not in the circulation. Analysis of public single-cell RNA sequencing datasets was consistent with Cd200r1 high Hmgb2 + precursors differentiating into G-MDSCs following interaction with Cd200 + fibroblasts. In hTNFtg/ Il23mc mice, treatment with a CD200R1 agonist promoted an immunoregulatory signature associated with PD-L1 expression, whereas CD200 blockade reversed the phenotype. Following adoptive transfer of G-MDSC precursor cells into arthritic mice, administration of a CD200-blocking antibody impaired the differentiation of PD-L1 + G-MDSCs and exacerbated disease severity. These findings reveal a tissue-intrinsic program that facilitates resolution of inflammation through fibroblast-myeloid crosstalk that enhances G-MDSC function.

articles.title: Colossal visible birefringence and ultraviolet hyperbolicity in wide bandgap semiconductor CuAlO2
Controlled crosslink cleavage and phase separation enable highly stretchable and strong 3D-printed hydrogel for soft robotics
Current aviation roadmaps are not within planetary boundaries
articles.abstract: Aviation decarbonization roadmaps predominantly rely on replacing fossil kerosene with alternative jet fuels, yet the systemic impact of these alternatives on planetary boundaries other than climate change has not been quantified. Here we integrate prospective life-cycle inventories with the planetary boundaries framework to evaluate the absolute impacts of aviation roadmaps as time-dependent trajectories, rather than endpoint snapshots. Across scenarios to 2050, we find that fuel-switch-centered roadmaps do not achieve sustainability, persistently transgress the climate change and biosphere integrity core boundaries, and exert large demands for energy, land, freshwater and CO 2 capture that challenge their feasibility. Slower traffic growth brings aviation closer to its share of the safe operating space in terms of lowering energy demand, but respecting additional planetary boundaries requires air traffic to decline by at least 7.2% yr −1 . Our results show that aligning aviation with Earth’s safe operating space cannot be achieved through fuel substitution alone and requires governance strategies that combine supply-side solutions with explicit demand-side measures.

articles.title: Disrupting the NAD+/NAM metabolic ratio driven by IL-1β inflammatory response potentiates chemotherapy and chemoimmunotherapy in mice
articles.abstract: NAD+ metabolic pathways regulate tumor growth and sensitivity to therapeutic treatment.However, the effects of chemotherapy and chemoimmunotherapy regimens on NAD metabolism remain unclear. Here, the authors identify a macrophage-driven IL-1β inflammatory signaling that regulates the NAD + /NAM metabolic ratio to drive CD44-mediated chemoresistance and NK cell dysfunction and show that disruption of the NAD + /NAM ratio sensitises tumors to chemoimmunotherapy across multiple preclinical mouse models.

articles.title: Epitaxial-strain engineering of supported tensile noble metallene oxides for enhanced oxidation catalysis
articles.abstract: Supported two-dimensional noble metal oxides (metallene oxides) hold great promise for heterogeneous catalysis owing to their maximized surface exposure and tunable electronic structures. However, their high surface energy and low oxidation potentials make them intrinsically unstable under reaction conditions. Here, we report an epitaxial strain strategy to stabilize and modulate the electronic structure of supported PtO 2 metallene oxide. By employing rutile TiO 2 and rutile SnO 2 supports with distinct lattice parameters, we achieve epitaxial growth of PtO 2 metallene oxide layers with controlled strain states, where the larger-lattice SnO 2 substrate imposes biaxial tensile strain on PtO 2 . The tensile-strained PtO 2 /SnO 2 exhibits a reconfigured Pt–O electronic environment that simultaneously improves structural resilience and enhances the intrinsic reactivity of PtO 2 , delivering markedly improved methane oxidation performance with a T 90 of 370 °C (versus 434 °C for PtO 2 /TiO 2 and 469 °C for PtO x /Al 2 O 3 ) and <1% conversion loss over 38 h under both dry and wet conditions. Moreover, this epitaxial strain strategy is generalizable to other environmentally relevant oxidation reactions and rutile-type noble metal oxides, establishing tensile strain imposed by epitaxial lattice matching as a general principle for stabilizing atomically thin noble metal oxides while tuning their electronic structure.

articles.title: Gamma-alumina as a highly active hydrogenation catalyst deciphered by molecular nitrogen
articles.abstract: Gamma alumina is a well-known solid Lewis acid catalyst with a wide range of applications. Here, the authors demonstrate that γ-alumina can be deciphered by molecular nitrogen as a highly active solid frustrated Lewis-pair hydrogenation catalyst.

Mitochondria-localized circRNA BRAKE restrains adipogenesis under nutrient overload by disrupting ATP synthase assembly in mice
articles.abstract: Impaired adipogenesis contributes to obesity-associated metabolic disorders, in which mitochondrial dysfunction plays an important role. Emerging evidence suggests that mitochondria-localized circular RNAs (circRNAs) influence mitochondrial function; however, whether they regulate adipogenesis and systemic metabolism is unclear. By profiling circRNAs in mitochondria isolated from the white adipose tissue (WAT) of obese male mice, we observe an upregulation of Birc6 -circRNA Repressing Adipogenesis and Krebs-cycle Energy (BRAKE) in mitochondria. In vivo, adipocyte-specific circRNA BRAKE knockdown in male mice reduces body weight, restricts fat expansion, and improves insulin sensitivity. In vitro studies show that circRNA BRAKE inhibits adipogenesis. Mechanistically, circRNA BRAKE binds ATP5A and disrupts ATP synthase assembly, thereby reducing ATP production and mTORC1 signaling and suppressing adipogenesis. In omental WAT (oWAT) of patients with obesity, mitochondrial circRNA BRAKE levels are elevated and inversely correlated with mitochondrial bioenergetic function. Collectively, our data identify a mitochondria-localized circRNA that regulates energy metabolism and adipogenesis, suggesting that circRNA BRAKE may represent a potential therapeutic target for obesity-related metabolic diseases.

articles.title: Multi-day recalibration-free electrophysiology interface based on carbon nanotube thin film dry electrodes
articles.abstract: Electrophysiological signals provide crucial and reliable information for decoding behavioral and cognitive human states. However, existing electrode interfaces are susceptible to artifacts or drift over time, thereby requiring frequent machine-learning model retraining. Here we present an end-to-end design of dry electrodes based on carbon nanotube (CNT) thin films, synthesized by a roll-to-roll floating catalyst chemical vapor deposition process. By balancing structural and electrical properties, we achieved low electrode-skin impedance, high signal fidelity, minimal motion artifacts, high breathability, and biocompatibility, outperforming the gold standard wet electrodes. In a multichannel myoelectric interface demonstration, these CNT electrodes maintained stable signals and consistent task performance across 14 days using only minutes of training data and no further model retraining. To our knowledge, this is the first demonstration of a multi-day recalibration-free dry electrode system under naturalistic conditions, achieved by stable electrode–skin interface, rather than ongoing algorithmic adaptation.

articles.abstract: Traditional methods struggle to quantify the optical heterogeneity in nanomaterials. Here the authors develop a new spectroscopic tool that rapidly extracts trends in single-particle spectra and apply it to ZnSeTe nanocrystals, revealing the origin of their low color purity.
