Reinforcement learning guided robotic platform that investigates and discovers asymmetric reactions
articles.abstract: Autonomous robotic platforms accelerate chemical discovery by coupling automated experimentation with algorithmic decision-making, but most lack integrated support for chirality and the sequential decision-making required to explore asymmetric reaction spaces with unknown reactivity and stereochemical outcomes. Here, we report a bespoke robotic platform guided by deep reinforcement learning that autonomously navigates a defined asymmetric reaction space by scouting reaction conditions, discovering chiral products, screening catalysts and mapping substrate scope. The structure-agnostic workflow is enabled by a digital twin of asymmetric catalysis, in which control policies are trained before transfer to the laboratory. We validate the approach in chiral phosphoric acid catalysis: over 30 days, the system made more than 3,000 decisions and uncovered four highly enantioselective transformations, including an axially chiral molecule and three allene syntheses, one involving the enantioselective functionalization of a pyrrolopyrrole moiety. These results highlight deep reinforcement learning-guided autonomy as a strategy for discovery in complex catalytic systems.

articles.title: Scellmate enables contamination aware curation and host mobilome linkage analysis of large SAG datasets
Securing critical rare-earth supply through end-of-life NdFeB magnets recycling via molten salt electrolysis with consumable Mg-cathode
articles.abstract: Molten-salt electrolysis with a consumable magnesium cathode recovers neodymium from end-of-life NdFeB magnets at high current efficiency, while life-cycle and economic analyses indicate potential for industrial-scale recycling.

articles.title: Soil proteogenomics uncover microbial strategies for soil depth-specific carbon cycling under whole-soil warming conditions
articles.abstract: Soils are Earth’s largest carbon reservoir, yet microbial mechanisms controlling decomposition, and their warming response, remain poorly resolved, especially in subsoils. Using genome-resolved proteogenomics within a replicated whole-soil warming experiment (0–90 cm, +4 °C, 7.5 years) we map microbial traits, their depth stratification, and warming responses. Depth is the dominant driver of microbial community and trait structure. Depth-wise, metabolism converge on low-molecular-weight and C1 compounds, challenging glucose-centric models, with surface soils enriched in methanol oxidation and deep soils in alcohol fermentation, CO oxidation and N₂ fixation. Abundant sialidases in deep soils implicate glycoproteins as a key carbon source. Warming effects are smaller and decrease over time but are depth-specific: surface soils show enhanced amino sugar and sugar alcohol transport, phosphorus mobilization, and stress tolerance, whereas mid- and deep soils exhibit stimulated C1 metabolism, CO oxidation, and altered nitrogen turnover. These depth-specific microbial trait shifts may critically influence soil carbon–climate feedbacks.

articles.title: Unmet care needs at the end-of-life among older adults with activity limitations
articles.abstract: Formal end-of-life care expansion in the US, Europe, and South Korea has not fully compensated for declining informal care, resulting in care gaps. Demographic transitions interact with development contexts to create distinct care landscapes.

A unique and equity-driven approach to immunology education in low- and middle-income countries
articles.abstract: We present a model for education that has proven transformative for faculty and students, fostering mentorship, inclusion and cross-border collaboration. By embedding training in local contexts, our framework builds confidence, skills and leadership among early-career scientists. These elements foster scientific autonomy and enable sustainable global engagement.

articles.title: Characterizing the onset and progression of cancer cachexia using routine clinical data
articles.abstract: In 52,236 patients with cancer, cachectic weight loss episodes were linked to lower survival rates, occurred at times of disease progression, and carried a consistent serological signature across routine laboratory markers. Specific tumor genotypes, including TP53 mutations, were also positively associated with cachexia risk. Statistical models were trained to predict a patient’s impending risk of cachexia.

articles.abstract: A small epilepsy monitoring study shows that a moderated, large language model-based chat interface lets patients converse with their electroencephalography monitoring in real time, using a smartphone, and patient feedback cut seizure-detector false alarms by about 80% without clinician input.

articles.title: From DNA to full-length proteins through nanopore sequencing
articles.abstract: Nanopore protein sequencing has advanced from a theoretical ambition to a practical technology, overcoming major challenges in protein unfolding, transport and signal detection to achieve single-amino-acid and post-translational modification sensitivity. With both full-length and peptide-based approaches progressing towards commercialization, the field is now focused on scaling throughput and refining analysis tools to unlock a new generation of single-molecule proteomics.

articles.title: From a single atom to manufacturable quantum processors in silicon
articles.abstract: Two decades on from the first atomic-scale devices, atom-based silicon quantum computers have progressed from proof of concept to scalable quantum processors that are rapidly gaining commercial traction. What remains is largely a matter of industrial-scale engineering and 3D integration.

articles.abstract: As the journal turns 20, we reflect on the journey nanoscale science has undertaken over the past two decades and how nanoscience-enabled technologies have had a real-world impact.

articles.title: How display technology adopted quantum dots
articles.abstract: Quantum dots — semiconductor nanocrystals whose optical and electronic properties can be tuned by controlling their size, composition and surface chemistry — have found commercial success for display technologies. Their transition from nanophotonics research into an applied modern nanotechnology exemplifies the bottlenecks that many emerging technologies must overcome on the path to commercialization.

articles.title: How lipid nanoparticles evolved from models of biological membranes to systems that enable RNA therapeutics
articles.abstract: Curiosity-driven studies of lipid organization and lipid asymmetry in biological membranes led to scalable methods for making liposomes, efficient loading of drugs and ionizable cationic lipids. In turn, these advances led to lipid nanoparticles enabling the RNA medicine Onpattro and the COVID-19 mRNA vaccines, and they are now facilitating gene therapies that can potentially treat most human diseases.

articles.title: How single-atom catalysis transformed from a nanoscience curiosity into a new paradigm for heterogeneous catalysis
articles.abstract: Single-atom catalysis has reshaped heterogeneous catalysis by shifting its central focus from surface and interface to isolated atom-centred active sites. This transition establishes a new paradigm for understanding reactivity, integrating experiments and theory, and advancing heterogeneous catalysis from empirical observations toward a more predictive and precise science.

articles.title: How spin-transfer-torque magnetoresistive random access memory bridged spintronics research and the microelectronics industry
articles.abstract: Spin-transfer torque magnetoresistive random access memory has emerged as a leading non-volatile memory technology replacing embedded Flash in diverse fields including aerospace, automotive and healthcare applications.

articles.title: Mosquito-based malaria control through genetic, microbial and immunological innovations
articles.abstract: In this Review, Dong and colleagues overview recent developments in mosquito-targeted malaria control, highlighting Anopheles population modification (rendering mosquitoes Plasmodium-resistant) and Anopheles population-suppression strategies based on gene drive technology, engineered microorganisms, vaccines and drugs, and discuss key knowledge gaps and the responsible implementation of these approaches in conjunction with existing malaria interventions.

articles.title: A general synthesis of tryptophan-crosslinked macrocyclic peptides enabled by a dual-functional directing group
articles.abstract: Tryptophan-crosslinked macrocyclic peptides display interesting therapeutic properties; however, methods for their synthesis are limited. Now a Rh-catalysed process enables their synthesis through the development of a dual-function directing group that promotes C–H activation and C–N bond formation. The method provides access to a range of macrocycles, including pharmacophores of micitide 982 and tryglysin.

articles.title: Synthesis of chiral allylic amines through regio- and enantioselective homologation of enamines using Ni catalysis
articles.abstract: Chiral allylic amines are key building blocks in the synthesis of bioactive molecules. Now a regio- and enantioselective method for their synthesis is reported. The Ni-catalysed process proceeds through homologation of enamines by cross-coupling with alkynes, forming a range of chiral allylic amines in good yield and with excellent enantioselectivity.

articles.title: Metabolic convergence on TOR signaling in the chestnut blight fungus and its regulation by host plant signals
articles.abstract: Proposed model of metabolic convergence on the target of rapamycin (TOR) pathway in Cryphonectria parasitica. Twelve core genes involved in diverse metabolic pathways act as upstream regulators or downstream effectors of TOR kinase. Dysregulation of these genes mimics an inhibited TOR state, leading to restricted hyphal growth and enhanced trehalose and autophagy, independent of Cryphonectria hypovirus 1 (CHV1) infection. Mutants carrying deletions in these genes display severe growth defects in response to CHV1 infection. Changes in CHV1 titer were genotype‐specific, with the genes functioning as antiviral, viral replicative, or defense factors in C. parasitica. Summary Transcriptomic analysis of the chestnut blight fungus Cryphonectria parasitica identified 22 core genes regulated by Cryphonectria hypovirus 1 (CHV1) infection and sectorization. Twelve genes with common phenocopies were analyzed: all mutants displayed restricted colonial growth, intense pigmentation, hyperbranched terminal hyphae with swollen globose cells, and reduced conidiation. Although gene‐specific mutant phenotypes existed, responses to most stressors were similar to those of the wild‐type. Mutant growth was highly sensitive to nutrient conditions, and growth restriction was notably alleviated by supplementation with 1.0 M sorbitol, nutrient‐deficient media, or skim milk. All mutants showed hallmarks consistent with reduced target of rapamycin (TOR) signaling. Trehalose accumulation, a canonical fungal response to TOR inhibition, was observed in mutants via transcriptional upregulation of core trehalose biosynthetic genes, resulting in altered hyphal osmolarity and common mutant cell phenotypes. Plant signals overrode the mutants' phenotypes, strongly promoting their growth and differentiation. Although a severely retarded growth defect was observed in mutants, mutants' virulence remained intact, which can be ascribed to the host‐plant signals. Cryphonectria hypovirus 1 (CHV1)‐infected mutants exhibited greater growth restriction, accompanied by genotype‐specific CHV1 titers. Despite gene‐specific variation, common phenocopies indicate that diverse metabolic pathways converge on the TOR pathway in the fungal response to host‐plant and CHV1 infection.

articles.title: PnMYB4a, a R2R3 transcription factor, modulates coumarin biosynthesis during melanization in the culms of Phyllostachys nigra
articles.abstract: Conceptual model describing the role of PnMYB4a in regulating coumarin accumulation and promoting melanization in Phyllostachys nigra culms. Summary Culm colour is one of the primary traits determining the ornamental value of bamboos. The black pigment shown to accumulate in Phyllostachys nigra was previously characterized as melanin, but the underlying regulatory mechanism for its deposition remains elusive. Herein, metabolomics data show that coumarins serve as precursor substrates for melanization in P. nigra, and RNA‐seq and weighted gene correlation network analysis (WGCNA) revealed that the transcription factor PnMYB4a is integral to coumarin biosynthesis. Overexpression of PnMYB4a promotes coumarin production in both Oryza sativa and Arabidopsis thaliana. Pn4CL4‐2, a biosynthetic gene involved in coumarin biosynthesis, was identified as a direct target gene of PnMYB4a. Additionally, PnWRKY8 and PnWRKY72‐2 were found to interact with PnMYB4a both in vivo and in vitro. Both PnWRKY8 and PnWRKY72‐2 positively promoted coumarin accumulation in transgenic rice, but they repressed the expression of Pn4CL4‐2 by directly binding to W‐box elements within its promoter. Interestingly, PnMYB4a was found to alleviate the inhibitory effect on Pn4CL4‐2 by forming complexes with both PnWRKY8 and PnWRKY72‐2. Collectively, these findings revealed a PnMYB4a‐PnWRKY8/PnWRKY72‐2 regulatory module involved in the coumarin biosynthetic pathway in P. nigra and provide new insights into the mechanisms of melanization and coloration in bamboo species.

articles.title: Addressing gender bias in sexual and reproductive health care: A scoping review of training tools and interventions
articles.abstract: Gender norms and bias influence how health workers interpret and deliver sexual and reproductive health and rights (SRHR) services, contributing to stigma, discrimination, and inequities in care. This scoping review aimed to map training tools and educational interventions designed to strengthen health workers’ competencies and address gender bias in SRHR care. This scoping review followed the Arksey and O’Malley framework and PRISMA-ScR guidelines. Searches were conducted across multiple databases and organizational websites for literature published between 2000 and November, 2025. Eligible records included manuals, curricula, toolkits, and educational interventions targeting health workers and addressing gender norms, bias, values, or stigma in SRHR care. Data were extracted and synthesized using descriptive and narrative approaches. A total of 128 sources were included, comprising 25 toolkits/manuals and 103 intervention reports representing 100 unique intervention approaches. Together, they covered diverse SRHR domains and used multi-component pedagogical approaches, including didactic instruction (98.4%), reflective or values-based learning (83.2%), and experiential methods such as role-play, simulation, and case-based learning (92%). Most interventions emphasized equitable, person-centered care (98.4%) and 68.8% incorporated gender-transformative elements, while 74.4% included system-level components. Across the mapped literature, gender-transformative and system-level approaches were incorporated to varying degrees, reflecting variability in their integration across educational interventions. Overall, the review highlights the breadth and characteristics of existing training approaches and identifies opportunities for greater integration of gender-transformative and system-level strategies in future SRHR training and evaluation.

articles.title: Adult-sourced fecal microbiota transplantation ameliorates early-life antibiotic-induced intestinal immune stress in juvenile mice associated with the modulation of the TLR4/MyD88 signaling pathway
articles.abstract: Early-life antibiotic (ABX) exposure profoundly disrupts gut microbiota assembly, triggering long-lasting intestinal immune stress. While fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) is a promising intervention, its immunological and ecological mechanisms in the juvenile gut remain underexplored. In this study, juvenile mice were subjected to a broad-spectrum ABX cocktail for 8 days followed by 4 days of adult-sourced FMT. 16S rRNA sequencing (n = 6/group) revealed that ABX drastically altered the microbial landscape, causing a severe relative reduction of core commensals and an opportunistic expansion of Bacteroides. Subsequent molecular analyses on day 13 (n = 3/group) demonstrated that this dysbiosis significantly upregulated the mucosal TLR4/MyD88 signaling axis and effector cytokines IL-17 and IL-22. Strikingly, adult FMT administration effectively attenuated the TLR4 cascade and reduced pro-inflammatory cytokine transcript levels while immunoregulatory IL-10 transcripts remained partially elevated. Ecologically, FMT did not merely revert the gut to its naive juvenile baseline. Instead, it suppressed Bacteroides overgrowth and established a distinctly new, highly complex community enriched with putative mature, adult-signature taxa such as Parabacteroides, Tannerellaceae, and Desulfobacterota. Interestingly, the downregulation of TLR4 occurred concurrently with the engraftment of these Gram-negative, LPS-bearing taxa. Collectively, adult-sourced FMT ameliorates ABX-induced immune stress not by restoring the original microbiota, but by driving the juvenile gut towards a putatively mature, structurally distinct, and potentially immunologically tolerant ecological state.

articles.title: Antimicrobial resistance and molecular characterization of blaCTX-M-producing Escherichia coli isolated from broiler chickens in Peru
articles.abstract: The misuse and overuse of antimicrobials in humans and animals contribute to the selection and dissemination of antimicrobial-resistant (AMR) bacteria. In animal production systems, antimicrobial use is a key driver of the emergence and spread of antimicrobial-resistant bacteria across humans, animals, and the environment within a One Health framework. A total of 300 cloacal swabs were collected from apparently healthy broiler chickens at two poultry collection centers in Lima, Peru. ESBL-producing Escherichia coli were isolated on CHROMagar™ ESBL and identified by conventional biochemical tests. Antimicrobial susceptibility testing was performed using the disk diffusion method according to CLSI guidelines, and ESBL production was phenotypically confirmed. CTX-M groups were detected by qPCR, and whole-genome sequencing (WGS) was performed on selected isolates. Seventy-nine ESBL-producing E. coli isolates were recovered (26.3%; 95% CI: 21.4–31.6). All isolates exhibited multidrug-resistant phenotypes. CTX-M group 1 was detected in 87.3% of isolates and group 9 in 12.7%. WGS analysis identified blaCTX-M-55, blaCTX-M-65, and blaCTX-M-3 distributed across multiple sequence types. Phylogenetic analysis revealed the presence of both closely related clonal clusters and genetically diverse isolates. These findings suggest that poultry production systems may serve as potential reservoirs of multidrug-resistant ESBL-producing E. coli in Peru. Given the study design and limited genomic sampling, the results should be interpreted as preliminary and highlight the need for expanded surveillance within a One Health framework.

articles.title: Application of a concise video to improve patient understanding of tumor genomic testing in community and academic practice settings
articles.abstract: by Deloris J. Veney, Lai Wei, Jaden Miller, Amanda E. Toland, Carolyn J. Presley, Heather Hampel, Tasleem J. Padamsee, Michael J. Bishop, James J. Kim, Shelly R. Hovick, William J. Irvin, Leigha Senter, Daniel G. Stover Purpose Tumor genomic testing (TGT) is standard-of-care for most patients with advanced/metastatic cancer. Despite established guidelines, patient education prior to TGT is frequently omitted. The purpose of this study was to evaluate the impact and durability of a concise 3–4 minute video for patient education prior to TGT in community versus academic sites and across cancer types. Patients and Methods Patients undergoing standard-of-care TGT were enrolled at a tertiary academic institution in three cohorts: Cohort 1-breast cancer; Cohort 2-lung cancer; Cohort 3-other cancers. Cohort 4 consisted of patients with any cancer type similarly undergoing SOC TGT at one of three community cancer centers. Participants completed survey measures prior to video viewing (T1), immediately post-viewing (T2), and after return of TGT results (T3). Outcome measures included: 1) 10-question objective genomic knowledge/understanding (GKU); 2) 10-question video message-specific knowledge (VMSK); 3) 11-question Trust in Physician/Provider (TIPP); 4) perceptions regarding TGT. Results A total of 203 participants completed all survey timepoints. Higher baseline GKU and VMSK scores were significantly associated with higher income and greater years of education. For the primary objective, there was a significant and sustained improvement in VMSK from T1:T2:T3 (Poverall p < 0.0001), with no significant change in GKU (p = 0.41) or TIPP (p = 0.73). This trend was consistent within each cohort (all p ≤ 0.0001). Results for four VMSK questions significantly improved, including impact on treatment decisions, incidental germline findings, and insurance coverage of testing. Conclusions A concise, 3–4 minute, broadly applicable educational video administered prior to TGT significantly and sustainably improved video message-specific knowledge in diverse cancer types and in academic and community settings. This resource is publicly available at http://www.tumor-testing.com, with a goal to efficiently educate and empower patients regarding TGT while addressing guidelines within the flow of clinical practice. Trial registration ClinicalTrials.gov NCT05215769

articles.title: Assessing primary health care facilities in six prioritized Nigerian states: Linking facility readiness with service availability
articles.abstract: Background Nigeria’s poor health indicators have been linked to its dysfunctional Primary Health Care (PHC) facilities. Policy gaps remain in achieving sustainable and equitable provision of PHC for Nigerians. Therefore, this study examined the relationship between health facilities’ readiness and service provision in Nigeria. Methods This was a cross-sectional assessment of 204 PHC facilities enrolled under the Basic Health Care Provision Fund program, in six prioritized states in Nigeria. The facilities were assessed for the provision of ≥80% of the three levels of primary healthcare services—Tier 1, Tier 2, Tier 3—as the outcome variables. The three tiers represent the minimum, intermediate, and comprehensive levels of essential PHC services, respectively, defined under Nigeria’s Minimum Service Package. Health Facility (HF) readiness (explanatory variable) was assessed across six domains, with five of the domains disaggregated into 3 levels (poor, fair, and good). Data were analysed using Principal Component Analysis (PCA) and multivariable logistic regression model (alpha = 0.05). Results The majority (81.9%) of the HFs have a functional management committee, 54.4% have an updated BHCPF annual quality improvement plan, 81.9% have standard operating procedures. While 16.2% met the World Health Organization standard ≥2.3 Health Care Workers (HCWs)/1000 population, none met the Minimum Service Package standard for HCWs across all cadres. The proportion of facilities with good readiness in each domain was: management and finance (42.6%); Health Management Information System tools/registers, supply chain tools/registers, and guidelines (40.2%); infrastructure and utility (33.3%); tracer equipment (34.8%); and tracer drugs (29.9%). The percentage of HF that provided ≥80% services was: Tier 1 (65.2%), Tier 2 (46.6%), and Tier 3 (35.8%); while 31.9% met ≥ 80% across all the service Tiers. Common predictors of providing ≥80% across the service Tiers were tracer drugs and equipment availability. The likelihood of delivering all Tiers of services was higher in HF with fair (aOR=2.38, 95% CI = 1.92-11.14, p < 0.05) and good (aOR=3.93, 95% CI = 1.96-8.49) levels of tracer equipment readiness compared to the poor. Conclusion Good PHC facility readiness supports the provision of health care services in Nigeria. Availability of tracer drugs and equipment predicts the provision of healthcare services in PHC facilities. Investment in PHC facility functionality and prioritization of funds for tracer drugs and equipment will therefore improve service availability and delivery in Nigerian public PHC facilities.

articles.title: Cost comparison of the ShangRing device versus Mogen clamp for early infant male circumcision in Sub-Saharan Africa
articles.abstract: Introduction The World Health Organization (WHO) endorses male circumcision as an effective human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) prevention intervention in settings where the expected impact is greatest, including Sub-Saharan Africa. Data on cost implications of early infant male circumcision (EIMC) are limited. The ShangRing (SR) is a WHO pre-qualified device for circumcision. We sought to perform a comprehensive cost assessment alongside a randomized controlled trial (RCT) of the SR versus the standard of care Mogen clamp (MoC) for EIMC to enable future scale-up towards a cost-effective HIV prevention strategy. Methods We collected resource utilization and economic data as part of an RCT of infants aged 0–60 days old undergoing EIMC in Kenya, Tanzania, and Uganda. Cost data for both the SR and MoC included baseline facility costs, direct costs, and indirect costs. The Decision Makers Program Planning Tool v1.0 was used to perform a direct cost comparison of these two devices. The Goals model was used to compare the costs of EIMC in 2023 using the present value of money to circumcise an adolescent male 15 years from now. Results A total of 1,378 infant males underwent circumcision, 689 via SR and 689 via MoC. The overall cost of a single EIMC in Kenya, Tanzania, and Uganda were 61.30 United States Dollars ($), $47.14, and $64.59 respectively for the SR, and $56.38, $50.43, and $58.57 respectively for the MoC. In Kenya, EIMC would be less expensive based on nominal present costs in 2023 compared to waiting for adolescent circumcision at age 15 years in 2038. This finding is reversed in Tanzania and Uganda. Conclusions The overall cost of EIMC via SR versus MoC is comparable in an RCT. With scale-up utilizing lower level personnel, the cost of SR may be further reduced. The SR is an attractive alternative for future EIMC initiatives in Sub-Saharan Africa to further reduce HIV burden.

articles.title: Experiences of palliative care for patients with pulmonary fibrosis: A qualitative exploration of patients and partners perspectives
articles.abstract: Background Pulmonary fibrosis is often a progressive disease associated with reduced life expectancy and quality of life. Palliative care aims to optimize quality of life for both patients and their informal caregivers. So far, multiple studies have shown unmet palliative care needs in patients with pulmonary fibrosis. This study explores the experiences and needs of patients with pulmonary fibrosis and their partners to identify opportunities for improving palliative care. Methods A qualitative study was performed with focus groups and individual semi-structured interviews with patients and their informal caregivers. Data collection and analysis were performed iteratively. A reflexive thematic analysis was performed, following the methods of Braun and Clarke. Results In total, fifteen patients and 10 informal caregivers participated. One focus group, 13 individual interviews, and 5 dyadic interviews were performed. Two themes were generated: ‘See me as a person’, and ‘Guide me through the trajectory’ with both two subthemes, reflecting the patient and partner perspectives. Patients seek recognition beyond their disease, valuing empathy, open communication, and holistic care. At the same time, both patients and partners express the need for clear guidance and support throughout the medical journey, from diagnosis to end of life care, including emotional, practical, and logistical aspects. Conclusions/discussion Patients and partners experience a ‘one-size-fits-all’ approach to care and reveal several gaps that can be improved. Patients expressed the importance of being acknowledged as a person beyond the disease and being supported in navigating care and anticipating future needs. Partners highlighted the need to be valued and to receive information that enables them to provide care and maintain a sense of control and security.

articles.title: First responders’ experiences and training needs at the scene of a suspected suicide in Ireland: A mixed methods study
articles.abstract: Background First responders are categorised as those who are the first to respond to emergency calls and attend the site of an emergency. They include, but are not limited to police, emergency medical technicians, firefighters, and water safety personnel. First responders play a critical role in suicide postvention, supporting those bereaved by suicide and preventing adverse outcomes. However, many responders feel uncertain about how to effectively support those bereaved by suicide and often lack formal postvention training. This study aimed to explore and understand the experiences and training needs of first responders when attending the scene of a suspected suicide. Methods A mixed-method approach was adopted. A national quantitative survey with first responders was conducted. The impact of previous suicide-related training on suicide literacy, attitudes, and postvention knowledge was analysed using multivariate ANOVA, adjusting for sociodemographic factors. Qualitative data were collected through focus groups and analysed using reflexive thematic analysis. Results A total of 1587 first responders completed surveys. Participants demonstrated positive and non-stigmatising attitudes towards suicide prevention and suicidal individuals, though lower scores were achieved for suicide literacy, postvention knowledge, organisation support, and preparedness. Previous suicide-related training was significantly associated with higher literacy, attitudes, and postvention knowledge, although effect-sizes were small. Qualitative findings from 10 focus groups revealed substantial gaps in training and confidence when responding to suspected suicides. Participants also described the considerable emotional toll of attending the scene and emphasised the need for support in the aftermath. Conclusion Attending the scene of a suspected suicide has an impact on first responders. Limited suicide prevention and postvention training creates challenges, particularly in communicating with the bereaved. These findings underscore the need for comprehensive suicide prevention and postvention training and the allocation of adequate support.

articles.title: Impact of chemical and herbal pre-treatments on shelf life and quality characteristics of dried mango (Mangifera Indica L.) slices
articles.abstract: The present research was carried out to study and determine the effects of chemical and herbal pre-treatments on dried mango slices stored for 180 days under ambient conditions. Discoloration, antioxidants, loss of nutrients, off-flavour, and microbial growth during storage were reported to be concerning parameters. The parameters included in the study were proximate composition, physicochemical analysis, antioxidant analysis, microbial analysis, and color analysis. Score for vitamin C content, antioxidants, and color analysis, was better in pre-treated samples as compared to untreated dried mango samples, but showed a decreasing trend with an increase in storage interval. The analysis conducted at various intervals of storage depicted that the herbal pre-treatments preserved the vitamin C and antioxidant content, and comparable results were recorded. The microbial population in untreated dried mango slices was recorded as more than pre-treated, but was under the permissible limit. Overall, it was concluded that the use of herbal pre-treatments in comparison to chemicals was also effective for the preservation of nutritionally good quality dried fruit.

articles.title: Integrating MaxEnt and MaxNet for climate-resilient habitat restoration: Predicting the ecological niche of Eucalyptus tereticornis in semi-arid landscapes
articles.abstract: Accurate modeling of species distribution is essential for effective biodiversity conservation, afforestation planning, and land-use management. This study presents a comparative analysis of two prominent presence-only species distribution models Maximum Entropy (MaxEnt) and MaxNet to evaluate their efficacy in predicting the ecological niche of Eucalyptus tereticornis in a semi-arid agro-climatic region. A total of 138 georeferenced occurrence records and 25 pseudo-absence points were used, incorporating key environmental variables such as wind speed, temperature range, precipitation, and root zone soil wetness. Both models were optimized and assessed using metrics including accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and the Area Under the Curve (AUC). Results indicate that MaxEnt outperformed MaxNet in most metrics, achieving an accuracy of 87.5% and an AUC of 0.956, compared to MaxNet’s accuracy of 75% and AUC of 0.926. Environmental variable importance varied by model, with MaxEnt highlighting surface pressure and MaxNet emphasizing wind speed. Probability density plots revealed that MaxEnt distinctly identified high suitability zones, whereas MaxNet offered a more balanced, conservative distribution across the landscape. These differences underscore the influence of algorithm design on ecological inference. This study emphasizes the importance of model selection and tuning in species distribution modeling and suggests that integrating outputs from both models can yield robust insights for habitat suitability assessment. The findings support data-driven afforestation strategies, especially under changing climatic conditions, and provide valuable guidance for sustainable plantation efforts involving Eucalyptus tereticornis in similar agro-ecological zones.

articles.title: Integrating Quantum Machine Learning and Ontology Matching for Efficient Semantic Web Services discovery
articles.abstract: by Mohammed Naif Alatawi Existing Semantic Web Service (SWS) discovery approaches based on classical machine learning suffer from limited representational capacity in high-dimensional semantic feature spaces and fail to fully exploit structured ontological knowledge for semantic alignment. This paper addresses these gaps by proposing a hybrid framework that integrates Quantum Machine Learning (QML) models with multi-type Ontology Matching to improve both the accuracy and semantic coverage of SWS discovery. In this paper, we discuss the use of quantum machine learning models and ontological matching techniques for the discovery of Semantic Web Services (SWS) in the Semantic Web. We contrast the effectiveness of different quantum machine learning models with their classical counterparts, including Quantum k-Nearest Neighbors (QkNN), Quantum Decision Trees, Quantum Random Forest, and Quantum Support Vector Machines (QSVM). Our experiments on the OWLS-TC v4 benchmark demonstrate that QSVM achieved the highest post-integration accuracy of 95.1% when paired with graph-based ontology matching, while Quantum Random Forest achieved the highest standalone accuracy of 92.2% without ontology matching. QSVM’s standalone accuracy was 63.0%, reflecting its sensitivity to noisy feature representations in the absence of semantic enrichment; ontology matching consistently recovered and surpassed its performance. Tables 7 through 10 report post-integration results per matching method. Table 13 reports standalone baseline accuracy. These two result sets are distinct and complementary, not contradictory. The application of ontological matching techniques to SWS discovery made the accuracy of SWS discovering much better in both quantum and classical machine learning models. QkNN was the one with the greatest accuracy improvement of 2.8% after adding ontological matching in the mix. Our results indicate that quantum machine learning models, for example Quantum Random Forest (QRF) and Quantum k-Nearest Neighbors (QkNN), are the best candidates for the discovery of SWS. The application of ontological matching methods together with machine learning models is advisable for the improvement of the accuracy of the SWS discovery process. Nevertheless, it should be mentioned that the efficiency of these methods may be different depending on the accuracy and the completeness of the ontologies that are the basis. This research gives a useful information about the possible of quantum machine learning models and ontological matching techniques for enhancing the SWS finding accuracy.

articles.title: Investigation of salivary microRNAs as non-invasive biomarkers for weaning stress in piglets: A preliminary study
articles.abstract: Weaning exposes piglets to abrupt nutritional and environmental changes that induce physiological stress. Saliva, unlike serum or tissue samples, enables repeated and stress-free sampling, making it a practical biological matrix for monitoring early-life adaptation. To evaluate whether salivary microRNAs (miRNAs) can serve as non-invasive indicators of these responses, we profiled miRNA expression in saliva collected from suckling and weaning piglets. Small RNA sequencing was conducted to detect salivary miRNAs and a total of 41 differentially expressed miRNAs (DEMs) were detected between the two groups, with 20 showing highly expression and 21 showing lowly expression in weaning piglets. Several of these DEMs have been previously associated with immune activity, inflammatory regulation, oxidative stress responses, and disease processes, highlighting their biological relevance during the weaning transition. Functional annotation of predicted target genes revealed enrichment in pathways such as TGF-beta, HIF-1, and AMPK signaling, as well as autophagy-related processes. These pathways are known to play key roles in stress adaptation, cellular metabolism, and immune modulation. These findings suggest that salivary miRNA profiles may reflect molecular changes associated with the weaning transition and may serve as candidate non-invasive indicators of physiological stress and health status in piglets. This approach may provide a basis for future development of saliva-based monitoring strategies after validation in larger cohorts and cost-effective targeted assays.

articles.title: Long-term trends of carbon monoxide over the North Pacific upper troposphere from in-situ airplane measurements 1991–2018
articles.abstract: Carbon monoxide (CO) is not a greenhouse gas, but as the dominant sink of the hydroxyl radical it governs the oxidising capacity of the troposphere and so indirectly forces climate. Its trends in the North Pacific upper troposphere matter disproportionately: this is the principal outflow corridor for Asian anthropogenic emissions, the fastest-growing combustion source of the past half-century, yet it has almost no routine ground-based monitoring and satellite retrievals resolve it poorly. We therefore combine in-situ CO measurements from the In-service Aircraft for a Global Observing System (IAGOS; 2012–2018) with earlier in-situ data from NASA/NSF/NOAA campaigns (1991–2019), the Measurements of Pollution in the Troposphere (MOPITT) satellite record, and the Integrated Modelling System (IMS) global chemistry transport model. Trends are computed separately for the monthly maximum, percentile, minimum and mean statistics, using a 10,000-sample perturbation regression framework. Mean CO increases by 0.15 ppb month–1 (18.0 ppb decade–1; 95% CI: −0.02 to 0.32) over 150∘E−140∘W, 45∘N−60∘N and by 0.06 ppb month–1 (7.2 ppb decade–1; 95% CI: −0.04 to 0.16) over 25∘N−45∘N; both intervals include zero but lie predominantly positive. The monthly maximum rises significantly over 25∘N−45∘N, by 0.31 ppb month–1 (37.2 ppb decade–1; 95% CI: 0.06 to 0.57), while the monthly minimum declines weakly. The most polluted air masses over the North Pacific are thus becoming more polluted even as background CO falls. The North Atlantic upper troposphere shows significantly decreasing CO over the same period. The opposing signs track the opposing trajectories of the upwind inventories: Asian emissions rose through most of the record and are lifted efficiently by summertime convection and warm conveyor belts, whereas North American and European emissions fell steadily and the Atlantic receives a larger share of CO-poor stratospheric air.

articles.title: Mechanical-acoustic-optical response properties in uniaxial compression failure of rock masses with different dissolution degrees
articles.abstract: To reveal the effects of dissolution cavities on the mechanical properties and failure mechanisms of surrounding rock, uniaxial compression tests were conducted on rock-like specimens with dissolution degrees of 0%, 5%, 10%, 15%, and 20%. A mechanical-acoustic-optical integrated system combining acoustic emission (AE) and digital image correlation (DIC) was used to characterize mechanical response, AE activity, strain field evolution, and failure behavior. The results indicate that with increasing dissolution degree, compressive strength, elastic modulus, peak axial strain, and deformation modulus decreased by 36.45%, 27.01%, 17.25%, and 41.28%, respectively. Post-peak failure gradually changed from rapid coalescence of a single dominant crack to progressive failure controlled by multiple defects. AE activity shifted from concentrated release near peak strength to continuous release throughout loading, accompanied by earlier crack initiation and an expanded pre-peak damage interval. Crack activity evolved from small scale microcracking to the propagation and coalescence of larger scale cracks. Combined AE and DIC results further showed a transition from axial tensile splitting failure to progressive mixed tensile-shear failure with multiple shear strain concentration zones and coordinated crack coalescence. These findings provide experimental evidence for stability assessment and disaster mitigation of dissolution voided surrounding rock in karst underground engineering.

articles.title: Modeling and experimental validation of dynamic defocusing effects in femtosecond laser ablation of complex gear surfaces
articles.abstract: Femtosecond (fs) laser ablation has emerged as a disruptive technology for the ultra-precision finishing of aerospace face gears. However, its application to complex 3D curved topologies is fundamentally bottlenecked by spatially varying nonlinear laser-material interactions. In this study, we propose a comprehensive 3D nonlinear mathematical model for the fs laser ablation of 18Cr2Ni4WA alloy steel to reveal the mechanism of spatial light field distortion. By discretizing the involute face gear topology, the model explicitly couples the localized incidence angle with dynamic defocusing, elliptical beam stretching, and incidence-dependent Fresnel reflection. Theoretical analyses demonstrate that geometrical variations severely distort the energy-coupling efficiency, with the dynamic defocusing distance being directly proportional to the tangent of the incidence angle (tanθ), drastically attenuating the absorbed volumetric energy density in highly inclined regions. Comparison with CNC gear-center measurements yielded descriptive model–measurement differences with a whole-grid MAE of 0.131μm, an RMSE of 0.137μm, and a maximum absolute difference of 0.255μm (6.53% relative difference). These differences were below the expanded measurement uncertainty and therefore are not interpreted as metrological proof of submicrometer resolution. The spatial error pattern is consistent with, but does not directly prove, enhanced plasma-plume shielding within geometrically confined concave valleys. This study provides a model-based foundation for adaptive multi-axis parameter compensation in advanced aerospace manufacturing.

articles.title: Modelling the impact of migration on FGM/C prevalence and risk in immigrant and diaspora populations
articles.abstract: by Sean Callaghan Previous estimates of the number of women and girls impacted by female genital mutilation and cutting (FGM/C) in the United States (US) failed to account for the impact of migration and acculturation. Similar studies in Europe applied a standard factor to estimate the impact across the entire immigrant population. Several of the resultant European estimates offered two scenarios: no impact, in which prevalence remained unaffected by migration and acculturation, and partial impact, in which risk was assumed to drop by 50% for native-born children. Each of these previous studies was based on adaptations of the extrapolation method, which produces estimates based on the product of three input variables: the immigrant population in the country of residence, the prevalence in the country of origin, and the mitigating impact of migration and acculturation. This paper offers several methodological innovations to better estimate the impact of migration and applies the results to the US. It develops methods to account for selective migration, the mitigating impact of legislation and law enforcement, and it considers the age of migration and the age of cutting to estimate the impact of migration timing on the likelihood that individuals were cut prior to migration. Using these innovations to model the impact of migration on the population in the US suggested that previous studies had underestimated the number of women living with FGM/C, while overestimating the number of girls who were at risk.

articles.title: Operant House: A versatile open-source platform for automated operant conditioning testing of mice in home cages
articles.abstract: Operant conditioning is a powerful method for probing cognitive functions, yet its widespread use is constrained by low throughput, labor-intensive procedures, and high costs. Here, we developed “Operant House,” a low-cost, programmable device equipped with a touchscreen, retractable levers, and a water-reward port, designed to enable automated operant conditioning with minimal experimenter intervention in individually housed mice within their home cages. Although individual home-cage testing requires careful attention to animal welfare, the system permits continuous monitoring through live camera observation and recorded videos. As proof of concept, we implemented two cognitive protocols: a delayed non-match-to-position (DNMTP) test for assessing working memory and a two-choice spatial discrimination (TCSD) test involving working-memory-related processes and behavioral flexibility. Because working memory impairment is one of the earliest clinical features of Alzheimer’s disease (AD), we further applied these protocols to a knock-in mouse model carrying familial AD-associated amyloid precursor protein mutations (AppNL-G-F mice). Using this model, we detected significant working memory deficits as early as 5 months of age. At this age, we also detected subtle and spatially heterogeneous synaptic alterations in the prefrontal cortex, whereas conventional electrophysiological measures were largely preserved. Together, these findings highlight the Operant House as a cost-effective, scalable platform for assessing higher cognitive functions in mice, offering an accessible tool for investigating neurological and neuropsychiatric disease models.

articles.title: Personalized assessment of high-definition slow-oscillatory transcranial direct current stimulation (so-tDCS) in older adults with sleep and subjective cognitive complaints: A study protocol for a randomized clinical trial
articles.abstract: Background Subjective cognitive decline (SCD) is increasingly recognized as an early and potentially modifiable stage in the trajectory of neurodegenerative diseases. In older adults with SCD, untreated sleep disturbances may accelerate the neurodegenerative process, potentially via mechanisms involving amyloid-beta accumulation, and contribute to more rapid cognitive deterioration. Currently, non-pharmacological treatment options that concurrently manage SCD and sleep disturbances remain scarce. High-definition slow-oscillatory transcranial direct current stimulation (so-tDCS) is an emerging, frequency-specific neuromodulation technique designed to enhance brain health and cognition. Methods and design This is a randomized, double-blind, sham-controlled clinical trial. Right-handed Chinese older adults with SCD and sleep disturbances will be randomly assigned to receive either high-definition 0.75 Hz so-tDCS or sham stimulation over a 4-week intervention period, with 40 participants per group. Outcome measures, including galvanic skin response, subjective cognitive complaints, sleep quality, salivary amyloid-beta levels, and domain-specific cognitive performance, will be evaluated at four time points: baseline, week 4 (immediately post‑intervention), and follow‑up at weeks 8 and 12. Conclusions Personalized neurophysiological signals, namely electrode-skin impedance, will be monitored using state-of-the-art measurement during so-tDCS. The successful implement of this signal will provide researchers with access to an “add-on” setting that enables them to easily, quickly and quantitatively evaluate real-time neurophysiological signals, thereby facilitating the incorporation of transcranial brain stimulation into clinical practice. Trial registration ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT07433738

articles.title: Evidence of Galaxy Cluster Rotation and Intrahalo Gas Motions in the Cosmic Microwave Background
articles.abstract: Thomson scattering of cosmic microwave background photons off rotating intracluster gas reveals a secondary anisotropy associated with the rotational kinematic Sunyaev–Zel’dovich effect.

articles.title: Far-from-Equilibrium Thermodynamics of Non-Abelian Thermal States
articles.abstract: Noncommutativity of observables is a defining feature of quantum physics. It plays a fundamental role in the formulation of the uncertainty principle for complementary variables and strongly affects the thermodynamic behavior of systems with noncommuting, that is, non-Abelian, conserved quantities. We here derive extensions of the first and second laws of thermodynamics, including nonequilibrium fluctuation relations, for driven quantum systems. We identify an additional non-Abelian contribution to the energy and entropy balances, without which these relations would be violated. This contribution can be harnessed to enhance both work extraction and nonequilibrium currents compared to what is achieved in commuting thermodynamics. These results demonstrate that noncommutativity is a potentially valuable thermodynamic resource.

articles.title: High-Performance Quantum Frequency Conversion from Ultraviolet to Telecom Band
articles.abstract: Quantum frequency conversion (QFC) is essential for bridging the spectral gap between stationary qubits and low-loss optical communication channels. Practicable QFC interfaces connecting ultraviolet and telecommunication bands are of great significance but have remained elusive, constrained by the dual challenges of a high-performance frequency converter and effective noise suppression in short-wavelength pumping configurations. We address this by demonstrating the phase-matching mechanism with domain defects and differential-tuning behavior of the spontaneous parametric down-conversion noises. Based on a quantitative analysis of performance degradation induced by domain defects, we propose specific fabrication guidelines and experimentally achieve an ultrahigh normalized conversion efficiency of $839%/(\mathrm{W}\text{ }{\mathrm{cm}}^{2})$ for the fundamental guided mode in thin-film lithium niobate waveguides. Meanwhile, we reveal a new noise control mechanism for short-wavelength pumping by utilizing the differential-tuning behaviors of difference-frequency generation and spontaneous parametric down-conversion processes. Then a single-stage QFC from 393 nm to the telecom C band with a record-high external efficiency of 28.8% and an ultralow noise level of 35 counts per second is achieved experimentally. The proposed mechanisms would enable other QFCs with higher efficiency and lower noise, advancing the development of scalable quantum networks. Furthermore, it holds significant potential for driving progress in both classical and integrated nonlinear photonics.

articles.title: Magnon Kerr Effect in a Magnetic Thin Film Strongly Coupled to a Microwave Resonator
articles.abstract: Progress in cavity magnonics relies on tunable nonlinearities in magnon-photon interactions for controlling magnon dynamics and frequency conversion. Here, we demonstrate the magnon Kerr effect in anisotropic magnonic systems comprising iron garnet thin films coupled to a loop-gap microwave resonator. The strong shape anisotropy, combined with strain, enhances the magnon Kerr effect compared to a sphere of equivalent volume by up to 3 orders of magnitude, while the cavity enables sensitive probing of magnetization dynamics. We demonstrate continuous tunability of the magnitude and sign of the Kerr shift by controlling the static orientation of the magnetization, in excellent agreement with theory. Our findings demonstrate a scalable approach to enhancing Kerr anharmonicity in hybrid magnon-photon systems while preserving coherent magnon-photon interactions.

articles.title: Multipartite Mixed-Species Entanglement over a Quantum Network
articles.abstract: We generate multipartite entangled states of two, three, and four matter qubits, where the entanglement is distributed over macroscopic distances via a photonic network link. Trapped-ion $^{88}{\mathrm{Sr}}^{+}$ qubits are entangled directly via an optical fibre link, and the entanglement is subsequently extended to $^{43}{\mathrm{Ca}}^{+}$ memory qubits cotrapped in each network node, using local mixed-species logic gates. We create remotely entangled ${\mathrm{Sr}}^{+}\text{\ensuremath{-}}{\mathrm{Ca}}^{+}$ and ${\mathrm{Ca}}^{+}\text{\ensuremath{-}}{\mathrm{Ca}}^{+}$ states, as well as mixed-species Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger (GHZ) states of up to four qubits. We demonstrate storage of the remotely entangled memory qubits for $\ensuremath{\sim}10\text{ }\text{ }\mathrm{s}$, more than $100\ifmmode\times\else\texttimes\fi{}$ the state creation time.

articles.title: Perturbative Approach to Symmetric Mass Generation
articles.abstract: The Landau paradigm has been a powerful framework for understanding phase transitions involving spontaneous symmetry breaking. In contrast, phase transitions between two symmetric phases, where neither phase breaks any symmetry, remain less explored. One intriguing class of such transitions involves ``symmetric mass generation'' (SMG), where interactions drive a transition from a gapless symmetric phase to a gapped symmetric phase. In this Letter, we develop a controlled perturbative approach to study a class of such transitions, based on an $\ensuremath{\epsilon}$ expansion around the critical dimension where the SMG-inducing interaction becomes marginal. Applying this method to two distinct models, we identify a single-parameter-tuned transition in each case, which we conjecture captures the universal critical behavior of the SMG transition in these models. We compute universal quantities associated with these transitions.

articles.title: Photon-Statistics Time Delay in Quantum Attosecond Photoelectron Interferometry
articles.abstract: Photoelectron interference can reveal otherwise hidden properties of quantum light through an apparent attosecond time shift.

articles.title: Mixed-State Phases from Local Reversibility
articles.abstract: Researchers establish a framework using local reversibility to correctly classify phases of matter in open and noisy quantum systems.

articles.title: Tripartite Haar Random State Has No Bipartite Entanglement
articles.abstract: Researchers demonstrate that bipartite Einstein-Podolsky-Rosen entanglement cannot be distilled from tripartite Haar random states by local operations.

articles.title: England’s “Babies Bill” explained: what it promises and what it needs to succeed
articles.abstract: What is the “Babies Bill”?Technically called the Infants, Parents and Carers Bill (but nicknamed the Babies Bill), this is a proposed piece of legislation to protect in law the services provided in England for infants, parents, and carers during a child’s first 1001 days.Extensive research shows that this period is critical to laying the foundations for lifelong emotional and physical wellbeing.The bill proposes that the government should have a legal duty to ensure access to services such as health visiting, midwifery checks, maternity services, infant feeding, and perinatal mental health support. It has been introduced as a private member’s bill by the Conservative MP Desmond Swayne.The bill passed its second reading in the Commons last month and faces its committee stage this week, where MPs will scrutinise the details and propose amendments. It must then face the Lords and other possible amendments before it can become law.What is the bill...

articles.title: From paediatrician to primary teacher: seeing children’s behaviour through a new lens
articles.abstract: I was an NHS paediatrician for over a decade, but it wasn’t until I left medicine and retrained as a primary schoolteacher that I realised how misaligned some of my attitudes were with the reality of children’s lives. I’d spent 15 years viewing children’s behaviour through a medical model of deficit and had completely overlooked the wider picture or what children and their families most needed from me. When children present with “challenging behaviour,” emotional distress, and difficulties attending school, doctors often see their role as making a diagnosis or needing to “fix” the problem. Healthcare professionals need to rethink our response and collaborate with parents and schools to better support the lived reality of families.As a paediatrician, I took histories from children who struggled to cope in mainstream classrooms and whose behaviour was sometimes violent or aggressive. I listened and nodded, perplexed at the mismatch between the parents’ accounts...

articles.title: Health equity in Scotland
articles.abstract: The UK is unhealthy. For healthy life expectancy, it ranks 20th out of 21 high income countries—only the US is lower.1 Within the UK, health in Scotland is worse than in England, Wales, and Northern Ireland.2 In Scotland, a steep social gradient exists: the more deprived the area, the worse people’s health.2 The gap in life expectancy between the most and the least deprived areas is 13.6 years for women and 16.3 for men.2 The gap in healthy life expectancy is even bigger.2It is worth asking what Scotland should do to achieve better health. It has progressive policies, excellent public health scholars and practitioners, collaborative planning, and a focus on community empowerment and high quality data that all have a bearing on the problems of health equity. Child poverty is lower in Scotland than in England.3 Actions such as minimum unit pricing have made a difference to Scotland’s alcohol related...

articles.title: Marmot review for Scotland sets out blueprint to reverse widening health inequalities
articles.abstract: Scotland requires a radical new approach to tackling health inequalities that includes redistributing funding to areas of greatest need, a landmark review has recommended.1The review, led by global expert in health inequalities Michael Marmot, says that Scotland’s efforts to reduce its widening health gap are being undermined by “structural inequalities” in power, money, and resources, which shape the conditions in which people live such as their income, housing, work, and communities.The report, A Fairer, Healthier Scotland, is based on work carried out over the past two years by the University College London Institute of Health Equity, led by Marmot, and Public Health Scotland, under the umbrella of the Collaboration for Health Equity in Scotland.It explored why Scotland’s relatively progressive policies and strong ambition for health equity have not delivered better health for everyone. There is now a life expectancy difference of 13.6 years in females and 16.3 years in males...

articles.title: Plague: Russian authorities must show “full transparency” over lab worker’s death, World Medical Association says
articles.abstract: The World Medical Association (WMA) has called on Russian authorities to share “all available information” about the death of a laboratory technician who worked at a plague research institute, saying the country’s lack of transparency is “of great concern.”1Darya Shipilova, who worked at the Irkutsk Antiplague Research Institute in the Siberia region of Russia, died on 2 October, two days after being admitted to hospital for severe pneumonia and placed on a ventilator.2Russian officials initially avoided publicly referring to plague. But Alexei Tsydenov, head of the neighbouring republic of Buryatia, said that the woman may have died from an unspecified form of plague.3The World Health Organization (WHO) has described the lab worker’s cause of death as “pneumonia of undetermined aetiology” and said that Russia has informed the agency that “no case of plague had been registered recently in Irkutsk Oblast.”4Russia has also said that laboratory testing of contacts has detected...

articles.title: UN adopts political declaration on pandemic preparedness—but without crucial consensus
articles.abstract: A hotly contested political declaration on pandemic prevention, preparedness, and response has been adopted by the UN.But officials have failed to agree on a fundamental part of the accord that would outline how the benefits from products created using shared pathogen data should be distributed.The text of the declaration was expected to be approved by consensus at a high level meeting on 25 September. But despite months of negotiations members were unable to agree on the terms of the Pathogen Access and Benefit Sharing (PABS) annex.Without the PABS annex being adopted the accord as whole cannot be fully formalised and is not legally binding.Talks on the annex have stalled amid a stand-off between developing countries and some high income European nations together with the United States. During negotiations, coalitions representing low and middle income countries in Africa, Latin America, and Asia said that they had shared virus samples and data...

articles.title: [Correspondence] Prioritising the future of youth is an urgent political choice
articles.abstract: Health professionals and policy makers should fully support the students currently protesting in France.1 Apart from the regrettable outbursts of violence happening during protests, this movement reflects the anger of youth at decades of successive policies, both at national and global levels, which have progressively widened educational inequalities. These educational inequalities have led to a cascade of further inequalities: access to employment and type of employment (manual or office-based); level of income—in the past 20 years, the Gini index in France increased from 0·27 to 0·30;2 living conditions and the environment (quality of food, water, noise, air, etc); and, eventually, health inequities.

articles.title: Degenerative cervical myelopathy: early detection and the potential for preventing disability
Emerging landscape of antibody–drug conjugates in lung cancer: a clinical review
articles.abstract: Lung cancer is a heterogeneous disease, and while targeted therapies and immunotherapies have improved patient outcomes, 5-year overall survival remains poor at approximately 20%. Antibody–drug conjugates (ADCs) target tumors using a targeted antibody that delivers a cytotoxic payload with clinically proven antitumor activity, and over a dozen ADCs are under consideration for solid tumors. Recent clinical trial data in metastatic non-small cell lung cancer have led to FDA approval of three ADCs: trastuzumab deruxtecan for patients with human epidermal growth factor receptor 2-mutated disease, telisotuzumab vedotin for MET-overexpressing tumors, and datopotamab deruxtecan for patients with epidermal growth factor receptor-mutated disease. In this article, we review the trajectory of individual ADC targets in lung cancer, describe the latest clinical trial results, and discuss future innovations in ADC therapies and potential mechanisms of resistance.

articles.title: A Rate Transfer Method: Convergence Rates in Stochastic Gradient Descent via Stochastic Calculus
articles.abstract: We develop a rate-transfer method that converts finite-time Lyapunov estimates for an associated stochastic differential equation (SDE) into finite-time convergence bounds for stochastic gradient algorithms. Under generic moment and smoothness conditions, the convergence analysis of the stochastic gradient method reduces to a calculus argument verifying a Lyapunov generator inequality for the SDE. The method recovers established rates for classical stochastic gradient methods and provides a way to establish convergence rates for new optimization algorithms through calculus arguments applied to their associated SDEs.

articles.title: AIRRI: Towards a Human-Readable, Machine-Resistant Reading Interface
articles.abstract: The rapid advancement of image-to-text extraction systems and large language models (LLMs) poses new challenges for educational assessment by making assignment materials easy to transcribe and solve with minimal human effort. To address this problem, we present AIRRI (Artificial Intelligence Resilient Reading Interface), a framework for generating machine-resistant educational content, a dataset of higher-education assignments for evaluation, and an initial evaluation of the human readability of AIRRI machine-resistant text designs. AIRRI employs two categories of machine-resistance techniques. First, AIRRI applies image transformations including character spacing, word spacing, line spacing, character opacity variation, stripe overlays, and image noise. Second, AIRRI applies decision-based adversarial attacks: RayS, SurFree, and ADBA. We evaluate AIRRI against three image-to-text systems: Tesseract, EasyOCR, and the transformer-based GOT-OCR2 model. Our results show that AIRRI substantially degrades automated text extraction performance. AIRRI increased character error rates for EasyOCR (6.9% to 55.9%), Tesseract (2.3% to 100.0%), and GOT-OCR2 (30.7% to 48.1%). Word error rates increased for EasyOCR (24.9% to 96.7%) and Tesseract (10.7% to 100.0%). Among the evaluated decision-based attacks, ADBA consistently produced the largest degradation in image-to-text performance, while RayS and SurFree produced more moderate reductions. EasyOCR and Tesseract were generally more susceptible to both image-based and adversarial perturbations than the transformer-based GOT-OCR2 model. Our findings suggest that AIRRI can significantly reduce the reliability of image-to-text-to-LLM workflows, increasing the effort required for AI-assisted assignment completion.

articles.title: AesCode: Aesthetic Code Generation with Decoupled Cross-Modal Rewards
articles.abstract: Generating information-rich visual artifacts such as slides, posters, and dashboards as code is appealing because the outputs are structured, editable, and verifiable. Yet code models cannot see how their choices of layout and color come together on the canvas, often limiting spatial planning and aesthetic quality. Image generators excel at visual design but can misrender requested content, making their outputs unreliable targets for direct reproduction. We therefore introduce AesCode, which generates code grounded in the content prompt while using an image generated from the same prompt as an aesthetic guidance. To do so, AesCode represents the target as a design graph that describes the whole canvas and makes each property attributable. From this graph, we derive complementary cross-modal rewards: deterministic verifiers score properties parsable from code and rendering, while a VLM judge assesses the non-parsable ones with a sample-specific Visual Graph Rubric (VGR) tied to graph elements and relations. We optimize these decoupled rewards through reinforcement learning with per-channel normalization to jointly improve spatial planning, aesthetic quality, and verifiable correctness. To evaluate this setting, we build a benchmark that scores verifiable correctness and visual quality separately, with visual scores highly consistent with human judgments. We find that reference images substantially improve the visual quality of code generated by existing models, and ablations show that AesCode benefits from references both as model input and as a source of visual rewards. Relative to same-scale Qwen3-VL baselines given the same references, AesCode-8B and AesCode-32B improve visual quality by 31.1 and 22.4 percentage points, reaching scores comparable to those of closed-source frontier models such as GPT-5.5 and Claude Opus 4.8.

articles.title: BLADE: Auditing Information Use for Failure Attribution in LLM Multi-Agent Systems
articles.abstract: Large language model multi-agent systems extend individual agents' capabilities through collaboration across specialized roles, tools, and workflows. Yet collaboration makes failures harder to diagnose: one agent may misinterpret a correct result while others carry the mistake forward. Failure attribution therefore seeks to identify the responsible agent and decisive error step. Recent methods trace dependencies, but knowing where information came from is not the same as knowing where it went wrong. We introduce BLADE (Blame Localization via Audited Dependency Evidence), a training-free framework that moves beyond tracing information to auditing its use. Using Jev for structured probabilistic judgments, BLADE uses dependency probabilities to select relevant source-decision handoffs for auditing. At these handoffs, it examines whether receiving decisions use their sources faithfully and within task requirements, distinguishing error introduction, propagation, and repair. These findings inform a global diagnosis that considers all execution steps. Without reference answers, BLADE achieves the best or tied-best step accuracy among eight strategies under a shared Jev decision interface on 1,228 failed runs across five Who&When and Who&When Pro subsets, outperforming All-at-once by 2.2-11.1 percentage points. Making responsibility evidence explicit offers a path toward more interpretable and reliable agentic systems.

articles.title: Back-Translation Still Matters: Leveraging Monolingual Data for Low-Resource Machine Translation with LLMs
articles.abstract: Pre-trained Large Language Model (LLMs) are effective on many tasks in zero-shot and few-shot settings. For machine translation of low-resource languages, the obvious options are few-shot prompting and fine-tuning on a small parallel set. We ask: what if moderate amounts of low-resource monolingual data are also available? We argue that, rather than continued pretraining, a more effective use of this data is the pre-LLM era technique of back-translation (BT). The current fine-tuned LLM translates monolingual sentences in each language, and the resulting pairs train it in the reverse direction. Updates on the parallel set are interleaved for stable learning. With 1K parallel pairs on Odia and Swahili, BT beats continued pretraining into the low-resource language by 7.7 to 16.4 XCOMET-XXL points in domain. With beam-decoded intermediate translations, it also beats a model with 10 time more parallel data. In-context examples retrieved from the parallel data further improve BT. We also analyze the source, quality and amount of monolingual text. Across five low-resource languages, with Hindi as a high-resource control, and two 3B backbones, BT improves translation into the low-resource language by 16 to 173% XCOMET-XXL over parallel-only fine-tuning. Blind human evaluation on Odia and Sanskrit agrees with the automatic metrics.

articles.title: Beyond the Verdict: Agentic Code Judging with Verifiable Feedback
articles.abstract: Test-time scaling for large language models (LLMs) can involve generating multiple candidate solutions for selection or revising an earlier attempt. To guide selection and revision, we need a verifier that can estimate candidate correctness and provide evidence of failure. In competitive programming, however, official judging systems provide authoritative verdicts under finite submission budgets, without revealing failure explanations or failing inputs. To provide informative feedback without consuming official submissions, we formulate a task in which a model judges and diagnoses a candidate program using only the problem statement and source code, with generated counterexamples serving as checkable evidence. To evaluate this task, we build USACO-JUDGE from the USACO 2026 contests, using accepted and unaccepted programs written by human experts and multiple LLMs. We then train ARBITER, a 35B mixture-of-experts (MoE) agentic verifier, with reinforcement learning in a generic execution sandbox. Training raises counterexample success on incorrect programs from 40.61% to 62.67% and mean binary verdict accuracy on USACO-JUDGE from 71.41% to 87.41%, approaching frontier verification performance. Beyond verification, ARBITER outperforms baselines in both code selection and refinement. In an IOI 2026 case study, ARBITER-guided refinement raises GPT-OSS-120B's expected score above the gold-medal threshold under the official submission limit.

articles.title: Bytes to Threats: Byte-Sequence Transformer For Malware Detection
articles.abstract: Existing malware detection approaches heavily rely on handcrafted features derived from static or dynamic analysis of the executable files. These methods require specialized domain expertise, dedicated analysis tools, and time-consuming analysis, which limits their scalability and robustness in the face of the increasing complexity and diversity of modern malware. Consequently, there is a growing interest in approaches that operate directly on raw bytes, which contain rich semantic and structural information. However, capturing long-range dependencies within executable files remains challenging for conventional static and CNN-based methods. This paper presents MalwareFormer, a transformer-based, byte-level malware detection framework that operates directly on raw bytes, without requiring domain knowledge or feature extraction. MalwareFormer achieves an accuracy of 98.35%, a balanced accuracy of 98.32%, a macro-F1 of 98.32%, and a false positive rate of 1.94%, outperforming both baselines across all threshold-dependent classification metrics and demonstrating that transformers provide a powerful and scalable approach for byte-level malware detection.

articles.title: Cepheid: Decoupling Scale from Structure for Cross-Family Motion Completion
articles.abstract: Sparse-to-dense motion completion recovers dense mesh motion from sparse vertex displacements. Residual priors trained on one geometry family frequently fail to beat parameter-free harmonic extension off-family. Moreover, cross-family training meets a scaling barrier: residual amplitude varies by more than an order of magnitude across geometry families and collapses as observations become denser. Since this scale depends on unknown target motion, it cannot be measured directly at test time. We decouple residual structure from physical scale by learning a dimensionless prior, estimating amplitude from observables and a lightweight correction fitted only on training sources. Our unified model surpasses harmonic extension across all evaluated families, including unseen cloth and legged bodies, without skeletons, registration, or cross-mesh correspondence. The same prior applies without retraining to point-tracked animal video and a robot grasping a soft body. Project page: https://su-terry.github.io/cepheid-website/

articles.title: ChunkAct: Action Chunking for Agentic Robotics
articles.abstract: Agentic robotics places a large language model (LLM) agent in the robot control loop, where it composes perception, motion, and vision-language-action (VLA) tools under the guidance of a memory and thereby generalizes to new tasks without retraining. This generality comes at a steep price in efficiency. Every primitive requires a round of LLM reasoning over the full interaction history, so the cost of an episode grows with the number of primitives. We find this reasoning largely redundant: once a sub-goal is chosen, its primitives follow a routine already prescribed by memory. We present ChunkAct, which introduces action chunking to agentic robotics. Online, a single call launches a chunk of chained primitives, which executes autonomously and returns control only upon failure. Offline, ChunkAct compiles the memory into these chunks, so execution is memory-free at test time and the planner is reserved for decisions that require reasoning. LLM computation therefore scales with the number of decisions rather than the number of primitives. On LIBERO-Pro, ChunkAct improves task success by 5.0 points over the state of the art in agentic robotics while requiring 2.9x fewer LLM calls, 4.4x fewer input tokens, and 2.3x fewer output tokens.

articles.title: Code-Switching Detection via Language-Selective Dimensions in Speech Foundation Models
articles.abstract: Code-switching (CS), the alternation between languages within an utterance, is common in multilingual speech but underrepresented in pretraining corpora. Increasing CS coverage requires finding relevant utterances in large speech collections so that they can be included in training data. One way to find such utterances is to transcribe the speech and detect language alternation in the text, but this depends on obtaining accurate multilingual transcriptions. We propose a lightweight method that detects CS directly from speech. It uses frame-level language information in pretrained speech encoders to determine whether both languages are present within an utterance. Specifically, we identify language-selective hidden-state dimensions using monolingual recordings and aggregate their frame-level activations into a CS prediction. With a small CS set used to tune a decision rule, we show that the Whisper-small encoder achieves a mean F1 of $0.798$ across 14 language pairs in CS-FLEURS, compared with $0.776$ for a CNN and $0.751$ for a HuBERT linear baseline trained for monolingual language identification. Our findings suggest that pretrained speech encoders already encode the information needed to identify CS utterances, and they provide a lightweight tool for building more representative multilingual corpora.

articles.title: Data Free Training of Diffusion Models for Lattice Field Theories
articles.abstract: Sampling equilibrium field configurations remains a major computational bottleneck in lattice field theory, motivating the development of generative samplers that can produce independent configurations.
