articles.abstract: All previously reported Ge(II) dications have remained chemically dormant, their reactivity confined to simple coinage metal coordination—a consequence of cationization‐induced lone pair contraction that renders the Ge center inaccessible to substrates. We report that dual σ/π‐donating carbodicarbene (CDC) ligands directly counteract this contraction, yielding [(CDC)2Ge][OTf]2 (4), the first two‐coordinate Ge(II) dication to display broad reactivity beyond coinage metal coordination. Crystallographic and computational analysis reveal a delocalized 3c‐4e C‐Ge‐C moiety and a less contracted Ge lone pair with retained Ge‐centered LUMO, underpinning an unprecedented reactivity profile encompassing 1,1‐oxidative addition, [1 + 4] cycloaddition, selenium insertion, and cooperative C–S bond activation. As a Ge‐donor ligand, 4 coordinates to Rh, Ir, and Ag with donor strength comparable to that of IMes and forms geminal bimetallic complex 8, featuring a rare noncluster Ag–Ge–Ag three‐center two‐electron bonding motif. These results establish CDC‐based low‐coordination stabilization as a productive strategy for accessing structurally simple yet reactive main‐group dications.

articles.title: Cerium Valence‐Gated Interfacial Exciton Reconstruction for Fluorescence Modulation
articles.abstract: Interfacial electronic coupling plays a decisive role in governing excited‐state evolution and signal transduction in optoelectronic systems, yet dynamically adaptive interfaces driven by valence‐state evolution remain largely unexplored in fluorescent sensing platforms. Herein, an Eu‐functionalized Ce‐MOF/CTF heterointerface is constructed to establish a valence‐responsive optoelectronic system for dual‐mode H2O2 sensing. Upon oxidative stimulation, the Ce‐MOF/CTF heterointerface dynamically reconstructs the interfacial charge‐transfer network through Ce3+/Ce4+ valence‐state evolution, enabling modulation of electron migration across the interface and synchronously regulating Eu‐centered luminescence, CTF‐derived fluorescence, and nanozyme‐mediated catalytic outputs. The results reveal that oxidative valence evolution induces adaptive interfacial electronic redistribution and excited‐state pathway reconstruction, thereby amplifying microscopic electronic perturbations into programmable fluorescence–catalytic responses. Beyond conventional sensing systems dominated by static emissive centers, this work demonstrates that adaptive interface states can function as dynamic optoelectronic units for intelligent signal transduction. Furthermore, the interfacial optical response can be integrated into flexible electrospun membranes and machine‐learning‐assisted visual recognition systems, enabling portable dual‐mode visual sensing. This work provides a new perspective for constructing adaptive optoelectronic interfaces through valence‐state engineering and establishes a general framework for next‐generation intelligent sensing platforms.

articles.title: Charge‐Delocalizing sp‐Hybridized COFs for Selective H2O2 Electrosynthesis
articles.abstract: Hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) is an important oxidant for chemical manufacturing, environmental remediation, and biomedical applications, yet its industrial production still relies mainly on the energy‐intensive anthraquinone process. Electrochemical H2O2 synthesis via the two‐electron oxygen reduction reaction (2e− ORR) provides a sustainable alternative but is often hindered by sluggish charge transport and insufficient O2 activation. Here, we develop a bond‐hybridization strategy by incorporating sp‐hybridized acetylene units into the vertex or linker of covalent organic frameworks (COFs). The resulting COFs feature extended π‐conjugation, enhanced charge delocalization, and electronically polarized pores, thereby strengthening O2 adsorption and activation. Compared with sp2‐dominated analogues, these sp‐hybridized COFs show faster charge‐transfer kinetics, higher H2O2 selectivity, and improved 2e− ORR activity. In a flow cell, the optimized catalyst delivers an H2O2 production rate of 27.8 mol g−1 h−1 and a peak Faradaic efficiency of 91.7% at 150 mA cm−2. Mechanistic analyses combining electronic‐structure calculations and in situ vibrational spectroscopy reveal that sp hybridization reshapes frontier‐orbital distributions and local charge density, thereby coupling framework‐wide charge delocalization with favorable O2 adsorption and *OOH stabilization. These results establish bond hybridization as a molecular‐level design parameter for catalytic selectivity in COFs, extending framework engineering beyond conventional functional‐group and building‐block modification.

articles.title: Controlled Presodiation of Sodium‐Ion Cathode via Electron Cloud Engineering
articles.abstract: Chemical presodiation offers a promising pathway to compensate sodium deficiency in cathode and anode materials, thereby enhancing the usable energy density of sodium‐ion batteries. This approach is particularly critical for P2‐ and tunnel‐type cathodes, such as Na0.44MnO2, where the as‐synthesized materials typically exhibit a 50%–60% sodium deficiency. However, conventional presodiation reagents possess excessively high reductive potential, often leading to oversodiation, structural degradation, and compromised electrode reversibility. Here, we report a rational electron‐cloud engineering strategy to precisely control the sodium chemical potential of presodiation agents. Guided by Hückel's rule, we demonstrate that tailoring π‐conjugation size and introducing electron‐withdrawing groups enables the adjustment of sodium chemical potential via a balance of conjugative and inductive effects. We identify 1‐indanone as an optimal presodiation reagent, capable of delivering sodium to Na0.44MnO2 cathodes without any oversodiation. The resulting electrodes exhibit fully restored sodium inventories, an unprecedented first‐cycle Coulombic efficiency of ∼100%, and improved capacity retention over 350 cycles compared to untreated controls. Our findings establish a versatile framework for controlling sodium delivery in chemical presodiation, providing a new avenue for the design of next‐generation sodium‐ion batteries with enhanced stability and performance.

articles.title: Discovery of a Potent and Selective First‐In‐Class Antagonist of GPR15 With In Vivo Anti‐Obesity Activity
articles.abstract: GPR15 (G Protein‐coupled Receptor 15), an atypical chemokine receptor, is implicated in the pathogenesis of multiple diseases, yet small‐molecule GPR15 antagonists remain undeveloped. Herein, we identify and characterize YL410, the first‐in‐class potent and selective GPR15 antagonist. In the cAMP‐GloSensor assay, YL410 inhibits GPR15 with an IC50 of 0.027 ± 0.005 µM, and displays high selectivity against a panel of related GPCRs and kinases. It suppresses GPR15L‐induced Jurkat T‐cell migration, and exhibits favorable pharmacokinetics and acceptable safety. Molecular docking, replicated molecular dynamics simulations, quantitative contact analyses, and mutagenesis experiments support a plausible orthosteric binding model for YL410, maintained by a reproducible network of polar and hydrophobic contacts, which rationalizes its potent antagonism and observed structure–activity relationships (SAR). Complementary AI‐based structure predictions (AlphaFold3, Chai‐1, and Boltz) recapitulated the energetically accessible orthosteric poses but not the dynamically stable pose selected by the MD simulations, underscoring the importance of kinetic‐stability validation in antagonist pose selection. Notably, in a diet‐induced obesity (DIO) mouse model, YL410 administration induced significant weight loss and exerted blood glucose‐lowering effects. Collectively, this study presents the first potent, selective, and in vivo efficacious GPR15 antagonist, providing new insights into the development of therapeutics for the treatment of obesity.

articles.title: Double‐Volcano Catalytic Response in Furfural Reductive Amination Over Inverse Ni─Al Catalysts
articles.abstract: Reductive amination of aldehydes and ketones to primary amines is an important route for biomass valorization, yet achieving efficient synergy between substrate and hydrogen activation in cascade reactions remains challenging. Herein, we construct a compositionally tunable Ni─Al catalyst system whose architecture evolves from conventional Ni/Al2O3 to inverse Al2O3/Ni. This structural evolution gives rise to an unusual double-volcano catalytic behavior in furfural reductive amination. Two activity maxima are identified over 30Ni/Al2O3 and inverse Al2O3/90Ni, respectively, with the optimal Al2O3/90Ni catalyst delivering 98.5% furfurylamine yield and a space-time yield of 65 mmol gcat −1 h−1 under mild conditions. Adsorption studies, initial-rate kinetic isotope effect and reaction-order measurements, apparent activation-energy analysis, and in situ infrared spectroscopy indicate that the double-volcano behavior reflects the coupled evolution of catalyst composition and architecture and a composition-dependent balance between Lewis-acid-assisted intermediate formation and hydrogen-dependent intermediate conversion. Hydrogen-dependent steps exert a stronger kinetic influence over 30Ni/Al2O3 than over Al2O3/90Ni, while the inverse catalyst exhibits enhanced H2 adsorption and activation and more rapid Schiff base conversion. These results indicate a shift in the dominant kinetic limitation between the two catalysts and provide a framework for designing efficient non-noble-metal catalysts for multifunctional cascade reactions involving coupled substrate and hydrogen activation.

articles.title: Engineering Polar Nanoregions in COFs via Controlled Symmetry Breaking Toward Piezocatalysis
articles.abstract: To address the limited piezocatalytic activity of covalent organic frameworks (COFs) arising from high structural symmetry and rapid charge recombination, an imine‐linked COFs (TFB‐TAPT) is synthesized by Schiff‐base condensation of 1,3,5‐triformylbenzene (TFB) and 2,4,6‐tri(4‐aminophenyl)‐1,3,5‐triazine (TAPT), followed by partial substitution of amino ligands with 1H,1H‐undecafluorohexylamine (UFHA) through a building‐block exchange strategy to afford TFB‐TAPT‐FA. This approach achieves controlled symmetry breaking with precise polar group distribution, without the lattice disruption caused by asymmetric monomers in one‐pot methods. The resulting randomly oriented polar nanoregions exhibit relaxation behavior, collectively generating a strong piezoelectric response under external stimuli. Piezoresponse force microscopy (PFM) measurements indicate that TFB‐TAPT‐FA has a piezoelectric coefficient of 140 pm/V, 2.5 times that of TFB‐TAPT. This amplification of the electromechanical response arises from the polar nanoregions, as evidenced by its higher calculated dipole moment (5.68 Debye). Consequently, TFB‐TAPT‐FA achieves an impressive piezocatalytic hydrogen production rate of 3.8 mmol g−1 h−1, marking a 17‐fold improvement over TFB‐TAPT. Notably, TFB‐TAPT‐FA enables efficient hydrogen production without cocatalysts or heterojunctions. More broadly, the introduction of polar nanoregions similarly enhances the performance of other imine‐linked COFs, demonstrating a potentially general strategy for designing piezocatalysts through nanoscale polarization engineering in COFs.

articles.title: Gold Single‐Atom Catalysts Enable Selective Shuttle Hydrochlorination of Alkynes
articles.abstract: Shuttle catalysis enables the transfer of reactive functional groups without relying on highly corrosive reagents. However, it remains largely confined to homogeneous systems, where catalyst recovery and reuse are often challenging. Here, we report a recyclable gold single‐atom catalyst (SAC) supported on activated carbon (AC) for the selective shuttle hydrochlorination of terminal alkynes to vinyl chlorides, which are key intermediates in pharmaceutical synthesis. Spectroscopic and catalytic studies indicate that the combination of Au(I) single atoms with the AC carrier is essential for the unique chemo‐ and stereoselectivity observed. This heterogeneous system displays broad substrate compatibility, including sterically hindered alkynes, heterocycles, acid‐labile groups, and drug‐derived substrates. Upon reuse, gradual aggregation of gold single atoms into nanoparticles leads to activity losses, but the associated speciation changes are reversible by oxidative redispersion, while quantitative metal retention ensures recoverability. Overall, this study demonstrates how to extend heterogeneous SACs to shuttle catalysis, highlighting the complementary reactivity and distinct catalyst design requirements for developing recoverable, safer, and more sustainable heterogeneous transfer reactions.

articles.title: Hydroxyl Regulation Enables Metal Promoter‐Free Iron Catalysts for Highly Efficient CO2 Hydrogenation to Light Olefins
articles.abstract: The efficient hydrogenation of CO2 to light olefins over Fe-based catalysts typically relies on the metal promoters, such as alkali or transition metals. In this study, we find that the intrinsic hydroxyl environments may be the crucial but long-overlooked factor governing the activity of Fe species. With the assistance of low-concentration guar gum, hydrogen-bond networks formed by dense hydroxyls are disrupted to generate isolated or terminal hydroxyl groups, which increase the active sites and significantly facilitate the product desorption. The resulting metal promoter-free Fe achieves a CO2 conversion of 30.1% and a light olefin selectivity of 38.1% at an ultra-high gas hourly space velocity of 300 000 mL gcat −1 h−1. Meanwhile, the space-time yield of light olefins reaches 3.3 kg kgcat −1 h−1, which outperforms all of the reported Fe-based catalysts modified by various promoters. These findings redefine hydroxyls as intrinsic promoters in Fe catalysts for CO2 hydrogenation and can potentially be extended to other heterogeneous catalytic systems and reactions.

articles.title: In Situ Metal Chelation for Topology Regulation and Single‐Site Construction in Covalent Organic Frameworks
articles.abstract: Precise regulation over the dimensionality and topology of covalent organic frameworks (COFs) through metal coordination remains a fundamental challenge. Herein, we report an in situ metal‐chelation strategy for topology regulation and single‐site construction in COFs using a bifunctional β‐hydroxy ketone‐functionalized HDBC monomer. Metal‐free Schiff‐base condensation of HDBC with TAPy affords a one‐dimensional covalent ribbon framework, named COF‐HDBC. Strikingly, in situ Cu2+ chelation during solvothermal crystallization redirects the assembly pathway toward a two‐dimensional bex‐type Cu‐COF‐HDBC containing framework‐embedded Cu─O coordination sites. Post‐synthetic metalation of preassembled COF‐HDBC fails to trigger this transformation, verifying the indispensable structure‐directing effect of in situ chelation during nucleation and growth. This strategy is extendable to Ni2+ and Co2+, affording isostructural metal‐chelated COFs. Multiscale characterizations and Cu K‐edge XAFS collectively support the proposed framework structures and the predominantly isolated nature of the Cu centers. As a functional validation, Cu‐COF‐HDBC enables selective CO2/CO electroreduction to CH4. This work establishes in situ metal chelation as a synthetic handle for programming COF topology and constructing framework‐embedded single‐metal sites, offering a versatile route to crystalline porous materials with complex architectures and tunable functions.

articles.title: Integrated Electromicrobial Production of Itaconic Acid From CO2 at Liter‐Scale Using Komagataella phaffii
articles.abstract: Coupling electrochemical CO2 reduction showing high selectivity with microbial biosynthesis offering metabolic versatility offers a promising strategy for converting CO2 into value‐added products. We present proof‐of‐concept of electromicrobially producing the platform chemical itaconic acid (IA) from CO2 using a robust yeast chassis. The hybrid systems integrates in a single reactor electrochemical CO2 reduction with microbial synthesis using a synthetic autotrophic Komagataella phaffii strain. Thereby CO2 serves as carbon source while electrochemically generated formate from CO2 provides reducing power to sustain microbial growth and drive IA production, reaching average titres of 110.1 mg·L−1. While demonstrating the feasibility of directly coupling electrochemical and microbial processes within a single reactor, we reveal key challenges associated with integration, including limited system performance, variability in product titers, anodic oxidation of cathodic products, and constraints in energy efficiency. Despite these current limitations, our results establish the operational feasibility of integrated electromicrobial CO2 conversion using industrial yeast and highlight critical parameters for process intensification.

articles.title: Mixed‐Valence Dimeric Olympicenyl Radical Cation With Improved Electrical Conductivity
articles.abstract: p-Type doping is an effective strategy for modulating molecular packing arrangement of organic compounds, thus improving their electrical conductivity. In this work, the first example of a mixed-valence radical cation dimer based on an odd alternant hydrocarbon, [OR5]2 +•[FeCl4]− (OR5-MV), was successfully prepared by the oxidation of olympicenyl radical (OR) derivative OR5 using FeCl3. X-ray crystallographic analysis revealed that cation-radical dimer [OR5]2 +•, acting as a fundamental building block, forms [OR5]4 2+ tetramer via a multi-center–two-electron bond, which further aggregates into a one-dimensional chain in the solid state. SQUID measurement reveals that the magnetic susceptibility is dominated by the FeCl4 – anions with no detectable OR5 moiety contribution. Theoretical calculations disclosed an open-shell singlet ground state for [OR5]4 2+ tetramer and demonstrated that the pancake-bond formation between OR5 cation-radical dimers confers significant energetic stabilization. Compared to the neutral compound, more uniform molecular packing and reduced intermolecular distance in the one-dimensional columnar architecture of OR5-MV facilitate effective intermolecular orbital overlap, leading to broader band dispersion along the molecular stacking direction. A substantially improved electrical conductivity of up to 10− 3 S cm− 1 is achieved compared to neutral radical (10− 9 S cm− 1), representing the highest value reported for monomeric odd alternant hydrocarbons.

articles.title: Near Infrared Photoswitching by Direct Excitation—A Next Frontier
articles.abstract: The field of molecular photoswitches has grown tremendously over the past decades and pervaded every applied field from chemistry, biology, physics, to materials science and beyond. A main driver for continuous progress is tailoring absorption properties as a fundamental tool for controlling the light response. So far, the shift of absorption from UV light addressability into lower‐energy visible and red spectral regions has unlocked numerous unique opportunities, both in capability increase as well as in applicability of photoswitches. A next frontier has been opened more recently by extreme redshifting of absorption, allowing to enter the near‐infrared (NIR) spectral realm via direct excitation. This minireview highlights these important developments, delineates design principles to achieve NIR responsiveness in molecular photoswitches, and showcases the specific benefits that come with such low‐energy light control over molecular states. The outlook glimpses into the future and points out the particular opportunities and challenges ahead.

articles.title: Proximity‐Engineered Dual‐Atomic Cobalt Sites Enable Adaptive Spin Catalysis for Simultaneous Oxygen and Peroxide Reduction
articles.abstract: Breaking the intrinsic adsorption conflicts among oxygen intermediates remains a central challenge in oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) electrocatalysis. Although spin‐state engineering offers an effective strategy for tuning catalytic activity, conventional approaches generally focus on a single‐spin configuration, which cannot simultaneously satisfy the distinct energetic requirements of different ORR intermediates. Here, we introduce an adaptive spin catalysis concept through proximity engineering of dual‐atomic Co sites confined within a one‐dimensional covalent organic framework. Precisely regulating the Co–Co separation while preserving the local coordination environment induces inter‐site electronic coupling, giving rise to coexisting high‐spin and low‐spin Co configurations. Combined spectroscopic characterizations and theoretical calculations support a mechanistic framework in which these coexisting spin configurations provide complementary catalytic functions for distinct intermediates along the multistep ORR pathway, thereby alleviating adsorption conflicts. Consequently, the proximity‐engineered catalyst delivers outstanding ORR activity with a half‐wave potential of 0.96 V versus reversible hydrogen electrode, outperforming both its spatially separated counterpart and commercial Pt/C. The catalyst also efficiently mediates both O2 and H2O2 reduction while suppressing peroxide decomposition, enabling enhanced performance in rechargeable zinc–air batteries and peroxide‐assisted aluminum–air batteries. This work establishes a molecular framework for exploiting spin‐state complementarity in atomic catalysts for advanced energy‐conversion reactions.

articles.title: Self‐Calibrated Luminescence Sensing Under Pressure in a Hybrid Manganese Halide
articles.abstract: Hybrid organic-inorganic manganese halides have emerged as a promising class of emitters, owing to their excellent optical properties, low toxicity, and rich structural diversity. However, achieving site-specific control over their high-pressure optical response remains a great challenge. In this study, we report a zero-dimensional manganese chloride, (HIm)6[MnCl4∙MnCl6] (HIm = imidazolium), which concurrently incorporates both tetrahedral and octahedral Mn2 + centers within a single lattice. Under pressure, the red emission of [MnCl6]4− exhibits a pronounced and linear redshift and intensity attenuation. However, the green emission of [MnCl4]2− remains stable in both peak position and intensity, serving as a rigid energetic anchor. By leveraging the invariant green emission as an internal reference and the pressure-sensitive red emission as a probe, a self-calibrated pressure sensing system is achieved. Synchrotron high-pressure x-ray diffraction, in situ optical spectroscopy and density functional theory calculations demonstrate that this decoupled response originates from the large structural compressibility of the [MnCl6]4− octahedra and high rigidity of the [MnCl4]2− tetrahedra. Our findings demonstrate that hybrid organic-inorganic crystals represent a promising class of self-calibrated optical sensing materials for next-generation metrology.

articles.title: Sterically Shielded Heavy‐Atom Strategy for Constructing Narrowband Pure‐Green MR‐TADF Emitters With Concentration‐Quenching Resistance and Fast Reverse Intersystem Crossing
articles.abstract: Multiple resonance thermally activated delayed fluorescence (MR-TADF) emitters with superior color purity and high photoluminescence quantum yields (PLQYs) hold great promise for organic light-emitting diodes (OLEDs). Nevertheless, the rigid planar structures and intrinsically slow reverse intersystem crossing rates (k RISC) of these materials lead to pronounced aggregation-caused quenching and significant efficiency roll-off. Here, we propose a sterically shielded heavy-atom strategy that simultaneously suppresses detrimental π–π stacking, accelerates k RISC, and reinforces the rigidity of the conjugated framework to retain narrowband emission. The proof-of-concept emitters BN-FLS, BN-FLSe, and BN-FLSSe show the green emission at 508–517 nm with the narrow full width at half maximums (FWHMs) of 25–26 nm in solution. Notably, BN-FLSSe achieves rapid k RISC of 4.2 × 106 s−1, maintains high PLQYs above 95%, and stable emission profiles over 1–30 wt% broad doping range. Non-sensitized OLEDs based on BN-FLS, BN-FLSe, and BN-FLSSe show pure-green electroluminescence with CIEy coordinates exceeding 0.70, high maximum external quantum efficiencies (EQEmaxs) of 41.7%, 41.1%, and 38.5%, and well-suppressed efficiency roll-offs, maintaining EQEs of 21.9%, 30.9%, and 32.7% at 1000 cd m−2, respectively. Impressively, even at high doping concentration of 30 wt%, these devices retain high EQEmaxs of 30.7%–33.1% with virtually unchanged emission spectra.

articles.title: Tailoring Backbone Angles of Regioisomeric Covalent Organic Frameworks: Distinct O2 Adsorption Modes Enabling Efficient H2O2 Electrosynthesis
articles.abstract: Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) possess periodic skeletons and well-defined catalytic sites, allowing precise molecular-level regulation of interfacial properties in electrocatalytic oxygen reduction. However, conventional structural modifications fail to systematically tune oxygen adsorption geometry and interfacial electronic coupling. Here, we report a linkage-angle engineering strategy that alters the bonding positions of reactive aldehyde groups to fabricate three regioisomeric COFs with predefined backbone dihedral angles of 180°, 120°, and 60°. The angle‑driven regioisomeric effect induces considerable differences in dipole moments together with uneven charge distribution. These collective structural features remodel oxygen‑surface interactions and modulate the intrinsic catalytic kinetics. Theoretical calculations confirm that the compact 60° framework of o-TPDA-COF reconstructs confined pore interfacial microenvironments. Unlike the Griffiths‑type oxygen adsorption favored in its angular analogues, molecular oxygen preferentially adopts the Pauling configuration within o-TPDA-COF to stabilize OOH* intermediates. Consequently, the optimal o-TPDA-COF reaches an excellent H2O2 productivity of 12.82 mol gcat −1 h−1 and a Faradaic efficiency (FE) of 91.64%. This work realizes controllable modulation of oxygen‑adsorption behaviors in COF‑based 2e– oxygen reduction, delivering a novel geometry‑oriented design paradigm for porous electrocatalytic frameworks.

articles.title: Empirical Research on Criminal Record Expungement: A Critical Review
articles.abstract: Many jurisdictions have sought to mitigate hurdles faced by people with criminal records by allowing those records to be expunged (or sealed). Expungement eliminates most legal restrictions triggered by records, and policymakers hope it could also improve access to employment and housing markets and reduce social stigma. Yet there remain significant questions about how well this intervention works. This article canvasses the nascent empirical literature on expungement, focusing on three areas. First, uptake studies consistently find that when eligible individuals must file legal petitions for expungement, only a small fraction do so. Second, studies of those who do receive petition-based expungement have mostly found positive effects on employment and other outcomes. However, the uptake problem introduces sample selection concerns that complicate causal inference, and one recent randomized control trial found a disappointing absence of effects. Third, research on automated expungement (carried out by the state without individuals petitioning) is especially limited, but there is some reason for skepticism about its effects, at least on employment.

articles.title: Labeling Theory: New Life and a Path Forward
articles.abstract: This review centers on the development of labeling theory in criminology. Our core argument is that modifications to labeling theory in the past several decades have veered research away from the theory's core propositions. We extend this argument by presenting a three-part conceptual model of secondary deviance, defined as persistence in deviant behavior as a result of punishment. First, a subtheory of punishment and social exclusion explains institutional and interpersonal exclusion after punishment as the result of selection, separation, and stigma. Stigma manifests as rejection, withdrawal, and homophily. Second, deviant identity is reintroduced as the central motivating mechanism of secondary deviance. Its development involves the links between actual and reflected appraisals and the internalization of reflected appraisals into self-appraisals. Third, peer and community contexts are sources of variation in the effects of punishment on social exclusion and deviant identity. Researchers should give special attention to how these processes unfold within individuals and across life stages. Our model serves as a framework for advancing understanding of the mechanisms that drive criminogenic consequences of punishment.

articles.title: Punitive Policing in the Americas
articles.abstract: Police violence remains pervasive across democratic societies in the Americas. This review brings the US literature on policing into dialogue with comparative research on Latin America to identify common forces that sustain what we call punitive policing—systems of law enforcement that systematically violate human rights, rely on excessive surveillance and coercion, and disproportionately target marginalized populations. Synthesizing scholarship from both regions, the review highlights three factors that help explain the persistence of punitive policing: colonial legacies, the militarization of public security, and deeply entrenched racial and socioeconomic inequalities that shape how police are deployed and whom they target with violence. Our review shows that punitive policing is a governance problem that undermines legitimacy, public safety, citizenship, and democratic stability. Yet the evidence also suggests that meaningful reform is possible when bottom-up, coordinated mobilization converges with top-down institutional intervention to constrain punitive policing.

articles.title: The Disciplined Worker In and Out of Prison
articles.abstract: Scholars of mass incarceration have tended to understand the prison as a labor market institution mostly in the negative sense: as a warehouse for those otherwise likely to be unemployed and as a site of status degradation that further reduces people's ability to find employment after release. In this article, we review recent work that has focused attention on the prison as a labor market institution in a more productive sense: as an organization that shapes the work activity of the many workers incarcerated within it, facilitates formerly incarcerated people's subordination in the labor market upon release, and may play a more active role than previously imagined in shaping the distribution of jobs available in the US labor market as a whole. We also introduce new evidence that the tightness of the labor market structures how a criminal record shapes people's labor market experiences after incarceration.

articles.title: Hydrodynamics, Sensing, and Control in Schooling Fish
articles.abstract: Fish schools are among the most spectacular examples of collective behavior in nature. Individual fish coordinate their motion with neighbors primarily through vision and flow sensing. Each fish generates flow disturbances that can influence the motion and energetics of nearby swimmers. Yet fundamental questions remain unresolved: To what extent can schooling be explained by passive hydrodynamic interactions, and where are individual-level sensing and control required to maintain group cohesion? This review examines collective swimming through the lens of fluid mechanics. By synthesizing experimental, theoretical, and computational studies spanning pairs of fish to large schools, I discuss how hydrodynamic interactions affect coordination, stability, and energetic cost. Flow interactions can yield robust pairwise coordination and locomotor benefits, but they can also drive collective instabilities and unequal benefit distributions in larger groups. These findings point to a fundamental interplay between hydrodynamics and sensory–motor feedback in the formation and maintenance of fish schools. More broadly, they suggest that hydrodynamics shapes collective swimming not only through energetic costs and benefits but also through the physical constraints it imposes on coordination, stability, and information flow within groups.

articles.title: Enhancer Hijacking in Hematological Malignancies
articles.journal: Annual Review of Pathology: Mechanisms of Disease
articles.abstract: Cell identity is established by tightly regulated transcriptional programs. Disruption of the regulatory mechanisms governing these programs leads to aberrant behavior and, frequently, cancer. Enhancer hijacking, the process whereby a gene comes under the control of an ectopic enhancer, is a major cause of transcriptional dysregulation. Although recognized since the 1980s, its detection has been traditionally hindered by the low resolution of karyotyping and incomplete knowledge of enhancer biology. This has changed with the development of high-throughput sequencing, leading to a surge in newly identified enhancer hijacking events over the past two decades. Furthermore, functional dissection of enhancers using techniques such as CRISPR/Cas9 has shed light on their mechanistic underpinnings, with acute myeloid leukemia (AML) emerging as a paradigm for this phenomenon. In this review, we outline the historical development of enhancer hijacking, highlight representative examples in hematological malignancies, and discuss the insights derived from this research, particularly in AML.

articles.title: Circadian Rhythms in Drug Response: From Molecular Clocks to Precision Dosing
articles.journal: Annual Review of Pharmacology and Toxicology
articles.abstract: Circadian rhythms organize mammalian physiology across the 24-h day through molecular clocks coordinated by the central clock in the suprachiasmatic nucleus and distributed to peripheral oscillators. These clocks regulate processes central to pharmacology, including drug absorption, distribution, metabolism, elimination, and target responsiveness. Consequently, drug efficacy and toxicity can vary substantially depending on the time of administration. Despite decades of progress in pharmacogenomics and systems pharmacology, consideration of time of day remains largely absent from clinical drug development and prescription. In this review, we evaluate emerging research on circadian regulation of drug responses, considering both pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics. We review chronotherapeutic strategies to treat diseases, including cancer, cardiovascular disease, and bipolar disorder. We also discuss the use of wearable technologies to enable time-resolved drug evaluation. Finally, we discuss the challenges to clinical translation and the integration of circadian timing into precision medicine and optimized dosing strategies.

articles.title: Endocannabinoid Signaling and Mood Regulation
articles.journal: Annual Review of Pharmacology and Toxicology
articles.abstract: The endocannabinoid (eCB) signaling system is a local regulator of synaptic activity across brain circuits involved in the regulation of emotional behaviors. Preclinical studies predominantly show that eCB signaling dampens acute stress responses, although notable exceptions exist. Various forms of chronic stress downregulate eCB signaling, and enhanced eCB tone can reduce the effects of chronic stress on avoidance behaviors and anhedonia. Studies in healthy humans generally align with these preclinical findings. Type 1 cannabinoid receptors (CB1Rs) and fatty acid amide hydrolase (FAAH), the enzyme that degrades the eCB N -arachidonoylethanolamine (AEA), are present in circuits that regulate emotion, and pharmacological and genetic manipulations of these proteins affect anxiety, stress responses, and reward. However, FAAH inhibitors have largely failed to demonstrate efficacy, and CB1R agonists have only modest effects in individuals with mood disorders. Advancing the therapeutic potential of CB1R/eCB signaling likely will require a deeper understanding of the factors contributing to inconsistencies between model systems and individuals with mood disorders.

articles.title: Exercise as Medicine: The Potential of Exerkines as Therapeutics
articles.journal: Annual Review of Pharmacology and Toxicology
articles.abstract: Exercise delivers a wide variety of health benefits through many mechanisms, including the release of exerkines, signaling molecules secreted by multiple tissues during physical activity. We evaluated 34 exerkines with therapeutic potential alongside IC7Fc (an engineered IL-6/CNTF derivative), classifying them based on ( a ) their translational readiness as therapeutics and ( b ) their primary clinical domains (cardiovascular, metabolic, neurological, musculoskeletal, anti-inflammatory, and oncology). Only four have clear clinical validation, and nine others have reached clinical testing or late preclinical development. Across these molecular entities, three challenges emerge: context-dependent effects, drug-delivery constraints, and network dynamics. We conclude with an assessment of opportunities and strategies for the creation of exerkine-based biomarkers and for using exerkines to facilitate therapeutic discovery. Finally, we present the Exerkine Atlas ( https://exerkineatlas.org/ ), an open-access web resource integrating curated literature and clinical trial data for all 35 molecules.

articles.title: Tobacco and Cannabis Use Disorders: Similarities, Differences and Therapeutic Approaches
articles.journal: Annual Review of Pharmacology and Toxicology
articles.abstract: Cannabis and tobacco are two of the most commonly used drugs worldwide. Both drugs can lead to a use disorder, characterized by compulsive use despite harm and mediated by neurobiological changes in reward and motivational circuitry. Co-use of cannabis and tobacco is common and influences disorder severity and outcomes. Both cannabis use disorder (CUD) and tobacco use disorder (TUD) share key features, such as dopaminergic reward system involvement, severity of withdrawal symptoms, and mental health comorbidities, yet they differ in neurobiological pathways, diagnostic profiles, and available pharmacotherapies. Diagnostic frameworks like the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders, Fifth Edition, and International Classification of Diseases 11 provide standardized criteria for assessment. Optimal management integrates pharmacological and psychosocial interventions, though approved medications exist for TUD and not yet for CUD. Understanding similarities, distinctions, and treatment strategies is critical for effective prevention and clinical care.

articles.title: Disease-causing helix-8 mutations reprogram parathyroid hormone receptor-1 effector selectivity
articles.abstract: Höppner et al. show that disease-associated substitutions in PTH1R helix-8 selectively rewire receptor coupling to G proteins and βarrestin. Distinct mutations bias PTH1R engagement toward either Gαq or βarrestin pathways and impair Gαs activation. These findings reveal mutation-driven shifts in effector selectivity as a previously unrecognized mechanism in PTH1R-associated disease.

articles.abstract: Wang et al. develop an oral metabolically engineered bacterial platform (EcN-HlpA-CGL [EHC]) for colorectal cancer immunotherapy, which triggers ferroptosis in colorectal cancer cells to boost immunogenicity, while the bacterial adjuvanticity reshapes the immunosuppressive microenvironment. This approach activates both systemic and gut mucosal immunity, effectively suppressing orthotopic tumor growth and metastasis.

articles.title: Continuous refrigeration and dehumidification using the lower critical solution temperature cycle
Exploring magnesium- and calcium-based compounds via solid-state metathesis reactions
Applications of Single-Atom Alloys in Thermal, Electro, and Photo Catalysis
articles.abstract: Single-atom alloys (SAAs) are an emerging class of heterogeneous catalysts that maximize atom efficiency by embedding isolated reactive metal atoms within a host metal surface, creating well-defined active sites. Atomic isolation imparts unique catalytic properties, including high selectivity, resistance to poisoning, coking, and sintering, and in some cases the ability to circumvent conventional scaling relationships that limit traditional catalysts. This article focuses on progress in the SAA field since our 2020 review (Chem. Rev.2020, 120, 12044−12088.), while incorporating earlier foundational studies where relevant. We first examine the fundamental principles governing SAA formation, stability, electronic structure, reactivity, and selectivity, drawing on insights from experimental single-crystal model systems and theoretical studies. We then review the application of SAAs in a wide range of industrially important reactions, including hydrogenation, dehydrogenation, selective oxidation, water–gas shift, Fischer–Tropsch synthesis, and dry reforming, among others. Beyond thermal catalysis, SAAs demonstrate great promise in electrocatalysis and plasmon-driven chemistry. Their structurally simple active sites have also enabled the rational design of novel catalysts and promoters that challenge conventional catalytic intuition. Looking ahead, recent advances in computing, including machine-learning potentials, offer the opportunity to explore vast compositional spaces and discover new alloy chemistries for challenging reactions using the SAA concept.

articles.title: Nonaqueous Redox Flow Batteries: Opportunities and Challenges for Sustainable Energy Storage
articles.abstract: Redox flow batteries (RFBs) have emerged as promising electrochemical energy storage technologies for long-duration stationary applications. Although aqueous RFBs represent the most commercially mature class, they are inherently limited by a narrow electrochemical stability window and high temperature sensitivity. Nonaqueous RFBs (NRFBs) expand the accessible voltage and temperature ranges, offering a promising route toward high-energy-density storage for long-duration and extreme-environment applications. However, their practical deployment remains impeded by several challenges, including high costs, insufficient power density, limited cycling stability, and safety concerns. This review offers a systematic synthesis of recent advances in key NRFB components, encompassing solvents, supporting electrolytes, membranes, electrodes, and redox-active molecules. We also highlight emerging methodologies expected to accelerate development, including machine-learning-enabled screening, advanced characterization, and life cycle assessment. Finally, this review compares aqueous and nonaqueous systems from commercialization and sustainability perspectives. Collectively, this review aims to advance design principles and optimization strategies for NRFBs, providing guidance for next-generation low-cost, high-energy-density flow battery technologies.

articles.title: Accurately Probing [Fe(CN)6] Defects in Prussian Blue Analogues
articles.abstract: Prussian blue analogues AxM[Fe(CN)6]1–y·zH2O (A = Na, K, M = Fe, Mn) possess a rich crystal chemistry that allows their use as insertion materials for batteries, water treatment, and smart windows, among others, applications. Despite being simple in appearance, their synthesis is complex and often results in defective, nonstoichiometric materials. These defects can be of neutral charge, such as interstitial water molecules, or charged, such as A+ vacancies or [Fe(CN)6]n− vacancies, whose presence implies charge balance by the remaining transition metal centers. In this work, a compound close to the Berlin green Fe[Fe(CN)6] nominal composition was synthesized, and its crystal structure, electrochemical properties, and electronic structure were investigated. Although usual characterization methods such as X-ray diffraction, X-ray absorption spectroscopy, and 57Fe Mössbauer spectroscopy agree well with the formation of Fe[Fe(CN)6], the material can only be intercalated to Na1.4Fe[Fe(CN)6]. This lack of capacity was hypothesized to arise from “hidden” [Fe(CN)6] vacancies. The charge balance associated with these vacancies implies partial reduction of the low-spin Fe, as confirmed by low-temperature 57Fe Mössbauer spectroscopy and further high-angular-resolution diffraction experiments. This study suggests that numerous materials previously described as “Berlin green” in the literature might actually be substantially hexacyanoferrate defective.

articles.title: Alcohol-Mediated Area-Selective Atomic Layer Deposition through Surface Chemical States Modulation
articles.abstract: Area-selective atomic layer deposition (AS-ALD) fundamentally relies on a distinct disparity in surface chemical states between growth and nongrowth area. For SiO2/Cu patterned architectures, the oxidation of the Cu surface serves as a primary driver for the loss of selectivity as the ALD process proceeds. Herein, an alcohol-mediated AS-ALD process is proposed, utilizing alcohols with varying carbon chain lengths to precisely modulate surface chemical states to enhance selectivity of AS-ALD WOx film. A competitive-synergistic mechanism involving surface reductive capability and steric hindrance is identified as the governing factor for process selectivity. Results demonstrate that while the reducing ability of alcohols on oxidized Cu surfaces diminishes with increasing carbon chain length, their steric hindrance increases. EtOH was identified as the optimal pretreatment agent, yielding an exceptional selectivity exceeding 99.9% on SiO2/Cu patterned surface. Moreover, the alcohol-mediated AS-ALD process is successfully extended to other oxide systems with precursors bearing analogous ligands, demonstrating the generality of the proposed strategy. This work provides a versatile methodology for modulating surface reductive capability and steric hindrance to achieve high-selectivity AS-ALD.

articles.title: Concerted Ge–H/Se–Se Bond Reorganization Enables Surface Selenylation of Germanium Quantum Dots
articles.abstract: Colloidal germanium quantum dots (GeQDs) hold promise for solution-processable optoelectronics, yet their performance is often constrained by the limited reactivity of hydride-terminated surfaces and the insulating nature of conventional capping ligands. Here, we introduce a room-temperature selenylation strategy that harnesses the intrinsically weak and polarizable Ge–H bonds on freshly etched GeQD surfaces to drive Se–Se bond activation of diorganyl diselenides. This polarization-assisted concerted process proceeds without radical initiators or external stimuli, yielding robust Ge–SeR surface linkages that effectively passivate the GeQDs against oxidation while introducing a soft, polarizable chalcogenide-rich surface. The resulting RSe-GeQDs show notably improved optical properties and charge carrier mobilities compared to oleylamine-functionalized GeQDs. The direct, catalyst-free nature of this approach offers a versatile platform for the development of solution-processable germanium-based optoelectronic devices.

articles.title: The Importance of Nanoscale Phenomena in Electrolyte Behavior: Acetonitrile-Aqueous Zinc Sulfate Electrolytes
articles.abstract: Electrolytes composed of mixed solvents are of significant scientific and technological importance in lithium-ion and beyond-lithium-ion batteries, and more broadly across physical chemistry. Their emergence has highlighted the importance of multiscale phenomena, particularly the development of nanoscale solution heterogeneities. It is therefore essential to assess how these inhomogeneities and nanoscale aggregates influence solvation, transport, and electronic properties. Here we investigate the solution structure and transport properties of aqueous zinc sulfate electrolytes with acetonitrile (ACN) additives, where the addition of ACN leads to improved cyclability. Using complementary anomalous small-angle X-ray scattering, X-ray pair distribution function, electrochemistry, and NMR, we identify the presence of salt-rich-water-rich and salt-poor-ACN-rich nanoheterogeneities and, at higher ACN concentrations, liquid–liquid phase separation. We find that the size of zinc sulfate ion clusters in the water domains increases slightly upon ACN addition, while the ACN-rich domains grow much larger as phase separation is approached. The inverse Haven ratio, determined using the ionic conductivity and diffusivity, is much less than unity and decreases slightly upon addition of ACN, which shows ion–ion interactions. We speculate that the increased ion–ion interactions with increased ACN are a result of a reduction in free water, the increase in zinc sulfate cluster size, and/or an increase in solution tortuosity. This work highlights key phenomena to consider when engineering new water-organic-salt electrolyte systems and establishes a phase diagram for water–ACN–ZnSO4 that can guide advances, such as self-adaptive electrolytes.

articles.title: Approach to Heart Failure With Mildly Reduced Left Ventricular Ejection Fraction
Cardiovascular Complications of Chronic Liver Disease
articles.abstract: Chronic liver disease is an increasingly prevalent and heterogeneous syndrome with important consequences for cardiovascular function. As the global burdens of chronic liver disease and cirrhosis continue to rise, cardiovascular disease has emerged as a major driver of overall morbidity and mortality in affected patients. Despite the growing recognition of the intersectionality between hepatology and cardiology care clinically, cardiovascular disease risk among patients with liver disease is underrecognized. This state-of-the-art review summarizes the current understanding of the bidirectional interactions between the liver and the cardiovascular system. Shared mechanisms—including inflammation, endothelial injury, and neurohormonal overactivation—that contribute to the development of adverse myocardial remodeling, atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, heart failure, arrhythmias, pulmonary vascular syndromes, and cirrhosis-associated cardiovascular syndromes are reviewed. A specific focus is placed on metabolic dysfunction–associated steatotic liver disease, the most common form of chronic liver disease, while highlighting the distinct cardiovascular manifestations associated with other types of chronic liver disease. These include alcohol-associated liver disease and infiltrative diseases that affect the liver and heart with cardiovascular implications across the spectrum from early stages of liver disease through cirrhosis. We discuss practical approaches to detecting liver disease, including the assessment of liver fibrosis noninvasively in individuals at risk. We discuss the approach to assessing cardiovascular risk through cardiac imaging, biomarkers, and cardiac functional testing once chronic liver disease is detected. Management considerations for commonly encountered cardiovascular conditions and a critical appraisal of the evolving evidence supporting cardiometabolic therapies in patients with chronic liver disease are discussed to underscore potential cardiovascular and liver benefits. Critical evidence gaps and future research priorities are identified, including the development and evaluation of liver-informed cardiovascular risk models, incorporation of cardiovascular end points into liver disease trials, and implementation of integrated cardiohepatometabolic care pathways. Improved recognition of chronic liver disease and related cardiovascular disease risk represents a major opportunity to facilitate earlier disease detection, enhance risk stratification, and improve outcomes across the spectrum of chronic liver disease.

Breaking the Rules: Museum Data Reveal Divergent Support for Classic Ecogeographical Rules in North American Flying Squirrels
articles.abstract: Ecogeographic generalizations or “rules”, such as Bergmann's rule and Allen's rule, propose that endotherms in colder climates evolve larger bodies and shorter appendages to minimize heat loss. These patterns are hypothesized to reflect physiological adaptations to thermal stress through reduced surface area‐to‐volume ratios. Although these rules have been extensively evaluated across birds and mammals, their applicability to arboreal gliders remains untested, with little consideration of how alternative ecological and evolutionary drivers may structure morphological variation in flying squirrels across environmental gradients. Using digitized museum specimens of North American flying squirrels (Glaucomys sabrinus, Glaucomys oregonensis, and Glaucomys volans), we tested these classic ecogeographic principles by examining how weight, total length, tail length, and ear length vary across a latitudinal gradient. We found significant support for Bergmann's rule, with body mass and total length increasing with latitude. In contrast, patterns in appendage morphology provided limited support for Allen's rule. Ear length exhibited a weak positive relationship with latitude, while tail length strongly increased with latitude, contradicting the prediction that appendages become shorter in colder climates. These findings suggest that thermoregulatory selection alone cannot explain morphological variation in North American flying squirrels and that functional demands, particularly those associated with gliding performance, may play a stronger role in shaping tail morphology. Overall, our results demonstrate that although classic ecogeographic rules provide a useful framework for understanding morphological variation, they do not fully capture the multiple selective pressures acting on Glaucomys species.

articles.title: Distribution Patterns and Environmental Correlates of Invasive Plants Along an Urbanization Gradient in a Medium‐Sized Mountainous City of Southwest China
articles.abstract: Against the backdrop of ongoing urban expansion, alien plant invasions are closely linked to the stability of urban ecosystems. However, few studies have documented invasive plant distribution and their statistical associations with landscape variables in mountainous medium‐sized cities, which serve as critical urban–rural transition zones. This study selected Anning City, a representative mountainous medium‐sized city in Yunnan, Southwest China, as the research case. We established 63 standard sampling plots spanning urban, suburban, and exurban zones along an urbanization gradient. Canonical Correspondence Analysis (CCA) and Monte Carlo permutation tests were adopted to quantify statistical associations between six major macro‐environmental variables and invasive plant spatial distribution, and to characterize the distribution features of invasive plants for reference in targeted monitoring work. The main observations are summarized as follows: (1) A total of 66 alien invasive plant species belonging to 24 families and 51 genera were recorded. Asteraceae was the most abundant family, accounting for 25.75% of all taxa; 68.18% of species originated from the Americas, and annual and biennial herbs dominated the community (75.75%), which tend to occur abundantly in frequently disturbed habitats. (2) This local dataset captured a site‐specific trend where invasion abundance declines as urbanization intensity rises: the total number of invasive species increased from urban to suburban and exurban zones, yet significant gradient differentiation only existed in plant abundance rather than species richness. Suburban and exurban plots had similar abundance values (p > 0.05), and both presented significantly higher invasive abundance than urban plots (p < 0.001). Dense invasive aggregations were frequently detected along transportation corridors and rural land, while forested areas generally corresponded to lower invasive plant coverage. (3) Invasive plant distribution displayed combined statistical associations with multiple environmental variables. Building density presented the strongest correlation with community composition (p = 0.004), while urbanization gradient, terrain attributes, and population density also showed significant associations; no meaningful statistical links were detected for road network density and land‐use type. Widespread and common species exhibited significant correlations with macro‐environmental predictors, whereas rare species showed no such associations. Collectively, this paper describes the site‐specific distribution features of invasive plants and their correlated landscape variables in mountainous medium‐sized cities of Southwest China. This work supplements case evidence for invasion ecology research in moderately urbanized mountainous regions and offers empirical references for invasive plant surveillance in comparable subtropical mountainous medium‐sized cities globally.

articles.title: Does Mother Provide? Re‐Examination of Maternal and Embryonic Microbiomes of Diploptera punctata
articles.abstract: The cockroach endosymbiont Blattabacterium cuenotii plays a central role in host nutrition throughout development, particularly during embryogenesis in the viviparous cockroach Diploptera punctata. However, the presence and potential functional relevance of non‐blattabacterial taxa in developing embryos of this species remain unclear. Previous studies of maternal and embryonic microbiomes in D. punctata, based on Illumina 16S rRNA sequencing, have yielded inconsistent findings, partly due to differences in how endosymbiotic sequences were treated. Here, we reanalyzed microbiome data from two studies, with and without Blattabacterial reads, to reevaluate the presence and composition of non‐blattabacterial taxa in embryonic microbiomes. Embryonic microbial communities (1) differed significantly from each other between datasets and (2) from associated maternal gut communities, suggesting that environmental (maternal, dietary, and laboratory) and sequencing factors may influence their acquisition and composition rather than reflecting a stable, consistently transmitted microbiome. Nevertheless, the detection of non‐blattabacterial taxa in embryonic microbiomes suggests the possible acquisition of non‐endosymbiotic bacteria by developing embryos. The functions of these microbes are speculated, but were not explicitly tested in this study and remain to be verified. Overall, our findings suggest that although non‐endosymbiotic embryonic bacteria may be environmentally acquired and variable, their biological relevance remains unresolved and cannot be determined from 16S amplicon data alone. This highlights the importance of investigating acquired non‐endosymbiotic bacteria and their potential functional roles in the development of viviparous cockroaches.

articles.title: Drivers of Taxonomic Bias in Ecology and Evolution: Insights From Ethologists and Behavioural Ecologists
articles.abstract: Taxonomic bias, that is, the disproportionate attention given to some taxa relative to their diversity, continues to hinder innovation and the pursuit of generality in ecology and evolution. Yet, the factors shaping ecologists' and evolutionary biologists' choices of study organisms mostly remain a mystery. We propose a framework explaining researchers' taxonomic choices along three major axes, supported by evidence from a preregistered survey of 868 researchers' experiences. First, rational considerations, such as logistical ease and societal relevance, were associated with the choice of research organisms within major animal groups but rarely across them. Second, contextual factors, like the prominence of certain organisms within peer networks or early‐career exposure to specific taxa, were also associated with researchers' decisions about which organisms to study. Third, emotional factors, including taxonomic affinities, closely mirrored taxonomic patterns in the literature, indicating that they are a major driver of organism choice at broad taxonomic scales. Based on these findings, we suggest actions to mitigate taxonomic bias, including promoting (i) outreach initiatives featuring neglected taxa, (ii) taxonomically equitable education and (iii) taxonomically diverse research experiences.

articles.title: Multiple Genetic Lineages and Inter‐Island Gene Flow in Nemadactylus monodactylus at Tristan da Cunha: Implications for Phylogeography and Taxonomy
articles.abstract: Tristan da Cunha (TDC) is a remote archipelago of four South Atlantic islands whose nearshore fish assemblages remain comparatively poorly studied. Genetic studies of such disjunct groups can provide valuable information on evolutionary history, taxonomy, and stock structure relevant for conservation and sustainable fishery management. Here, we address such topics in the Five‐finger (Nemadactylus monodactylus), an abundant nearshore fish harvested for subsistence at TDC, using a combination of mitochondrial control region sequencing and microsatellite analysis. Mitochondrial data, including publicly available data for Southern Hemisphere congeners, recovered four well‐supported clades. Three clades were polyphyletic, containing sequences previously assigned to N. macropterus or N. bergi, whereas one was newly described and may be endemic to TDC. These patterns add to evidence for a complex evolutionary history within Nemadactylus and suggest that current taxonomic designations warrant re‐evaluation. mtDNA also confirms colonisation of TDC by multiple lineages. Neither mtDNA nor microsatellites provided consistent evidence of genetic differentiation among islands, including between the distinctive Gough morphotype and the northern islands. These results are consistent with substantial archipelago‐wide connectivity, but the limited nuclear marker set means that weak structure cannot be excluded. We therefore regard a single archipelago‐wide population as a provisional working hypothesis rather than a confirmed management unit. Broader geographic sampling and genome‐wide nuclear data are needed to test species limits, reconstruct evolutionary history, and resolve fine‐scale population structure relevant to management.

articles.title: Plastomes of Ten Blumea Species (Asteraceae): Comparative Analysis and Phylogenetic Relationships
articles.abstract: Blumea (Asteraceae) comprises about 100 species distributed across tropical Asia, Africa, and Australia, many of which have medicinal value. However, morphological variation caused by hybridization has left the taxonomy of this genus unresolved. In this study, we assembled the chloroplast genomes of six Blumea species (B. repanda, B. axillaris, B. sinuata, B. martiniana, B. megacephala, and B. formosana) and compared them with those of four published species (B. oxyodonta, B. tenella, B. aromatica, and B. balsamifera). The six new plastomes are similar in size (150,783–151,281 bp), with a typical quadripartite structure, each containing 131 genes (86 protein‐coding genes, 37 tRNAs, and 8 rRNAs). Comparative analyses revealed conserved genome architecture, stable IR/SC boundaries, and no rearrangements. Six non‐coding and four coding regions were identified as candidate DNA barcodes. A total of 395 dispersed repeats, 79 tandem repeats, and 547 SSRs were identified. Among the 59 preferred codons, 29 were high‐frequency (RSCU > 1), and 28 of these ended in A/U. Additionally, positive selection was detected in 21 genes, for example, ycf1, ycf2, rpoB, and ndhA. Phylogenetic analyses (ML and BI) based on 23 taxa (21 Inuleae species plus two outgroups) showed that Blumea is a highly supported monophyletic group (BS = 100%, PP = 1.00), internally divided into three subclades: subclade I (B. axillaris, B. oxyodonta, B. megacephala, B. repanda, B. sinuata, and B. tenella), subclade II (B. balsamifera), and subclade III (B. aromatica, B. formosana, and B. martiniana), with the latter three species all belonging to Section Macrophylla. These genomic resources lay a foundation for future phylogenetic, population‐genetic, and biotechnological studies of Blumea.

articles.title: Pollinator Visitation Within a Single Crown of the Rare Rainforest Tree Firmiana daweishanensis Is Associated With Floral Colour Change
articles.abstract: Floral colour change can signal floral state, but its role in rainforest canopy trees remains poorly understood. We investigated colour change and pollinator visitation in Firmiana daweishanensis, a Plant Species with Extremely Small Populations endemic to southeastern Yunnan, China. Using a 25‐m scaffold, we observed 16 flowering branches on one adult tree for 128 branch‐hours. We combined these observations with measurements of linalool emission, nectar accumulation, reproductive function, calyx reflectance and bee visual modelling. Six hymenopteran taxa visited the tree, with Megachile bees dominating visitation. Mixed models showed that yellow flowers received more visits and greater cumulative visitation time per flower‐hour than red flowers within both sexes. Neither the omnibus sex tests nor the colour × sex interactions were significant. Branch‐level floral abundance and colour composition were not significantly associated with visitation. This contrast was consistent with, but did not demonstrate, selection at a fine spatial scale; limited statistical power remained an alternative explanation. Yellow flowers showed higher linalool emission and stronger modelled green‐receptor contrast against a green background. Nectar availability and reproductive function were generally greater during earlier floral stages. Neither pollinator‐excluded nor artificially geitonogamously self‐pollinated flowers produced fruit, whereas naturally exposed flowers showed 6.19% fruit set. These observations support a contribution of floral visitors to fruit set, but the absence of a hand‐cross‐pollinated control prevented a conclusive assessment of self‐incompatibility. Because colour, age, scent, reward and reproductive state covaried, their individual contributions to visitation could not be distinguished. Floral colour change may therefore form part of a multimodal indicator of floral state, while any display function of retained red flowers remains hypothetical. This within‐tree case study documents canopy visitation patterns whose generality requires replication across individuals and populations.

articles.title: Targeted eDNA Survey Enables Consistent Detection of the Invasive Blue Crab in Trans‐Border Adriatic Coastal‐Marine Ecosystems
articles.abstract: The invasive blue crab Callinectes sapidus poses a significant ecological and economic threat to Mediterranean marine ecosystems, highlighting the need for sensitive and reliable tools for its early detection. We developed and validated a species‐specific environmental DNA (eDNA) assay designed for sensitive detection of C. sapidus. Species‐specific primers targeting a 464 bp fragment of the mitochondrial COI gene were designed, and their specificity was confirmed through in silico analyses using Primer‐BLAST and Sanger sequencing, and their effectiveness was validated via high‐throughput sequencing (HTS) of environmental DNA (eDNA) samples. The assay based on eDNA proved to be reliable and robust in confirming the presence of blue crab DNA in five cross‐border Adriatic pilot areas impacted by this invasive species. In addition, the dominant OTU was consistently present in all sites, while haplotype network analysis using ASVs revealed a shared central haplotype across Adriatic populations, supporting their genetic cohesiveness and a common invasion history. These results emphasize the importance of molecular tools for tracking invasion dynamics and reinforce the potential for uniform genetic profiles to facilitate management efforts. Overall, our findings demonstrate that targeted eDNA approaches are essential for effective early detection and containment strategies in marine ecosystems threatened by biological invasions, and that the blue crab in the Adriatic Sea constitutes a potential genetically cohesive invasive entity.

Retracing the olive (Olea europaea L. subsp. europaea) origin and its early history diffusion among the civilizations overlooking the Mediterranean coasts: an integrated approach
articles.abstract: The olive tree is one of the most important crops in the world, but even more, one of the most identitarian plant for the countries of the Mediterranean basin. In this article, the vast consultation of scientific literature, archaeological, historical and anecdotal sources, allowed to outline a global reasoned vision on the olive origin, its spread during early history and how olive fruit fly may represent as proxy for tracing its early diffusion. The reconstruction of the first forms of exploitation, propagation and trade routes yielded a chronologically coherent westward emergence of integrated olive-oil economies and cultures throughout the Mediterranean Basin, with the exception of some independent cultivation events tied to the widespread diffusion of the wild olive tree from the end of the last Glacial Period. Written sources, iconography, and archaeological installations further anchor this spatio-temporal narrative, leading to the transition from -wild- olives gatherers to olive growers.

articles.title: Correction to ‘Differential effects of pollen nutritional quality on male and female reproductive success within a diverse co‐flowering community’
The effect of prenatal environment on brain mitochondrial function and prey detection in a lizard
articles.abstract: Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog. Abstract The ability to detect prey is crucial for survival in many animals. However, prey detection is a cognitive process that can be influenced by early life conditions such as prenatal stress or temperature. Mitochondrial function is likely to underlie these effects because cognitive abilities are energetically demanding (i.e. dependent on efficient metabolic function) and because metabolic‐derived oxidative stress and oxidative damage can impair cognitive function. Yet, whether prenatal stress and thermal environments affect prey detection, and whether mitochondrial function mediates such effects, remains poorly understood. Here, we investigated the links between prenatal environments, mitochondrial function and prey detection in the delicate skink (Lampropholis delicata). We manipulated egg corticosterone (CORT) levels—a key stress hormone in reptiles—and incubation temperature and assessed the ability of lizards to detect chemical and visual prey stimuli. Then, using flow cytometry, we measured metabolic function, oxidative stress and oxidative damage in the olfactory bulbs and optic tecta, two brain regions involved in sensory processing. While metabolic function and oxidative stress remained robust to early life conditions, CORT and temperature interacted to influence oxidative damage. Particularly, CORT decreased DNA damage in the olfactory bulbs of cold‐incubated lizards but had no effect on hot‐incubated lizards. In both brain regions, lipid peroxidation was lower in CORT‐treated lizards incubated at high temperatures compared to CORT‐treated cold‐incubated lizards, but no other between‐treatment differences were detected. Additionally, CORT‐treated lizards responded faster when presented with chemical cues but not visual stimuli. We did not find any relationship between mitochondrial function and prey detection. Our findings suggest that prenatal conditions have lasting effects on DNA damage and prey detection, but prey detection appears decoupled from mitochondrial function in L. delicata. Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog.

articles.title: Phenological Flexibility in Nesting Grassland Birds Over a Half Century Informs Timing of Management
articles.abstract: The timing of biological events for wildlife species reflects and influences ecological and evolutionary processes and helps guide management actions to meet conservation objectives. Climate change may cause phenological shifts across trophic levels and ecosystems, which can have broad ecological impacts. Shifts may also result in mistiming between management practices based on historical conditions and current biological events, reducing the effectiveness of natural resource management and conservation efforts. We analyzed nesting phenology patterns over recent decades across North America for 44 species of grassland‐nesting birds, including waterfowl, upland gamebirds, shorebirds, and passerines, many of which have experienced precipitous population declines. Understanding nesting phenologies of these species is important to their conservation, as grassland management activities often conflict with reproductive periods leading to high nest and young mortality. We compiled a dataset of over 172,000 nest records spanning five decades and evaluated environmental factors influencing long‐term shifts and short‐term flexibility in nesting phenology. We found considerable variation in responses among species, with differences in both direction and magnitude of spatiotemporal effects on nest initiation dates. Notably, the community‐level nesting season lengthened over time, but shifts exhibited spatial heterogeneity within this community of grassland birds. Nesting dates shifted asymmetrically across the breeding season with differential changes in early, peak, and late nesting dates whereas long‐term changes were mediated by weather and geographic gradients. For example, nest initiation was earlier in warmer and wetter years. By applying a quantile‐based analysis, we provide estimates of the full nesting period that could serve as a flexible tool for scheduling monitoring efforts and balancing management and human activities with periods of reduced nesting activity. Our collaborative effort illustrates the challenges and opportunities of collecting long‐term data on avian communities necessary for answering questions across large regions but highlights the value of research coordination for bird conservation.

articles.abstract: Tissue-resident memory T (TRM) cells are heterogeneous, but how pathogenic subsets drive relapse in allergic dermatitis remains unclear. Asahina et al. identify a pathogenic CXCR6+ CD4+ TRM subset sustained through CXCL16-dependent clustering with CD301b+ cDC2s, revealing the TRM-DC niche as a potential therapeutic target for allergic dermatitis.

articles.title: Cost effectiveness of synthetic fuel and CO2 removal for net-zero aviation
articles.abstract: Aviation's climate impact goes beyond CO2, yet current policies such as the EU's ReFuelEU regulation push almost exclusively toward sustainable fuels, overlooking an alternative: permanently capturing CO2 from the air via DACCS while continuing to burn fossil jet fuel. Comparing long-term costs of both approaches, we find DACCS is 49%–69% cheaper than synthetic fuels and needs far less renewable electricity, suggesting that current policy may be locking aviation into a costlier decarbonization path than necessary.

articles.title: High-frequency inductively heated molten salt bubbling beds for methane pyrolysis
articles.abstract: Methane pyrolysis can produce hydrogen while sequestering solid carbon, but efficient high-grade heat delivery and coking management remain challenging. This study shows that high-frequency magnetic induction directly and volumetrically heats molten salt bubbling beds with stable power delivery, providing a scalable route for methane pyrolysis while managing solid carbon formation. These principles have applicability more broadly to molten salt chemical conversion and thermal energy storage systems.

articles.title: Host‐mediated filtering and interspecific associations structure strongyle parasite communities in Sable Island horses
articles.abstract: Using individual‐level nemabiome metabarcoding of 3147 samples from 916 horses on Sable Island over 10 years, we generate the largest dataset of its kind to date. This unprecedented scale enables a rare test of the processes structuring parasite communities in a natural system, revealing dominant host‐mediated filtering and predominantly positive species associations. Abstract Mixed‐species parasite infections are common in wildlife, yet the ecological processes that structure these communities remain poorly understood. We hypothesized that host‐mediated and extrinsic environmental filtering, alongside biotic interactions, act concurrently to shape parasite community composition, and that these structuring patterns would depend on parasite traits or evolutionary history. We applied nemabiome DNA metabarcoding to 3147 faecal samples from 916 feral horses with no history of anthelmintic treatment, collected over 10 years as part of a long‐term individual‐based study on Sable Island, Canada. Using joint species distribution models, we tested whether strongyle parasite communities were structured by host‐associated factors, extrinsic environmental variables or interspecific interactions. Host factors, particularly age and individual identity, explained the greatest proportion of variation in both parasite prevalence and infection intensity, indicating strong host‐mediated environmental filtering. In contrast, spatial location and year explained minimal variation, suggesting weaker effects of extrinsically mediated environmental filtering. Parasite traits such as body size and gut site preference had limited associations with species' environmental responses. Positive species associations were common, particularly among species occupying the same gut region, suggesting that strong, consistent competitive interactions were not prominently reflected in the residual covariance structure. Negative associations were less frequent but consistently involved Strongylus equinus, indicating potential context‐dependent biotic interactions involving this species. By integrating species‐level molecular data with hierarchical joint species models, this study quantifies patterns of host‐related filtering and species co‐variation within a natural parasite community and provides a framework for examining mixed infections in wild systems.
