In Amborella, we recovered the well‐documented fusion of moss and green algae mitochondria, and discovered prevalent HGTs from the New Caledonian parasitic plant Hachettea (Mystropetalaceae). In the parasitic Orobanchaceae, non‐native MTPTs are strongly linked with their sympatrically distributed host plants. HGTScanner is an efficient and flexible tool that can drive discoveries of HGT without a priori knowledge regarding the donor identity. The sympatric distribution of donor‐recipient pairs in HGT events suggests that HGTs can serve as valuable genetic markers for organismal interactions across time and terrain.

articles.title: Limited Lifetime Costs of Inbreeding in a Large Wild Population of Superb Fairy‐Wrens
articles.abstract: Inbreeding depression can have major negative effects on both individual fitness and population performance. The impact of inbreeding depression in wild populations remains poorly understood, and our knowledge is primarily based on estimations in insular populations with limited dispersal, which has been predicted to enhance the capacity for outcrossing. Limited migration and small population sizes, which make insular and endangered populations tractable models for fieldwork, often experience low genetic variation and may be subject to stronger inbreeding effects. Estimating inbreeding effects is difficult in many populations because pedigrees of migrants are unknown. Genomic data offer methods to estimate realised inbreeding even in migrants. Here, we apply genomic methods to a superb fairy‐wren (Malurus cyaneus) population that has been subject to detailed study of fitness variation over three decades. The population has sex‐biased dispersal, resulting in many immigrant females. We use genomic inbreeding estimates to explicitly test for inbreeding depression across several key components of individual fitness, including nestling condition, juvenile survival and adult traits. Genomic methods were able to recover previous pedigree‐based findings of inbreeding depression in early nestling condition and additionally identified some evidence for inbreeding depression in fledgling but not juvenile mortality. The only adult fitness trait affected, male extra‐pair paternity, is highly variable and under strong sexual selection. Our findings suggest that natural populations experiencing high effective population sizes and regular dispersal might be less affected by inbreeding depression than previously assumed based on studies of often insular and smaller populations.

articles.title: High-output elastomeric SBS/PAN piezoelectric nanofibrous membranes via thermal engineering
[Editorial] Rethinking threats to human survival
articles.abstract: Much health advocacy is driven by single-issue activism. Communities with a common interest—from AIDS to child health, climate to tobacco control—focus intensely on their own domain. And understandably so. Important progress has been made through often courageous direct action. But this sharply competitive approach is, according to a new Lancet Commission on 21st Century Global Threats to Health, dangerously flawed. Indeed, perhaps the most important contribution of this Commission is to move global health beyond the consideration of individual harms.

articles.title: [Health Policy] Strengthening health systems to prioritise, provide care, and prevent osteoarthritis: a roadmap for global health policy
articles.abstract: By 2050, almost 1 billion people are expected to live with osteoarthritis—a disabling musculoskeletal condition with currently no cure. Despite its burden and costs, osteoarthritis remains largely invisible in national and global health agendas, is poorly integrated within service models for other chronic health conditions, and is frequently perceived as inevitable with ageing and associated with limited therapeutic options. This context drives an osteoarthritis identity problem that fuels frustration among those living with the disease and health-care professionals, perpetuates stigma and inequities, undermines access to effective interventions, and crucially, deprioritises osteoarthritis in health policy.

articles.title: Emerging trends in redox-neutral phosphorus(V) organocatalysis
articles.abstract: Phosphorus-mediated reactions that leverage the thermodynamic driving force of phosphorus(III) oxidation are crucial in all areas of the chemical industry. While substantial progress has been made in phosphorus(III/V) redox organocatalysis to develop catalytic alternatives, the rising field of redox-neutral phosphorus(V) organocatalysis has revealed new modes of phosphorus-based reactivity in chemical transformations without requiring stoichiometric reductants. This review highlights key advances in redox-neutral phosphorus(V) organocatalysis with a focus on fundamental phosphorus(V) reactivity, organized by the catalyst structure and emphasizing its role as a Lewis acid, Brønsted acid/base, nucleophile, superbase, or single-electron transfer agent. We close with remarks connecting established reactivity paradigms that will likely be applied to new generations of phosphorus(V) catalysts capable of solving modern synthetic challenges.

articles.title: Kernel-Level Constant-Potential Molecular Dynamics in GROMACS
articles.abstract: How charge rearranges within an electrode shapes the behavior of batteries, supercapacitors, and other electrochemical devices. Molecular simulations can capture this response by allowing the charge on each electrode atom to adjust to its surroundings, but repeatedly calculating these charges adds substantial computational cost. We present an open-source implementation of the constant-potential method in GROMACS that integrates these calculations into the program's optimized CPU and GPU routines. Comparisons with established codes validate the electrode charges, while charging, voltammetry, and impedance simulations demonstrate the response to changing electrical conditions. The implementation also supports electrodes that move or deform and models of finite metallic screening and electron spillover. In a pair of charged carbon nanotubes, allowing charge to move away from the facing surfaces reduces the repulsive force at contact by about half at an intermediate charge and keeps the pair bound where a uniform-charge model opens within the simulated time. These capabilities make the electrical response of electrodes accessible within GROMACS for studies of interfacial structure, charging dynamics, and electrode motion.

articles.title: Molecular Vibronic Complexity as a Quantum Resource for Optimal Control: Nonadiabatic Mixing Creates Protected Coherence Subspaces in Dissipative Environments
articles.abstract: In molecules, electronic coherence typically decays within a few hundred femtoseconds, a timescale usually attributed to the environment. We show that it is set to a large extent by which coherences are excited: the molecule can host coherences that the bath barely sees, and optimal control can find and exploit them. Using gradient-based optimal control (GRAPE) with Redfield dynamics, we maximize the total vibronic coherence between the electronic ground and an optically bright electronic excited state in a three-state model with nonadiabatic features, in two regimes of low and high nonadiabatic mixing and for different system-bath coupling strengths. The Liouvillian spectrum reveals, in both regimes, a well-separated coherence mode with substantial ground-bright character that decays on a picosecond timescale. This mode is protected by mixing with the dark state, which brings the geometry of the optically accessible excited state close to that of the ground state and thus weakens its coupling to the bath. Without prior information, GRAPE finds this mode and keeps the photoexcited wave packet near the Franck-Condon region. At equal fluence, it increases the coherence at 800 fs by more than two orders of magnitude over a Gaussian pulse at the weakest coupling, and by many more at stronger coupling. The Liouvillian predicts the bath dependence of the long-lived coherence to within 1\%, and a Gaussian pulse tuned to the mode frequency comes within 10\% of the best pulse found. Beyond two-level and spin systems, our study puts forward the vibronic structure of molecules as a route to protected coherence subspaces, identifying a dark-state protection mechanism and a design criterion based on molecular parameters. These results lay the groundwork for our goal of using vibronic molecular systems as a resource for long-lived, controllable coherences in molecular quantum information science.

articles.title: Tersoff-NN: Hybrid Machine-Learned Bond-Order Extension of the Tersoff Potential
articles.abstract: Accurate, robust, and efficient interatomic potentials are highly desirable for large-scale molecular dynamics simulations. Although machine-learning interatomic potentials can reproduce first-principles potential-energy surfaces with high accuracy, they typically incur higher computational costs than conventional empirical potentials and may be less reliable outside their training domains. We developed Tersoff-NN, a hybrid machine-learning potential for Si, which retains the analytical radial interactions and cutoff structure of the Tersoff potential while representing its environment-dependent bond-order factor using compact neural networks (NNs). Benchmarks for 32,768-atom systems show that Tersoff-NN is 4-12 times faster than the Behler-Parrinello-type NN potentials tested in this study. Tersoff-NN improves the short-range structure of liquid Si relative to the conventional Tersoff potential, closely reproduces the ab initio radial and angular distributions, and reproduces the equilibrium structure of diamond Si and qualitative energetic trends among several crystalline phases. Furthermore, melt-quench simulations reveal a disordered solid with predominantly four-coordinated, tetrahedral-like local environments. Additionally, characteristic reconstruction motifs are retained on Si surfaces despite their exclusion from the training dataset. A direct comparison with an alternative atom-centered bond-order NN highlights the critical role of physical constraints in ensuring dynamic stability. Despite exhibiting comparable validation errors, the selected triplet-based architecture remains stable, while an alternative model exhibits unphysical bond-order growth and atomic collapse. These results confirm that learning only the bond-order term improves the description of diverse Si environments while retaining substantial computational efficiency and enhancing dynamical stability.

articles.title: The RAS-CCSD model, with applications for open-shell molecules
articles.abstract: The restricted active space coupled cluster singles and doubles (RAS-CCSD) model, and its pilot implementation is detailed. The approach offers a simple, pragmatic way to formulate a coupled cluster theory for open-shell and multireference systems. For ground state energies, errors (compared to FCI) are shown to be similar to those of unrestricted (spin-orbital) CCSD. For excited states, the errors of RAS-CCSD are generally larger, and adaptations to the methodology are needed to achieve an approach which is balanced for both ground and excited states. However, unlike unrestricted CCSD, the approach is spin-adapted and can be used to add dynamical correlation to a multideterminantal reference state.

articles.title: CNT-Mediated Integration of Pd and In2O3 Circumvents Activity–Stability Trade-Off in CO2 Hydrogenation to Methanol
articles.abstract: Metal promotion is a widely adopted strategy to enhance the activity of indium oxide (In2O3) catalysts for CO2 hydrogenation to methanol. However, intimately contacted metal promoters on In2O3 often result in rapid catalyst deactivation, as excessive local H2 supply induces undesirable structural degradation of the In2O3 domain. Here, we address this limitation by implementing a carbon nanotube (CNT)-mediated hydrogen transport pathway, which spatially separates the H2 activation sites (Pd) from the CO2 hydrogenation sites (In2O3) at the catalyst preparation stage. Intriguingly, upon reductive activation, the initially separated components spontaneously evolve into a distinctive interfacial configuration. In this configuration, InOx migrates onto and partially covers the Pd nanoparticles, forming an InOx@Pd inverse interface. Unlike the directly constructed Pd–In2O3 interface, which suffers from over-reduction to metallic In0 accompanied by sintering and alloying with Pd, this CNT-derived interface preserves the In3+ oxidation state and serves as a non-destructive junction for hydrogen delivery. Combined with long-range hydrogen spillover across the CNT network, this architecture transforms a concentrated and destructive hydrogen flux into a regulated supply that reaches distal In2O3 domains without driving over-reduction. Consequently, the Pd/CNT + In2O3 system exhibits both improved catalytic activity and enhanced long-term stability (>230 h), whereas the conventional Pd/In2O3 catalyst deactivates continuously. These findings demonstrate that a controlled hydrogen delivery system between H2 activation sites and active sites on the oxide domain offers an effective way for developing active and durable catalysts involving reduction-sensitive oxide phases.

articles.title: Curvature-Induced Electric-Field Effects Govern Controllable N2 Electrocatalysis on Single-Atom Catalysts
articles.abstract: Electric field-enhanced electrocatalysis represents an innovative strategy for improving the efficiency of electrochemical transformations. However, quantitative evaluation of microscopic electric-field effects under operando conditions remains challenging, limiting a rigorous, predictive understanding of field-mediated reaction regulation. Here, by integrating rigorous numerical methods, constant-potential microkinetic simulations, and machine learning models, we establish electric-field intensity as a quantitative descriptor that directly correlates local fields with catalytic performance. Using curvature-engineered M–N–C single-atom catalysts as a model platform, we demonstrate that curvature-induced electric fields modulate electron occupation at active sites and shift the potential of zero charge in a controllable manner. This field-driven electronic perturbation selectively tunes adsorbate binding energetics, thereby dictating limiting potentials, steering reaction pathways, and governing the thermodynamics and kinetics of interfacial proton-coupled electron transfer in nitrogen electroreduction. Notably, we uncover an inverted volcano–type dependence of catalytic activity on curvature, wherein optimal activity is achieved within a moderate field-strength window. This nonmonotonic trend underscores the necessity of balanced curvature regulation, rather than simply maximizing field intensity, in optimizing electrocatalytic performance. These findings provide a quantitative framework for monitoring and regulating catalytic trends under realistic operating conditions via curvature-induced electric fields, offering generalizable design principles for diverse SAC systems and electrochemical reactions.

articles.title: Diffusion-Selective Modulation Strategy for Enhanced Propane Dehydrogenation via Mixing Inert CHA Zeolite
articles.abstract: Achieving a high propane conversion in propane dehydrogenation to propylene (PDH) carries tremendous scientific and economic value, particularly if achievable with established industrial units. Here we propose a diffusion-selective modulation strategy driven by large-scale machine-learning computation, where the key to success lies in finding auxiliary materials to drive the PDH reaction forward by enlarging the diffusion-rate difference between H2 and C3 species. This strategy is demonstrated theoretically via high-throughput computation and then validated experimentally through the introduction of inert siliceous CHA zeolites as a diffusion-selective modulator within the catalyst bed. By simply physically mixing CHA with various PDH catalysts, we show that the single-pass propane conversion can increase by 1–5% from industrial space velocities (10 h–1) to significantly higher throughputs (256 h–1), consistently improving performance across multiple reported catalysts without compromising stability. This “plug-and-play” methodology can be directly implemented in existing industrial PDH units without altering either the catalyst formulation or the reactor configuration, providing a readily implementable and scalable route for upgrading current PDH infrastructure.

articles.title: Hydration Changes are Essential for Efficient Breakdown of Faropenem by the L1 Metallo-β-lactamase
articles.abstract: Metallo-β-lactamases (MBLs) are key contributors to antimicrobial resistance (AMR). The L1 MBL, originally from Stenotrophomonas maltophilia, is a tetrameric, dizinc, subclass B3 MBL that efficiently hydrolyzes most β-lactam antibiotics and evades inhibitors that act on other MBLs. Using quantum mechanics/molecular mechanics (DFTB3/MM) simulations with enhanced sampling, we mapped the full reaction pathway and minimum free energy profile for L1-catalyzed hydrolysis of faropenem, a penem antibiotic whose reaction can yield alternative enamine and imine products. Benchmarking against B3LYP-D3/6-31G(d) shows that DFTB3 provides the best correlation between energy and structure for this system. We test different possible mechanisms and find that changes in hydration at the metal site during the catalytic cycle are critical for efficient hydrolysis. Our results show that a zinc-bridging hydroxide acts as the nucleophile, with the conserved active site residue D120 participating in back-and-forth proton-transfer events and stabilizing the enzyme-intermediate (EI) complex. The direct reaction of EI, however, involves a large energy barrier; the second stage is facilitated by diffusion of a water molecule into the active site. This water molecule was observed during long-timescale MM MD simulations using the Extended Zinc Amber Force Field (EZAFF). Direct proton transfer from this water to the substrate amide nitrogen forms an enamine product, while imine formation requires rotation of the faropenem 6α-hydroxyethyl substituent to enable proton transfer from water to the substrate C2. The calculated free energy barriers for the formation of both products are consistent with the experimentally determined catalytic constant, and the calculated greater stability of the imine with its crystallographic observation. These simulations provide dynamic insight into L1 catalysis, highlighting features that can be exploited for inhibitor design.

articles.title: Mild Heterogeneous Thiophene Hydrogenation Enabled by a Modified Palladium Catalyst
articles.abstract: Thiophenes are readily available sulfur heteroarenes and prominent motifs in medicinal and synthetic chemistry, but their direct heterogeneous hydrogenation to thiolanes remains challenging due to sulfur-induced catalyst deactivation and competing hydrodesulfurization. Here, we report a chloroform-induced surface modification strategy that enables the heterogeneous Pd(OH)2/C-catalyzed hydrogenation of thiophenes to saturated sulfur heterocycles. The method proceeds under mild hydrogenation conditions and provides access to a range of alkyl-, silyl-, aryl-, and benzofused thiolane derivatives. A hydrogenation-focused robustness assessment revealed compatibility with several functional groups that are commonly sensitive under Pd/H2 conditions, while preparative scope studies showed that functional-group-containing thiophenes can be converted when potentially interfering motifs are separated from the thiophene core by suitable alkyl or aryl spacers. Mechanistic experiments indicate that CHCl3 is not merely a beneficial solvent: CHCl3/H2 pretreatment of Pd(OH)2/C generates a catalytically competent material whose activity is retained after replacing CHCl3 with 2-MeTHF. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) and time-of-flight secondary ion mass spectrometry (ToF-SIMS) analyses support the formation of persistent chloroform-derived organochlorine/C–Cl-type surface environments and chlorocarbon fragments. These findings establish solvent-induced catalyst modification as a useful design principle for challenging heterogeneous hydrogenations of sulfur-containing heteroarenes.

articles.title: Formamidinium-Solvent Intermediates Mediate Self-Seeding Crystallization for Efficient Inverted α-FAPbI3 Perovskite Solar Cells
articles.abstract: Formamidinium lead iodide (FAPbI3) perovskites are promising for high-performance solar cells; however, the low surface energy of self-assembled monolayers (SAMs) impedes α-phase nucleation in inverted devices. Here, we report a formamidinium (FA)-solvent intermediate-mediated self-seeding crystallization strategy to enable quality α-phase FAPbI3. By employing N-formylmorpholine (NFM) as a non-toxic solvent, (FA···NFM)PbI3 intermediates are formed, thereby lowering the phase-transition barrier and promoting the spontaneous formation of α-phase nuclei at the early stage of crystallization. These preformed nuclei serve as intrinsic seeds, facilitating rapid nucleation and orientated crystal growth. Consequently, NFM-based devices achieve efficiencies of 26.41% and 26.56% using 2-methoxyethanol (2-Me) and N,N-dimethylformamide (DMF) as primary solvents, respectively, with a 1 cm2 device reaching 25.47%. The unencapsulated devices retain 85% and 90% of their initial efficiencies after 1200 h illumination and 1400 h thermal aging at 85 °C, respectively.

articles.title: Improving the Calendar Life of Silicon Anodes with Inorganic Solid–Electrolyte Interphases
articles.abstract: Silicon anodes unlock higher energy density in Li-ion batteries but suffer from poor calendar life due to inadequately passivating solid–electrolyte interphases (SEIs). Here, we contrast the calendar aging behaviors of single- and mixed-salt locally superconcentrated electrolytes (LSCEs) against carbonate electrolytes. Mixed-salt LSCE cells retained 96% and 44% of precalendar capacity after one month and then after five months, while carbonate electrolyte cells retained 77% and 1%, respectively. The mixed-salt LSCE advantage is tied to the formation of a predominantly inorganic SEI, evidenced by nanoscale Fourier transform infrared spectromicroscopy, X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, and 3D time-of-flight secondary ion mass spectrometry. After 5 months, however, perturbations to SEIs were evident in all cells, accelerating voltage decay and capacity loss by lithium inventory loss associated with SEI growth. These findings suggest that future electrolytes may benefit from strategies that continuously reinforce the SEI through controlled anion and solvent redox in LSCEs.

articles.title: Membrane-Anchored Dual-Targeting Aptamer Engagers for Programmable T Cell Redirection in Solid and Hematological Cancers
articles.abstract: Inefficient immune synapse formation limits the therapeutic efficacy of T cell-based immunotherapy in both solid tumors and hematological malignancies. Here, we report a fully synthetic, membrane-anchored dual-targeting aptamer engager, AptE 2, that acts as a programmable artificial immunological interface to redirect cytotoxic T cells toward cancer cells without genetic engineering. Constructed entirely from DNA aptamers through optimized bioorthogonal conjugation and enzyme-mediated ligation, AptE 2 integrates multivalent tumor recognition, T cell binding, enhanced nuclease resistance, and prolonged membrane anchoring within a single modular scaffold. In colorectal cancer models, AptE 2 promoted stable T cell–tumor cell engagement, enhanced cytotoxicity and cytokine secretion, and drove pronounced tumor regression with increased intratumoral CD8+ T cell infiltration and minimal systemic toxicity. Importantly, AptE 2 also demonstrated broad applicability in leukemia. In CCRF-CEM cells, AptE 2 exhibited strong surface binding, sustained membrane retention for up to 6 h, and superior resistance to wash-off compared with monovalent aptamers and bivalent controls. AptE 2-prearmed TALL-104 cells markedly enhanced leukemia cell clustering, increased cell lysis to over 90% under optimized coculture conditions, and amplified IFN-γ secretion. In a disseminated CCRF-CEM-Luc leukemia mouse model, AptE 2-mediated T cell therapy suppressed systemic leukemia progression, improved peripheral hematological profiles, and showed favorable tolerability without detectable major organ injury. These findings establish AptE 2 as a generalizable, nonprotein-based and nonviral immune engager platform for programmable T cell redirection across both solid and hematological cancers.

articles.title: Oncolytic Virus-like Nanoparticle Targets the Golgi Apparatus via Sphingomyelin
articles.abstract: The Golgi apparatus (GA) has emerged as a promising target for cancer therapy. Commonly, therapeutics are guided to the GA by recognizing specific receptors on the GA membrane. However, the low and heterogeneous expression of these receptors often results in suboptimal targeting efficiency. Here, we present an oncolytic virus-like nanoparticle for GA targeting by exploiting sphingomyelin, an abundant component of the GA membrane. This nanoparticle consisted of a polymeric nanocarrier complexed with a plasmid encoding the secreting peptide-deleted α-hemolysin (αHL), a pore-forming protein with high affinity for sphingomyelin. The nanoparticle could transfect cancer cells to induce intracellular expression of αHL, enabling GA targeting through binding to GA-associated sphingomyelin while bypassing the cell membrane. Consequently, the transfected cells exhibited GA structural disassembly and underwent a pyroptosis-like programmed cell death with immunogenic characteristics. Notably, αHL-rich microvesicles were subsequently secreted, effectively killing neighboring tumor cells. Intratumoral administration of this formulation significantly suppressed subcutaneous tumor growth and elicited robust antitumor immunity, preventing tumor rechallenge. Furthermore, by incorporating iRGD-modified polymers, we constructed a tumor-targeting oncolytic virus-like nanoparticle with neutral surface charge. Following intravenous administration, this iRGD-modified nanoparticle could efficiently suppress tumor growth without causing obvious systemic toxicity. Collectively, this work presents a robust strategy for GA-targeting via sphingomyelin recognition, providing a potential approach for GA-targeted anticancer therapeutics.

articles.title: pH-Programmed Poly(amino acid) Nanoparticles for Mucus-Penetrating and Bacteria-Targeted Eradication of Helicobacter pylori
articles.abstract: The global prevalence of Helicobacter pylori (H. pylori) infection stands in stark contrast to the limited clinical efficacy of antibiotics, primarily attributed to their rapid inactivation under gastric acidity and poor penetration through the gastric mucus barrier. Here, we report a pH-programmed poly(amino acid)-based nanoplatform for the precise eradication of H. pylori. This platform is constructed from poly(amino acid) block copolymers (FAR) incorporating d-aminoalanine side chains and rhamnolipid (RHL) moieties, which self-assemble into amoxicillin-loaded nanoparticles (Am@FAR NPs). Under strongly acidic gastric conditions (pH < 3), Am@FAR NPs undergo extensive protonation, adopting a compact, stabilized configuration that suppresses premature drug release and preserves antibiotic activity. Upon entering the gastric mucus layer (pH ∼ 4–6), partial deprotonation induces surface charge reversal, reducing nonspecific mucin adhesion and facilitating efficient mucus penetration. Cooperative recognition, mediated by RHL and d-aminoalanine residues, enables selective targeting of H. pylori within the mucus niche; here, further local pH elevation (∼6–7) triggers particle swelling and on-site drug release. Consequently, Am@FAR NPs achieve 99.99% eradication efficiency against H. pyloriin vivo, offering a highly effective and biocompatible strategy for the treatment of gastric H. pylori infections.

100‐Fold Reductivity Enhancement of Nanoscale Zero‐Valent Iron After 1‐Year Aging in Water via Regulating Corrosion Reactions
articles.abstract: Nanoscale zero‐valent iron (nZVI) is the most promising reductant for in situ groundwater remediation, but its field application around the world is quite limited for decades, due to significant reductivity loss by water oxidation during long‐term (e.g., years) application. Herein, we report a polysiloxane(Fe)‐modified nZVI (PSO(Fe)‐nZVI, 269.0 ± 23.5 nm) featuring loosened hydrophobic C16 chains and Si─O groups on the surface and interior. Remarkably, after 420‐day aging in water, PSO(Fe)‐nZVI exhibits 102‐fold and 211‐fold enhancements of reduction rate constants for trichloroethylene and Cr(VI), respectively, 4‐order‐of‐magnitude higher than nZVI. The loosened C16 chains on PSO(Fe)‐nZVI could regulate Fe(0)→Fe(II) reaction in water to enhance specific surface area by 131 folds and expose more active Fe species. The Si─O groups could combine with Fe(II) and inhibit the Fe(II)→Fe(III) reaction to reserve 70.8% of active Fe species. This work highlights the regulation of corrosion reactions by surface engineering to boost the reduction performance of nZVI for long‐term groundwater remediation.

articles.title: A Bioinspired Antifreezing Electrolyte Enabling Stable and Low‐Temperature Fluoride‐Ion Batteries via Hydrogen‐Bond Reconfiguration
articles.abstract: Fluoride‐ion batteries (FIBs) are appealing for their high theoretical energy density and low cost, wherein aqueous electrolytes provide the exceptionally high fluoride‐salt solubility and fast ion transport. However, the strong H2O−H2O hydrogen‐bond network promotes the proton/hydroxide shuttling and leaves the reactive free water at interface, leading to parasitic reactions, corrosion and active‐material dissolution, which severely limit cycling stability. Here we show that reconfiguring the hydrogen‐bond network of water offers a molecular‐level pathway to stabilize aqueous FIB chemistry. We report a bioinspired hydrogel electrolyte by introducing hyaluronic acid (HA) into CsF aqueous electrolyte, together with ethylene glycol (EG) as an antifreezing co‐solvent. HA reorganizes the hydrogen‐bond network to immobilize free water and suppress water activity, while HA/EG jointly regulate the solvation environment of F−, reducing the hydration level and facilitating the interfacial fluoride transfer. The HA‐based electrolyte forms a robust, chemically rich CEI containing organic (O/N‐containing) and fluoride‐rich inorganic components, which mitigates interfacial side reactions and suppresses active species dissolution. A CuF2||Pb full cell delivers the stable cycling with a ∼0.5 V discharge plateau and retains over 100 mAh·g−1 after 160 cycles, and further demonstrates the reversible FIB operation down to −20°C for the first time.

articles.title: A Cytochrome P450 Enzyme‐Catalyzed Acetyl Migration in Cyanogramide Biosynthesis
articles.abstract: Cyanogramide (1) is a unique spirooxindole alkaloid derived from a marine actinomycete and is characterized by its distinct spirocyclic pyrrolo[1,2‐c]imidazolidin‐4‐one scaffold. Although we have successfully elucidated the biosynthetic pathway of 1, the mechanism underlying the formation of the characteristic imidazolidin‐4‐one remains unclear. In this study, we demonstrate that the cytochrome P450 monooxygenase CyaI catalyzes an oxidation reaction through a zwitterionic intermediate and facilitates a subsequent unusual C→N acetyl migration, which triggers a spontaneous intramolecular cyclization to forge the imidazolidin‐4‐one ring during 1 biosynthesis. In addition, CyaI is identified as a bifunctional enzyme that also catalyzes N‐demethylation. High‐resolution crystallography and mutagenesis studies determine Thr245 as a crucial catalytic residue that modulates the balance between imidazolidine‐4‐one synthesis and demethylation. This work not only expands the catalytic repertoire of P450 enzymes but also opens the way for the development of multifunctional biocatalysts in the synthesis of complex natural products.

articles.title: A Dual‐Interface Stabilizing Additive for High‐voltage Sodium Metal Batteries
articles.abstract: High-voltage sodium metal batteries (SMBs) suffer from fast degradation stemming from the interfacial incompatibility between electrolytes and electrodes. In this study, potassium 3-pyridyltrifluoroborate (KPBF3) is proposed as a dual-interface electrolyte additive, where the pyridine moiety can effectively modulate the anion's electronic structure, lowering its lowest unoccupied molecular orbital energy level and enhancing its binding affinity for Na+. This promotes the preferential reductive decomposition of PBF3 −, forming a robust NaF-rich solid electrolyte interphase that suppresses Na dendrite growth. Simultaneously, the cleavage of B─F bonds facilitates the formation of a thin and uniform NaF-rich cathode electrolyte interphase (CEI), significantly suppressing electrolyte oxidation and greatly improving the high-voltage stability. Consequently, Na||Na symmetric cells achieve an ultra-long cycling life of 6000 h at 5 mA cm−2, while Na||Cu cells exhibit a high average Coulombic efficiency (ACE) of 99.89%. Moreover, Na||Na3V2(PO4)2F3 cells demonstrate 90.8% capacity retention over 10000 cycles at 10 C and 4.3 V, and 90.0% retention after 2500 cycles at 4.4 V. Notably, this additive also enables SMBs with a low N/P ratio of 2.65 to deliver a high capacity retention of 88.4% after 1000 cycles.

articles.title: A Full‐Spectrum‐Responsive MOF‐on‐MOF Heterojunction Photocatalyst for Concurrent Nitrate Reduction and Biomass Oxidation
articles.abstract: Photocatalytic nitrate reduction reaction (PNitRR) offers a sustainable route for ammonia (NH3) synthesis and wastewater treatment. The insufficient utilization of near-infrared (NIR) light and sluggish reaction kinetics of coupled water oxidation result in unsatisfactory performance. Herein, a conductive metal organic framework (cMOF)-on-cMOF S-scheme heterojunction is reported as an efficient full-spectrum photocatalyst for driving an innovative hybrid system of PNitRR to NH3 and photocatalytic 5-hydroxymethylfurfural oxidation reaction (PHMFOR) to 2, 5-furandicarboxylic acid (FDCA). The integration of Co-cMOF and Ni-cMOF with dual NIR-response features and well-matched band structures into an S-scheme heterojunction enables sufficient light utilization and efficient charge separation. Moreover, the formation of interfacial Ni-Co dual sites with modulated electronic structures accounts for PNitRR and PHMFOR, respectively, with enhanced activity and selectivity. The designed cMOF-on-cMOF S-scheme heterojunction photocatalyst exhibits production rates of 4677.5 and 5932.5 µmol gcat −1 h−1 with apparent quantum yields of 13.3% and 13.1% at 500 nm for NH3 and FDCA production, respectively. This work opens new avenues for the development of advanced photocatalysts and integrated photocatalytic systems to produce valuable chemicals.

articles.title: A Metal‐COF‐Based SERS Platform for PPb‐Level Toluene Sensing With Tailored Metal Selectivity
articles.abstract: Ultrasensitive detection of nonpolar toxic VOCs like toluene remains a great challenge for environmental monitoring. This work presents a rationally designed SERS platform based on metallized covalent organic frameworks (M‐COFs, M = Fe, Ni, Cu) obtained by a mild metal‐modulation strategy that enables metal‑tunable COF crystallinity and porosity. M‐COFs were one‐pot synthesized from PyTA and PDA under 70 °C and atmospheric pressure. Spectroscopic characterizations confirm atomic dispersion of M2+ with four‐coordinate M─N/O bonding in the frameworks. Particularly, Fe─COF exhibits superior crystallinity and an enhanced BET surface area of 2078 m2 g−1 with a pore size of 1.87 nm, whereas Ni‑ and Cu─COF show reduced structural order. The Au/Fe─COF SERS platform achieves a toluene detection limit of 0.1 ppb with an enhancement factor of 1.5 × 106, outperforming Ni─COF (0.5 ppb), Cu─COF (1 ppm), and metal‐free COF (10 ppb). DFT calculations verify Fe─COF ’s ultrahigh toluene adsorption affinity with an adsorption energy of −34.17 kcal mol−1 and its higher crystallinity compared to its counterparts. This platform also shows excellent anti‐interference and enables specific toluene detection in complex gas mixtures. The M‐COF‐based SERS system offers a practical solution for ultra‐trace nonpolar VOC monitoring.

articles.title: A Narrow‐Bandgap Fused‐Ring Acceptor for Organic Short‐Wavelength Infrared Imager
articles.abstract: Organic short‐wavelength infrared (SWIR) imaging is a promising technology for consumer electronics and a broad range of other applications. The bottleneck of organic SWIR imaging is the lack of electron acceptors with ultrasmall bandgaps. Herein, we develop ultrasmall‐bandgap electron acceptors by cyclizing the exocyclic vinylene linkers of a typical acceptor–donor–acceptor (A–D–A) electron acceptor with tetrafluorobenzene moieties. This tetrafluorobenzene cyclization redshifts the absorption spectrum by 224 nm and reduces the trap density of states of the neat film by nearly one order of magnitude. The resulting organic photodetector exhibits a peak responsivity of 0.36 A W−1, a noise current of 1.41 × 10−11 A Hz−1/2 at 1 kHz, a specific detectivity exceeding 109 Jones at 1140 nm under −1 V bias, and a linear dynamic range of 82 dB. Monolithic integration of this organic photodetector with thin‐film transistor arrays yields a 256 × 256 pixel imager capable of high‐contrast SWIR imaging. This work establishes tetrafluorobenzene cyclization as a powerful molecular paradigm for ultrasmall bandgap organic semiconductors, paving the way for low‐cost, heavy‐metal‐free SWIR imagers in consumer electronics.

articles.title: A Temperature‐Sensitive Dual Ion Channel Based on Quinoline Helix for H+/Cl− Cotransport With Remarkable Antitumor Effect
articles.abstract: Synthetic ion channels with efficient ion transport activity can disrupt the ion homeostasis of cancer cells and exhibit potential for tumor therapy. Herein, a helix‐based ion channel was constructed via a one‐pot synthesis strategy. This channel is composed of two interconnected proton channel (quinoline helix) and chloride ion channel (aligned thiourea moieties), which is named as “dual ion channel.” This dual ion channel can insert into the phospholipid membrane through a single‐molecule form and flux H+ and Cl− across the membrane simultaneously. Interestingly, this dual ion channel also exhibits “ON‐OFF” switchable ion transport behaviors in response to external temperature variation. Under physiological environment (37°C), this channel achieves highly efficient ion transport and reveals remarkable anticancer activity against U87 cells with an IC50 value of 0.14 µM, which is comparable to commercial chemotherapy drugs. The mechanism induces mitochondrial membrane potential loss and destabilizes subcellular organelles, including lysosomes, leading to the release of reactive oxygen species (ROS) and cytochrome c, which ultimately activates the intrinsic apoptosis pathway and results in programmed cell death of tumor cells. This dual ion channel not only serves as a potent anticancer agent but also provides an entry point for future design of functional ion channels.

articles.title: Accelerating H* Redistribution via Hydrogen Spillover for Enhanced Electrochemical Hydrogen Production From Formaldehyde
articles.abstract: Producing hydrogen from formaldehyde oxidation reaction (FOR) offers a promising low-energy approach for generating clean fuel. However, the FOR involves continuous C─H bond cleavage of adsorbed intermediates to generate abundant surface H*. This necessitates rapid transfer and consumption of H* to sustain fast oxidation kinetics. Herein, we developed a hydrogen-spillover strategy to redistribute these surface H* to accelerate FOR kinetics by constructing RhCu single-atom alloy supported on a Cu single-atom-rich carbon matrix (RhCu@CuSANC). In this design, Cu incorporation creates a favorable landscape for H* migration toward the CuSANC support, which acts as efficient H* acceptors and H─H coupling centers. Verified through multiple analyses, this hydrogen-spillover mechanism is demonstrated to enhance FOR activity by accelerating H* redistribution. Consequently, RhCu@CuSANC shows outstanding FOR performance, achieving a current density of 800 mA cm− 2 at 0.39 V with nearly 100% H2 selectivity and excellent durability. When integrated into a hybrid alkali-acid cell, it provides an open circuit voltage of 1.72 V and peak power density of 152.6 mW cm− 2 with stable H2 production for over 1200 h at 10 mA cm− 2. These results demonstrate that hydrogen spillover boosts oxidative electrocatalysis, providing a general design principle for multicomponent catalysts with coordinated hydrogen dynamics.

articles.title: Activating Triplet Excitons in COFs via Layer‐Bridging Co Single Atoms for Photocatalytic H2O2 Production and Tandem C─N Coupling
articles.abstract: Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) are promising photocatalysts for solar energy conversion in energy and environmental applications. However, their performance is intrinsically limited by weak spin–orbit coupling (SOC) arising from van der Waals interlayer interactions, thereby suppressing intersystem crossing and triplet-exciton utilization. In this study, we demonstrate that layer-bridging Co single atoms activate triplet excitons in COFs by synergistically enhancing SOC and inducing energy-level splitting via Co─N coordination. This layer-bridging Co coordination markedly promotes singlet-to-triplet conversion, enabling efficient O2 activation and substantially boosting the generation of both 1O2 and O2 •−. Consequently, the Co-bridged COF achieves highly efficient photocatalytic H2O2 production and tandem C─N coupling. This work establishes layer-bridging single-atom coordination as a promising strategy for regulating triplet-state reactivity in COFs, offering new opportunities for reactive oxygen species (ROS)-mediated photocatalysis and tandem organic transformations.

articles.title: Adaptive Assembly of Dative B←N Frameworks for Dimension‐Controlled Hetero‐Engineering
articles.abstract: Luminescent heterostructures with spatially resolved emission hold great promise for optoelectronic applications, yet dimension‐controlled hetero‐assembly for stimuli‐responsive heterostructures remains a significant challenge owing to the uncertain integration of distinct components. Herein, we reported an adaptive assembly strategy in dative B←N framework, enabling dimension‐controlled synthesis of luminescent heterostructures with stimuli‐responsive properties. The conformational flexibility of boroxine units permit the epitaxial ligand to form the similar conformation as the seed ligand, triggering the adaptive hetero‐assembly between different frameworks. Moreover, the structural similarity on side chains of seed and epitaxial ligands determines the spatial matching degree at heterointerface, and thus adjusting the structural types of ligand side chains enables precise regulation of both the interfacial lattice matching and assembly orientation, thereby constructing one‐dimensional and two‐dimensional B←N framework heterostructures. The resulting heterostructures exhibit spatially‐resolved stimuli‐responsive emission by inheriting intramolecular charge transfer of ligands, functioning as photonic barcode labels with multi‐level authentication capability. These findings provide insights into optical heterostructures that combine tunable dimensionality with responsive functionality.

articles.title: Adaptive Solvation Evolution by Molecular Design Enables High‐Performance Wide‐Temperature Lithium‐Ion Batteries
articles.abstract: The solvation structure is a decisive factor for the performance of lithium‐ion batteries (LIBs) under extreme environments, and its evolution with temperature changes is particularly elusive. This work reports a strategy to regulate the coordination interactions between solvents, Li+, and anions through a local steric shielding effect of α‐methyl‐substituted solvents, thereby forming a temperature‐adaptive evolution of the solvation structure, ensuring efficient ion transport over the entire temperature range (from −80°C to 100°C). Practical pouch cells demonstrated outstanding performance: 1 Ah LiFePO4 (LFP)||graphite (Gr) commercial pouch cells retained 87.4% capacity after 2000 cycles at 2 C and 25°C, and delivered stable discharge capacities down to −60°C (0.47 Ah). Meanwhile, the 1 Ah LiNi0.8Mn0.1Co0.1O2 (NMC811)||Gr pouch cells maintained 83.2% capacity over 4000 cycles at 1 C and 25°C, while also delivering 0.49 Ah at −80°C and maintaining operational functionality even at 100°C. The strategy offers a practical route toward LIB electrolytes with broad temperature adaptability and long cycle life.

articles.title: Aminosulfine‐Based Donor Platform for Controlled Release of Sulfenic Acid (HSOH)
articles.abstract: Reactive sulfur species derived from hydrogen sulfide are central regulators of redox signaling; however, sulfenic acid (HSOH) has remained largely inaccessible owing to the absence of chemically defined donor systems. Here we report a mechanistically delineated strategy for controlled HSOH generation based on an intramolecular cyclization–release platform incorporating an aminosulfine (thioamide S‐oxide) motif. Aminosulfine derivatives containing an ester group can undergo a unique acyl transfer process via the nucleophilicity of the α‐amide ion, followed by intramolecular cyclization to release HSOH, providing a chemically tractable route for transient HSOH release. Systematic structure–activity relationship and kinetic studies further indicate that achieving efficient HSOH release requires precise kinetic matching between the acyl transfer rate and the intramolecular cyclization rate. Using complementary chemical trapping approaches and a persulfide‐selective fluorescent probe, we demonstrate that transiently generated HSOH exhibits exceptionally high reactivity, rapidly undergoing disproportionation and efficiently promoting thiol persulfidation even at low concentrations. Importantly, HSOH signaling confers protection against oxidative injury in a cellular oxygen–glucose deprivation model. This work establishes a chemically defined framework for probing HSOH‐initiated sulfur signaling and provides fundamental insights into the reactivity and biological implications of this elusive reactive sulfur species.

articles.title: Amorphous Intermediates Mediate van der Waals Nanosheets Formation via Anion‐Exchange‐Driven Symmetry Breaking
articles.abstract: Fe3GeTe2 has attracted considerable attention as a two‐dimensional (2D) van der Waals (vdW) magnetic material owing to its exceptional electromagnetic properties and potential for spintronic applications. However, complex thermodynamic competition among multiple metal species, together with severe kinetic barriers associated with the transformation from dense non‐vdW frameworks to vdW layered structures, has thus far prevented the solution phase synthesis, thereby severely limiting in‐depth property research and mechanistic understanding. Here we report a colloidal anion exchange strategy that enables the solution phase synthesis of Fe3GeTe2. By combining experiments with density functional theory (DFT) calculations, we identify an amorphous intermediate that kinetically decouples compositional evolution from structural reconstruction, thereby lowering the energy barrier and enabling a crystalline–amorphism–recrystalline phase transition. In this process, anion exchange induces symmetry breaking of the initial lattice and subsequent structural reorganization, ultimately driving the transformation from a non‐vdW framework to vdW layered structure. Moreover, this strategy is readily extended to other 2D material systems, leading to the successful synthesis of paramagnetic CuFeTe2 and NiTe2 as well as topological layered Bi2Te3, thereby establishing a general methodological pathway for accessing complex 2D vdW layered magnetic materials.

articles.title: Anchored Oxygen‐Release‐Suppression Phase Stabilizing High‐Voltage Ni‐Rich Cathode Materials
articles.abstract: The Ni‐rich LiNixCoyMn1−x−yO2 (x ≥ 0.9) cathode materials (NCMs) have been considered promising for next‐generation Li‐ion batteries owing to their high‐energy density. However, their practical application is hindered by gas evolution and rapid capacity degradation, primarily caused by irreversible oxygen release and structural instability. Herein, a facile one‐step anchoring strategy is proposed to overcome this challenge by engineering a precisely tailored dual‐architecture LiNi0.9Co0.05Mn0.05O2 (DA‐NCM). This strategy constructs a dual‐phase surface architecture on Ni‐rich cathodes, where perovskite‐phase La4LiNiO8 mitigates surface oxygen instability and interfacial degradation, and inert La2Mo2O9 anchors the lattice to avoid the detachment of La4LiNiO8 during cycling via enhanced La─O bond pinning effect. This dual‐architecture design provides a robust strategy for stabilizing the interface, surface, and bulk phase of Ni‐rich cathodes, enabling durable oxygen regulation, suppressed structural degradation, and stable high‐voltage operation under demanding cycling conditions. Thus, our DA‐NCM cathodes demonstrate excellent capacity retention of 95.7% at 4.3 V and 93.6% at 4.5 V after 200 cycles and remarkable stability even at an elevated temperature (50°C) and high voltage (4.5 V), confirming their markedly enhanced electrochemical stability. This precision design of dual architecture provides a new pathway for developing high‐energy‐density cathode materials with long cycle life.

articles.title: Asymmetric Dual Sites Enable Spatially Resolved Biradical‐Mediated C–N Coupling for N,N‐Dimethylformamide Photoelectrosynthesis
articles.abstract: N,N‐dimethylformamide (DMF) is a quintessential industrial solvent and precursor, and its energy‐intensive, high‐temperature conventional synthesis necessitates the development of mild, sustainable biomass‐derived alternatives. Photoelectrocatalysis (PEC) offers a promising green route; however, its performance is limited by competitive adsorption and inadequate control over reaction selectivity. Herein, we engineered an asymmetric dual‐site earth‐abundant semiconductor to achieve biradical‐mediated C–N coupling, attaining a Faradaic efficiency of 86.6%, a selectivity of 90.1%, and a DMF yield of 145.5 mmol m−2 h−1. For practical implementation, the parallel‐connect stacked PEC device, with an area of 175 cm2, was recorded as the state‐of‐the‐art PEC system for DMF photoelectrosynthesis. Mechanistic investigations revealed that bismuth vacancies, possessing a high p‐band center, preferentially activated methanol to generate *CHO radicals, whereas BiOx sites, characterized by a moderate electronic environment, selectively catalyzed dimethylamine to form *N(CH3)2 radicals. This dual‐site architecture effectively decouples the competitive adsorption of alcohol and amine substrates, enabling spatial segregation and achieving biradical‐mediated C–N coupling. Importantly, the system demonstrated broad substrate adaptability, including cyclic secondary amines, highlighting its potential for constructing valuable amide derivatives. Our work provides a practical strategy for the mild valorization of biomass feedstocks and establishes an electronic structure‐guided paradigm for selectivity control and kinetic optimization in biradical‐mediated C–N coupling.

Practical Considerations for Operando 7Li Nuclear Magnetic Resonance in Coin and Pouch Cells
articles.abstract: Operando nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy provides unique insight into chemical changes in batteries during use but has largely been limited to custom plastic cells. Unfortunately, the metal casings that house commercial batteries distort and shield radiofrequency (RF) fields required for excitation and detection in NMR. Here, we use operando7Li NMR spectroscopy to study metal-encased batteries in both coin and pouch cell formats without modifying the cell or casing. We benchmark NMR spectra obtained from stainless-steel coin cells and aluminum-laminate pouch cells to plastic coin cells and show that casing composition, auxiliary hardware, and sample placement strongly influence observed shift, signal intensity, and line shape due to bulk magnetic susceptibility effects and RF attenuation upon interacting with cell parts. These effects are most severe in stainless-steel coin cells (and in particular 304-grade stainless steel) but can be mitigated through the use of Al spacers while retaining the stainless-steel caps and springs. In light of these considerations, we leverage operando7Li NMR to track lithium plating/stripping and monitor the accumulation of electrochemically inactive “dead” lithium (Li0) during galvanostatic cycling in coin and pouch cells. In pouch cells, the lean electrolyte volume allows us to resolve changes in the 7Li electrolyte signal during formation that are consistent with electrolyte redistribution and wetting. Taken together, these results demonstrate how to alter cell susceptibility to improve NMR signals during operando measurements in commercially relevant form factors while also establishing the cell design constraints that limit quantitative interpretation.

articles.title: Unraveling the Mystery of Near-Infrared Emission in an Antimony Halide Dimer Driven by the Jahn–Teller Effect
articles.abstract: Most zero-dimensional hybrid metal halides enable emission in the first near-infrared (NIR-I) region (650–950 nm), and the shorter wavelengths result in poor photon penetration depth. Here, we report the observation of an NIR-II emission signal (band gap = 1.13 eV) from a (BTBAC)2Sb2Cl8 single crystal at room temperature. Although a variety of mechanisms are involved in the explanation of such a broad band with a large Stokes shift, the exploration of the structural origin of the NIR optical activity remains challenging due to misconceptions about excitons and experimental limitations. A strategy that spatially confines 5s2 ions within edge-shared [Sb2Cl8]2– units with controlled lattice distortion is proposed to cause a Jahn–Teller effect (JTE) during the interconfiguration transition (3P1 → 1S0). A family of hybrid metal halides doped with Bi3+,In3+ or Bi3+/In3+ demonstrates that the fine interplay between the Jahn–Teller effect and spin–orbit coupling (SOC) takes into full consideration orbital degeneracy and electron flipping, thus boosting the photoluminescence quantum yield to 12%. TD-DFT calculations visualize the symmetry of the two lattices within a dimeric structure varying with specific modes, and the rational assignment of the energy gap (ground state: 3.69 eV; excited state: 1.22 eV) between 1S0 and 3P1 is highly consistent with the experimental findings (λex = 330 nm; λem = 1100 nm). Leveraging the (BTBAC)2Sb2Cl8 sample, electroluminescence pumped by a UV-LED chip yields a highly efficient NIR-II emission, and the phosphor displays diverse functions in night vision and anticounterfeiting.

articles.title: Snail Inventories for Short‐Term Impacts: Methodological Differences and Their Underlying Causes
articles.abstract: In research on terrestrial gastropod communities, a fundamental methodological question is whether to include empty shells in the investigations alongside living individuals. In this study, we examined potential biases introduced in the analyses by the inclusion of fresh empty shells (with intact periostracum). We started by reanalysing a dataset about the short‐term effects of mowing and mulching on a grassland snail community. For the original analysis, only live specimen data were used, whereas here we used a so‐called combined dataset including live individuals and fresh empty shells. While the live data revealed significant negative impacts of mowing on the snail community, these effects were undetectable with the combined data. Concurrently, we observed substantial interspecific variation in the overrepresentation value among species (the ratio of a species' combined abundance to its live abundance), which represents a distortion in the distribution of the total number of individuals across species. To explore the underlying causes of this phenomenon, we investigated the physical and chemical resistance of the shells of eleven species under laboratory conditions and simulated the effects of life history traits and shell‐degradation rate on overrepresentation using a multistage population model. Contrary to expectations, our results indicated that this variation in overrepresentation was not explained by shell resistance but rather by shell size: significantly higher overrepresentation was observed in smaller species, even though their shells are weaker, so may decompose faster. This relationship may be driven by the faster life cycles and higher turnover rates of smaller species, a finding corroborated by our population model. We concluded that the inclusion of empty shells can significantly distort the perception of the instantaneous state of the community and mask short‐term temporal changes. We recommend prioritising live data for detecting short‐term impacts and explicitly stating and justifying the chosen data type in scientific publications.

Shrubs benefit from being functionally more conservative and distinct from neighbour trees
articles.abstract: Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog. Abstract Multi‐strata forests can enhance ecosystem functioning, with interactions between overstorey trees and understorey shrubs playing a pivotal role. However, how the structure and composition of neighbouring trees, together with shrub traits, influence shrub growth remains poorly understood. In a large‐scale subtropical biodiversity experiment manipulating tree and shrub species richness, we inventoried 4411 shrubs and their surrounding trees after 11 years of interactions. We found that individual shrub biomass declined with increasing neighbour tree species richness, basal area and functional diversity, but exhibited a U‐shaped trend with the proportion of ectomycorrhizal‐associated neighbour tree individuals. Shrubs with more conservative resource‐use strategies attained higher biomass, particularly when surrounded by trees with low functional diversity and a high proportion of ectomycorrhizal associations. Biomass was also greater when shrubs were more resource‐conservative and functionally distinct from the neighbouring trees. Our findings highlight how shrub functional traits, combined with tree diversity, competition and functional traits, shape tree–shrub interactions, with shrubs benefiting more from resource‐conservative and functionally distinct traits relative to their neighbouring trees. articles.title: Why don't all birds lay early? Causes and consequences of breeding timing for a long‐lived migratory seabird
articles.abstract: Why don't all birds lay early? Our 16‐year study of Manx shearwater behaviour shows that selection on breeding timing fluctuates among years. We also find that lay dates are influenced by persistent individual differences, variation in non‐breeding duration, and pair synchrony, potentially constraining breeding phenological advancement under ongoing climate change. Abstract The relationship between earlier laying and higher breeding success is well‐established in avian species. However, a wide distribution of breeding timings is often maintained within a population, and the causes and consequences of this variation require further exploration, particularly as many avian species advance breeding phenology in response to climate change. Using a 16‐year dataset combining colony observations and biologging of Manx shearwaters (Puffinus puffinus), we show that earlier laying does not always result in higher breeding success, with later laying becoming less costly in recent years. We additionally report a slight advancement in breeding timing within breeding pairs, despite finding no temporal trends in spring bloom onset. Nonetheless, birds adjusted lay date in response to interannual variation in phytoplankton bloom timing, and years with stronger Celtic Sea blooms exhibited stronger selection for early breeding. Breeding timing was also influenced by repeatable individual differences in migratory behaviour, with birds undertaking generally earlier, shorter migrations to less southerly destinations laying earlier across years. However, lay date was not determined solely by individual behaviour. In this long‐lived species with stable pair bonds, the arrival date of the second‐returning bird constrained advancement in laying. This study suggests that variation in breeding timing is maintained through the combined effects of fluctuating selection, persistent individual differences, variation in non‐breeding duration and pair‐level processes. Competing Magnetic Configurations Enable Low-Field Magnetoresistance Switching in Cr3Te4
articles.abstract: Large magnetoresistance typically emerges from transitions between distinct electronic phases or magnetic configurations, yet controllable switching between competing magnetic configurations within a single metallic material remains challenging. Here we investigate magnetotransport in Cr3Te4 and demonstrate a magnetic-field-switchable resistance modulation of up to −37.6%, enabled by the near degeneracy between antiparallel and parallel magnetic configurations. Remarkably, a magnetic field of ∼0.25 T suffices to induce switching between these competing magnetic configurations, accompanied by a reconstruction in electronic transport supported by Boltzmann transport calculations. Substituting 5% of Cr with Co suppresses the switching behavior, consistent with a suppression of the competition between the nearly degenerate magnetic configurations, while the magnetoresistance evolves into a negative longitudinal magnetoresistance, suggesting a possible Weyl-band-related contribution associated with a Co-induced upward shift of the Fermi level. Our results establish competing magnetic configurations as an effective route toward large magnetoresistance in structurally simple metallic systems.

articles.title: Continuously Tunable Localized Surface Plasmon Resonance of Anisotropic Gold Nanopolyhedrons for Multiplexed Surface-Enhanced Raman Scattering Imaging
articles.abstract: Surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) is attractive for multiplex bioimaging owing to its excellent photostability and ultranarrow spectral bandwidth. However, achieving synergistic enhancement of excitation and Raman scattering fields remains challenging. Herein, the relationship between geometry and localized surface plasmon resonance (LSPR) was investigated by continuously tuning the aspect ratio (AR) of anisotropic Au nanopolyhedrons (Au NPHs). Central-body modulation while preserving sharp terminal tips enables continuous LSPR tuning while retaining tip-associated electromagnetic enhancement. The SERS behavior was further analyzed by considering the spectral matching between the LSPR and the excitation/scattering wavelengths. For different excitation wavelengths, the optimal SERS response can be achieved by selecting Au NPHs whose LSPR band best matches with the excitation and Raman scattering wavelengths. These results demonstrate that Raman enhancement is governed by spectral matching rather than a fixed optimal geometry. The optimized Au NPHs enabled the use of dual SERS probes for proof-of-concept multiplex biomarker imaging.

articles.title: Experimental Signature of Transient Symmetry Breaking in a Cavity Dirty-Limit Superconductor
articles.abstract: Transient states of matter far from equilibrium may exhibit physical properties beyond those allowed by the equilibrium-state crystalline symmetries. We explore ultrafast and direct electronic excitations of transient states in a dirty-limit superconductor with time-resolved terahertz-pump terahertz-probe spectroscopy. By embedding the superconductor into a designed microcavity structure of metallic split-ring resonators, we can sensitively probe the pump field-induced transient variations of the superconducting states around the cavity’s resonant frequency. Our results show that the strong terahertz field can transiently modify the symmetries of the electronic subsystems via the injection of a picosecond supercurrent, leading to high-order nonlinear dynamical responses that are not compatible with the equilibrium-state symmetries, which is evidence for transient symmetry breaking on the picosecond time scale.

articles.title: Probing Valence Electron Distributions at Subatomic Resolution in a Charge Density Wave Material
articles.abstract: Probing the internal electronic structure of complex materials with atomic spatial resolution has remained an outstanding challenge in condensed-matter science. A promising approach is convergent-beam electron diffraction (CBED) in four-dimensional scanning transmission electron microscopy (4D-STEM). Here, we apply 4D-STEM CBED to the charge-density-wave (CDW) material 1T-TaS2. We demonstrate a qualitative breakdown of the conventional independent atom model (IAM) in reproducing the experimental CBED patterns. A robust low-angle intensity maximum is systematically absent in IAM-based simulations but is consistently reproduced in simulations that use electrostatic potentials derived from density functional theory. A comparison of CBED patterns with projected charge densities reveals a remarkable correspondence between the local real-space valence charge distribution and diffracted intensities, reflecting site-dependent charge density variations within the CDW structure. These results establish atomic-resolution CBED as an experimental probe of valence electron contributions to the scattering potential and open a route to resolving complex electronic ordering phenomena.

articles.abstract: The Lancet Commission on 21st century global threats to health's report by Christopher J L Murray and colleagues uses forecasts based on expected cumulative amenable disability-adjusted life-years (DALYs) to quantify and compare threats from 2025 to 2100.1 The Commission's intent is to equip governments with the tools to make smart long-term decisions that reduce risk based on “systematic, repeatable risk assessment and preparedness planning” as opposed to “short-termism and localism”.
