In Situ Analysis of Chiral Gold Nanorod Growth by Nanofluidic Liquid-Phase Electron Microscopy
articles.abstract: Chiral gold nanoparticles exhibit unique chiroptical properties, but their integration into plasmonic devices requires an understanding of the formation of chiral features and controlling their growth on substrates. Here, we combine microfluidic synthesis and liquid-phase transmission electron microscopy (LP-TEM) to study the growth of chiral wrinkled gold nanorods (AuNRs). Microfluidic growth from AuNR seeds produced g-factors of up to 0.01, approaching values reported for colloidal synthesis. Complementary LP-TEM experiments in a nanofluidic reactor generated gradients of gold precursor and reducing agent concentrations, enabling the direct observation of wrinkle formation under different conditions within a single experiment. Both methods showed that a higher gold precursor availability promotes longer wrinkles and stronger chiroptical activity. Higher flow rates in microfluidics produced larger nanoparticles with enhanced chiroptical responses, while LP-TEM revealed that increased reducing agent concentrations accelerate wrinkle growth. Reagent depletion ultimately limits the growth. Overall, wrinkle development is governed by precursor availability and reduction kinetics, determining the chiroptical performance.

articles.title: Laser Writing of Hexagonal Boron Nitride Patterns with Low Global Thermal Budget
articles.abstract: Direct integration of hexagonal boron nitride with temperature-sensitive substrates is constrained by the high global temperatures used in conventional growth. Here, we combine low-temperature deposition of an ammonia-borane-derived precursor on SiO2/Si (substrate temperature ≈ 70 °C) with spatially confined conversion by a focused 532-nm continuous-wave laser under ambient surroundings. Laser-written regions develop a persistent Raman band near 1370 cm–1 with a full width at half-maximum of 56.41 cm–1, and hyperspectral Raman imaging localizes this response to the irradiated sites. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy shows dominant B–N bonding and a B/N atomic ratio of 1.24 after conversion. High-resolution transmission electron microscopy reveals short, curved layered fringes with a median spacing of 0.349 nm, while scanning transmission electron microscopy–energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy establish nanocrystalline order and spatially colocated B and N within an oxygen-bearing, heterogeneous material. This approach enables low-temperature integration of hexagonal boron nitride with temperature-sensitive electronic and photonic platforms.

articles.title: Mode-Selective and Anharmonicity-Dependent Energy Transport in Cavity-Coupled Water
articles.abstract: Recent experiments demonstrate the modification of chemical dynamics via cavity-enhanced vibrational energy transport. Here, we provide a microscopic account of both photonic and mode-selective energy transport using direct mesoscale on-the-fly simulations of cavity-modified transport under vibrational strong coupling. We find that molecular anharmonicity leads to nonlinear driving-dependent photonic transport and localization, which we demonstrate in cavity-coupled water by tuning the photon frequency close to either the harmonic bending or the anharmonic stretching modes. We reproduce these effects in simple model systems, suggesting that the underlying mechanism extends beyond the specific case of cavity-coupled water. We also demonstrate that the diffusion of mode-selective temperature, quantified via the variance of the H–O–H bond angle or O–H bond length, depends on the cavity frequency, which we rationalize using an analytical model. Our results highlight the rich dynamical interplay of molecular and photonic degrees of freedom that persist in real atomistic systems.

articles.title: Ordered MoS2 Nanochannels Regulated by CNT for Conformation-Dependent Sieving in High-Salinity Organic Wastewater
articles.abstract: The rapid expansion of the pharmaceutical and fine chemical industries has escalated the discharge of high-salinity organic wastewater, which contains complex solutes and biotoxic antibiotics that are difficult to treat conventionally due to their high osmotic pressure and environmental persistence. Here, we developed a high-performance composite nanofiltration membrane by incorporating hydroxylated single-walled carbon nanotubes (SWCNT-OH) into electrochemically exfoliated monolayer MoS2 nanosheets. SWCNT-OH acts as a structural regulator, preventing MoS2 restacking and constructing stable, highly ordered 1.5 nm interlayer channels. At an optimized mass ratio of 6:1, the membrane achieves a water permeance of 28.0 L·m–2·h–1·bar–1 and a separation factor of 59.8 for oxytetracycline (OTC)/NaCl mixtures. Notably, rejection is governed by the molecular projected cross-sectional dimension relative to the 1.5 nm channels, demonstrating a conformation-dependent selectivity. These results highlight MoS2/CNT membranes as a durable solution for sustainable industrial wastewater treatment.

articles.title: Ultrahigh Responsivity and High-Detectivity Lateral GaN Ultraviolet Nanogap Field-Emission Photodiodes
articles.abstract: Vacuum nanoelectronic-based photodetectors operating via photoassisted field emission have the potential for significantly improved performance and robust operation under high-temperature and high-radiation environments. Here we demonstrate on-chip, GaN-based UV lateral nanogap field-emission photodiodes (NFEPs) with bandgap-dependent ultrahigh responsivity up to 2.21 × 107 A/W and corresponding detectivity of 5.0 × 1014 cm Hz1/2 W–1. The high performance is proposed to occur by a surface photovoltage effect that dramatically lowers the barrier for field emission across the nanogap upon above-bandgap illumination. These results show promise toward a new class of integrated and high-performance, bandgap-tunable, deep-UV photodetectors operable in harsh environments.

articles.title: AI-assisted scoping review of code sharing in clinical prediction model research
articles.abstract: Clinical prediction models are increasingly deployed to support diagnostic and prognostic decisions, making reproducibility essential for assessing their reliability and generalizability. Analytical code supports independent assessment of these processes, yet its availability in the literature remains limited. This scoping review quantifies current practices in sharing analytical code to inform the development of TRIPOD-Code, a reporting guideline for code availability and reproducibility. Here a large-language-model-assisted pipeline was developed to screen articles citing TRIPOD or TRIPOD+AI, extract repository links and assess retrieved repositories against 14 predefined reproducibility-related features. Among 3,967 articles, 482 (12.2%) included code-sharing statements. Sharing prevalence varied widely by journal and country. Repository assessment showed substantial heterogeneity in reproducibility features. These findings underscore the need for clearer expectations beyond code availability, including documentation, dependency specification and executable structure. Strengthening these practices may improve the usability of clinical prediction model studies and support their deployment in real-world clinical settings. An analysis of code availability in the open-access published literature shows that code sharing in clinical prediction models remains limited and reveals significant variability in practices and documentation quality.

articles.title: Lift from the flow
Order from chaos with adaptive circuits on quantum hardware
articles.abstract: Programmable quantum devices provide a platform for controlling the coherent dynamics of quantum wave functions. Monitoring and feedback can control classically chaotic dynamics, but extending these approaches to quantum systems is challenging because chaotic evolution amplifies perturbations and is sensitive to noise and decoherence. Here we demonstrate adaptive monitored quantum circuits that incorporate conditional feedback into non-unitary evolution, using local mid-circuit measurements and resets to control quantum chaotic dynamics. We perform the experiments on an IBM superconducting quantum processor with up to 100 qubits, implementing a quantum version of the classically chaotic Bernoulli map. The map scrambles quantum information, whereas local measurements and feedback attempt to steer the dynamics towards a fixed point of the map. This competition drives a dynamical phase transition between quantum and classical dynamics, which we observe experimentally and describe theoretically using noisy simulations, matrix product states and mappings to statistical mechanics models. By successfully applying up to nearly 5,000 entangling gates and 5,000 non-unitary mid-circuit operations on systems up to 100 qubits, the quantum processor yields accurate estimates of the universal critical properties. Controlling quantum chaos requires using measurement and feedback that survive noise and decoherence. Such control is now achieved in a superconducting quantum processor and reveals a critical transition between quantum and classical dynamics.

articles.title: Climate drivers of mesophyll conductance: temperature and water deficit alter CO2 diffusion and leaf anatomy in cotton
articles.abstract: Temperature responses of photosynthesis, mesophyll conductance and stomatal conductance to water across Gossypium hirsutum cv Sicot 71, Gossypium arboreum, Gossypium bickii, Gossypium gossypioides and Gossypium sturtianum. Summary Mesophyll conductance (g m) limits CO2 delivery to Rubisco, yet its responses to temperature, heat and water deficit are poorly resolved in cotton (Gossypium hirsutum). We characterised photosynthetic and g m temperature responses in five Gossypium species, then examined cultivated G. hirsutum and the Australian native Gossypium bickii under combined elevated temperature and soil water deficit to link physiological responses with mesophyll anatomy. Plants were grown under controlled glasshouse conditions. We quantified g m using simultaneous gas exchange and online stable carbon isotope discrimination (Δ, ‰) and measured leaf anatomy. Across species, photosynthesis and g m exhibited broad thermal optima (33–36°C). In G. hirsutum, water deficit at control temperature reduced g m and induced thicker, more porous mesophyll and thicker cell walls, while assimilation declined only under combined heat and water deficit. In G. bickii, g m and assimilation remained stable under combined stress, and g m was stimulated by elevated temperature without anatomical adjustment. g m emerged as a stress-sensitive trait in cultivated cotton, whereas G. bickii exhibited stress resilience, with responses incompletely explained by anatomical acclimation. Further research on g m responses to environmental stresses and on the mechanisms underpinning these responses is required to inform model development and identify traits for climate resilient crops.

articles.title: Harnessing genetic variation for grain quality from diverse wheat landraces
articles.abstract: Grain protein content is usually measured on bulk samples, hiding variation between individual grains. We used hyperspectral imaging to predict protein in c. 15 000 single grains from over 500 Watkins wheat landraces grown in two environments, resolving both mean protein content and grain-to-grain uniformity. Genome-wide association mapping identified six protein loci, two grain weight loci and SGPH-A1 on chromosome 6A controlling uniformity. Haplotypes at 6D raised protein without reducing grain weight, and haplotypes at 1A and 6A raised grain weight without diluting protein, offering routes to break the protein–yield trade-off. Summary The grain quality traits of protein content, grain weight and size are socially and economically important for wheat (Triticum aestivum) breeding. Modern wheat germplasm has limited genetic variation for vital traits, including grain quality, underscoring the need to investigate ancestral varieties/landraces for beneficial allelic diversity. Here, we develop a reliable and sensitive single-seed hyperspectral imaging-based phenotyping platform to quantify grain protein, weight and size in 827 diverse wheat landraces, achieving improved predictive accuracy (R 2 = 0.91) vs previous methods. We identified novel genetic variants (or loci) for grain protein content and its heterogeneity between individual grains in a genotype, and grain weight, and validated them through bi-parental linkage mapping. Many loci we report are rare and absent from modern breeding germplasm. Beneficial haplotypes at these loci improved mean protein content and homogeneity without compromising grain weight; these haplotypes represent valuable genetic variation for agriculture. We identify a stable locus on chromosome 6A contributing to protein heterogeneity within single grains, suggesting homogeneity in protein content could be a selectable trait for breeding. Our findings demonstrate how integration of advanced phenotyping into breeding strategies can harness untapped genetic diversity for grain quality improvement in wheat, providing an opportunity to enhance grain nutritional value.

articles.title: Coupling Free Electrons to a Trapped-Ion Quantum Computer
articles.abstract: Freely propagating electrons may serve as quantum probes that can become coherently correlated with other quantum systems, offering access to advanced metrological resources. We propose a setup that coherently couples free electrons in an electron microscope to a trapped-ion quantum processor, enabling nondestructive, quantum-coherent detection and the accumulation of information across multiple electrons. Our analysis shows that single electrons can induce resolvable qubit excitations, establishing a platform for practical applications such as quantum-enhanced, dose-efficient electron microscopy.

articles.title: First Experimental Evidence of Helicon Current Drive
articles.abstract: Helicon current drive has been observed experimentally for the first time in dedicated DIII-D tokamak experiments, providing a proof-of-principle and an attractive source of efficient current drive in reactor-grade tokamak plasmas.

articles.title: Information Bound on Navigation Speed in Smart Active Matter
articles.abstract: Intelligent behavior in lifelike systems often arises from the ability to gather, process, and act on information. While active matter provides a framework for studying lifelike dynamics, it typically omits internal information processing and decision making. Here we introduce an adaptive active par…

articles.title: Interaction Potential between Anisotropic Particles: From Measurements to Tailored Design
articles.abstract: We extend the classical test particle insertion (TPI) method to anisotropic systems and develop an anisotropic test particle insertion (ATPI) framework that efficiently extracts anisotropic interaction potentials from dense fluids using a small number of equilibrium snapshots. The method leverages the parallelizability of the insertion process, enabling rapid reconstruction of complex anisotropic interactions via high-performance computing. The ATPI method is quantitatively validated for liquids in both simulations and colloidal experiments. With a few modifications, this method is able to extract anisotropic interactions from solid lattices. By exploiting the theoretical equivalence between interaction measurement and design, we further demonstrate that ATPI can be used to construct interaction potentials that drive the system into target structures such as honeycomb lattices, kagome lattices, and dodecagonal quasicrystals. Our approach opens a new avenue for the inverse design of self-assembling systems.

articles.title: Kink-Boundary-Induced Polarity Revealed by Nonreciprocal Charge Transport in ${\mathrm{FeTe}}_{0.7}{\mathrm{Se}}_{0.3}$ Superconductor
articles.abstract: Nonreciprocal charge transport, characterized by direction-dependent electrical response, provides a powerful probe of electronic structure and a platform for rectification. However, its realization is typically governed by intrinsic crystal symmetry, restricting the range of suitable materials. Her…

articles.title: Microelectromechanical System Vapor Cells with Passive Internal Cavities
articles.abstract: Microelectromechanical---so-called ``MEMs''---vapor cells are a key component in atom-based quantum sensors, such as clocks, gyroscopes, electric field sensors, and magnetometers. MEMs vapor cell fabrication for Rydberg atom radio frequency sensors is particularly demanding. The Rydberg states used for the sensor can shift in a constant electric field which can be generated by the internal surfaces of the vapor cell cavity. The ratio of the detection wavelength to vapor cell size can span a large range, meaning that the radio frequency field--vapor cell interaction is a critical design consideration. In many radio frequency sensing cases, there is a desire to minimize the interaction between the vapor cell and the target radio frequency field, as well as assure that every vapor cell behaves uniformly. These criteria favor MEMs vapor cells with low background electric fields. Known inert, organic coatings cannot survive the bonding temperatures required for conventional anodic bonding of a MEMs vapor cell. Applying inert, organic coatings to the internal cavities of MEMs vapor cells is a long-standing challenge. In this Letter, we present a low temperature bonding scheme that is compatible with coating the internal cavity of a MEMs vapor cell with octadecyltrichlorosilane [${\mathrm{CH}}_{3}({\mathrm{CH}}_{2}{)}_{17}{\mathrm{SiCl}}_{3}$, OTS]. The coating prevents the Cs used in the vapor cell from sticking to the walls. Spectral linewidths of $\ensuremath{\sim}300\text{ }\text{ }\mathrm{kHz}$ are obtained using Rydberg spectroscopy, with energy shifts corresponding to electric fields $<10\text{ }\mathrm{mV}\text{ }{\mathrm{cm}}^{\ensuremath{-}1}$.

articles.title: Non-Ohmic to Ohmic Crossover in the Breakdown of the Quantum Hall States in Graphene under Broadband Excitations
articles.abstract: Graphene, through the coexistence of large cyclotron gaps and small spin and valley gaps, offers the possibility to study the breakdown of the quantum Hall effect (QHE) across a wide range of energy scales. In this Letter, we investigate the breakdown of the QHE in high-mobility graphene Corbino dev…

articles.title: Nonuniform Thermal Conductivity in Nanoscale Multiple Hotspot Systems
articles.abstract: Nanoscale hotspot thermal transport is critical for thermal management of electronic devices. Here, the thermal transport in nanoscale multiple hotspots is investigated by solving the phonon Boltzmann transport equation. To address the limitations of the conventional black-box treatment, a formal local thermal conductivity is proposed, which extends the classical framework to nanoscale nondiffusive regimes. The results reveal a highly nonuniform local thermal transport capability with up to a 13-fold variation across the system. A substantial heat flux deflection is also observed, which significantly deviates from the direction predicted by Fourier's law. Furthermore, closely spaced nanoscale hotspots are found to enhance heat flux by up to 40%. This enhancement arises from a mechanism in which diffuse boundary scattering at hotspot spacing regions can enhance rather than impede thermal transport. This Letter challenges the long-standing black-box treatment of nanoscale thermal transport and offers fundamental insights for the thermal management of high-power-density integrated circuits.

articles.title: Optical Readout of the Magnetic State Using Terahertz Electric Fields
articles.abstract: Resonant excitation of $f$-electrons by a terahertz optical signal rotates the magnetization in rare-earth iron garnets, establishing a new ultrafast magnetoelectric coupling that can potentially be used for ultrafast magneto-optical readout in magnetic data storage.

articles.title: Size and Shape of Condensing Steam Jets and Plumes
articles.abstract: Droplet-laden cloud dynamics emerge from coupled phase transitions and turbulent mixing. Combining experiments and mean-field theory, we establish scaling laws for steam-injected clouds in unsaturated air seeded with condensation nuclei. Depending on whether the cloud is confined to the initial momentum-dominated zone of the jet or extends into the buoyancy-dominated plume, two asymptotic regimes arise. In the momentum regime, cloud dimensions scale with the injector radius. In the buoyancy regime, size follows a ${\stackrel{\ifmmode \dot{}\else \textperiodcentered \fi{}}{m}}^{2/5}$ scaling, where $\stackrel{\ifmmode \dot{}\else \textperiodcentered \fi{}}{m}$ is the injected steam mass flow rate. Assuming interdroplet air remains humidity saturated, our mean-field analysis predicts cloud persistence governed by enthalpy and humidity mixing. These findings bridge microphysical processes and macroscale dynamics, offering a quantitative framework for atmospheric cloud evolution.

articles.title: Unitarity Bounds and Sum Rules in the Standard Model Effective Field Theory
articles.abstract: We present a comprehensive reassessment of perturbative unitarity bounds in the dimension-6 standard model effective field theory, exploiting a new formalism based on spinor-helicity techniques to derive partial-wave unitarity bounds for generic $N\ensuremath{\rightarrow}M$ scattering amplitudes. We find that, in several cases, these theoretical constraints are already competitive with, or even stronger than, the corresponding experimental bounds for energy scales above a few TeV. This is especially the case for four-fermion operators under realistic flavor assumptions, where unitarity bounds can be further strengthened by exploiting sum rules. These results provide a valuable and timely contribution toward the ambitious program of new-physics searches with minimal theoretical priors supplemented by restrictive, yet general, first-principles criteria.

articles.title: Breakdown of the Kerr-Cat Qubit Tunneling Time Induced by Auxiliary Circuit Modes
articles.abstract: Researchers show that auxiliary circuit modes trigger multiphoton resonances that break down Kerr-cat qubit coherence under strong driving.

articles.title: Fluidic Hysterons and Memory in Flow Networks
articles.abstract: Soft elastic fibers in microfluidic channels can create a fluid system with memory of previous actions through a flow-structure feedback.

articles.title: Next-generation materials and devices by combustion processes
A bifunctional actuator to correct loss-of-function deficits in cardiac voltage-gated sodium channels
articles.abstract: Despite their emerging prominence, ion channelopathies have remained challenging to correct, as ion channel dysfunction linked to disease is multifaceted, involving changes in activity and/or localization. Yet, current corrective strategies typically focus on restoring only one aspect leading to incomplete efficacy. Here, focusing on the voltage-gated sodium channel, Na V 1.5, whose dysfunction is linked to life-threatening cardiac arrhythmias, we develop a genetically encoded bifunctional actuator as a proof-of-concept molecular strategy to reverse pathophysiological changes in channel function. Specifically, we engineer a high affinity nanobody targeting Na V 1.5 with two moieties: (i) a peptide that restores proper inactivation and (ii) a linkage-specific deubiquitinase that promotes surface-membrane localization. Functional validation in heterologous systems and in human and mouse cardiomyocytes demonstrated restoration of Na V 1.5 trafficking and/or gating. In all, this approach shows promise for reversing molecular deficits observed with Na V channelopathies and provides a framework to engineer multifunctional modulators targeting ion channelopathies.

articles.title: A helix-loop-helix gene orchestrates male fate in common carp
articles.abstract: Fish show exceptional diversity in sex-determination mechanisms, making them a powerful system for studying how these pathways evolve. However, no definitive master sex-determining gene has yet been identified in Cyprinidae, a widely distributed and species-rich fish family. Here, we identified a male-specific gene in common carp encoding Pangu, a helix-loop-helix (HLH) domain peptide localized to Sertoli cells. Loss- and gain-of-function analyses demonstrate that pangu is both necessary and sufficient for male sex determination. Expression and reporter assays indicate that pangu represses cyp19a1a , a key regulator of ovarian differentiation, and disruption of cyp19a1a restores testicular development in the feminized phenotype of XY pangu mutants. These findings establish pangu as the master sex-determining gene in common carp and link an HLH domain peptide to sex differentiation.

articles.title: A neuronal GPCR modifies neuropeptide signaling to suppress proteostasis in distal tissues
articles.abstract: The proteostasis network (PN) safeguards the integrity of proteins by promoting various cellular activities. However, with aging, the PN’s competence declines and aggregated proteins accrue within cells. This process underlies the development of neurodegenerative disorders such as Alzheimer’s and Huntington’s diseases. While the PN functions within cells, proteostasis is regulated across the organism by intertissue communication, which is partially governed by neurons. We previously found that reducing the expression of gtr-1 , which encodes a neuronal heterotrimeric guanine nucleotide–binding protein–coupled receptor, mitigates the toxicity of the Alzheimer’s disease cause, Aβ peptide. Here, we investigated the mechanism that is acted upon the knockdown of gtr-1 and found that it differentially modulates gene expression profiles, including of neuropeptide-coding genes, and dissimilarly modifies protein aggregation in worms that express distinct proteotoxic proteins. The knockdown of gtr-1 also enhances protein degradation. These findings highlight the roles of neuropeptides as organismal coordinators of proteostasis in the face of distinct proteotoxic challenges.

articles.title: ALIX-dependent small extracellular vesicles from tissue-resident mesenchymal cells regulate pancreatic β cell proliferation in obesity
articles.abstract: Cells throughout the body release small extracellular vesicles (sEVs), including exosomes, that function as modulators of both local and systemic metabolism. Using mice in which ALIX, a key regulator of sEV biogenesis, was selectively deleted in PDGFRα + mesenchymal progenitors (Pα-ALIXKO mice), we demonstrate a critical role for mesenchymal sEV production in metabolic regulation. In high-fat diet–induced obesity, Pα-ALIXKO mice exhibited reduced weight gain and smaller subcutaneous adipocytes compared with control mice. Despite similar insulin sensitivity, these mice showed impaired glucose tolerance, which was associated with reduced pancreatic β cell area and smaller islets. sEVs isolated from conditioned media of knockout (KO)–derived mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) exhibited a reduced capacity to promote β cell proliferation. Furthermore, MSCs isolated from subcutaneous adipose tissue of KO mice showed elevated mRNA expression of inflammatory genes. Together, these findings indicate that ALIX in tissue-resident mesenchymal progenitors is required for pancreatic β cell proliferation and glucose homeostasis in obesity.

articles.title: B1-like innate B cells are present in adult human organs in homeostasis
articles.abstract: Innate-like B cells produce natural antibodies and include marginal zone (MZ) B cells and B1 cells. B1 cells are well characterized in mice, where they prenatally seed serous cavities and produce regulatory cytokines. Putative B1 cells have been identified in human prenatal organs, but whether they persist into adulthood remains unclear. Here, we identified B1-like cells in the IgM + and IgA + memory compartment across adult human organs. These cells transcriptionally resembled murine and human prenatal B1 cells but not MZ B cells. They expressed canonical murine B1 cell markers, including AHNAK , and spontaneously secreted IgM. B cell receptor sequencing of paired kidney-spleen samples revealed lower diversity and mutation rates in kidney IgM/IgA clones, suggesting spleen-independent seeding. Adult B1-like cells expressed the regulatory cytokine TGFB and had abundant inferred interactions with tissue myeloid cells, which reciprocally expressed B cell prosurvival cytokines. These findings support the presence of B1-like cells across adult human organs in homeostasis.

articles.title: Follicle-associated epithelial tuft cells amplify type 2 mucosal immunity and IgA production
articles.abstract: Peyer’s patches (PPs) in the intestinal mucosa coordinate antibody responses to luminal microbes and dietary antigens. The follicle-associated epithelium (FAE) is traditionally recognized by the presence of microfold cells (M cells) that mediate antigen sampling in PPs. By analyzing Gfi1b -eGFP reporter mice and human PP biopsies, we identified tuft cells as an additional, evolutionarily conserved FAE population that regulates mucosal immunity. Using mouse models and intestinal organoids, we demonstrate that M cells and tuft cells are distinct lineages arising from Pou2f3 + progenitors, whose differentiation is reciprocally regulated by RANKL and interleukin-13 (IL-13), respectively. Tuft cell–derived IL-25 activates type 2 innate lymphoid cells (ILC2s) in PPs. Furthermore, IL-13 production by ILC2 enhances immunoglobulin A class switching and antigen-specific immunity. These findings reveal a dual surveillance system in the FAE, where developmentally related epithelial lineages use distinct mechanisms to coordinate mucosal immunity.

articles.title: The IKK complex and TBK1/IKKε are recruited to STING through distinct mechanisms to activate NF-κB signaling
articles.abstract: Stimulator of interferon genes (STING) is a highly conserved signaling molecule that coordinates an antiviral innate immune response through activation of the nuclear factor κB (NF-κB) and interferon regulatory factor 3 (IRF3) signaling pathways. In addition to an antiviral response, STING-mediated NF-κB signaling also leads to an inflammatory response, which can cause substantial pathology. However, the molecular mechanism whereby STING drives inflammation is poorly understood, and this has hindered the development of anti-inflammatory strategies targeting this pathway. Here, we define an evolutionarily conserved mechanism whereby STING activates NF-κB signaling via recruitment of inhibitor of NF-κB kinase subunit γ (IKKγ) in an M1-linked ubiquitin-dependent manner. We also show that the more recently evolved carboxyl-terminal tail of STING cooperates with the IKKγ-IKK complex for NF-κB–dependent expression of pro-inflammatory genes in mammalian cells through the kinases TBK1 (TANK-binding kinase 1)/IKKε. Thus, the expression of the key inflammatory genes CCL3 and CCL4 requires the formation of M1-linked ubiquitin and the activation of NF-κB, but we do not detect a role for IRF3 in STING-driven NF-κB signaling.

articles.title: ADHD and autism review: NHS must move away from diagnosis linked support system, report says
articles.abstract: ADHD and autism diagnosis in England needs a “fundamental shift,” say the authors of a major government backed review.The Fonagy review1 was tasked with investigating rising demand for mental health, attention deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), and autism services in England and the factors driving this.Chaired by the clinical psychologist Peter Fonagy, the review was commissioned by then health and social care secretary Wes Streeting, against a backdrop of surging demand for NHS services in these areas. It found that more than 254 000 people were on the autism assessment waiting list in December 2025, while 560 000 were waiting for an assessment for ADHD.The report adds that estimates using NHS data suggest that autism has increased among 6-11 year olds more than 20-fold and among 12-17 year olds more than 40-fold.Published today, the almost 600 page report warns that “continuing as we are is not sustainable.” It advises, “The current system...

articles.title: Flu, covid, and winter pressure: “Ominous” signs of pressure build in hospitals, officials warn
articles.abstract: Health officials are warning of “ominous” signs of winter pressure already building in hospitals in England, as new data show flu levels soaring for this time of year.The UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) said that flu levels were currently higher than the previous four years at the start of the agency’s winter reporting season.The UKHSA’s first weekly winter respiratory virus surveillance report1 shows that, while still at very low levels, flu has been rising since August, suggesting a potential early influenza season.The weekly reports are based on a range of indicators provided by GPs, hospitals, laboratories, and the wider community. This first report recorded that flu positivity—based on a percentage of people who test positive for the virus in hospital—was 6.5% in the week ending 4 October, up from 5% the week prior. In comparison, the previous four years have seen figures of about 1-3% at this time of year.Overall,...

articles.title: GLP-1s: Novo Nordisk and Eli Lilly face lawsuits over vision loss and eye damage
articles.abstract: Dozens of people claiming to have sustained eye damage from using GLP-1 medications are suing Eli Lilly and Novo Nordisk, the makers of the blockbuster drugs.1Semaglutide and tirzepatide are now among the most widely used drugs to treat type 2 diabetes and promote weight loss.Semaglutide is a glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonist marketed by Novo Nordisk under the brand names Ozempic, Wegovy, and Rybelsus. Tirzepatide, which acts on GLP-1 and glucose dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP) receptors, is produced by Eli Lilly and available under the brand names Mounjaro and Zepbound.The condition at the centre of the lawsuits is non-arteritic anterior ischaemic optic neuropathy (NAION). It is sometimes described as a “stroke” of the optic nerve and is the most common acute optic neuropathy in people over 50.2Kevin Gendreau, an obesity medicine physician at the Weight & Wellness Center at Signature Healthcare in Brockton, Massachusetts, said of NAION: “Blood flow to...

articles.title: Is the flu season starting early—and when should I get vaccinated?
articles.abstract: Has the flu season started early?For the second year in a row, it looks like the influenza season has started early in England.“It is very early in the season, but the number of hospital admissions for flu are the highest that I can remember seeing at this time of year,” says Frankie Swords, national medical director at NHS England, speaking at a briefing on winter viruses on 8 October.The latest surveillance report from the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA)—covering 28 September to 4 October 2026—shows that influenza activity is increasing, with a flu test positivity rate of 6.5%, up from 5% the previous week.1Meanwhile, hospital admissions for flu are at 1.97 per 100 000. As this is the first week of reporting on this figure, there is no comparison.The agency says that, although levels are still low, “flu trends have been rising since August, and there are possible signs that...

articles.title: Supporting equity, diversity, and inclusion in research
articles.abstract: A lack of equity, diversity, inclusion, and accessibility (EDIA) considerations is a well described challenge that threatens the scientific and ethical integrity of healthcare research.1 Underrepresentation is costly, unjust, and harms patients.1 Unintentional exclusion of patients who may most benefit from trial evidence is a central focus of many efforts to improve EDIA considerations in research, with the exclusion of black participants from cancer trials being an important example.1 Intentional exclusion of pregnant23 or cognitively impaired45 participants from trials that may most benefit these populations is an emerging area of concern. Further, a lack of understanding of structural discrimination relevant to the trial discipline can lead to erroneous conclusions. An important example is attributing findings from observational studies showing worse outcomes from covid-19 infection in black populations6 to biological mechanisms7 without considering how systemic overestimation of blood oxygen by pulse oximetry used on skin of colour8 influences access to treatments...

articles.title: The plan to allow physician assistants to see undifferentiated patients is irresponsible and poorly evidenced
articles.abstract: The Leng Review became a deep disappointment after it was first published in summer 2025.1 Instead of being the moment when physician and anaesthesia assistant roles were reined in and refocused on supporting members of healthcare teams, it simply became another example of delaying tough decisions.As the BMA said at the time, it was an inadequate response to a patient safety scandal, particularly in its lack of support for a national scope of practice for physician assistants (PAs), and its failure to clearly reject PAs seeing undifferentiated patients.It was the latter that was most ominous—we have seen far too many examples of patient harm resulting from PAs being put in the position of being the only staff member that saw gravely ill patients when it could make a difference. The case of Emily Chesterton was only the most prominent of these.2Although the prescription fell well short, Leng’s diagnosis was accurate....

articles.title: Invasive interval breast cancer rates after digital breast tomosynthesis plus synthesised mammography versus digital mammography screening (TOSYMA): 24-month follow-up of the multicentre, open-label, randomised, controlled, superiority trial
Time to say goodbye to full-field digital mammography in population-based screening?
Metabolic enzymes moonlighting as protein kinases and phosphatases
articles.abstract: Protein phosphorylation is a central and reversible mechanism regulating virtually all cellular processes and is classically mediated by the canonical protein kinome and phosphatome. However, beyond their traditional roles as metabolic catalysts, a subset of metabolic enzymes also exhibits noncanonical ‘moonlighting’ activities as protein kinases or phosphatases, directly linking metabolic states to phosphorylation-dependent signaling. These unexpected functions of enzymes involved in glucose, fructose, lipid, nucleotide, and creatine metabolism influence a broad spectrum of cellular processes, including chromatin remodeling, transcription, cell cycle progression, metabolism, autophagy, cell survival and death, and immune responses. As a result, metabolic enzymes are increasingly recognized as key regulators that bridge cellular metabolism and signaling networks, with important implications for both normal physiology and disease.

articles.title: Trait-based inference of fragmentation-driven extinction risk
articles.abstract: Habitat fragmentation is a leading cause of plant extinctions, yet predicting which species are most vulnerable remains a key challenge. We propose that population connectivity, and thus gene flow via pollination and seed dispersal, can be inferred from plant traits. We integrate these traits into a connectivity–trait dimension, which, together with breeding system, life-history traits, and landscape context, ranks species at risk of genetic erosion and local extinction, providing an early-warning triage tool. By linking traits to gene flow mechanisms, the framework helps prioritise investment in detailed population genetic analyses and provides a scalable tool to identify species most at risk of genetic inbreeding and extinction in fragmented landscapes.

articles.title: AI Models Can Provably Hide Arbitrary Capabilities
articles.abstract: Capability evaluations aim to surface dangerous model behaviors before deployment, but their reliability depends on the assumption that hidden capabilities can be elicited. We show this assumption does not hold under adversarial conditions by constructing backdoor attacks that embed encrypted neural networks within host model weights, decrypting and executing them only upon receiving a secret trigger. Using digital lockers, these hidden circuits remain provably hard to elicit and interpret under cryptographic assumptions, even given full access to model weights, extending prior work from hiding fixed strings to arbitrary computations. We implement our proof of concept constructions in PyTorch and evaluate elicitation through fine-tuning, weight noising, gradient-based trigger search, and latent adversarial training on a small chemical reaction prediction task - a proxy for CBRN-relevant capabilities. Our results demonstrate resistance to these methods and, together with our cryptographic guarantees, reveal a limit of elicitation-based capability audits. We release our models to support the improvement of defenses.

articles.title: Adaptive Variance Reduction without Knowing Oracle Smoothness
articles.abstract: Variance reduction improves the convergence rate of stochastic non-convex optimization under the average smoothness condition. Existing adaptive variance reduction methods are especially designed for average smoothness and do not adapt to standard smoothness. In this paper, we study how one algorithm can adapt to these two settings and the noiseless setting without knowing the smoothness constants or the variance bound. Given the gradient budget $T$, we develop a two-phase method. The first phase compares two independent gradients and switches to normalized momentum when their difference exceeds a threshold. This phase provides both a candidate with standard smooth and noiseless guarantees and also ensures a bounded expected function gap for the second variance reduction phase. The resulting rates are $O(T^{-1/3})$ under average smoothness, $O(T^{-1/4})$ under standard smoothness, and $O(T^{-1/2})$ without noise. When $T$ is unknown, we propose a method with two paths that attain the corresponding rates with logarithmic factors in the stochastic settings. Here, we use a variance reduction path to deal with average smoothness and employ the AdaGrad-Norm for standard smoothness and noiseless setting. Neither method restarts from the initial point or requires a growing number of oracle calls in each round.

articles.title: Accuracy of Vibrational Properties of Machine-Learning Force Fields for Molecular Crystal Transformations
articles.abstract: Machine-learning force fields (MLFFs) enable the calculation of transformation pathways in molecular crystals at a fraction of the computational cost of density functional theory (DFT). However, a good agreement in energies and structures does not necessarily imply an accurate description of vibrational properties, which are essential for characterizing transition states and determining free energies at finite temperatures. Herein, we assess the accuracy of system-specific SO3krates MLFFs trained on PBE+MBD reference data for describing vibrational properties of molecular crystal transformations. As examples, we consider a polymorph transition of 1,4-diiodobenzene and a single-crystal-to-single-crystal Diels-Alder reaction. The transition state structures obtained from solid-state nudged-elastic-band (NEB) calculations with the MLFFs exhibit a single imaginary $Γ$-point frequency associated with the respective transformation. Compared with PBE+MBD, the mean absolute errors of $Γ$-point vibrational frequencies and relative harmonic free energies at 300 K are about 3 cm$^{-1}$ and 1 kJ/mol, respectively. Furthermore, we compare for the Diels-Alder reaction a collective transformation pathway with a sequential one, in which individual diene-dienophile pairs react successively, and demonstrate that PBE0+MBD single-point corrections can significantly affect the predicted reaction energetics. These results demonstrate that system-specific MLFFs can reproduce not only the energies and forces but also the local curvature of the potential-energy surface with high accuracy, enabling reliable calculations of harmonic vibrational free energies, providing a basis for extending the studies of molecular crystal transformations to larger supercells.

articles.title: All-electron RT-TDDFT with Exact Exchange based on Numeric Atom-centered Orbitals for Condensed Matter
articles.abstract: Real-time time-dependent density functional theory (RT-TDDFT) has become a widely used first-principles method for studying excited-state and nonequilibrium electron dynamics. Hybrid exchange-correlation (XC) functionals, which incorporate a fraction of nonlocal exact exchange, are particularly important for accurately describing processes such as charge transfer and hot-carrier dynamics. However, the high computational cost which accompanies exact exchange, as required in hybrid XC functionals, has largely restricted RT-TDDFT simulations of condensed matter systems to using semi-local XC functionals. In this work, we present an all-electron implementation of exact exchange for RT-TDDFT based on numeric atom-centered orbitals, extending an efficient ground-state resolution-of-identity (RI) framework to the complex, time-dependent Hamiltonians required for real-time propagation. We validate the implementation against an established RI approach, for an isolated water molecule, finding exact agreement for both valence and core (K-edge) excitations. We also demonstrate the method on two extended periodic systems, crystalline silicon and silicon carbide. For silicon, the HSE06 spectrum reproduces previously reported real-time TDDFT results and agrees with experiment to within approximately 0.2~eV, consistent with plane-wave pseudopotential implementations. For silicon carbide, we compute valence and X-ray absorption spectra at the silicon $L$-edge and carbon $K$-edge. These results establish an efficient, all-electron route to hybrid-XC functional RT-TDDFT for both molecular and condensed matter systems.

articles.title: Electron-Density-Informed Molecular Property Prediction Using Surrogate Functionals
articles.abstract: Machine learning methods are increasingly used to predict chemical properties directly from the molecular structure to bypass the often prohibitive cost of quantum mechanical calculations. Recent work has shown that including the ground-state electron density as input to the machine learning model can improve accuracy in this setting. This work employs the recent surrogate functional framework originally developed for orbital-free density functional theory and extends it to predicting molecular properties. We show that passing the ground-state density as input to the model, while simultaneously enforcing it to be the minimum of the surrogate functional, surpasses state-of-the-art performance for six out of seven extensive properties of the QM9 dataset. Additionally, the approach shows improved generalization to larger molecules taken from the QM40 dataset. On all extensive properties of both datasets, our approach outperforms models that are informed by the ground-state density but do not enforce the surrogate functional constraints.

articles.title: Mn--Cr dopant association in dilute co-doped $\mathrm{ZnAl_2O_4}$ revealed by combined EPR and optical spectroscopy
articles.abstract: Efficient and durable phosphors made from abundant elements underpin energy-saving solid-state lighting, near-infrared light sources for sensing, and X-ray and biomedical imaging. Co-doping is a standard route to brighter phosphors, yet the fate of the co-dopants is rarely established. We combine quantitative electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) spin counting with photoluminescence, photoluminescence excitation, and X-ray-excited spectroscopy across two dilute Mn/Cr co-doping series of hydrothermally grown $\mathrm{ZnAl_2O_4}$ nanoparticles and show that the two ions can form an exchange-coupled, edge-sharing Cr--Mn defect complex, with $\mathrm{Mn^{2+/4+}}$ entering an octahedral site next to $\mathrm{Cr^{3+}}$. The octahedral Mn lifts the inversion symmetry of the $\mathrm{Cr^{3+}}$ site and strengthens its parity-forbidden absorption, enhancing the $\mathrm{Cr^{3+}}$ emission without energy transfer. The population of the defect complex follows the law of mass action, and above a threshold Mn concentration, Mn re-partitions into EPR-silent octahedral configurations that quench both emissions. Concentration optima in co-doped phosphors can thus reflect defect speciation, not only energy-transfer efficiency, which opens a structural design handle for brighter emitters.

articles.title: NucleoNet: A Nuclear-Aware Determinant Ansatz for Multi-Geometry Neural Variational Monte Carlo
articles.abstract: Neural-network variational Monte Carlo provides an accurate route to solving the electronic Schrödinger equation, but many neural wavefunctions are optimized for a single nuclear geometry, requiring separate calculations to map out a potential energy surface. We introduce NucleoNet, a nuclear-aware determinant ansatz in which electrons and nuclei form a unified particle set propagated through a shared electron--nucleus backbone that jointly evolves one-particle and two-particle representations. Nuclei carry learned representations that evolve alongside the electronic representations and condition orbital construction, while antisymmetry is imposed only by electronic determinants. On equilibrium small-molecule benchmarks, NucleoNet achieves accuracy comparable to established neural-wavefunction baselines with substantially fewer parameters. For each molecular system, a single model optimized jointly across geometries describes the N$_2$ dissociation curve, Li displacement in LiCN, and the ethane and formamide minimum-energy paths for bond dissociation. Sparse-geometry training generalizes to unseen geometries for N$_2$ and LiCN without further optimization, and N$_2$ ablations show that nuclear streams substantially improve this interpolation. These results show that a compact wavefunction with jointly evolved nuclear representations can describe the geometries of a molecular system with a single set of parameters.

articles.title: Precursor stoichiometry controls dopant structure, defect chemistry, and valence in Mn-doped ZnGa$_2$O$_4$ nanocrystals
articles.abstract: The luminescence of doped nanocrystals is usually optimised through the activator; here we show that the host cation ratio is an equally decisive, and largely overlooked, design variable. Mn-doped ZnGa$_2$O$_4$ nanocrystals (Mn:Zn = $4\times10^{-4}$) were grown hydrothermally at nominal Zn/Ga ratios between 0.30 and 0.75 (stoichiometric: 0.50) and post-annealed at 400--1100$^\circ$C, and the resulting composition--temperature matrix was mapped by X-ray- and UV-excited luminescence, EPR, Rietveld-refined X-ray diffraction, Raman spectroscopy and SEM. The as-grown crystals are phase-pure spinel at every composition and accommodate their off-stoichiometry internally as a point-defect inventory, reflected in a 0.4\% variation of the lattice parameter; on annealing, the excess gallium is exsolved as $β$-Ga$_2$O$_3$ in amounts set by the solution composition. The Mn$^{2+}$ emission separates into two optima, near-stoichiometric crystals annealed at 400--600$^\circ$C and Zn-excess crystals annealed at 1100$^\circ$C, the latter being twice as bright under X-ray excitation. Under X-ray and 365~nm excitation the two optima are separated by a minimum at 800$^\circ$C that coincides with a collapse of the Mn$^{2+}$ EPR population and has no counterpart in the Raman linewidths, identifying transient, defect-compensated oxidation of the dopant rather than lattice degradation as its origin. The most Zn-rich composition shows neither Mn$^{2+}$ nor Mn$^{4+}$ emission at any annealing stage, whereas its trace Cr$^{3+}$ emission is strong, indicating that Mn is rejected already during growth. Solution stoichiometry therefore acts on two levels, dopant capture and native-defect inventory, while annealing controls dopant valence and lattice order. The brightest high-temperature phosphor is thus not the nominally stoichiometric one, but the composition whose excess is consumed on its way to stoichiometry.

articles.title: Quantitative modeling of acid-base equilibria
articles.abstract: Simulating acid-base equilibria from first principles is a tremendous challenge, as it requires modeling bond-breaking events in a complex hydrogen-bonding environment. The quantum mechanical behavior of the protons is often important, complicating simulations even further. We show that by combining state-of-the-art machine-learning potentials, accelerated sampling of the dissociation process, and an efficient estimation of nuclear quantum corrections it is possible to reliably compute the dissociation constants of different species in water. We demonstrate the transferability of this workflow, applying it successfully to the autoionization of water and to the entire ladder of the aqueous dissociation of phosphoric acid. The definition of the dissociation constant, the choice of order parameters, sampling artifacts and finite-size effects, as well as quantum nuclear effects all play a non-trivial role in determining the outcome of the calculation, so that cutting corners is likely to introduce biases that can only be compensated by fortuitous cancellations of errors.

articles.title: Quantum dynamics of an ion in an RF quadrupole trap with weak octupolar anharmonicity
articles.abstract: We investigate the quantum dynamics of a single ion confined in a radio-frequency (RF) Paul trap in the presence of weak octupole-induced anharmonicity, as can occur in realistic ion-trap potential. The explicitly time-dependent quadrupole potential is treated in a reference-oscillator Fock basis, allowing the effects of the RF drive and the quartic correction to be resolved directly at the level of motional-state couplings. While the quadratic RF interaction generates $Δn=\pm2$ transitions and Gaussian squeezing, the quartic contribution opens additional $Δn=\pm4$ coupling pathways. Starting from the reference-oscillator vacuum, we show that the octupole interaction broadens the even-parity Fock-state distribution and enhances the phonon-number fluctuations more strongly than the mean occupation. At the same time, the RF-induced sub-vacuum quadrature squeezing remains robust, although its magnitude and orientation are modified by the quartic interaction. The number statistics and quadrature fluctuations therefore respond differently to the same nonlinear perturbation, reflecting the distinct roles of Fock-space redistribution and phase coherence. The resulting dynamics provide a quantum-mechanical characterization of weak octupole corrections beyond the ideal quadrupole approximation and clarify how realistic anharmonicities modify nonclassical trapped-ion motion. Importantly, the motional nonclassicality remains robust against the weak octupole perturbation, as evidenced by persistent sub-vacuum quadrature squeezing and Klyshko-inequality violation. These results characterize how realistic anharmonic corrections reshape trapped-ion motion beyond the ideal quadrupole approximation.

articles.title: Spin Migration in the Argon Dimer
articles.abstract: We introduce the concept of \emph{spin migration}, i.e. time-dependent spin density, and the absolute smallest example of molecular spintronics. We illustrate the concept by \emph{ab initio} calculations of the coupled vibronic motion of the electrons and the nuclei in the argon dimer cation, in which the vibrational level spacing is similar to the spin--orbit splitting of the atomic argon cations. We find that the spin density varies on multiple time scales, given by the natural time scales of the electronic and nuclear wavepackets.

articles.title: UGME: A python package for non-Markovian protein folding dynamics
articles.abstract: Biomolecular processes, including protein folding, protein-protein association, and protein-DNA recognition, often occur on timescales beyond what individual atomistic molecular dynamics (MD) simulations can reach. To access these longer-timescale dynamics, practitioners commonly combine many parallelized, short trajectories into reduced kinetic models, such as Markov state models (MSMs), that describe how the biomolecules interconvert between a handful of biomolecular configurations (e.g., folded and unfolded states of a protein). Central to MSM construction is the assumption that, at sufficiently long time lags, these projected dynamics become memoryless, such that the future evolution of the system depends only on its current state. Yet, projecting high-dimensional biomolecular dynamics onto a small set of states necessarily discards information about unresolved degrees of freedom, including solvent reorganization, side-chain rearrangements, and intermediate configurations. Because these unresolved motions can continue to influence subsequent dynamics, the resulting dynamics retain memory that is absent from a Markovian description. Here, we present ugme, a modular, open-source Python package for constructing and validating generalized master equations (GME) models that explicitly account for these non-Markovian (memory) effects.

articles.title: Unveiling the Influence of Graphitic Nanocarbon Structures, Defects, and Surface Functional Groups on Supercapacitive Performance in LiTFSI Electrolyte
articles.abstract: When investigating the performance of supercapacitors (SCs), it was found that they offer high-power density and long life but are limited in capacity and energy density. Water-in-salt electrolytes, i.e., 21___m lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl) imide (LiTFSI), offer a solution by expanding the electrochemical window compared to a diluted aqueous environment. While significant research has been dedicated to improving these electrolytes, the impact of carbon properties on energy storage remains relatively underexplored. This study investigated the influence of carbon structures, defects, and surface functional groups on supercapacitive performance in LiTFSI electrolytes. For this purpose, a series of carbon materials, including carbon nano-onions and porous conductive carbon black (ENSACO), were synthesized and systematically modified by oxidative and reductive thermal treatments. Our results indicated that higher specific surface area and active surface area improve the ion adsorption and capacitance, while specific oxygen functionalities, such as carboxylic and anhydride groups, were found to significantly enhance capacitance. Furthermore, crystallinity and graphitic characteristics play a role in capacitance, with smaller graphene domains and greater disorder promoting ion storage. The study demonstrates a direct correlation between carbon microstructure and electrochemical behavior, providing insights into the rational design of carbon electrodes in high-performance SCs.

articles.title: Alter-excitons in Altermagnets: Symmetry, Splitting and Dispersion
articles.abstract: Magnetism provides a fertile platform for discovering emergent quantum phenomena governed by symmetry. Recent developments of spin-space-group (SSG) theory have revealed altermagnets as a distinct class of nonrelativistic collinear magnets with unconventional spin-dependent electronic structures. Here, we demonstrate that altermagnetic symmetry imposes fundamentally different constraints on electronic and excitonic excitations. Although the quasiparticle and two-body Hamiltonians possess identical SSG symmetries, we find that symmetry-protected degeneracies present in the electronic band structure can be intrinsically lifted in the exciton spectrum at specific momenta. This splitting arises solely from the many-body nature of excitons and does not require spin-orbit coupling or noncollinear magnetic order. Combining symmetry analysis with many-body perturbation theory, we predict a novel class of spin-split excitonic quasiparticles, termed alter-excitons, and reveal their characteristic dispersions in altermagnetic systems. Our results establish excitons as a sensitive probe of hidden spin-space symmetries and uncover a new route toward symmetry-engineered many-body phenomena in collinear magnets.

articles.title: Assessing quantitative phase reliability in electron ptychography using a twisted trilayer WS2 thickness staircase
articles.abstract: The phase of an electron wave is sensitive to the local electrostatic environment and can therefore provide information about atomic-scale structural variations. In electron ptychography, however, specimen thickness, multiple scattering and projected atomic overlap can complicate the quantitative interpretation of the reconstructed phase. Here, we use a twisted trilayer WS2 thickness staircase containing monolayer, bilayer and trilayer regions as an internal reference, with all regions measured under identical experimental conditions. The mean W-column phase increases by approximately 13.2% from the monolayer to the bilayer region, compared with only 4.7% from the bilayer to the trilayer region, revealing a nonlinear thickness dependence. W-S overlap has little effect on the W-column phase, whereas short-range projected W-W overlap increases it by approximately 8-9%. These results provide a benchmark for evaluating quantitative phase measurement in multilayer WS2 and for assessing phase-based mapping of local electrostatic potential, charge-density and three-dimensional atomic-scale polarization.

articles.title: Aubry-André transition in photonic time quasicrystals
articles.abstract: In one dimension, Anderson localization by a disordered potential sets in at any strength, whereas localization by a quasiperiodic potential in the Aubry-André model occurs through a transition at a critical strength. Disordered photonic time crystals exhibit a temporal counterpart of this Anderson localization, in which light, instead of decaying in space, stops propagating and grows in time. Whether a counterpart of the Aubry-André transition exists in photonic time quasicrystals remains an open question. Here we show that it does, and that the transition occurs at mobility edges in momentum rather than in energy. These edges arise even under impulsive modulation, where the field obeys the self-dual almost-Mathieu equation exactly, and for general analytic modulations Avila's global theory reveals the condition under which they form. The Aubry-André transition thus extends from spatial lattices to the time domain, where it sorts light by wave number into components that propagate and components that stop and grow.

articles.title: Dislocation mediated twin boundary faceting in $β$-Sn
articles.abstract: Grain boundaries (GBs), including twin boundaries (TBs), play a critical role in plastic deformation by interacting with dislocations. The deformation and strengthening mechanisms in $β$-Sn are of significant interest because Sn-based alloys are widely used as solder materials. Recent experiments have shown deformation-induced faceting in $β$-Sn arising from twin-dislocation interactions. Using molecular dynamics (MD) simulations informed by a recently developed machine-learned interatomic potential (MLIP), we demonstrate a $\langle c\rangle$ dislocation-absorption mediated faceting reaction along $(301)$ TBs in $β$-Sn in which facet length grows with the number of absorbed dislocations. We show that the predicted facet length is consistent with isotropic elasticity theory only when the disclination character of the asymmetric twin facet is taken into account. We discuss analogies to faceting reactions in other low symmetry metals and hypothesize that the ubiquity of $(301)$ twins in $β$-Sn stems from their ability to grow rapidly through a forest of dislocation obstacles.

articles.title: Doubly Metastable Synthesis for Accelerated Quantum Materials Discovery
articles.abstract: New physics emerges from new materials, which in turn rely on the development of new synthesis techniques. Identifying the enlargement of metastable synthesis window as enabling for realizing novel materials, we develop diffusion-activated epitaxy, a technique which combines two metastable synthesis methods of diffusion and epitaxy. We observe that within a narrow window of investigated synthesis space we can experimentally identify the stabilization of four distinct phases, three of which show X-ray diffraction and scanning transmission electron microscopy characterization data that are incompatible with the crystal structures registered in experimental and computational inorganic structure databases. These results suggest an enlarged metastable synthesis window is enabled by this synthesis approach, identifying doubly metastable synthesis as a promising method for exploration of quantum materials.

articles.title: Evolution and breakdown of chiral anomaly in Weyl semiconductor tellurium
articles.abstract: Chiral anomaly in topological materials manifests as negative longitudinal magnetoresistance, yet the tunability and evolution of this effect remain elusive. Here we show that doped tellurium serves as a versatile platform to realize a giant negative longitudinal magnetoresistance that is highly tunable via the Fermi level and magnetic field. By moving the Fermi level towards the Weyl point, we observe a pronounced enhancement of negative magnetoresistance, which arises from chiral anomaly and robustly persists up to ambient temperature. Beyond the quantum limit, the system exhibits positive linear magnetoconductance, serving as a compelling transport signature of the chiral anomaly in the lowest Landau level. Notably, in the extreme quantum limit at cryogenic temperatures, the magnetoresistance undergoes a dramatic reversal from negative to positive. This reversal points to a potential field-induced phase transition into a collective electronic state driven by enhanced electron-electron interactions. Our findings provide valuable insights into the unconventional chiral transport and emergent correlated quantum states under extreme magnetic fields.

articles.title: Ferroelectric Domain-Wall Motion, Stability, and Frequency Responses under Different Screening-Charge Conservation Laws
articles.abstract: We analyze ferroelectric domain wall motion, shape, and internal structure arising from coupling between polarization and screening charge. Universal cases are organized by electrical boundary conditions, charge conservation and dynamics, and polarization free energy. We consider exposed surfaces, interfaces beneath a dielectric layer and top electrode, and interfaces with a blocking mixed ionic-electronic conductor. Screening occurs through local exchange, exchange with lateral transport, or strictly conserved redistribution. Analytical derivations and finite-depth calculations establish screening drag, velocity branches, and conditions for spatial instability. For an isolated wall joining differently compensated domains, strict surface conservation and zero far-field current exclude steady translation of the screening profile, while allowing transient displacement, finite-sample arrest, and charge-balanced structural changes. Conservation also constrains long-distance transport around a moving junction in an adjoining conductor. Large-field simulations in the top-electrode geometry reveal nonlinear corrugation, transfer toward longer wavelengths, and coupled polarization rotation. First-order polarization energetics allow two interphase fronts enclosing a paraelectric core; multiaxial polarization permits wall rotation and competing intermediate ferroelectric domains. A driven structural-screening reduction supports stable periodic behavior. Reduced-variable diagrams summarize motion and structural regimes, while BaTiO3 and BiFeO3 examples connect them to material thermodynamics. Small-signal analysis distinguishes displacement, polarization, and electrostatic response functions. These results provide a framework for wall dynamics and structural transitions under different driving and screening conditions.

articles.title: High-Throughput Discovery of Chiral Carbon-Boron Semimetals with Weyl Topology and Phonon-Mediated Superconductivity
articles.abstract: Chiral crystals provide a natural platform for unconventional topological fermions, while light-element carbon--boron frameworks are promising for phonon-mediated superconductivity owing to strong covalent bonding and high phonon frequencies. Here, we combine Wyckoff-position-based structure generation with high-throughput first-principles calculations to search for C--B crystals in selected hexagonal chiral space groups. Starting from 972 generated $\mathrm{C}_m\mathrm{B}_n$ structures ($m,n=1\text{--}4$), successive filters based on energetic stability, dynamical stability, electronic metallicity, topological band features, and thermal stability identify six stable candidates: $(\mathrm{C}_3\mathrm{B}_2)_8$, $(\mathrm{C}\mathrm{B}_2)_3$, $(\mathrm{C}\mathrm{B}_4)_6$, $(\mathrm{C}_3\mathrm{B}_2)_6$, $(\mathrm{C}_2\mathrm{B}_3)_6$, and $(\mathrm{C}\mathrm{B}_2)_6$. These materials host diverse topological semimetal states near the Fermi level, including charge-one, charge-two, and charge-three Weyl points, nodal rings, and nodal-surface states. Notably, $(\mathrm{C}_3\mathrm{B}_2)_8$ exhibits screw-symmetry-protected charge-three Weyl points and strong electron--phonon coupling, yielding a McMillan transition temperature of $31.1\,\mathrm{K}$ for the Coulomb pseudopotential parameter $μ^* = 0.10$. In addition, $(\mathrm{C}\mathrm{B}_2)_3$ hosts multiple charge-one Weyl points and pronounced anisotropic multiband superconductivity revealed by fully anisotropic Eliashberg calculations. These results extend the materials scope of topological semimetals with phonon-mediated superconductivity to chemically designed chiral light-element structures.

articles.title: Improved screening of doped ZrO$_2$ catalysts for CO$_2$ hydrogenation from graph-based machine learning
articles.abstract: Dopants can tune the activity of zirconia-based CO$_2$ hydrogenation catalysts through changes in adsorbate and transition-state (TS) energetics. Computing these quantities with density functional theory (DFT) becomes expensive when several dopants, reaction intermediates, and TSs must be screened. Here, we further develop the graph-based machine learning method Wasserstein Weisfeiler-Lehman Gaussian Process Regression (WWL-GPR): we introduce additional electronic-structure and local-environment features relevant for oxide surfaces and use the resulting model to predict adsorption and TS energies on ZrO$_2$(101) surfaces doped with Al$^{3+}$, Cd$^{2+}$, Ga$^{3+}$, In$^{3+}$, and Zn$^{2+}$. Adsorbate-surface structures are represented as attributed graphs that combine bonds connectivity and features. We benchmark WWL-GPR against thermodynamic scaling relations (TSR) for reaction intermediates and Bronsted-Evans-Polanyi relations (BEP) for TSs, and then propagate the predicted energies to microkinetic CH$_3$OH-yield estimates. WWL-GPR consistently improves the prediction of reaction intermediate energetics relative to linear scaling approaches and provides TS estimates that are competitive with BEP-based models. These improvements become especially relevant when the predicted energetics are propagated through the reaction network. Microkinetic calculations show that WWL-GPR-derived energies give CH$_3$OH yields closer to DFT-derived yields than the linear-relation workflow. Degree-of-rate-control analysis links the activity errors to dopant-dependent rate-controlling steps, including HCOO* formation, H$_2$COOH* dissociation, and H$_3$CO* formation. These results support WWL-GPR as a data-efficient surrogate for connecting atomistic energetics with catalyst-screening observables on doped oxide surfaces.

articles.title: A Hardware-Native Trapped-Ion Hybrid Qudit-Oscillator Instruction Set
articles.abstract: Scaling trapped-ion processors by adding ions remains challenging. A complementary route exploits the multilevel internal structure of each ion to increase the computational Hilbert space per ion. We introduce a hardware-native hybrid qudit-oscillator instruction set for a general d-level internal register coupled to bosonic modes and prove that three of its native operation families suffice for universality of one qudit coupled to several modes. Adding an entangling operation between ions extends universality to a connected register of several qudits. The architecture natively supports both phase-space and sideband instruction sets and is implemented in the open-source framework HybridLane. As a representative application, we reproduce the dissipative vibronic dynamics of a three-chromophore complex previously simulated on a hybrid qubit-oscillator superconducting platform. Moving from a one-qubit-per-state register to a single qudit stores the entire electronic manifold in one ion, so every electronic coupling becomes a local intra-ion transition and the lab-frame Hamiltonian compiles directly into the ISA. Under the stated sequential timing model from a 40Ca+ qudit processor, one Trotter step is projected to run about ten times faster on the qudit, with an average RMSE of approximately 1.1 percent against the published reference.

articles.title: A scalable sample-based quantum diagonalization solver for general Pauli-sum Hamiltonians
articles.abstract: A scalable ground-state solver to be used in sample-based quantum diagonalization (SQD) is presented. The solver is built on JAX API, and is intended to be run on GPU platforms and possibly many-GPU high-performance computing facilities. It is capable of subspace diagonalization in up to $2^{30}$-dimensional subspace, with possible upgrades to enable even larger-scale operations. The two main components, a general-purpose eigensolver and an SQD-specific matrix-vector operation function, are described in detail. Efficiency of the eigensolver with respect to the GPU memory is demonstrated using a simple physics model. Furthermore, good strong scaling of the eigensolver in many-GPU environment is observed.

articles.title: An Annealing-based Quantum Neural Network with Discrete Wavelet Transforms for Enhanced Air Pollution Nowcasting
articles.abstract: Air pollution poses a significant threat to public health, exacerbated by the rapid industrialization and urbanization of modern society. While traditional deep learning offers predictive capabilities, recent advancements in quantum machine learning (QML) present a compelling alternative. Here, we introduce a scalable hybrid framework that integrates variational quantum circuits with quantum annealing. Leveraging a neuromorphic quantum computing platform to transcend the qubit limitations of the NISQ era, we model particulate matter (PM$_{2.5}$) dynamics using high-density urban data from the UK. We demonstrate that our Quantum Neural Networks (QNNs) exhibit an intrinsic resilience to input volatility, significantly outperforming classical baselines (MLP and LSTM) on raw, high-entropy environmental data. Furthermore, we successfully scaled the model to 172 qubits, observing a synergistic enhancement when coupled with wavelet decomposition that achieves state-of-the-art predictive fidelity. These findings establish a critical benchmark for quantum utility, proving that scalable, neuromorphic quantum machine learning can now address complex, non-linear real-world problems.

articles.title: Bicycle Race: small two-block codes on the Pareto frontier
articles.abstract: Two-block group-algebra codes are among the simplest quantum LDPC codes, and many of them are translation invariant on a twisted torus, which suits neutral-atom arrays and other platforms with movable qubits. We ask how far they go at small sizes when searched systematically across all groups. To tackle this question, we use a series of algebraic constraints and screens to design a search pipeline capable of enumerating broad and complete swathes of two-block codes on a laptop. With it we census about $10^8$ two-block codes with up to $320$ qubits at check weights five to nine. Several of these censuses are exhaustive, and support complete statements; for instance, the Gross code is, up to equivalence, the only abelian weight-six two-block code with $n \le 200$ to reach $kd^2/n=12$, and the known $[[64,18,8]]$ is the best two-block code by $kd^2/n$ across weights five to nine with $n \le 94$. The censuses are also large enough to give insights into where good codes live - they concentrate in a handful of groups; abelian groups give the best codes at small $n$ and non-abelian groups at large $n$, with the crossover appearing to move out as the check weight grows; and high quality codes become $100$ to $1000$ times rarer per draw from weight six to weights eight and nine. Using the group algebra and the census data to steer a statistical search finds four to fifteen times as many good codes as uniform draws in equal time. Among the codes found are $[[102,20,10]]$ and $[[120,24,10]]$ at check weight nine, which we simulate in noisy syndrome-extraction circuits, and $[[288,16,16]]$, the best weight-six two-block code with $n \le 300$. At check weights seven to nine, our best codes exceed the best published $kd^2/n$ with exact distance at the same check weight in most length bands up to $320$ qubits. All codes are available in a public database.

articles.title: Bottom-Up Surface-Enhanced Raman Scattering for the Detection of Micro-Objects and Globular Analytes
articles.abstract: Surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) is typically achieved by depositing the analyte on a metal or semiconductor substrate. We propose a bottom-up approach, enabling SERS by depositing a metal on the surface of the object being studied. A Mie-theory analysis of electric-field enhancement in dielectric core-shell particles is presented. A correlative approach combining SERS, atomic force microscopy, and scanning electron microscopy is employed to model the conditions required for sensitive SERS detection and spectral analysis of polystyrene microspheres (PMSs) as models of globular and vesicle-like objects. Based on these findings, we propose a SERS-active system that provides strong signal enhancement (up to four orders of magnitude for a single globular object) while maintaining spectral fidelity, where PMSs act both as model analytes and as integral components of a metal-dielectric resonator.

articles.title: Chiroptical Nonlinearity Found in Covalent Organic Frameworks
articles.abstract: Chiroptical nonlinearity is vital for modern optics and photonics. However, it remains a central challenge to obtain a material simultaneously with large second-order nonlinearity and strong nonlinear optical chirality. Here we uncover the strong chiroptical nonlinearity in COF-330-a, owing to the formation of unique chiral, polar structure with large p-electron conjugation via structural transformation. A large effective second-order nonlinear susceptibility of ~ 101 pm/V and a strong nonlinear chiroptical response (SHG-CD: -1.60 to +1.66) have been demonstrated in individual COF-330-a microcrystals, transcending the performance trade-off limitation in conventional chiroptical materials.
